The same comparison, a joy that surpasses liquor because it needs no drinking, is made of love in the Kural and of breath in the Tirumanthiram.

A near-repeat: 568 gives the measures of breath as sixteen in, sixty-four held and thirty-two out (ஈரெட்டு ... அறுபத்து நாலு ... முப்பத்திரண்டு); 573 repeats the same sixteen, thirty-two and sixty-four (ஈரெட்டு ... முப்பத்திரண்டு ... எட்டெட்டு) and adds that the exhalation goes by pingala.

569 says if one draws in the air and holds it, the ripened body becomes unripe (பழுக்கினும் பிஞ்சாம்); 722 says if one ties fast the horse of twelve legs, the body will not leave for thousands of years (பேராது காயம்). Both promise that the held breath keeps the body from ageing.

577 figures the breath as twelve elephants (பன்னிரண்டானை) the mahout must come to know; 722 figures it as a horse with twelve legs (ஈராறு கால்) to be tied fast. The same count of twelve, the breath's finger-breadths on the traditional reading, gives the beast its form in both.

The Kural asks one to draw in the five senses like a tortoise for protection through seven births; Tirumular's withdrawal goes on past restraint to what is found inside: the one the Veda searched for.
Both place the inner power two fingers above the lower opening and two below the genital one: 580 calls it kundalini, 584 only a light.
Both end with the same line, that Siva will not leave, and both make it the fruit of the breath held within.
audit_text_issue: 586 line 1 (புறப்பட்ட வாயுப் புகவிடா) is hard to construe.

note: 582 says a line of light is flawless supreme bliss (கோதில் பரானந்தம்) and that the body, with moonlight at the throat, becomes உன்மத்தம். 2779 calls staggering and falling Siva's bliss (திண்டாடி வீழ்கை சிவானந்தம்) and says drinking more brings உன்மத்தம். Both use the word for madness as the sign of bliss, one from the yogi's inner light, the other from the sight of the dance.

587 and 1794 are the same verse with small differences: the world appears within intention (குறிப்பினின் உள்ளே குவலயம் தோன்றும்), the Lord stands when aversion's darkness goes, and the knowing vision makes one like the immortals (அறிப்புறு காட்சி அமரரும் ஆமே). 1794 reads வெறுப்பிருள் நீங்கில் where 587 has the obscure நங்கி, which supports reading 587 as 'gone'. The near-repeat sits once under pratyahara and once under grace.
audit_text_issue: 587 நங்கி likely a corruption of நீங்கி

note: Both use the heron that waits motionless: in the Kural it is the king biding his time before striking, in Tirumular the yogi who holds still in breath and mind.
Both say no one who came before has escaped death: the Naladiyar shows it in kings under their umbrellas, Tirumular in all who came before.
580 places the coiled kundalini at the root; 590 has the power rising from the root region roused and joined above, with the return to youth as its fruit.

588 tells the yogi to fix the mind and stay as eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear (காணாக்கண் கேளாச் செவி) to stop life's days running out. 1610 says Nandi came and showed an eye that does not see and a hearing that does not hear (காணாத கண்ணுடன் கேளாத கேள்வியும்) together with the awareness at nada's end. The same paradox is a practice the yogi takes on in 588 and a gift shown by the teacher in 1610.

583 gives a method (close the lower door, mind on the upper door, eyes open to the void) and calls it the way to conquer time (காலத்தை வெல்லும்). 592 explains why it works by the pun on கால் as breath and time: the life is the pressure of the breath, and if the breath is bound (காலது கட்டின்) the body's time stands still (காலமும் நிற்குமே). 592 gives the reason behind 583's promise.

593 says those who do not open the mouth (வாய்திறவாதார்) hold a treasure in the mind, and those who open it drive it out with breath. 1780 places the object the teacher told him to think on daily below the crown and above the uvula, held with the mouth not opened (வாய்திற வாதே). The closed mouth is in both a condition of inner practice, which helps fix the sense of the obscure 593.

595 asks the fool what he will do when five of the ten (ஈரைந்தில் ஐந்து, the vital airs) have gone, and says those who make a way can bag the monkey of the mind. Thiruppugazh 1036 counts the breaths by hundreds and thousands by which the little life runs out (ஓடுஞ் சிறுவுயிர்) and asks whether the good yoga that turns it back (மீளும்படி நல யோகம்) is not to be had. Both set the running-out of breath against a yoga that can still be practised, one as warning, the other as prayer.
audit_text_issue: Both verses flagged uncertain; TM 595's கொட்டை பொதியலும் is obscure.

note: Both call the yogic body a bedchamber (பள்ளி அறை): in 594 it is the great chamber with two doors where held breath lets one live long, in 611 the chamber where it is always day.
Both promise the yogi the body's survival for an aeon (ஊழி): 591 through binding the breath at the lower door, 612 through rising up the spine through the three mandalas.
Both measure the yogic body from the navel in fingers: 580 places coiled kundalini four fingers below it, 616 places the point of contemplation four fingers above.
audit_text_issue: 616 நடலித்த, மடலித்த, கடலித்து may be corrupt.

note: 598 names among meditation's parts the meditation on Siva who comes as guru (குருவார் சிவத்தியானம்). 1780 shows what such meditation is in practice: the teacher (ஆசாரியன்) set a place and told him to think on it daily (நிச்சலும் என்னை நினை). 1780 gives the guru-given object that 598 only lists as a kind of dhyana.

Kural 27 says the world lies with the one who discerns the kinds of the five, taste, light, touch, sound and smell (ஐந்தின் வகைதெரிவான் கட்டே உலகு). 599 places within the gathering of eye, tongue, nose and ear one ancient being who tunes them (பண்ணாக்கி நின்ற பழம்பொருள்). The Kural credits the person who masters the senses; Tirumular credits a presence within them that saves by breaking the self (புண்ணாக்கி நம்மைப் பிழைப்பித்த).

601 repeats that people never once contemplate (ஒருபொழுது உன்னார்) the life in the body, Siva in the life, or the mind where Siva dwells. 2390 uses the same verb: they do not think of the One or the soul (ஒருவனை உன்னார் உயிர்தனை உன்னார்), yet the One stands within, knowing, and feeds them. 2390 adds what 601 leaves out: their neglect does not withdraw the indweller.

Kural 299 says not all lamps are lamps; for the worthy the lamp that does not fail, truthfulness, is the lamp (பொய்யா விளக்கே விளக்கு). 602 sets lamps against each other: light the mind's lamp, smother the lamp of anger (சினத்து விளக்கு), and the mind's lamp becomes one that does not die (மாயா விளக்கு). Both rank lamps and keep one as the true one, the Kural an ethical virtue, Tirumular the mind made steady by meditation once anger is put out.

603 says that even after eight thousand years of yoga no one sees the nectar in the eye (கண்டறி வாரில்லை), but looking within the inner channel he stands merged as in a mirror. 2522 says none who have entered within truly know Nandi (உணர்ந்தறி வாரில்லை), yet the poet, eyes closed, saw his form. Both deny the vision to the many and then report it for the one who looks the right way within.

604 and 605 give the same practice in nearly the same words: both gazes set at the middle of the nose (நாட்டமும் இரண்டும் நடுமூக்கில், நயனம் இரண்டும் நாசிமேல்). 604 ends in identity, 'we become Siva' (சிவனவ நாமே); 605 adds holding the breath and ends with a body without fear (காயம் பயமில்லை). The pair shows one technique given two fruits, one spiritual and one bodily.

606 lists the ten inner sounds and says none but those who have bowed (பணிந்தவர்க்கு அல்லது) can perceive them. 607 lists them again and says none but the yogi who knows firmness (திடமறி யோகிக்கு அல்லால்) can know them. The same sounds are conditioned once on humility and once on steadiness; read together, the two conditions qualify each other.

608 says the Lord is a sound that spreads like its own fragrance (ஓசை அதன் மணம் போல விடுவதோர் ஓசையாம் ஈசன்). 1459 says Siva's fragrance (சிவமணம்) has blossomed within the soul as scent dwells in a flower. Both use fragrance for a presence that pervades without being seen, 608 in sound, 1459 in the soul.

609 places Shakti, good yoga, the aim and the poison-throated Lord at the end of nada (நாத முடிவிலே). 1435 names those who have seen the end of nada (நாதாந்தங் கண்டோர்) as yogis who do not waver (நடுக்கற்ற யோகிகள்) and sets them beside the Vedantin and the Saiva. 1435 places 609's goal within Tirumular's ranking of paths.

617 says devotees go beyond the thirty-six (ஆறாறு அகன்று) and shatter maya by grace (அருளாலே). 2020 says Nandi made known the nature of the thirty-six, and after it was known by grace (அருளால் அறிந்த பின்) he stood beyond the thirty-six (ஆறாறுக்கு அப்புறம்). Both make grace, not technique, the step past the tattvas, one inside the chapter on dhyana, the other in the poet's own voice.
552 lists the eight limbs from yama to samadhi; 618 draws the consequence that samadhi is reached only through yama and the rest, so the ethical limbs are the way to the highest.
618 makes samadhi the fruit of the limbs; 631 says that for one who goes with the Lord samadhi is not needed and for one who becomes him there is none, so the chapter's goal is itself relative.
583 calls closing the lower door and fixing the mind on the upper one the way to conquer time; 622 says that once the upper door opens Death's word is not heard even in dreams.
The Kural says those who have won the power of austerity can even leap past Death; Tirumular names a yogic means, the upper door seen open, for the same escape.

The Naladiyar says no one here has leapt clear of Death and escaped, so give your wealth now; Tirumular says the yogi who sees the upper door will not hear Death even in dreams. The conflict holds on the literal reading of 622, that the yogi escapes death; if it means only freedom from fear of death, it dissolves.

604 sets the two gazes at the middle of the nose and lists what ceases, seeking (தேட்டம்) among them; 624 turns the gaze back to the eye and settles the breath in the ground 'without seeking' (தேட்டற்ற), and names the fruit.

620 says where the abiding mind is the breath is, where it is not the breath is not (மன்மனம் எங்குண்டு வாயுவும் அங்குண்டு), and that the mind's dissolving comes within the mind. 2981 says the mind's spreading and drawing in is the breath (மனம் விரிந்து குவிந்தது வாயு) and that the mind's ending is release. Both hold mind and breath to be one movement, so that stilling the mind is the goal of breath-practice.

621 says the yogis reined the horse with the bridle (குதிரை குசைசெறுத்தாரே) in the inner landscape. 1679 tells people to hold firmly the bridle of the running horse (ஒடுங் குதிரைக் குசைதிண்ணம் பற்றுமின்) rather than put on an ascetic's garb. The horse and bridle are the restless breath or mind and its control in both; 1679 sets it against outward show.

624 promises the yogi who locks the breath and turns the gaze within that the mango in the garden hangs within reach (தோட்டத்து மாம்பழந் தூங்கலு மாமே). 2933 has the mango in the garden dug out and fallen (தோட்டத்தில் மாம்பழம் தோண்டி விழுந்தக்கால்), and calling the jackal is then useless. The same garden mango is the fruit held in 624 and the fruit lost in 2933.

626 says the seekers made love the means (அன்பினை யாக்கி), subdued desire, climbed and worshipped the light in red gold. 270 says love and Siva are not two (அன்பே சிவமாவது) and those who know it rest as love that is Siva. 626 makes love the way to the goal; 270 makes it the goal itself.

628 calls samadhi the state in which, free of imagining (கற்பனை யற்று), one becomes the Supreme (தற்பரமாக). 2943, in the chapter on silent samadhi, says he is not the Supreme (தற்பரம் அல்ல), not Sadasiva, not formless or with form, but mingles without imagining (கற்பனை இன்றிக் கலந்து). Both require the end of imagining; 2943 refuses even the name தற்பரம் that 628 gives as the goal.

602 makes putting out the lamp of anger (சினத்து விளக்கினைச் செல்ல நெருக்கி) part of meditation. 629 lists among the fruits of absorption that anger is broken and goes (குலைப்பட் டிருந்திடுங் கோபம் அகலும்) and the yogi stays in balance (துலைப்பட்டு). Anger's end is a discipline in 602 and a result in 629.

630 says the God who stood as the single flame becomes the soul standing within (உள்நின்ற சீவனும் ஆகுமால்). 2017 says there is no difference called soul and Siva (சீவன் எனச்சிவன் என்னவே றில்லை). The agreement holds on the reading உள்நின்ற; the variant முன்நின்ற (standing before) would weaken 630's claim.

Both speak of the one who goes upon the flower and of those who reach his feet. The Kural promises they live long upon the earth (or, as Parimelazhagar takes it, in the world of release); Tirumular promises Amaravati, then in the following verses the Siva-state.

597 defines dharana as holding with the Supreme (தரித்தது தாரணை தற்பரத்தோடே) after dissolving body into elements and mind; 639 defines samadhi as joining the Supreme (தற்பரஞ் சேர்தல்) after going beyond all upadhi. The two limbs differ as holding and joining.
585 makes pratyahara the separating and dissolving of upadhi from the inner light; 639 makes samadhi the going beyond upadhi altogether, so the two verses mark stages on one line.
audit_text_issue: Both verses are technical and partly obscure (639 தாரியல்).

note: Kural 2 asks what learning has achieved if the learned do not bow at the good feet of the pure knower (வாலறிவன் நற்றாள் தொழாஅர் எனின்). 633 joins the two: those who hold his feet with love and learn the Supreme's praise (பதத்தன்பு வைத்துப் பரன்புகழ் கற்றிருந்து) reach the Siva-state. The Kural makes worship the fruit of learning; 633 makes learning his praise part of the devotion that reaches him.

Kural 25 says Indra, lord of the wide heavens, is witness enough to the strength of one who quenched the five senses (ஐந்தவித்தான் ஆற்றல்). 634 says those who worshipped and did austerity become king of the gods (வானவர் கோவாய்), hailed as lord of Amaravati. Both measure the ascetic by Indra; the Kural puts him above Indra as witness, while 634 gives him Indra's throne, which 635 then goes beyond.

604 ends its account of the gaze at the nose with 'we become Siva' (சிவனவ நாமே). 636 shows what that looks like from outside: when the yogi arrives the gods of the directions ask who he is and are told 'this is Hara' (அரனாம் இவன்), and this is called proof that he truly saw Siva. 636 makes 604's claim of identity something others recognise.

Kural 50 says one who lives on earth as life should be lived is placed among the gods in the sky (வானுறையும் தெய்வத்துள் வைக்கப் படும்). 637 says householders of unshrinking giving (இல்வழியாளர் சுருங்காப் பெருங்கொடை) may reach the gods' many ways, yet it becomes the way of the earth (பார்வழி யாகுமே). On the reading that the heavens lead back to earth, the household's highest reward in the Kural is in 637 short of release; on the reading 'a way for the world' there is no conflict.

634 says those who worshipped and did austerity become king of the gods and dwell in bliss in Amaravati, and calls this the Lord's grace. 637 says those who reach the gods' realms by good speech and great giving find it becomes the way of the earth (பார்வழி யாகுமே). On that reading 637 limits the heaven of 634: a godly realm is not yet the Siva-state of 635.

639 defines samadhi as going beyond the limiting adjunct that is effect (காரியமான உபாதி) so the seven causes (காரணம் ஏழும்) come to oneself, and joining the Supreme. 2505 says the bound soul mixes in the seven effects and Parasiva in the seven causes (காரியம் ஏழில், காரணம் ஏழில்), beyond which he is the Supreme. 2505 supplies the scheme of seven effects and seven causes that 639 assumes without naming.
Both say a discipline can carry one past Death: the Kural's power gained through tapas leaps over Yama (கூற்றம் குதித்தல்); Tirumular's yogis of the brow and staff have no Yama (நமனில்லை).

The Naladiyar says no one has leapt clear of Death and escaped, so give while you can; Tirumular says those who know the yogic way have no Yama. The conflict holds if நமனில்லை means escape from bodily death; if it means freedom from Yama's judgement after death, the two need not clash.

The Naladiyar's wise renounce in childhood because grey hair will surely come; Tirumular says that by the eighth stage of practice grey hair and wrinkles do not appear. The conflict depends on reading 647 literally, as a claim about the body, and not as a figure for inner freshness.

Both say not every lamp is the lamp: the Kural's one true lamp is truthfulness, Tirumular's is the higher inner light that makes release easy. The image is shared, the light is moral in one and yogic in the other.
669 says the eight siddhis come by eightfold yoga and mastered breath; 670 adds that they come into being only when Shakti Tripurai grants grace. Technique is necessary but not sufficient.
Two lists of the eight siddhis in one chapter. 668's is closer to the standard anima list; set side by side they show the items were not fixed in wording.
audit_text_issue: 649 has known variants (நோன்மையும், ககனமும்); 668's நேர்மை / இணுகாத வேகார் uncertain

note: 641 credits the siddhis and the end of birth to grace given to one who sought the Lord's feet; 707 says outward travel finds nothing, and love alone knows where the Lord dwells.

640 says that bowing and worshipping the Lord in the eight directions (தொழுதெம் பிரானை) set the eight great siddhis in place. 1006 says that if one comes and worships (எய்தி வழிப்படில்) the eight siddhis come (எண்சித்தி உண்டாகும்), after Indra's wealth and before release. Both make the siddhis a fruit of worship, and 1006 shows they are a middle stage, not the end.

641 says the eight great siddhis are not hard for him (அரியது எனக்கில்லை அட்டமா சித்தி) because the Lord gave grace and cut off his birth. Thiruppugazh 281 asks to be set at the red-gold feet that make all powers and the eight siddhis easy (அகில சத்தியும் எட்டுறு சித்தியும் எளிதென). In both the siddhis become easy through the Lord's gift and stand second to the release or the feet asked for.

642 says that by the guru's grace, with the shambhavi and khechari seals joined (சாம்பவி கேசரி சேர), the great Siva-state is the gain of the eight siddhis. 1897 names the yoga mudra as the eight siddhis (யோகத்தின் முத்திரை ஓர்அட்ட சித்தியாம்) and sorts khechari and shambhavi between yoga and knowledge. The pairing shows the two seals tied to the siddhis in both places, with 1897 setting them under separate paths.

643 speaks of one beginningless knowledge (அறிவொன்று அனாதியே) that body, elements, kala, time and maya do not reach, and makes entering another body possible when it joins the Lord. 2181 says the thirty-six tattvas are without knowledge (அறிவொன்றிலாதன) and that he learned from Nandi that he himself is the knower. 2181 says what 643's knowledge apart from the tattvas is: the soul as knower, made known by the guru.

643 says that when the beginningless knowledge joins the Lord, entering another body (பரகாயம் மேவல்) becomes possible. 1906 says the faultless jnani-yogi, leaving the body, becomes That and does not take another body (பரகாயம் சாராதே). Read together, the power 643 promises is one the perfected knower of 1906 no longer uses.

644 says twenty thousand eight hundred kinds of karma, mantra and yoga only tire the body (காய உழைப்பாகும்), and for siddhi they come down to four. Naladiyar 135 says learning has no shore and life is short, so learn what is fitting, like the bird that leaves the water and drinks the milk. Both answer a boundless stock of means with the same move, reducing it to the few that serve the end.

646 lists powers that come in order: freedom from disease and poison, arts and learning, long intellect and keen wisdom (கலைகல்வி நீள்மேதை கூர்ஞானம்), hearing from afar. 705 repeats the same items: removing poison, revered learning and great wisdom (வணங்குற்ற கல்விமா ஞானம்), hearing from afar (தூரங் கேட்டல்). The near-repeat shows the chapter counting learning and wisdom among the siddhis, not only as their means.

652 says those whose mind becomes full of Siva and who have reached silence (மோனர்) are freed in Siva (சிவமுத்தர்). 1611 says that for those to whom silence has come (மோனங்கை வந்தோர்க்கு) release comes and the siddhis stand before them. Both put silence and release above the powers this chapter lists; 1611 adds that the powers then follow of themselves.

653 says the nine airs are in accord (ஒத்த) with dhananjaya above them, and while it stays in accord body and life stay together; 654 and 655 list the swellings that follow when it does not. Kural 941 says the three humours beginning with wind (வளிமுதலா எண்ணிய மூன்று) cause disease whether in excess or deficiency. Yogic and medical texts share one logic: health is the balance of the body's airs or humours, disease their disorder.

655 lists swellings, tumour (கழலை), leprosy and anaemia (சோகை) as diseases of a disordered dhananjaya. 263 gives anaemia (சோகை) and tumour (கழலை) a moral cause: they come to those who do not do dharma and stay away from those who do. Set side by side, the same diseases get a bodily cause in 655 and a moral one in 263, and neither verse mentions the other's.

657 says Isa, Tirumal and Brahma stood without ceasing and knew (உணர்ந்திருந்தாரே) the radiant light reached through the sound in the channel. 88 says Brahma and Vishnu, seeking foot and crown, did not see his form (படிகண்டிலர்), and Brahma lied that he had. The conflict holds if 657's light is the same Lord 88 calls unseen; if it is an inner yogic light, 657 may be saying that stillness found what the search of 88 missed.

658 places in the body of nine gates (ஒன்பது வாசல்) a place of nine channels, and those who still them gain visions. Naladiyar 47 calls the body a pot that seeps filth from nine openings (ஒன்பது வாய்ப்புலனும்) to shame the lover. The same nine openings are a cause for disgust in the Naladiyar and a site of practice in Tirumular.

658 speaks of the body with nine gates (ஒன்பது வாசல்) holding nine channels that can be stilled. 470 says the Lord set the body with nine gates as sluices (மடைவைத்த ஒன்பது வாய்தலும்) and set fire at the lotus of the head. Both treat the nine openings as built for a purpose, and 470 names the builder.

661 says those who ran and saw the one thing raise nada within the channel (நாடியி னுள்ளாக நாதம் எழுப்புவர்), drink the honey and bind the enemies in the camp. 667 repeats the line on binding the enemies in the camp (பாடியுள் நின்ற பகைவரைக் கட்டிட்டு) after seeking with the sound of nada in the channel, and ends in a jewelled lamp. It is a near-repeat inside the chapter; 667 gives the end as light where 661 gives it as honey.

667 ends the inner search with the nada in the channel as a jewelled lamp in one hand (மணிவிளக் கானதே). 820 says that when the breath rises the temple daubed with black, the body, becomes a jewelled lamp (மையணி கோயில் மணிவிளக் காமே). Both use the gem lamp for the light that held breath and inner sound kindle in the body.

669 says the eight siddhis come by eightfold yoga and mastered breath, when the fire at the root of the central channel (நடுநாடி மூலத்த னல்) drives the sun and lets the moon drink. Thiruppugazh 1045 describes the breath stopped, the fire kindled at the root (மூல ... அனல்மூள) and the nectar drunk, with the powers of striking Yama and travelling the sky. The same yogic sequence of root fire and drunk nectar is a path to siddhi in Tirumular and, in Arunagiri, a step toward loss of the self.
audit_text_issue: 1045 has a corrupt glyph in பான ஧ம்முல.

note: 670 says the siddhis come into being when Shakti Tripurai grants grace (திரிபுரை சத்தி அருள்தர). Thiruppugazh 194 says that if one knows Murugan as the gem, everything comes, and that mercury and the metals (இரதாதிகளால்) give only charcoal. Both deny that technique alone yields the powers and give them to a deity's gift, Shakti in one and Murugan in the other.

671 says those who have gained the eight with the Supreme are siddhas because they reach the supreme world (சித்தர் பரலோகஞ் சேர்தலால்). 1674 says the Siva-jnani, being one of silence, is released and a siddha (முத்தனாஞ் சித்தனாம்). Both define the siddha by the goal rather than the powers, and 1674 reaches it by knowledge and silence instead of the eight.

674 says that if the times of dying stay in one's own control (சாகின்ற காலங்கள் தன்வழி நின்றிடின்), great lightness comes in five years. Naladiyar 6 says the appointed days cannot be exceeded and no one has leapt clear of Death. The conflict holds if 674 means control over the hour of one's own death, as its wording suggests.

677 says after seeing the light of the breath (காலொளி) the passing times no longer pass. 680 repeats the last two lines word for word (போகின்ற காலங்கள் போவது மில்லையே) after the light of lightning (மின்னொளி). It is a near-repeat in the chapter, with the light named differently.

677 says that after seeing the breath's light, the passing times do not pass (போகின்ற காலங்கள் போவது மில்லையாம்), playing on கால் as breath and time. Kural 334 says the day is a blade that saws through life (உயிர் ஈரும் வாளது) for those who see it. The conflict holds if 677 means that the master of breath is no longer worn down by time; on a reading where it describes only an inner experience, the claims do not meet.

681 says that for those who know there is nothing that goes, nothing that comes, nothing that dies (போவதொன் றில்லை வருவது தானில்லை சாவதொன் றில்லை). 2854 says that for those who examine the hidden thing there is no going, no coming and no ruin (போக்கொன்றும் இல்லை வரவில்லை கேடில்லை). The near-repeat, in a chapter on powers and a chapter on seeing Siva, puts the knower's changeless state beyond the lights 677 to 680 describe.

682 says that dwelling in Parashakti for a year makes entering another body (பரகாய மேவல்) possible. 2133 uses that power as a simile: the subtle body, after heaven and hell, takes a new birth like a yogi who enters another body (பரகாய யோகிபோல்). The same act is a hard-won siddhi in 682 and, in 2133, what every soul does in rebirth.

686 says the yogi becomes able to create, protect and destroy (தானே படைத்திட ... அளித்திட ... சங்காரத் தலைவனு மாயிடும்), and that it is said of him, he is himself the one. 1809 uses the same தானே refrain for the Lord, who creates, protects, destroys, conceals and himself grants release. 1809 keeps concealment and the granting of release with the Lord, two acts 686 does not give the yogi.

686 gives the yogi who has gained the siddhis the power to create, protect and destroy. 1611 says that for those to whom silence has come the five acts come forward (ஐந் கருமமும் முன்னுமே). Both let the Lord's acts pass in some measure to the perfected one, by siddhi in 686 and by silence in 1611.

688 turns vashitva into being the very self of all lives (உயிர்க்கெல்லாந் தற்பொருளாகிய தன்மையன்). Thiruppugazh 1045 asks for the state in which 'mine' and 'I' fall away and everyone and everything becomes oneself (எவரும் யாதும் யானாகும்). Both make the highest power an identity with all beings rather than control over them.

706 counts escaping death and old age (மரணஞ் சரைவிடல்) among the twenty-one powers. Thiruppugazh 1316 asks whether, fattening the belly with food every day, one can gain the yogic power that lengthens life (உயிரினீடு யோக சித்தி), and seeks instead the feet of knowledge. The song doubts that the indulgent can win the power 706 lists, and sets the feet above it.

707 says circling the world and walking till the feet ache is of no use (பயனில்லை), and those who see the Lord in love know where he dwells. 509 says there are many holy waters within the heart, and those who do not bathe there wander over hollow and height (பள்ளமும் மேடும் பரந்து திரிவரே). Both set the inner place against the pilgrim's road, by love in 707 and by inward bathing in 509.

707 says walking round the world till the feet ache brings no gain (பாதங்கள் நோவ நடந்தும் பயனில்லை). 1445 tells the reader to seek through lands, towns and temples (நாடு நகரமும் நற்றிருக் கோயிலுந் தேடித் திரிந்து), singing and bowing, after which the Lord takes the heart as his temple. The conflict holds if 707's 'no use' is absolute; if it means walking without love, 1445's chariyai is the outward stage that 707 assumes is already passed.

The same charge in two parts of the yogic body: no one knows how the breath is wasted (அழியும் படியை அறிகிலர், 720), people do not know how much bindu is lost (1936). In both the knowing is the remedy: 720 says the one who learns it can join the breath to Nandi.

712 makes love the way (காதல் வழிசெய்து) to the forehead-eyed Lord and to guarding oneself, repeating the phrase in every line. 270 states the ground of that: love itself is Siva (அன்பே சிவமாவது), and those who know it rest as love that is Siva. 712 applies to yogic practice the identity 270 states outright.

713 says the four inner instruments, the sixteen kalas and the breath can all be guarded if one stands with the mind fixed (கருத்துற நில்லே). 578, in the pratyahara chapter, says that drawing the mind within (உள்ளே கருத்துற வாங்கிடில்) lets one see many qualities and stay with the one the Veda sought. The same phrase names the condition in both: one verse for guarding the body's powers, the other for finding the Lord.

714 compares the steadied breath to a lamp that stands still (சிலைபெற நின்றது தீபமும் ஒத்து). 1139 has Shakti well up, steady, with the light of a good lamp (தேறியிருந்து நல் தீபத்து ஒளியுடன்) for those with inner sight. Both use the unflickering lamp for the stilled interior where the practice succeeds.

716 says people do not know how much time remains, and the true practitioner looks to lengthening it (பெருக்கின்ற காலப் பெருமை) by holding the breath. Thiruppugazh 1036 asks for the good yoga by which the little life that runs out in hundreds and thousands of breaths (அறுநூறும் ... ஓடும் சிறுவுயிர்) may be turned back (மீளும்படி). Both reckon life as a stock of breaths that practice can extend; the song asks for what 716 claims.

719 says the Lady of the tattvas makes her way through the flesh (ஊனே வழிசெய்து) and the body becomes Siva's temple (சிவாலயமாகுமே). 1823 builds the temple out of the person: the heart the great temple, the body of flesh the shrine (ஊனுடம்பு ஆலயம்), the mouth the gate, the senses the lamps. 719 says how the body becomes a temple, through Shakti; 1823 lays out its parts.

721 says testing shows the day the Lord parts from the Lady (நாதனும் நாயகி தன்னிற் பிரியுநாள்); 723 says the senses' counts show the day the radiant Lady and Lord part (தேசியும் தேசனும் தன்னிற் பிரியுநாள்). The two verses use the same figure for death, the parting of Siva and Shakti in the body, and pairing them fixes that reading of both: 721 sends the reader to the guru, 723 to the failing senses.

On what the body is worth: the Naladiyar calls it a pot seeping filth from nine openings, attractive only through its skin, and the man who praises it a fool; Tirumular says he once held the body base (இழுக்கு) but found the Lord had made it his temple, and so cherishes it. The conflict holds if the Naladiyar's verse is read as a verdict on the body and not only as a remedy for lust.

Both value the body for what it yields, but the Naladiyar has the body thrown away like crushed cane once its juice is taken, while Tirumular says the body must be nurtured because life and true knowledge perish with it.

Both rest on the three humours of the medical writers, wind among them: the Kural says excess or lack of them brings disease, Tirumular names the time of day at which practice removes each, and promises the end of age as well.
The Kural says that eating in measure is how one who has a body keeps it long; Tirumular counts the reduction of food among the means of perfecting the body.
Both claim that Death can be overcome: the Kural by the power gained through austerity, Tirumular by seeing the Lord's feet in the inner fire before Death strikes.

726 says that turning and filling the breath at the lotus loosens the impurity (கழற்றி மலத்தை) until the body becomes like collyrium. 2177 says that when the breath runs in its measured count the five malas bow (வணங்கிடும் ஐம்மலம்) and the breath rises. Both make the regulated breath the means of overcoming malam, the bodily practice reaching the soul's bonds.

730 says one who has mastered left and right in Shakti's temple can hear music at midday (வாத்தியங் கேட்கலாம்), and the dance and Siva appear. 606 lists ten inner sounds, bell, sea, elephant, flute, cloud, bee, beetle, conch, drum and lute (பேரி கையாழ்), perceived only by those who have bowed. 606 names what 730's music is, and adds humility as the condition where 730 gives breath mastery.

732 says that raising prana from the navel and apana by contemplation, with Siva's mantra, one becomes Siva (சிவன் அவன் ஆமே). 631 says that if one goes with the Lord no samadhis are needed (சமாதிகள் வேண்டாம் இறையுடன் ஏகில்), and if one becomes him there is no samadhi at all. 631 limits the claim 732 makes for technique: the practice serves until the becoming, and is not needed once it is reached.

734 says that those who embrace the blue-hued lady will, as the world sees, lose grey hair and wrinkles (நரைதிரை மாறிடும்) and become young. Naladiyar 11 takes grey hair as certain (நரைவரும் என்றெண்ணி), so the wise renounce in childhood and the rest end leaning on a staff. On the plain reading the two disagree over whether age can be undone; the Naladiyar answers it by renunciation, Tirumular by yogic union.

735 says that if food is reduced there are many means (உண்டி சுருங்கில் உபாயம் பலவுள), and the breath stays firm when the body contracts. Thiruppugazh 1316 asks whether one can gain the yogic power that prolongs life (உயிரின் நீடு யோக சித்தி) while fattening the wretched belly with food every day (நிதமும் ஊணினால் உயர்த்தி). The song's question assumes the answer 735 gives: restraint of food is a condition of the life-prolonging yoga.

736 promises that the yogic practice makes a fine body (நற்காயம்) that women with flower-decked hair look at with desire (கண்டிச்சிக்கும்). Naladiyar 41 mocks those who praise a girl's beauty without seeing the body's paltry dwelling: tear a fly's wing of skin and a stick is needed to drive off the crows. On the reading that 736 offers outward attractiveness as a good, the two make opposite claims about the body's beauty.
Both make time the quiet cutter of life: the Kural's day is a saw for those who understand it, Tirumular's naazhigai run out while people know everything else.
Both say that discipline can carry a person past death: the Kural credits the power of austerity, Tirumular the ability to seek the Siva-state within.
Both analyse Om into A, U and M; 1926 adds bindu and nada's end, 765 places M in the inner channel where the Lord settles.
762 says the unpassing thing is found by looking within the passing; 786 says no one knows the perishing thing, and that the poet has come to know the knowing.
724 says Tirumular learned how to nourish the body and so the life; 758 takes the claim to its limit, the yogi's body kept a thousand years and more.

748 tells the practitioner to complete the practice humbly without beating a drum about it (பறையறையாது). Kural 1076 calls the base beaten drums (அறைபறை) because they carry and proclaim any secret they hear. Both use the beaten drum for publishing what should be kept; 748 turns it on one's own practice.

752 says the yogi who has run up the staff to the head (தண்டுடன் ஓடித் தலைப்பெய்த யோகிக்கு) keeps the body in accord, while others struggle when the body parts. 711 says those who plant the staff till sparks rise (பொறியெழத் தண்டிட்டு) have no Yama. Both make the staff, the spinal channel, the way past death; 752 adds the contrast with those who die struggling.

753 says the life that came with honour falls apart and goes whirling on, ending for the dog (சுணங்கனுக்காக). 167 asks what it matters if crows carry off this nest (காக்கை கவரிலென்) once the dancer within has left. Both set the corpse before scavengers; 753 uses it as the end of a wasted life, 167 to say the body no longer matters once life has gone.

755 says those who see many qualities in the Dancer's sign stand at the head of the sastras (சாத்திரந் தன்னைத் தலைப்பெய்து), and if they look within for experience (அனுபோகம்) the Lord unfolds as one with them. Thiruppugazh 1316 asks to be freed from the torment of worldly books (உலக நூல்கள் வாதையற்று) and given blissful experience (அநுபூதி). Both put inner experience past book learning; the song treats the books as torment, while 755 lets mastery of them come first.

757 says that gazing on the lotus with delight one may attain the hundred (சாத்திடு நூறு), a hundred years. 479 reckons life by the breath: if it runs five, life is a hundred (ஆயுளும் நூறாகும்), if four, eighty, and the yogi who discerns it can direct it. 479 gives the measure by which 757's hundred years is reached.

758 says those who have reached the hundred guard the body and see it held for a thousand (காத்துடல் ஆயிரம்), and those who stay joined age into a crore of ages. Thiruppugazh 211 asks to be rid of the yoga that refuses to think this stained body will not last (கறைபடு உடம்பு இராதெனக் கருதுதல் ஒழிந்து), turning back the breath and fanning the fire. On the plain reading the song rejects as anxious fancy the bodily longevity 758 promises.

759 says the yogis, seeing a crore of ages (உகங்கோடி கண்டும்), stand unwavering and rise in Siva. 1042 says those who guarded the body and dwelt in thought within it grew old in it and saw a crore of ages (மூத்துடல் கோடி யுகங்கண்ட வாறே). The two verses make the same claim in nearly the same words; 1042 adds that the guarding is by dwelling in thought within the body.

761 says those who cannot see pass away, the shameless talk pleasantly and let it go (நயம்பேசி விடுவர்கள்), and all that has passed goes unseen. 2085 asks what people gain by arguing (வாதுசெய்து) though they see time slipping away in a moment. Both set talk in place of practice against the passing of time; 761 stresses not seeing, 2085 seeing and arguing anyway.

764 says that for those able to seek there is no Yama and no ruin (நமனில்லை கேடில்லை). Thiruppugazh 1045 asks for the state reached as the pure breath stops and the fire is kindled at the root, striking Yama (எமனை மோதி) and gaining the power to travel the sky. The song asks for the yogic victory over death that 764 says belongs to those who seek.

766 and 2660 are the same verse, word for word except the last line (அவனிவ வாகுமே / அவன்இவன் ஆமே): no one knows where the Lord dwells (அண்ணல் இருப்பிடம் ஆரும் அறிகிலர்), he settles within those who search, and whoever sees him becomes him. The repeat sets the identity of seer and Lord in two chapters, the time-wheel and the vision of the jnana guru.

766 says no one knows where the Lord dwells, and whoever sees him becomes him (அவன் இவன் ஆகுமே). 2017 runs the same shape: souls do not know Siva (சிவனாரை அறிகிலர்), and once they know him they remain as Siva. Both make not-knowing the only barrier and knowing the becoming.

767 says no one knows how he becomes this one (அவன் இவன் ஆகும் பரிசு) and explains it: he unites in this one's sound and light and stands as his circle. 1011 states the mutual becoming: the self becomes He and He becomes the self (தான் அவனாக அவனே தான் ஆயிட), and the knower becomes Siva. 767 gives the yogic means, sound and light, for the identity 1011 calls the fourth way of love.

769 says one can see Brahma and Hari, the dark-throated Isa, Sadasiva and Shakti, all set together (கலந்துடன் வைத்ததே). 1731 names the same rising order, Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Isa, the five-faced one, bindu, nada and Shakti, and says Sadasiva is what is common to them (சாதாரணமாம் சதாசிவம்). 1731 explains what 769 leaves vague: how the gods seen together are one.

Both make the body a temporary dwelling: the Kural's life has only borrowed shelter in it, Tirumular's body is a fair hut the Lord has shaped. The Kural laments the lack of a home; Tirumular looks to loosening the bond of the old dwelling.
741 says people perish without noticing their time run out; 786 names what measures it, fire and breath, and claims the knowledge others lack.

770 reads the span left from a bodily sign and says a sound (ஓசை) comes to the life daily in the last month; 723 counts the senses' signs of the parting day, beginning ஓசையில் ஏழும் (seven in sound). Both treat hearing as a herald of death, and 770 adds the timing in months that 723 leaves unnumbered.

771 says those who have gone beyond sound (ஓசை இறந்தவர்) contemplate the Lord, who is the awareness that knew the sound; 3009 calls the one great god ஓசையும் ஓசை ஒடுக்கமும், both the sound and the subsiding of sound. 3009 explains why going beyond sound in 771 still finds him: he is the stilling as well as the sound.

772 says that watching the breath that is wasting away (அழிகின்ற வாயுவை நோக்கிடில்) brings good and mastery; 786 says no one knows the breath that measures or the thing that perishes (அழிகின்ற அப்பொருள்), yet the speaker has known. Together they name the same perishing breath as what most cannot see and the yogi learns to watch.

773 opens தலைவன் இடம்வலம் சாதிப்பார் இல்லை, none master the left and right; 730 says one who mastered left and right in Shakti's temple (இடம்வலம் சாதித்தான்) hears music at midday and sees Siva. On the plain reading of சாதிப்பார் இல்லை as 'no one', 773 denies the very mastery 730 claims was achieved; if it means only 'few', the two agree.

781 counts இருபதில் ஆறு (six in twenty) and இருபதுடன் ஆறு ... இரண்டு (two at twenty-six); 746 in the previous chapter gives ஆறும் இருபதுக்கு (six for the twenty) and இருபத்தொடு ஆறு with இரண்டு. The same number pairs recur, so the two chapters draw on one counting scheme, which reading them together makes visible even though its units are lost.

782 shows at twenty-seven 'one rising mingled' (இருபத்தேழில் ... கலந்தெழும் ஒன்று); 746 assigns இருபத்தேழு to மதியொன்று, the one moon. Both pair twenty-seven with one, and 746's moon suggests the twenty-seven lunar mansions behind 782's count.

Kural 337 says people do not know whether they will live even one moment (ஒருபொழுதும் வாழ்வது அறியார்); 786 agrees that no one knows the breath that measures life or the thing that perishes (ஆருமறியார்), then adds அறிவறிந்தேனே, 'I have known'. Tirumular grants the Kural's common ignorance but makes the measuring of life knowable to the yogi.

741 says all that is known by the five senses (உற்றறிவு ஐந்தும்), by learning and by mixing them, still does not notice the nazhigai of life being cut away; 787 says knowing is with the breath and the five (வாயுவொடு ஐந்தறிவு), and if one searches within it shines. 787 names the condition, turning the same senses inward with the breath, under which 741's knowing would not be blind.

788 says 'that' gives grace and the world is its grace (அருளானது உலகம்); 1806 says grace is all the elemental world (அருளே சகலமும் ஆய பவுதிகம்) and the moving and unmoving. Both identify the world itself with grace rather than with what grace saves one from.

792 lists Thursday (வியாழம்) simply among the days when the breath runs on the right; 790 splits Thursday, the day of பொன், by the moon: left in the waxing fortnight (வளரும் பிறையிடம்), right in the waning. 790 adds the condition that 792 leaves out.

724 says Tirumular learned the means (உபாயம்) of nurturing the body and so nurtured life, without naming the means; 791 gives one: if the breath runs on the left on Friday, Monday and Wednesday, the bright body has no flaw (காயத்துக்கு ஊனமில்லை). The weekday rule is an instance of the body-keeping 724 argues for.

793 has moon and sun rise and fall through இடை and பிங்கலை and life welling up in the middle, without naming the middle channel; 857 runs all the kalas through ida and pingala and through சொல்லா நடுநாடி, the middle channel 'not spoken'. Both leave the central channel unnamed between the two named ones.

793 places life in the middle between ida and pingala; Thiruppugazh 188 asks that the breath run from the root by பிங்கலை நாடி and the middle way up the spine to the Lord's feet. Arunagirinathar's song uses the same three-channel map as Tirumular's verse, as a prayer rather than an instruction.

795 describes the breath that will not stay in the middle (நடுவு நில்லாமல்) but runs left and right and does harm, until it is led as it should go; 1962 names the goal as நாற்றிசை ஓடா நடுநாடி, the middle channel that does not run in four directions, where the nectar is drunk. 1962 states where 795's straying breath is to be led.

The Naladiyar counts those who prattle astrology among the greatest fools, beside those who neglect their real task; Tirumular sets weekday omens inside a yoga tantra. Whether this is a true conflict depends on whether the Naladiyar's சோதிடம் includes such day lore or means endless study that displaces the work of release.

797 sets out where the trident (சூலம்) falls on six weekdays, east, north and west; 798 adds Thursday's south and gives the consequence: behind or to the left, no grief (துக்கமும் இல்லை), ahead or to the right, trouble upon trouble. 798 completes the rule and supplies its use, which 797 omits.
Both end on the same words, நட்டம் இருக்க நமனில்லை: in 574 after holding the breath by measure, in 799 after sealing the body for khechari. Tirumular gives the same promise to two practices.

The Kural says those who have gained the power of austerity can even leap past Death; Tirumular says Yama has no hold on the yogi who seals the body. Both make death conquerable, the Kural by austerity in general, Tirumular by a named technique.
The same closing lines, grey hair and wrinkles undone and the yogi made a child by Nandi's command, follow two different means: union with a woman in 734, the breath set in the palate in 805.
audit_text_issue: 805: ந்யாலம் is a corruption of ஞாலம்.

note: 725 says Tirumular once held the body worthless, then found the Lord's temple inside it; 820 shows how that temple is lit, with held breath as its gem lamp.

Both call the body a bag (பை). The Naladiyar says it should be looked at as a bag turned inside out, a covered foulness to be shunned; Tirumular says that inside the same bag a light shines and it becomes a temple. The conflict holds if 820's பை is read as the body, as tradition takes it.

The Kural asks what worth is if one does not do sweet things even to those who harm one. Tirumular's inward yogis are good even to the hostile, but worse than fire to doers of evil, so their goodness has a limit the Kural's does not state.

800 banks the edges of the plank so that the sky-river (விண்ணாறு) let in fills the tank without leaking; 2920 speaks of water that pours where no rain falls (மழைபொழியாது பொழிபுனல்) and does not stay on high ground. Both picture an inner water from above that must be held, and 800 gives the banking that 2920 says is needed.

Kural 339 makes sleep the figure of death (உறங்குவது போலுஞ் சாக்காடு); 801 says those who drive out sleep (உறக்கத்தை நீக்கி) and stay aware need not die (இறக்கவும் வேண்டாம்). The yogi takes the Kural's likeness literally and reverses it: removing sleep removes death.

801 promises deathlessness to those who can drive out sleep; in 1107 Manonmani comes while the poet sleeps, says உறங்கல் ஐயா, 'do not sleep, sir', and gives him the means (உபாயம்). The goddess's command in 1107 is the wakefulness 801 makes the condition of the practice.

802 says that with discerning practice nectar wells up and becomes the sphere of the moon (நிலாமண்டலம்); 335 says yogis who bind the breath taste the nectar of knowledge-bliss from the bright moon (ஒண்மதி ... அமுது). Both place the nectar in the moon within, and 335 adds the contrast with the drinker of liquor.

599 says the ancient one tuning the senses shows an unbroken light within the palate (அண்ணாக்கின் உள்ளே அகண்ட ஒளி); 803 says that if the tip of the tongue is pressed into the middle, the soul and Siva dwell there. 803 supplies the bodily act, the tongue turned up, that reaches the place 599 names.

804 speaks of the high mountain's peak where the sky's juice flows, which no one knows (வகையறிவாரில்லை); 625 says the gods churned the dark mountain for nectar but will not climb the rare mountain (அருவரை) to drink the nectar there. Both set an inner mountain whose nectar is unknown or unsought against outward drinking.

810 says that for those who worship within, the place he dwells becomes a temple (உள்ளுறை கோயில்); 1823 says the heart is the great temple and the body of flesh the shrine (உள்ளம் பெருங்கோயில் ஊனுடம்பு ஆலயம்). 810 reaches by yogic practice the same inner temple that 1823 lays out in the terms of worship.

812 lists where he dwells: on the heads of evildoers (தீவினையாளர் தம் சென்னியில்), in the golden abode of those who offer flowers, in the minds of the great; 1760 gives a like list: the minds of devotees as temple and the heads of the gods (தேவர்கள் சென்னியின் மன்னும்). The same catalogue form puts him on the heads of gods in 1760 and on the heads of evildoers in 812.

813 says he is sixteen like the rays rising from the moon (மதியின் எழுங்கதிர் போலப் பதினாறாய்); 854 counts the moon's high kalas as ten and six (பத்தினொடாறும் ... பான்மதி). 854 confirms that 813's sixteen are the moon's kalas.

814 has Shakti sit with the kalas around her, moon-faced, pouring nectar (அமுதம் பொழிந்தே); 685 says that if the moon's kala joins, the yogi becomes the rising moon's light and coolness. 814 places a goddess in the moon that 685 says the yogi becomes.

815 has two silvers (இருவெள்ளி) poured into the golden earthen enclosure (பொன்மண்ணடை) and kept from leaving; 834 has goldsmiths keep the silver from melting and running off by the way of the gold (வெள்ளி உருகிப் பொன்வழி ஓடாமே). Both use silver held within gold for the retained bindu.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 815: last line (கொழுந்தது வாகுண்- குணமது தனே) garbled.

note: 1936 says people do not know how to guard within what is leaving (கழிகின்ற தன்னையுட் காக்கலும் தேரார்), of the bindu; 819 says the breath that is going out can be guarded (கழிகின்ற வாயுவுங் காக்கலுமாகும்). The same words make the claim of the breath that 1936 makes of the bindu, and 819 says it can be done.

820 says that when the breath rises the soot-dark temple of the body becomes lit with a gem lamp (மையணி கோயில் மணிவிளக்காமே); 1823 makes the body the shrine and the five senses its bright gem lamps (காளா மணிவிளக்கே). Both light the body-temple with a மணிவிளக்கு, by breath in 820 and by the senses in 1823.

705 lists among the attainments சித்தி தூரங் கேட்டல், hearing from afar; 822 names far sight (தூர தெரிசனம்) as what comes when the five elements are joined. 822 gives a cause for a power of the kind 705 only lists.
audit_text_issue: 822 lines 1-2 are marked corrupt (stray 'f'); 705 line 3 is garbled.

note: 823 says that setting the mind on the lovely lamp, the whole earth is before one as in daylight (பாரார் உலகம் பகல்முன்னதாமே); 680 says that after seeing the rising light of lightning one can see the spreading worlds (பரப்பவை காணலாம்). Both make an inner light the means of seeing the world spread before one.

1729 says great Nandi took the body as his temple with the ten nadis as its gates (கோயில்கொண்டான்); 824 says that setting a lamp in the rising nada below the navel one becomes lord of the temple that rises in oneself (தன்னெழு கோயில் தலைவன்). 824 makes the practitioner lord of the body-temple 1729 gives to Nandi.
Both use the weekday planets. In 790 வெள்ளி and பொன் name Friday and Thursday in a rule for the breath; in 826 and 836 the same words become silver and gold, a code for the bindu and the body.
1936 laments that people neither know how much bindu is lost nor how to guard it; 828 gives one answer: guard it in union itself, so that the very act that spends it keeps it.

Both make union life-giving. In the Kural the lover feels his life put out shoots at each touch, as if her shoulders were ambrosia; in Tirumular union practised as yoga lets one live on earth for many ages. Love's hyperbole in one is a technique in the other.

825 makes reaching the needle's eye (ஊசித் துளை) in union with the woman the unflagging practice; 2613 says there is no use babbling about the breath and the needle (வாசியும் ஊசியும்) and tells one to cut desire and attachment instead. If ஊசி in 2613 is the same needle-fine channel, it dismisses as talk the very practice 825 teaches through desire.

Kural 6 praises the one who quenched the five senses (பொறிவாயில் ஐந்தவித்தான்); 829 says the practitioner becomes lord when knowledge, enjoyment and the five go his way (தன்வழி அஞ்சே). Both make mastery of the five the mark of the lord, but 829 has them go his way within போகம், not quenched.

809 says that saying Sivaya nama and raising the tongue will bring the Ganga (கங்கை தருவிக்கும்), the nectar; 832 makes the one who set the sky's Ganga in his spread locks (விண்ணந்த கங்கை விரிசடை வைத்தவன்) the one who holds the nectar in the five nazhigai. The Ganga on Siva's head stands for the nectar in both.

834 has cunning goldsmiths (கள்ளத் தட்டார்) cover the silver with charcoal and hold it fast; 2876 has a goldsmith (தட்டான்) on the top floor seize a red bud, 'folding away the truth'. Both use the goldsmith's craft, with a note of stealth, for the secret work of the practice.
audit_text_issue: 2876 அசுத்தில் is likely a misreading of அகத்தில்.

note: 826 uses வெள்ளி (Venus, silver) and வியாழம் (Jupiter, gold) for what is held and where it turns back; 836 uses the sun, சனி, செவ்வாய், gold and silver between the partners. Read together they show the planet names working as one code for bodily things through the chapter.

838 says the rising fire, led ahead, works on the body as melting does on wax (மெழுகுருகும் பரிசெய்திடும் மெய்யே); Thiruppugazh 1192 says the women's embrace melts body and life like wax in fire (உள முருகி தீ மெழுகு). The same melting is the yogi's work on the body in 838 and the lover's undoing in Arunagirinathar.

839 says knowing the space and, in the middle of the space, knowing the light (வெளியை ... வெளியினடுவே ஒளியை); 1490 says within yoga-samadhi is the wide space, within it light, within it Shakti. Both nest light inside an inner space, and 839 credits the knowing to Nandi.

844 is a riddle of negatives: no earth, no water, yet a lotus bloomed (பாரில்லை நீரில்லை ... தாமரை பூத்தது); 2920 says there is green in a land watered without water (நீரின்றிப் பாயும் நிலத்தினிற் பச்சை) which no one can know. Both name an inner growth that needs none of the ordinary ground or water.
Both promise the end of grey hair and wrinkles (நரைதிரை) from a bodily practice: 727 from breath held at fixed hours, 848 from drinking the shore-water the witless shun.

The Naladiyar treats grey hair as certain to come, so the wise renounce in childhood; Tirumular says that for those who drink this water grey hair and wrinkles change and Yama is absent. The conflict holds if 848 is read literally of the body, not as a figure for spiritual youth.
audit_text_issue: 848 வரைவரை and the identity of the water (amuri) are obscure

note: 845 says that drawing the body's own water 'by the one way, for the one purpose' spares life distress (நடலைப் படாது உயிர்). 724 gives the principle behind it: if the body perishes the life perishes, so 'I nurtured the body and nurtured life' (உடம்பை வளர்த்தேன் உயிர்வளர்த்தேனே). 845 is one of the means of nurture that 724 says he learned.

846 promises that drinking the Siva-water makes the body faultless within a year and turns it to gold (காயம் கனகமதாமே). Thiruppugazh 815 calls the body a filthy hut that perishes faster than a water-bubble and confesses he desired it and kept trying worthless medicines and many yogas (சாரமில் அவுடதமும் பல யோகமும்) until his mind cried 'enough'. One verse offers a body-perfecting medicine; the other renounces such medicines as futile and seeks only the feet.

847 says Siva's water with a hundred peppercorns (நூறு மிளகு) has no rival as medicine and, applied to the crown, makes the hair grow anew (மறுமயிராமே). 849 extends the recipe, adding gooseberry, turmeric and neem to the pepper (மிளகு நெல்லியும் மஞ்சளும் வேம்பு), and gives the same result on the head: the skull darkens (இருளும் கபாலம்). Together they show the chapter building one remedy for the hair, step by step.
audit_text_issue: 849 களவு காயம் is obscure, possibly corrupt

note: 850 names the Siva-water the hero's, the gods' and the primal medicine (ஆதி மருந்து) and says this medicine of light cannot be told. Naladiyar 132 says that in no world is there a medicine like learning for cutting away delusion (கல்விபோல் மம்மர் அறுக்கும் மருந்து). Both claim a matchless medicine, one for the body's decay, the other for the mind's confusion.
1936 faults people who do not know how bindu is lost or how to guard it; 877 describes the yogi in whom bindu does not go out, held at the base for want of desire.
724 says that if the body perishes life perishes, so Tirumular learned to nourish the body; 879 gives the condition for their not parting: awareness and body kept in balance.
Both use the moon's two fortnights: the Kural for friendship with the good that fills and with fools that wanes, Tirumular for the inner moon whose growing and shrinking the yogi must learn.

Both use the eclipse serpent that seizes the moon: the Naladiyar's spares the young crescent, as the worthy spare a fallen enemy; Tirumular's enmity of serpent and moon is ended and the two held together, an inner joining.

851 says the body climbs and descends (ஏறி இறங்கும்) like the moon's kalas through the two fortnights (இருவகைப் பக்கத்துள்). 793 says moon and sun, alternating over the two fortnights, rise and fall (ஏறி இழியும்) through ida and pingala, with life welling between them. 793 names the channels in which 851's waxing and waning happen.

852 gives fire ten kalas beside the moon's sixteen and the sun's twelve (ஈரெட்டு ஆறிரண்டு ஈரைந்து). 854 gives fire eight eights, sixty-four (அங்கியது எட்டெட்டு உயர்க்கலை), and 855 and 856 repeat that count. Read as counts of the same thing, the two numbers for fire's kalas conflict; the tension disappears only if ஈரைந்து in 852 counts something other than fire's kalas, which the verse does not say.

859 says the nine, five elements, three lights and the star, become the pranava, the great way (பிரணவமாகும் பெருநெறி). 227 says the faultless Brahmins grasp the pranava that is the great way (பெருநெறியான பிரணவம்). Both verses call Om the பெருநெறி; 859 builds it from the elements and lights, 227 makes it the Brahmin's discipline.

860 ends that the star within the star is one's own form (தாரகைத் தாரகை தானாம் சொரூபமே). 2574 sets the teaching of Om in the bliss of one's own form (சொருபானந்தம்) in turiya. The pairing holds on the reading of தாரகை as tāraka, the saving syllable Om; on that reading 2574 says what 860 points at.

862 says rousing the fire (அங்கி எழுப்பி) and feeding the sun, with the moon, ends the senses' outward going: the yoga that joins moon, sun and fire. Thiruppugazh 506 asks when, from the fire in the root lotus (மூலகமலத்து இலங்கியை), driven through the nadis to join the moon (இந்துவின் ஊடுற இணக்கி), he will drink the nectar. The song turns 862's instruction into a prayer for the same ascent.

863 says the base see the sixteen kalas in the body and do not think of it, until harsh Death sets them where he intends (கன்றிய காலன் கருத்துழி வைத்தபின்) and they fall. Naladiyar 331 compares those who revel in the world while great Death waits to seize them (கொலைவல் பெருங்கூற்றம் கோள்பார்ப்ப) to a turtle playing in a pot over the fire. Both make the fault not seeing what is plain while Death prepares; Tirumular names the unheeded thing as the inner kalas.

864 says that when fire, moon and sun join (அங்கி சசிகதிர் கூட), the star arises and what abides there becomes everything (சகலமுமாமே). 1990, in another chapter, says that when the sun joins fire and moon (அருக்கன் அனல்மதியோடு ஒன்ற), that is the fullness (பூரணை). Both make the union of the three lights the point of completion.

866 prescribes setting the sun's breath on the left and the moon's on the right so that the axle-pin will not shake for a thousand years (ஆணி கலங்காது அவ் ஆயிரத்தாண்டே). Thiruppugazh 355 prays not to become a foolish yogi who, thinking this impermanent flesh will last (அனித்தமான ஊன் நாளும் இருப்பதாகவே), holds the breath in the nostrils. The one teaches breath-craft for a lasting body; the other names that very aim a delusion.

866 makes the goal of breath-craft that the axle-pin should not shake (ஆணி கலங்காது). 309 says that even when the axle turns and the pin is shaken (அச்சு உழன்று ஆணி கலங்கினும), the First comes near only to those who know him with longing. Read with the pin as the body's hold on life, 309 limits 866: a steady pin is not what brings the Lord near.

867 says the heart resounds with the drum's sound (பறையோசை) in the nine and the sun is the conch (சங்கு) at dawn, with the Supreme standing as a lamp. 606 lists the ten inner sounds, among them conch and drum (வளை பேரி), and says only those who have bowed can perceive them. 606 places 867's drum and conch in the full list of inner nadas and adds the condition for hearing them.

869 says that once the mantra meeting the light from the navel lotus is known, the son is born before the father (தந்தைக்கு முன்னே மகன் பிறந்தானே). 1026 says the six-faced one appears before his father (தந்தைதன் முன்னே சண்முகம் தோன்றலால்) and is to be held as the son. The same reversal of son before father appears in both; 1026 names the son as Skanda, which offers one key to 869's unsolved riddle.

870 calls those who recite yet know nothing mutes (ஓதியும் ஏதும் அறியாத ஊமர்கள்), and says the Lord appears only to those who can join beginning and end. Kural 834 says there is no greater fool than one who studies, understands and teaches but does not restrain himself (ஓதி உணர்ந்தும் பிறர்க்குரைத்தும் தானடங்கா). Both judge recitation empty without an inner act; the Kural names it self-restraint, Tirumular an inner yogic joining.

872 says not to sleep until what was eaten has settled (அயின்றது வீழ்வளவும் துயிலின்றி). Kural 942 says the body needs no medicine if one eats only after what was eaten is digested (அருந்தியது அற்றது போற்றி உணின்). Both time the next act by the settling of the last meal; the Kural applies it to eating, the Tirumanthiram to sleep, within its moon regimen.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 872: மேவுன்ய் is an encoding slip.

note: Kural 334 says what shows itself as a day is a blade that saws through life (நாளென ஒன்றுபோற் காட்டி உயிர் ஈரும் வாள்). 874 says yogis who stay through the aeon measure Yama by the nazhigai (நாழிகையாக நமனை அளப்பர்). On the reading that they count Death's span as a mere nazhigai, the yogi measures time rather than being cut by it, against the Kural's claim that time cuts every life.
audit_text_issue: 874 line 4 is corrupt (தாழவல் லார்.க் இச் சசிவன்ன ராமே).

note: 876 asks who knows how the kalas of sun and moon blossom, run twelve finger-breadths (பன்னிரண்டு அங்குலம் ஓடி) and fall. 2764 says to seek where the life-breath rises and runs twelve finger-breadths (பன்னிரண்டு அங்குலம் ஓடும் உயிர்): that is the hall where the Lord of nada's end dances. 2764 answers 876's question with a place and its meaning.

879 says that if awareness and body stand matched, they never once leave each other (உணர்வும் உடம்பும் ஒருகால் விடாவே). 2148 says people cling to body after body without knowing the bond between body and life (உடம்பொடு உயிரிடை நட்பு அறியாதார்). 879 states the bond 2148 says people miss, and how it is kept.

880 says the mind joined with the breath binds the five senses (ஐம்புலன் கட்டுண்ணும்) and that is release (வீடு). Naladiyar 59 says one who can guard, without wavering, the craving that enters through the five gates of body, mouth, eyes, nose and ears will surely reach release (வீடு பெறும்). Both make holding the five senses the way to வீடு; 880 does it by breath and inner sound, the Naladiyar by firm guarding.

880 hooks the mind to the sound of Siva's conch (சிவசங்கின் நாதம்) and ends with drinking nectar (அமுதமே). Thiruppugazh 506 asks for the conch-sounding bindu-nada (சங்கொலி விந்துநாதம்) at the front and then to drink the gods' nectar (வானவமுதத்தை உண்டு). The same sequence, inner conch-sound then nectar, appears in both.

881 says that those who gather the five lights and drive them through the staff on the bank of the nectar river have no Yama (நமன் இல்லை). 622 says that once the upper door at the summit of the root channel is seen open, Death's word does not reach one even in dreams (காலன் வார்த்தை கனாவிலும் இல்லையே). Both promise freedom from Death to the one who carries the ascent through the central channel to the top.
audit_text_issue: 881: தண்டோ ட்டி, நமன்இகில்லை, நாளனஇல்லை look corrupt

note: 882 is a near-repeat of 336: both open with 'opening the spring of the inner water's nectar' (உண்ணீர் அமுதமுறும் ஊறலைத் திறந்து), turn to the lotus feet (இணையடித் தாமரை), samadhi, and end with the eye's stream and the breath's way (கண்ணாற்றொடே சென்று கால்வழி). In 336 the feet are the guru's and the breath's way is seen (காணுமே); in 882 the clear water is sent to the feet and the breath's way changes (மாறுமே).

724 says that if the body perishes life perishes and true knowledge cannot be reached, so he learned to nurture the body. 883 says that when moon and its partner reach the head by the staff, the body comes to no harm (ஊறு படாது உடல்) and undecaying joy wells up on earth (பாறுபடா இன்பம் பார்மிசை பொங்குமே). 883 gives the fruit of the nurture 724 argues for: joy here, in the kept body.

The Kural says only those who reach the Lord's feet cross the sea of births; 905 promises no further birth to whoever chants the five letters, and 898 has already made the Lord's feet the letters. The means is narrowed from the feet to the mantra that is the feet.

Both free a person from deeds through the Lord's name: the two kinds of deed do not cling to those who delight in his true praise (Kural), and subtle karma is destroyed by chanting the subtle mantra (909). Tirumular adds a count and a technique.

115 names Pati, Pasu and Pasam and says Pasu and Pasam do not stand when Pati draws near; 895 names the three impurities (anava, maya, karma) and sets the stainless dance among them, on the traditional reading that the dance is where they end.

In 589 the holy dance goes on in a hall reached by a waterfall through the long nadi, an image usually read as inside the body; 886 names the outer hall at Chidambaram. Together they show the hall Tirumular means is both.
725 turns from despising the body to cherishing it as the Lord's temple; 906 goes further and promises that the mantra makes the capable one's body gold.

884 ends by raising up the Lord as the one letter (நம்பிரான் ஓர் எழுத்தே). 962 says that those who utter it with no other letter win life by one letter (ஓரெழுத்தாலே உயிர்பெறலாமே). The pairing turns 884's praise of the one letter into its fruit: the letter that is the Lord is the letter by which the soul is won.

The Kural says that as A is first of all letters, the Primal Lord is first of the world (அகர முதல எழுத்தெல்லாம் ... முதற்றே உலகு). 885 says that by one letter he became the whole world (ஓரெழுத்தாலே உலகெங்கும் தானாகி), and goes on to two, three and the great letter. Where the Kural uses the letter as a likeness for the Lord's priority, 885 makes the letter the means by which he becomes the world.

886 gives four names to the one hall where the gods dwell: சிற்றம்பலம், சிதம்பரம், திருஅம்பலம், தென்பொது. 2722 says that Chidambaram and the holy dance are everywhere (எங்கும் சிதம்பரம் எங்கும் திருநட்டம்), because Siva is everywhere. Read together, the named southern hall of 886 is one place of a dance that 2722 refuses to confine to any place.

887 calls the golden hall's unceasing dance (அனவரத் தாண்டவம்) also the dance of dissolution, and speaks of plural rare dances of destruction (சங்காரத்து அருந்தாண்டவங்கள்). 2727 says the dances are five (ஆன நடம் ஐந்து) and are danced as the five acts. The pairing places 887's dances of destruction as one act among the five that 2727 counts.

888 says the dance is the work of grace (தாண்டவமானது அனுக்கிரகத் தொழில்). 2799 assigns each of the five acts to a part of the dancing Hara and gives grace to his foot for ever (அரனடி என்றும் அனுக்கிரகம்). 2799 locates in the dancer's body the grace that 888 names as the dance itself.

A near-repeat: 889 and 901 share the line தானே அகார உகாரமதாய் நிற்கும் and the same frame of the tattva-dance (தத்துவக் கூத்துக்கு). 889 makes the dance one of the supreme light (பரஞ்சுடர்) with the Lord as his own ground (தனக்குத் தராதலம்); 901 makes it the dance of ரீங்காரம் and has him dance alone in the world (உலகில் தனிநடம்). The two versions show the same claim, that the dancer needs nothing outside himself, set once to light and once to the seed syllable.

889 says the Lord himself stands as the tattva and as A and U (தத்துவமாய் நிற்கும் ... அகார உகாரமதாய் நிற்கும்). 2180 ends that the tattva that is real is the letter A (தத்துவம் ஆவது அகார எழுத்தே). Both join the tattva to the letter A, 2180 as the result of sorting true tattvas from false, 889 as the Lord's own standing.

890 plays on வாசி within the five letters: spoken, the ground becomes வாசிய, and its yoga is தயாவாசி. 946 gives orders of the five letters set around the supreme five and ends பரமாய வாசி மயநமாய். Both texts are obscure and perhaps corrupt, but both take வாசி, which is also the Siddha word for breath, out of the syllables of சிவாய; the pairing shows that the play is a device of these chakra chapters, not a one-off.
audit_text_issue: 946: syllable strings (மவயரசி, stray ர) look corrupt

note: 891 says A and U are the Siva-forms, the place no one knows is the supreme, and Siva's way is bliss (சிவகதி ஆனந்தம்). 2844 says that in speechless bliss and silence A merges into U and M and in the speechless letter is the inner light (உரையற்ற காரத்தில் உள்ளொளி). 2844 carries 891's A and U one step further, into the letter beyond speech, and ties the same bliss to silence.

270 says the ignorant call love and Siva two, no one knows that love is Siva, and those who know it rest as love that is Siva (அன்பே சிவமாவது ஆரும் அறிகிலார்). 892 says the three blisses and two knowledges become one, few know that bliss is சிவாய (ஆனந்தம் சிவாய அறிவார் பலரில்லை), and to those who can know it the Lord is caught as the dance of bliss. The two verses run the same pattern, two made one, an identity few know, and knowing it is having it, once for love and once for bliss.

893 says what the masters of many arts attain is the two, Omkara and the five letters (ஓங்காரம் பஞ்சாக்கரங்கள்), and the angles by which it spreads (கோணம் பரந்திடும் வாறு). 922 sets the pranava in the middle and on both sides of a chakra, with நமசிவாய in the centre and சிவாயநம in the outer circle. 922 gives the drawn layout in which 893's pair of Om and the five letters is spread.

895 names the concealing power next to the stainless one and calls it bliss (அமலம் திரோதாயி ஆகும் ஆனந்தம்), alongside the three impurities and the place of the dance. 2799 makes concealment one of the five acts of the dance, the pressing foot on which Hara rests (அணைப்பில் அமரும் திரோதாயி), next to the raised foot of grace. Both put திரோதாயி inside the Lord's dance rather than among the impurities it hides.

896 says of the Lord, line after line, தானே தனக்கு: he is his own lord, his own mountain, his own substance. 2228 uses the same frame of the person, who is his own enemy and friend, his own two worlds and the eater of his own deeds, and ends with the same line as 896, தானே தனக்குத் தலைவனும் ஆமே. The shared line describes self-sufficiency in the Lord and self-responsibility in the soul bound by deeds.

897 builds four lines of தலைவனுமாய் நின்ற to land on the pair of feet (தாளிணை), which are lord of the supreme dancer and of the knowledge that opens like a flower (தாதவிழ் ஞானம்). 2425 says the foot is Shakti and grace, the head is knowledge, and release comes when the foot shows the soul that knowledge (கால் அந்த ஞானத்தைக் காட்ட வீடாகும்). 2425 spells out the relation of feet to knowledge that 897 only names.
audit_text_issue: 2425 has the typo ஞானத்கைக் for ஞானத்தை.

note: 898 counts the paired feet as eight letters, twice five, fifty-one and seven thousand (கழலிணை ஏழாயிரமே). 900 says the mantras that exist are seven thousand and that the mantra is Siva's holy body (மந்திரம் சிவன் திருமேனி). Together they make the feet one part of the mantra-body: the seven thousand of the feet in 898 are the seven thousand of the body in 900.

899 multiplies the seven thousand mantras into seven crores and countless mantras (எண்ணிலா மந்திரம்) and then says they stand as seven and two. 2178 numbers the tattvas in crores and thousands and says they are contained in the ninety-six and then in the twenty-five (ஐ ஐந்துள் ஆகும்). The same move, a count beyond reckoning folded into a small number, is made once for mantras and once for tattvas.

900 says the mantra is Siva's holy body (இருக்கின்ற மந்திரம் சிவன் திருமேனி). 2379 defines mantra as the beginningless one that is not body (அனாதி உடல் அல்லா மந்திரம்). If உடல் in 2379 means any body, the two make opposite claims about whether mantra is a body; if it means only the physical body, 2379 rules out a fleshly body and 900's திருமேனி is a form of another kind.

901 makes the Lord's tattva-dance the dance of ரீங்காரம் (ரீங்காரத் தத்துவக் கூத்துக்கு), danced alone in the world. 1073 says the goddess, Omkari who became Ahankari and bore the five, sits sweetly within ரீங்காரம். Read together, the syllable in which 1073 seats Shakti is the syllable 901 names as the Lord's dance.

902 ends that the dance is the Sivalinga, good copper and gold (நடம் சிவலிங்கம் நலஞ்செம்பு பொன்னே). 1720 lists refined copper and gold among the substances any one of which, clearly known, can be the Sivalinga (கன்றிய செம்பு ... பொன் ... தெளி சிவலிங்கமே). The same copper and gold sit beside the linga in both; 1720 makes them its material, while 902 sets them in the alchemy by which copper becomes gold.

903 says saying சிவாயநம becomes red gold and ends that the holy hall is red gold (செம்பொன் ஆன திருஅம்பலமே). 2742 praises the valiant dancer in the holy hall of red gold (செம்பொன் திருமன்றுள் சேவகக் கூத்தன்). The red-gold hall of the dance is shared, and 903 adds that the five letters make the chanter's gold one with the hall's.

A near-repeat across chapters: 904 has the chakra drawn by scoring twice six lines into twenty-five cells (ஈராறு கீறி ... இருபத்தைஞ்சாக்கி) as the holy hall. 920 describes the same figure, six lines and twenty-five cells (இருமூன்று இரேகை ... அறைகள் இருபத்தைஞ்சு), and places A in one cell. 920 shows that 904's chakra is the one the next chapter fills with letters.

906 says the golden mantra, for the capable who take it in, makes the body gold (பொன்னாகும் வல்லோர்க்கு உடம்பு). 2709 says that for those who recite சிவாயநம with melting minds the Lord uses it as an alchemist's pill and turns their bodily cage to gold (குளிகை யிட்டுப் பொன்னாக்குவன் கூட்டையே). Both promise the body turned gold by the mantra; 2709 names the mantra and the melting mind, 906 the capable and the golden feet.

907 says seeing the golden feet makes the body holy and their command turns copper to gold (செம்புபொன் ஆயிடும் ... திருமேனி ஆயிடும்). 293 says that those who praise the Lord night and morning have a body as if alchemised in the herb (வல்லியுள் வாதித்த காயமும் ஆமே), set against the learned who pass away. The alchemy of the body that 293 gives to daily praise, 907 gives to the vision of the feet.

908 says that by speaking the secret one may enter another body and take pleasure there (ஒருகூட்டில் புக்குச் சுகிக்கலாம்) and the serpent of bonds departs. 668 lists entering another body (பரகாய மேவல்) among the eight siddhis. 908 gives to the subtle secret of the dance a power that 668 names in the list of yogic attainments, and sets the loss of the bonds beside it.

912 gives the dance as the five letters in changed orders, சிவாயநம, நமசிவாய, சிவயநம, one formula turning (கோளொன்று மாறே). 923 sets out the same rotations of the mantra, சிவாயநம, மசிவாயந, நமசிவாய and on, taken in order from சி. 923 states as a chakra rule what 912 states as the dance.
audit_text_issue: 912 seed-letter spellings vary (ஈ/இ), possibly copying errors

note: 912 turns the five letters through their orders and calls each order the dance (கூத்தே சிவாயநம ... நமசிவாய). Thiruppugazh 425 chants செயசெய அருணாத்திரி with the five letters in each rotation, சிவயநம, மசிவயந, நமசிவய, யநமசிவ, வயநமசி, and later names the dance in the space of light. The same device of rotating the five letters, a rule of the chakra in the Tirumanthiram, becomes the metre of a Thiruppugazh song.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 912's vowel strings and spellings vary from line to line and may be scribal.

note: 913 has one and two dance, then seven, then nine dance with him, and ends with the ruby dance in the hall (மன்றினில் ஆடனான் மாணிக்கக் கூத்தே). 2782 has the nine, the sixteen, the six paths, the seven and the fifty-six dance with him, and ends with the dance of bliss (ஆனந்தக் கூத்தே). Both make the dance a gathering of numbered things that dance with the one, and neither fixes what the numbers are.
Both use the letter A to point beyond itself. The Kural makes A, first of letters, the image of the Primal Lord first in the world; Tirumular makes A the soul and gives the Supreme to U.
Both put a goad over 'the five'. In the Kural it is firmness of mind (உரன்) that guards the five; in Tirumular the five elephants in the forest are goaded by the five syllables.
Both make control of the five senses the way in: the Naladiyar's one who steers the craving of the five gates reaches release, Tirumular's one who holds the five together lets the First enter.
Both say deeds lose their hold on one devoted to the Lord: the Kural through his true praise, Tirumular through his name kept up without tiring, with the Lord coming to remove the grief of deeds.
Both define the Brahmin by something other than birth, if 940 is read that way: the Kural by kindness to all life, Tirumular by the five syllables dwelling in him.
The same verse recurs in the ninth tantra's gross pancakshara, with 'once the order of the fifty is known' for 'once what the fifty become is known'.
A near-doublet in the Bhairavi mantra chapter; there the lady herself departs and cuts away the babble, here the speaker does.
audit_text_issue: tm:1115 line 1 மேலி is probably a corruption of மேவி.

note: Both make the recited syllables drive out the impurities: here the three malams flee crying out, in 2712 sivaya removes all impurity and yields Siva-jnana yoga.
885 builds a ladder of one, two and three letters from the one letter that becomes the world; 962 says the six letters must be recited as one, and that by one letter life is won.
Both use the alchemist's pill (குளிகை) that makes gold: here the realised true object is the pill like purified gold, in 2709 sivayanama is the pill that turns the body's cage to gold.
Both move the temple inward: 1823 makes the body a shrine and the heart the great temple, 919 makes the five syllables and the subtle within the temple where the Lord sits.
audit_text_issue: 919 obscure (தூலம்/சூக்குமம் may be body or mantra)

note: 958 mocks those who perform the twilight rite without knowing the mantra within; 978 says those who join with Shakti at the root need no rite at all.
Near-doublets: the same breath-joined recitation with O, ending on 'the first Lord MA', one starting from NA and one from SI.
