198 sends those who say 'kill, strike' bound to hell; 1000 gives a rite for killing by mantra and diagram. The conflict holds if 1000 is read as offering the rite for use; read as a catalogue of what mantra can do, it is a report, not an endorsement.

916 repeats அரகர என்ன four times: no one says it, saying it they become gods (அமரரும் ஆவர்), and birth is cut off (அறும்பிறப்பு). 2716, in the subtle-pancakshara chapter, has the same frame with சிவசிவ: evil-doers don't say it, saying it ends evil deeds, they become gods (தேவரும் ஆவர்) and reach Siva's state. The two are one verse-form far apart, with the name changed and the reward moved from ending birth to சிவகதி.

Kural 10 says only those who reach the Lord's feet swim the great sea of births (பிறவிப் பெருங்கடல் நீந்துவர்). 916 names a means for the same end: merely saying அரகர cuts off birth (அறும்பிறப்பு), yet people don't know to say it. The Kural leaves the way of reaching unstated; the Tirumanthiram makes it the spoken name.

Both verses turn on the pair அவ்வு and சவ்வு and on no one knowing it: 933 says no one knows what ச stands for, and to those who know, ச is Shakti and Sadasiva; 957 says the mantra அவ்வொடு சவ்வு is known to no one (ஆரும் அறிகிலர), and once known it becomes the beginningless (அனாதி). Read together, the two show the same seed pair glossed once as Shakti with Sadasiva and once as the beginningless.

888 in the ajapa chapter says the dance is the single letter, the one letter (தாண்டவமான தனியெழுத்து ஓரெழுத்து). 935 turns that into practice: of the many signs for seeing the Dancer, reciting the first of the Dancer's letters (கூத்தன் எழுத்தின் முதலெழுத்து) makes one stand at one with him, and that is the sign. The identity of dance and letter becomes the way to see the Dancer.

941 places the five letters on the body: ந at the feet, ம at the navel, சி and வ at the shoulders, ய as the light above. 2701 places them elsewhere: mouth, throat, heart, navel, linga, up to the crown (இருமத்தகம்). Both map the syllables onto the body from low to high, but only the navel is shared, so the book carries more than one bodily scheme for the same mantra.

A near-repeat: 951 has அ, உ, சி in the middle and வ with the six joined with the breath (வளியுடன் கூடி), and the Lord of ஓ pleased; 976 has ந, ம, சி in the middle, the two வ joined with the breath, begun with ஓ and uttered once, and the Lord ம in the mind. The shared frame (நடுவாய், வளியுடன் கூடி, ஓகார) with different letters shows the formula reworked within the chapter.

954 says what the people of the world know is writing on water (நீரில் எழுத்து), and no one sees the one letter in the sky. 64 says that even countless crores of Agamas are writing on water (நீர்மேல் எழுத்தே) if one doesn't know what the Lord declared. Both use the image for knowledge that misses its one point, and 954 names that point as a single letter.

958 says a mantra rises in the navel, and people perform the twilight rite (சந்திசெய்யாநிற்பர்) without knowing it, worship at dusk and leave noisily. 2703 says at the times of sun and moon no one knows the fitting mantra (ஆயுறு மந்திரம் ஆரும் அறிகிலார்), but one may recite the five letters with the mouth. Both judge the timed rites by the mantra their performers miss; 2703 adds a plain remedy.

959 says the mantra within the life is a goad (ஆவிக்குள் மந்திரம் அங்குசமாமே) when one looks to it without letting go; 977 makes the five letters the goad (அங்குசம்) for the five elephants living in the forest. The goad is the same in both; 977 names what it drives, the five, and 959 places it inside the breath-life.

962 says those who recite the six letters don't know them, and for those who can utter it without another letter, life can be won by one letter (ஓரெழுத்தாலே உயிர்பெறலாமே). 2720 says though one recites the Vedas, limbs and Agamas, what is ours is in one letter (எழுத்து ஒன்றில்), and mastering it reaches the farther shore. Both reduce the recited many to one letter, and 2720 sets the whole of scripture against it.

965 says the fifty letters are all the Vedas and Agamas, and once known they become the five letters (ஐம்பது எழுத்தும்போய் அஞ்செழுத்தாமே). Thiruppugazh 1326 names Siva as the three-eyed light who teaches the four Vedas in the five letters (ஐந்தெழுத்ததனில் நான்மறை உணர்த்து). Both hold the Vedas within the five letters, the song in passing within Murugan's praise.

885 says by one letter he became everything in the world (ஓரெழுத்தாலே உலகெங்கும் தானாகி), then two, three and the great letter. 966 gives the same work to the five letters: by them he made the five elements, the many wombs, and bears the wide world (அஞ்செழுத்தால் இவ் அகலிடம் தாங்கினன்). Read together, the letter as the stuff of creation runs from the one letter to the five.

975 reads the letters as categories: சி is Siva, வ the form, ய the soul, ம impurity. 2710 lists Siva, Shakti, the soul, choking impurity and maya (சிவன்சத்தி சீவன் செறுமல மாயை) and says when the bonds go the soul joins Siva with Shakti. 2710 gives the same five without naming letters, which supports reading 975's வடிவம் as Shakti and makes clear what the letter key is for: separating the bonds from the soul.

980 says once the truth of the five letters is known the Supreme stands in the heart, there is no deceit or ruin to the house, and declares this the refuge (தஞ்சம் இதுவென்று). 2702 says when the soul leaves its instruments and death lays hand on it, the five letters bring shelter (அரணம் கைகூட்டுவது அஞ்செழுத்தாமே). The same protection is claimed for life in the house and for the hour of death.

981 says சிவாய with அ, recited clearly in the heart, becomes Siva's form. 2712 says that when the impurity named நம is removed and that beginning left, what one chants is சிவாய, the truth free of impurity (சிவாயமலமற்ற உண்மை). 2712 explains why 981 recites சிவாய without நம: the dropped syllables are the bond.

984 says those who search, at one with Siva, reach the clarity that they are what is called Siva (சிவம்என்பது தானாம்), and that what lacks tapas is only tattva. 2393 names that state as the goal of both systems: becoming Siva is Vedanta and Siddhanta (சிவமாதல் வேதாந்த சித்தாந்தமாகும்), and apart from it each is in vain. 2393 sets 984's claim at the head of the doctrine.

977 makes the five letters a goad for the five elephants and promises the First to those who can hold all five together (தடுக்கவல்லார்). 985, after setting Nandi within knowledge, says the five who danced become kin there (ஆடிய ஐவரும் அங்கு உறவு ஆவார்கள்). The same five are first restrained by force, then made kin once Nandi is within, which qualifies the restraint as a stage.

994 says the six letters are six mantras, matched to the twenty-four of the Savitri, whose one head-letter, if discerned, ends birth. Thiruppugazh 1326 ends with the Brahmins of the six letters (ஆறெழுத்து அந்தணர்) praising Murugan's feet at Eragam. Both tie a six-letter mantra to the Brahmin; in 994 it is measured against the Savitri, in the song it has become the Brahmin's own mark.
1003 to 1006 prescribe flowers, pastes and lamps and promise every fruit; 1008 says the Lord's servants, the Siva-yogis and the desireless do not want such ritual work, only love.
1012 places the mantra's syllables in the body; 1013 says what the parts of நமசிவாய stand for: நம the bound soul, சிவ the Lord.

Both promise the end of sorrow to those who come to the Lord's feet; Tirumular reaches it through worship with lamps and offerings, the Kural through reaching the feet of the one without liking or aversion.
The Kural praises the path of the one who quenched the five senses; Tirumular says those who seek through the senses (பொறிவழி) only lament, and the Lord is found within.

1003 is only a list of flowers ending in the command சாத்திடே, offer them. 1848 grants worship with வானுற மாமலர், flowers heaped to the sky, but says the goddess cannot be reached except by those who put away flesh and perceive (ஊனினை நீக்கி உணர்பவர்க்கு அல்லது). Read together, the flower offering is set out in full and then made conditional on what the worshipper has given up.

1004 lists sandal, kunkumam, camphor and agil mixed with rosewater and closes on அன்பொடே, worship with love. 1452 takes the same materials, கோடி கடிகமழ் சந்தனம், and says even crores of them do not reach the honeyed feet except for those who eat having removed flesh (ஊனினை நீக்கி உண்பவர்க்கு). One verse makes love the manner of the rite, the other makes abstention from flesh its condition.

1006 repeats எய்தி வழிப்படில், if you come and worship, and promises Indra's wealth, the eight siddhis and at last முத்தி. Thiruppugazh 1127 asks for the same fruits, ஆநந்த சித்தி and பரமாநந்த முத்தி, but asks not to be bewildered (மருளாதே) by the pomp of worship, its mantras, halls and burning fuel, and to be called directly instead. The song keeps the goal of 1006 while warning that the rite itself can become a distraction.
audit_text_issue: Thiruppugazh 1127: some compounds in the first half (சவாலம்பனத்து, வேதண்டமத்த) do not split securely.

note: 1007 ends its list of the worshipper's disciplines with மன்னும் மனம் பவனத்தோடு வைகுமே, the mind settling with the breath. 880 opens on the same phrase, விடாத மனம் பவனத்தொடு மேவி, and carries it on: joined to the sound of Siva's conch, the five senses are bound and that is release and nectar. What 1007 gives as the outcome of disciplined worship, 880 treats as the yogic path to release.

1008 says four times வேண்டார்கள் கன்மம்: the Lord's servants, the desireless and the Siva-yogis want no ritual work, only love (அன்பே). 1444 ranks the kinds of puja and calls invoking a deity into a form outer puja (புறப்பூசை), while love at the end of fault (செயிற்கடை நேசம்) is Siva-puja. Both put love above the rite the chapter has been prescribing.

1008 says the Siva-yogis and those who have examined do not want கன்மம், ritual work, but love. Thiruppugazh 1127 asks not to be bewildered (மருளாதே) by ஆராதன ஆடம்பரம், the pomp of worship, its mantras and sacrificial fuel, and asks instead for the state where 'you and I' cease (நீநானற). The Murugan song makes the same turn from rite to inner state that Tirumular makes for the advanced worshipper.

1009 says the Lord is not found by searching through the senses but within, in the struck bell (எறிமணி யுள்ளே). 2436 uses the same word: having driven off lust, anger and delusion, the speaker reached the abode within the Om-sound of the struck bell (எறிமணி ஓமெனும் ஓசையின் உள்ளே). The pair shows the bell is the inner sound of meditation, and 2436 names that sound as Om.

1010 sets மருள் (delusion) and அறிவு side by side in one heart, like darkness and light, and says only those who have broken மருள் are knowers. Kural 351 names the same மருள் as taking what is not real for real, and says it produces birth without worth. The Kural gives what மருள் is and costs; Tirumular gives where it lives and who has left it.

1010 divides the heart into அறியாமை and அறிவு, darkness and open light, and praises those who break delusion. 2362 says the world cries அறிவு, அறிவு, yet no one knows knowledge and ignorance, and the way is to pass beyond both (அறிவுஅறியாமை கடந்து) and become knowledge. 2362 takes 1010's division one step further, beyond the pair itself.

1011 describes தான் அவனாக அவனே தான் ஆயிட, the self becoming He and He the self, and calls it the love of one on the fourth way. 2381 opens with the same தான் அவனாகும் and calls it a சமாதி in which all six 'ends' (kalanta, nadanta, yoganta, bodhanta, Siddhanta) become knower, known and knowledge. 1011 names this union as love, 2381 as the meeting point of every doctrine.

1012 places ஓங்காரம் below the navel, வகாரம் in the throat, நகாரம் in the forehead and விந்து and நாதம் above, a placing of syllables in the body. 1752 does the same with the linga: ஓங்காரம் is its pedestal, மகாரம் its neck, உகாரம் its inner circle, அகாரம் the linga, filled with விந்து நாதம். The same layering of syllables from base to bindu and nada is applied to the body in one verse and the emblem in the other.

1013 splits the mantra: நம is the பசு and சிவ the பதி, and when நம falls away (நமவற) joining the great silence that is Siva is true release. 2291 says the soul passes beyond the thirty-six, leaves நம (நமவிட்டு), and release follows gathered into சிவாய. Both make dropping the syllables நம, the soul's part, the step into release.

1014 says that when clarity comes சிவஅமுது ஊறும், Siva's nectar wells up, and the Lord who gives the open space remains as வெளி. Thiruppugazh 452 asks that சிவவமுது ஊறுக on the tongue and that he reach the வெளி with neither day nor night (பகலும் இரவும் இலா வெளி) as the supreme state. Arunagiri asks for the same two signs, welling nectar and open space, that Tirumular describes as the state reached.
1030 and the verses around it give the Lord counted feet, faces and eyes in the fire; 1031 says the endless one has no place, no measure and no word that reaches him. The forms are aids, not limits.
724 says Tirumular learned to nurture the body so as to nurture life; 1042 says those who guarded the body and dwelt within it lived through a crore of ages.
Both say deeds cannot cling to the one turned to the Lord: the Kural through his true praise, Tirumular through seeing the fire rise within.

1015 announces the நவகுண்டம், the nine fire-pits, and the good that rises in them. 360, in the story of Daksha's sacrifice, names the same நவகுண்டம் ஒன்பதும், which the gods ask Siva to make a source of joy for the good. The term that the chapter turns inward into places of the body appears in 360 as the outward sacrificial altar.

1016 lists among the kunda's parts பகைத்திடு முப்புரம், the hostile triple city, with fire. 343 says fools take it literally that Siva burned the three cities, and that முப்புரம் is the work of the three impurities (மும்மல காரியம்). 343 supplies the reading by which the triple city in 1016's fire-pit is the soul's malas being burned.

1017 speaks of a செஞ்சுடர், red flame, that knew the breath (கால் அறிந்து) and entered thought within. 1777 has the practitioner pass through the rising செஞ்சுடர் while the breath (ஆவி) rises as far as the body allows, and says holding this is the supreme state. Both place the red flame and the breath together as the inner fire of yoga.

1018 ends: the whole spread of the ancient Veda (பண்டையுள் வேதம்) I have set out today as a spoken text (இன்றுசொல் நூலாய்). In 81 Tirumular says the Lord made him well so that he would render the Lord well in Tamil (தமிழ்செய்யுமாறே). Together they show the poet's view of his own book: a new telling, in Tamil, of what was already revealed.

1021 sees a form rising as நற்சுடர், the good flame, and names her நல்லது என்றாள், the goddess. 1091 sees the young creeper, Shakti, within ஓமப் பெருஞ்சுடர், the great flame of the fire rite, and the fine smoke rising in it. Both make the flame of the homa the place where Shakti is seen.

1022 says those who do not ask her who stands gently take her for stone, even though they have learned (கற்றும்); the last line is unclear and may be corrupt. 318 calls those who have learned yet lack Siva-knowledge (கற்றும் சிவஞானம் இல்லா) wretches and fools. On the reading of 1022 given, both say learning without inner knowing leaves one blind to what is holy.
audit_text_issue: 1022 line 4 'கல்லதென் றாளையும் கற்றும் வின் வாளே' looks corrupt.

note: 1023 ends: the supreme flame (பரஞ்சுடர்) took its place within my body (என் ஆகத்துள்ளே இடங்கொண்டவாறே). 2324 says the flawless Shakti, the light of a great gem, was seen within the flesh (ஊனிடைக் கண்டதே). Both locate the supreme light in the speaker's own body, 1023 through the image of the fire-pit.

1025 calls the three-eyed one (முக்கணன்) the whole flame (முழுச்சுடர்), the one who swallowed all and saw the eight directions. 2684 explains the three eyes: sun and moon are his eyes and fire is the other eye in his forehead, making his body one of light. 2684 spells out why the three-eyed one of 1025 is himself the flame.

1026 says the six-faced one appears before his father (தந்தைதன் முன்னே சண்முகம் தோன்றலால்) and tells the meditator to hold him as the son (மைந்தன்). Thiruppugazh 602 names Murugan as the one who taught his father, who keeps Shakti at his side, the whole truth of the Veda (மறைநூலின் தத்துவ தற்பரம் முற்றும் உணர்த்திய). Tirumular places Skanda in the father's fire as the son; Arunagiri makes the son the father's teacher.

1031 says the endless one has no place wide enough, no one to measure him and no word that reaches him, and is known only by devotion (பத்தே). 448 says he is vast (அகன்றான்), the seven wide worlds one in him, and not easy to point to as 'this is he' (இவன்தான் என... எளியனும் அல்லன்). Both deny that the Lord can be measured or pointed out, and 1031 adds devotion as the way to know him.

1032 has the measured kunda (மட்டிட்ட குண்டம்) bloom as a lotus that stands bound (கட்டிட்டு நின்று). 662 uses the same words: in the stalk of the bound lotus (கட்டிட்ட தாமரை) the adorned maidens (மட்டிட்ட கன்னியர்) joined the Lady, standing bound (கட்டிட்டு நின்று). The shared wording shows the kunda's lotus is the same inner lotus of the yogic body.
audit_text_issue: 662 line 3 variants are garbled, as the marker says.

note: 1033 gives Parvati's partner by counts: twenty hands, ten faces with eyes, two flower feet and a flaming crown. 1730 gives Sadasiva the same way: two feet together on the pedestal, arms two and eight, five faces. Both describe a form of Siva by numbered limbs, and the counts differ, so the numbers belong to particular forms rather than one fixed image.

1034 says that to join the fire (வன்னியைக் கூடுதல்) is release. 2987 says those who can perform a thousand fire offerings (ஓமம் ஓர் ஆயிரம்) have seen through a thousand desires and are done with them. 2987 credits the outer homa with ending desire; 1034 goes further and makes union with the fire itself mukti.

1035 says those who seek without attachment (பற்றற நாடி) and pass through the spreading light have joined the one who is the whole flame. Kural 350 says to cling to the one without clinging (பற்றற்றான் பற்றினை) in order to let clinging go. Both make the end of attachment the condition for reaching the Lord, and Tirumular's பற்றற echoes the Kural's paradox.

1038, mapping a form onto the kunda, has the red face bloom with மற்றைக்கண் நெற்றி, the other eye in the forehead. 2684 uses the same phrase: fire is மற்றைக்கண் நெற்றி, the third eye, beside the sun and moon. The shared words show the forehead eye in the kunda form is the fire-eye of the Lord's body of light.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 1038 line 2 corrupt (stray Y in மகாரத்தார் Yமூக்கு).

note: 1039 ends with the Lord's light flourishing as Shakti, சத்திமானாகத் தழைத்த கொடி, the creeper. 2445 has the young creeper (இளங்கொடி) hang down and do good after the speaker reaches the First of the three-tiered circle within. In both the creeper is Shakti growing within, as the light of the Lord the speaker has reached.

1041 rhymes on மாதனம் and சாதனம்: the fire growing as great wealth, and the guru perfected with it as his means. 721 tells the reader to worship the guru who is the means (சாதனமாகும் குருவை) and value him as great wealth (மாதனமாக). The same two words make the guru both the means and the treasure in both verses.

1042 says those who guarded the body (காத்துடல்) and dwelt within it in thought grew old in it and saw a crore of ages (மூத்துடல் கோடி யுகம்). 758 says those who reached the hundred guard the body (காத்துடல்) and live into a crore of yugas (மூத்துடன் கோடி யுகம்). The near-repeat restates Tirumular's claim of long life in the guarded body.

1043 says the nine kundas are alike and the yogi who has seen within raises them in the நாடி. 658 places in the nine-gated body one place with nine channels (ஒன்பது நாடி), and says those who can still them gain visions. 1043 maps the nine fire-pits onto that inner set of nine, making the rite a matter of the channels.

Both name Mahamaya and speech among the first powers; in 1925 they shine within bindu, in 1045 they and the bindu-born (வயிந்தவம்) are all forms of one Tripura. The bindu chapter's cosmology here gets a goddess's face.

Both make the Goddess the one who unfolds as nada and bindu: 1048 has Tripura grant nada and nada's end while the supreme bindu becomes the worlds, 1138 has Sivashakti spread out as bindu and nada within the mind.
Both portraits give the Goddess the noose and goad. Tripura (1049) adds the sugarcane bow and flower arrows; Bhairavi (1081) adds the trident and skull. Same emblems, gentle and fierce forms.

1053 says no god fails to know her and nothing the five do is done without her; 1087 says the many gods, Siva, Brahma and Vishnu among them, look to the Lady as cause. Both put the Goddess behind every god.
1066 has her stand as his body and life; 1137 says the lady and he stand in one form and people do not see it. Both deny any gap between Siva and Shakti.

The Kural calls a head that does not bow at the feet of the Lord of eight qualities as useless as a sense that cannot sense; Tirumular tells the head to wear the Goddess's feet and the mouth to praise her. The same claim for the head, turned to the Goddess.

The Kural traces joyless birth to the delusion (மருள்) that takes what is not real as real (பொருள்). Tirumular uses the same pair: the Goddess turns the deluded mind into one that has found the true thing, so grace is the remedy for the Kural's diagnosis.

1046 strings the Goddess's names, திரிபுரை சுந்தரி அந்தரி ... நாரணி ... மனோன்மனி, and says the one great one stands as many. Thiruppugazh 916 opens its closing praise with the same run, காளி திரிபுரை யந்தரி சுந்தரி, adding சண்டிகை and the sister of Mal. The pairing shows the Tirumanthiram's litany of Tripura surviving almost word for word as the stock name-chain for Murugan's mother.

1047 says the three-coloured Tripura herself grants போகமும் முத்தியும், enjoyment and release. 1714 says Sadasiva remains giving போகமும் முத்தியும் புத்தியும் சித்தியும். The same pair of gifts is claimed for the Goddess and for Sadasiva, which fits the book's teaching that the two are not apart.

1049 puts மலர்க்கன்னல் வாளிவில், the sugarcane bow with flower arrows, among the Goddess's emblems beside goad and noose. In Thiruppugazh 133 the same கருப்புவில் and arrows are Kama's, the weapons women's glances are likened to and the source of the bewilderment the poet asks to escape. The pairing shows one weapon as the instrument of delusion in one book and an emblem held by the Goddess in the other.

1052 says the great Shakti is all the tattvas and also அணோரணி, smaller than the atom. 2008 calls the First Lord அணுவில் அணு, the atom within the atom, reached only by dividing it a thousandfold. The same Upanishadic figure of the smaller-than-small is given to Shakti in one verse and to the Lord in the other.

1054 reports that the knowers say Parashakti is அருவுரு, formless and with form, and that the Supreme is in her. 1763 says Parasiva takes உருவும் அருவும் உருவோடு அருவும், form, formlessness and both together. The pairing shows the three-fold form-formless description used for Siva applied to Shakti.

1055 says that wherever there is flesh the Lord is there as உள்ளுயிர்க் கால், the breath of the inner life, and stands everywhere. 2761 says that as the breath (பிராணன்) rising in the heart spreads through hands and feet, so the dancer dances everywhere (எங்கணும்). Both use the breath pervading the body to picture the Lord pervading all.

Kural 39 says only the joy that comes through virtue is joy: அறத்தான் வருவதே இன்பம். 1056 names Parashakti herself as புண்ணியம் ஆகிய போகம், the enjoyment that is merit. The Kural defines rightful pleasure by its source in virtue; the Tirumanthiram makes the Goddess that pleasure.

In 1058 the poet, using the love lyric's words, says he desired the coral-bodied maiden and placed her within himself: என் உள்ளே நயந்துவைத்தேனே. In Kural 1128 the woman keeps her lover in her heart (நெஞ்சத்தார் காதலவர்) and so fears hot food. The beloved lodged inside the self is the same figure, turned in 1058 on the Goddess.

1059 lists the many lives and the workings of mind and instruments (சித்தக் கரணச் செயல்கள்) together with the Shakti who makes them act. 2803 says Shakti as Tatpara gives will (இச்சை) to the Supreme and to souls and conducts the distinctions beginning with knowledge. 2803 names the will as what she gives, where 1059 only says she makes the faculties act.

1060 calls the Goddess தலைவி and says she has filled the poet's heart so that it is steady (உள்ளம் நிலைபெற). 1105 calls her தானே தலைவி and says she set him apart, filled him and stands seeking his heart (உள்ளம் நாடிநின்றாள்). Both make the Goddess's entering and filling the heart the point, and 1060 adds that the heart is made firm by it.

1061 says Manonmani settled into the poet's inner self (அகம்படிந்து), became one with him and closed (அடைத்தாள்). 1115 says the jewelled one joined his heart (இயைந்தனள் என்உள்ளம்), desired the words namasiva there and cut away his other babble (பிதற்று அறுத்தாள்). 1115 makes plainer what the closing in 1061 may mean: her union with the heart ends its wandering speech.

2024 says that though the mahout has learned good books and goads it, the leaping beast of the senses will not keep to the road. 1062 says people do not discern how Manonmani closes off the mind that churns (மத்தடைகின்ற). Together they say that learning and effort cannot stop what the Goddess stops.

1063 says that when the lady of fragrant hair and he stand joined (மங்கையும் தானும் புணர்ந்துடனே நிற்கும்), she grants the goal to the ripened. 1137 says no one perceives that the lady and he stand together in one form (மங்கையும் தானும் உடனே உருவொத்துநின்றமை). 1137 stresses that the union goes unseen; 1063 makes it the condition of grace.

In 1064 the poet's inner self is like a sour mean fruit (புளியுறு புன்பழம்) that the Goddess clears and then eats (உண்டாள்) to save him. In 1523 the sweet girl, once all that stands within is gone, becomes the ripe fruit (கனி) that has beheld the First. Both carry the soul's ripening under the Goddess as a fruit going from sour to ripe.

1065 says what was called 'is' and 'is not' took form and filled the hall of Tillai (வண்தில்லை மன்று), and that people have not seen it (கண்டிலர்). 2723 asks who can know the dancer of golden Tillai (பொன்தில்லைக் கூத்தனை யார்அறிவாரே). Both make the presence in the Tillai hall what people fail to know.

1068 says that praising (தோத்திரம் செய்து) and worshipping her paired feet sets the way of worship. 33 says that even those who can recite many hymns of praise (துதிபல தோத்திரம்) lack understanding and wither within. 33 limits 1068: hymns alone, without seeing the one truth, do not suffice.

1069 says that practising the Goddess's name on the fingers makes light grow and the three times appear (முக்காலமும் தோன்றுமே). 127 says those who became Siva remained knowing the nature of the three times (முக்காலத்து இயல்பு). 1069 gives a practice whose fruit 127 attributes to the realised.

1070 makes the Goddess the sixteen beginning with Medha (மேதாதி ஈரெட்டும்). 1492 places the sky-light at the end of the sixteen kalas beginning with Medha (மேதாதி யீரெண் கலாந்தத்து) in the path of sahamarga. The same rare sixteen is a form of the Goddess in one verse and a stage of yogic ascent in the other.

1071 praises the red feet that hold the rare thing of the one who changes the deluded mind: மருளுற்ற சிந்தையை மாற்றி அருமைப் பொருளுற்ற சேவடி. 2599 repeats the line almost word for word as the cause of gaining grace: மருளுற்ற சிந்தையை மாற்றி அருமைப் பொருளுற்ற சேவடி போற்றுவோர். This is a near-repeat in a distant chapter, applied in 1071 to Bhuvanapati and in 2599 to the Lord.

1073 says Omkari, becoming Ahankari, bore the five (ஐவரைப் பெற்றிட்டு). 2677 says the five elements arose within omkara (ஓங்காரத் துள்ளே உதித்தஐம் பூதங்கள்). Taking the five as the elements, 2677 states as doctrine what 1073 puts as the Goddess giving birth.

1074 says Tatparai (தற்பரை), as leader, herself sowed lives and is the nature of the way to Siva. 2803 says Shakti as Tatpara gives will to souls and, dancing in grace, brings them to love Hara's feet. 2803 shows how the Tatparai of 1074 leads souls on that way.

The chapter opens with Bhairavi as the first of twelve kalas, a count in a mantra, and closes with her as the first of the twelve again; by the end the count is a name of the goddess praised as beginning and beginningless.
1106 leaves the maiden asleep in the middle channel; 1107 has Manonmani come in sleep, embrace and say 'do not sleep'. Read together, the waking is hers and his at once.
1118 ends calling maya darkness; 1119 opens by saying darkness is Shakti and light is the Lord, so the darkness is not rejected but given to her as one of two powers.
audit_text_issue: 1118 line 2 is corrupt (துன்னியங fகைவரைப் has a stray character)

note: 1115 says she cut away the poet's babble with the five-syllable mantra; 1116 says the foolish who went on babbling passed away, while she stands before those whose effort is complete.
The same line of names (woman, samadhi, Manonmani, the auspicious one) in both; in 1114 she joins the heart, in 1120 she blossoms in it, a refrain that marks the hymn's stages.
Both make reaching or bowing at the divine feet the end of births: the Kural's sea of births, Tirumular's cruel births. Tirumular gives it to the goddess, the Kural to the unnamed Lord.
The Kural says the two kinds of deed do not cling to those who praise the Lord truly; 1122 praises her by name after name and ends that she drove out the poet's deeds.

1076 says the fourteen at the end is Bhairavi, who as முந்து நடுவும் முடிவும் becomes அந்தமும் ஆதியும். 1749 has the fourteen (ஈரேழு) bearing the fire and, in their middle (நடு), ஓங்கிய ஆதியும் அந்தமும். The same cluster of fourteen, middle, beginning and end in two distant chapters suggests a shared yogic scheme that neither verse explains.

1076 says the great Shakti rising in the heart-lotus becomes அந்தமும் ஆதியும். 1927 gives the same words, அந்தமும் ஆதியும் ஆகி, to Paraparan, the pervader who does the five acts. The pairing shows the book giving Siva's own title of end and beginning to the goddess.

1078 sets the practice by the moon that goes round the reckoned twenty-seven days (எண்ணிய நாட்கள் இருபத்தேழ் சூழ்மதி); 1080 says that when awareness joined with the moon runs twenty-seven days (இருபத்து எழுநாள் புணர்மதி), Bhairavi's trident comes to rule. Read together, the twenty-seven lunar days are the span of the mantra's practice and 1080 names its fruit.

1081 puts trident, skull, noose and goad (சூலம் கபாலம் ... பாசாங்குசம்) in Bhairavi's hands and makes her the upper limb of the form Mal and Brahma could not know. 2780 puts பாசம், அங்குசம், சூலம், கபாலம் in the hands of the dancing Siva who has the woman as one half (மங்கையோர் பாகமாய்). The same weapons held by both fit 1081's claim that she is part of his body.

1083 gives the goddess eyes of sun and moon (சூரிய சோம நயனத்தள்) with fire (வன்னி). 2684 gives Isan the sun and moon as eyes (ஞாயிறும் திங்களும் கண்கள்) and fire as the other eye in his forehead. The three lights as three eyes belong to both, as the verses that make her his half would lead one to expect.

1084 places a noble lady in an eight-petalled flower, with eight maidens (எண்மர் கன்னியர்) and sixty-four women who come and see the Shakti. 662 has nine adorned maidens (மட்டிட்ட கன்னியர்) joining the Lady (மாது) in the stalk of a bound lotus. Both picture the goddess in a lotus with a ring of maiden powers; 662 places it on the yogic path to the brow.

1086 goes from outer worship (பூசனை, scent, flowers, banners) to inner sound and to seeing Tripura shine. 1524 says what such worship of her yields: for those who worship her with honour (சிறப்பொடு பூசனை) she cuts birth, grants great austerity and cuts forgetfulness. 1524 names the fruit of the worship that 1086 lays out.

1087 says the many gods look different as ornaments of one gold look many (பூணும் பலபல பொன்போல), and the goddess is the cause of Siva, Brahma and Mal. 110 says the ignorant, not knowing that one light stood as three and five, babble dividing it into Isan, Mal and Ayan (பேதித்தவரைப் பிதற்றுகின்றாரே). Both deny that the three are really separate, though 110 traces them to Siva's light and 1087 to the goddess.

1087 makes the goddess the cause (காரணி) even of Siva, along with Brahma and Mal. 1119 says Shakti is the darkness and our Lord is the light (இருளது சத்தி வெளியதுஎம் அண்ணல்), and that grace is given by the Lord. Read as claims about which comes first, the two conflict: one puts Siva among her effects, the other ranks her below him as the dark to his light.

1088 joins the Karani mantra recited in the lotus to பூரண கும்ப விரேசம், the filling, holding and emptying of breath. 568 defines those phases with their counts: பூரகம் sixteen, கும்பம் sixty-four, இரேசகம் thirty-two. 1088 applies the breath control of the yoga chapter to the goddess's mantra.

1089 tells the reader to place the mantra on the fingers and to understand clearly the beginning of fine Tamil (செந்தமிழ் ஆதி தெளிந்து) and worship. 66 says that the Tamil word and the northern word (தமிழ்ச்சொல் வடசொல்) both teach the Lord. 1089 puts 66's claim to use: here Tamil is the material of the mantra rite. This holds only if செந்தமிழ் ஆதி means the Tamil letters.

550, in the chapter on eightfold yoga, promises to tell for Parashakti the true armour, the placings and the gestures (கவச நியாசங்கள் முத்திரை). 1092 to 1096 carry this out for Bhairavi: 1093 names the armour (கவசம்), the eye (நேத்திரம்) and the trident and yoni mudras. 1093 fills in the rite that 550 only lists.

1097 names the goddess by her fierce names, வயிரவி நீலி நிசாசரி, and makes her the one who enters the heart. In its praise, thiruppugazh:578 names Murugan's mother திரிபுரை, காலாக்கினி கோப பயிரவி and நீலி. The pairing shows that the Thiruppugazh's litany of the mother uses the names of the Tirumanthiram's Bhairavi worship.

1098 says the first mother stands with her power as the Veda, the moving and unmoving (சராசரம்), the five elements, darkness and open space (இருள்வெளி) and the many lives. 1806 says grace is the whole elemental world and the moving and unmoving (அருளே சராசர மாய), and the Lord is called darkness and open space (இருளே வெளியே). Both list the same things to say that the Shakti, or grace, pervades them all.

1099 says that if one recites and realises (ஓதி உணரில்) Bhairavi, body and life become the Lord and births are destroyed. Kural 357 says that if the mind ponders and realises what is (உள்ளது உணரின்), one need not think again of birth. Both make realising, not the act alone, what ends birth; the Kural names truth as the object, the Tirumanthiram the goddess.
audit_text_issue: Kural 357 text reads உணரான் where the sense needs உணரின்.

note: 1101 ends the goddess's work with என்னை உய்யக்கொண்டாளே, she took me so that I was saved. 1779 ends with the supreme guru who took the one who could not save himself, உய்யக் கொண்டானே. The same act of taking the soul to be saved is credited to the goddess and to the guru.

1104 describes the goddess wearing the young crescent (இளம்பிறை) with a pure crown of matted hair (தூய கடைமுடி) and holding the trident (சூலினி). In its praise, thiruppugazh:764 names Murugan's mother திரிபுரை பயிரவி, who wears the moon (திங்கள் சூடிய) on her shining matted hair. The Thiruppugazh keeps the Tirumanthiram's picture of Bhairavi as Siva's double, with crescent and matted hair.

1105 places the maiden (குமரி) in the sweet southern corner (இனிய தென்மூலை) as the sole lady and leader. 2755 names Kumari, the maiden at the land's end (ஈறான கன்னி குமரியே), among the holy places of the pure southern land. Read together, 1105's maiden in the southern corner is the Kumari of the cape, so the goddess of the hymn is tied to a place.

In 1107 Manonmani embraces the sleeper, spits her shining betel into his mouth (தம்பலம் வாயில் உமிழ்ந்திட்டு) and says 'do not sleep'. In thiruppugazh:961 the poet thought it a pleasure to drink and eat the coral lips and the betel (தம்பலமும்) the women gave, and fell into their embrace. The same gift of betel from a woman's mouth sinks the man into desire in the song and wakes him in the Tirumanthiram.

Kural 367 says that if one cuts off craving thoroughly (அவாவினை ஆற்ற அறுப்பின்), unfailing deeds come as one wishes. In 1108 craving is held down (அவாவை அடக்கிவைத்து) inside the whirl that lights the breath, and the goddess does it, saying 'fear not'. Set beside the Kural's self-effort, 1108 makes the subduing of craving the goddess's work, and it is held down rather than cut off.

1112 has the goddess staying in the forehead's one eye, looking towards the discernment at the bow's head (சிலைத்தலை, the brow). 2770 tells the reader to gaze steadily at the space between the brows (புருவத்து இடைவெளி), where the mantra shines and the Supreme sits. 2770 makes the practice explicit where 1112 gives the goddess's seat.

1113 says the goddess entered the four fingers (பொருந்திய நால்விரல் புக்கனள்) and joined the perfected pillar. In the breath chapter, 576 has the breaths reaching out eight finger-breadths and cutting back four (நால்விரல்), becoming the five letters when gathered in. If the four fingers of 1113 are the same breath measure, then the goddess's entry is the breath drawn in. The verse does not say this, so the link is tentative.
audit_text_issue: 1113: ஒன்fறி has a stray Latin letter

note: 1114 and 1124 open with the same line, ஆதி அனாதி அகாரணி காரணி, the beginning and the beginningless, the causeless and the cause. 1114 makes her the light of light who joined the poet's heart; 1124 makes her the lone flame for the Vedic ones and the first of the twelve. The repeated line runs through the hymn, and 1124 uses it to close the chapter.

1116 says foolish men (பேதை மனிதர்) babbled and passed away, while the first mother gives grace to those complete in effort (முயற்றியின் முற்றி). naladiyar:52 says the best do their own work, mindful of death, and none are more foolish (பேதையார்) than those who babble (பிதற்றும்) endless grammar and astrology. Both set useless talk against effort and call the talker a fool.

1119 says Shakti is the darkness and the Lord is the light (இருளது சத்தி வெளியது). 2341 says Shakti, as grace, is like heat in fire (அனல் வெம்மை போல), inseparable from him, and that darkness is the three malams. If 1119's darkness means what obscures, as 1118's 'this maya is darkness' suggests, the verses disagree about whether Shakti is the obscuring dark or the grace that removes it.

1121 says the first one stands as caste, difference and the tattvas (சாதியும் பேதமும் தத்துவமாய் நிற்பன்). thiruppugazh:359 describes the supreme light as without caste or clan (சாதி குலமும் இலது). On the reading that 1121 makes caste a form the Lord takes, the two disagree. If 1121 means only that caste is among the tattvas, the conflict goes away.
audit_text_issue: 1121 is obscure; the marker flagged it.

note: 1122 calls the goddess the mistress of the cool shore of Avaduturai (ஆவடு தண்துறை) and Siva's woman, who drove out the poet's deeds. In the account of the poet's life, 78 names the glorious one at Siva's Avaduthurai (ஆவடு தண்டுறை), who cut off his birth and took him as her own. Both credit the goddess of the poet's own shrine with ending his deeds and births.

1123 says she abides as the inner light (உள்ளொளி) in the hearts of those whose deeds are driven out and stands as the tattva for all who reach her. 1063 says she stands as the inner light (உள்ளொளி யாகி), joined with the Lord, and grants the goal to those who rise ripened. Both make the goddess the inner light that leads the ripened soul to its end.
audit_text_issue: 1063 has the typo நிறகும் for நிற்கும்.

note: The two verses share a frame (தார்மேல்/தாமேல் உறைவிடம், பார்மேல், பூமேல் உறைகின்ற ... வந்தனள்): 1130 fills it with Brahma and the goddess of speech, 1141 with the lotus petals and the bangled lady. They may be variants of one verse.
audit_text_issue: 1141 line 2 (இதழ்பழி னெட்டிரு நூறுன) looks garbled; 1130's ஒரு நூறு is unexplained

note: Both make the goddess and bindu one: 1925 sets Mahamaya, the goddess of speech and kundalini within bindu, 1138 has Shakti spread out as bindu and nada.

Both cut a pride (செருக்கு) voiced as possession: the Kural's 'I' and 'mine', Tirumular's 'my mother, my father' said of the divine parents. Tirumular extends the Kural's renunciation of ownership to the soul's claim on God.
audit_text_issue: 1129 line 3 has a stray Latin letter: உரைசெய்Yயும்.

note: Both set love (அன்பு) against bone (என்பு). For the Kural a body without love is bone wrapped in skin; Tirumular has the father reached through love and the mother present in the bone within bondage. The pairing depends on reading என்பிற் as 'in the bone'.

Both join penance, power and the defeat of death: the Kural says those who gain the power (ஆற்றல்) of austerity can leap past death; Tirumular's goddess of rare penance stands in his power (ஆற்றல்) and drives Death (கூற்றம்) away.

Tirumular opens every line of 1125 with அளந்தேன், 'I measured' the bounds of the wide world and its first Lord (ஆதிப் பிரானை), by examining his grace. In 95 he asks who knows our Lord's greatness, who knows his breadth and length (அகலமும் நீளமும்), and says he speaks of his not knowing the root. On the plain reading the same poet both claims and disclaims the measuring of the Lord; 1125's அவனருள் ஆய்ந்து suggests the measure is possible only through grace, which 95's humility verse leaves out.

571 says no one knows the measure (கணக்கு) of holding the breath, and that for those who know it, it is the means to kick Death. 1126 says breath retention (கும்பகம்) comes by the path the maiden, Shakti, brings (கன்னி கொணர்ந்த வழிகொண்டு). Read together, the knowledge of the breath's measure in 571 is in 1126 given by Shakti's grace rather than by technique alone.

The Kural's one who guards the five (ஓரைந்தும் காப்பான்) with the goad of firmness (உரனென்னும் தோட்டி) is a seed for heaven. 1127 has the same team, five elephants and the mahout with his goad (கும்பக் களிறுஐந்தும் கோலொடு பாகனும்), but they do not end under control: with the Lord and the lady they all merge and are lost in the union of love (அன்பிற் கலவியுள் ஆயொழிந்தாரே). The image is the same; the Kural ends in restraint, 1127 in absorption.

2023 has five elephants in rut (ஐந்து களிறு) that will not come to the post of the Agamas, and says yoga comes right only after the mahout and the elephants are both worn out (பாகனும் எய்த்து அவை தாமும் இளைத்தபின்). 1127 ends the same struggle differently: elephants, mahout and goad are lost together in the union of love. The pair shows two ways the senses' contest closes in the Tirumanthiram: by exhaustion or by absorption.

270 says love and Siva are not two (அன்பே சிவம்) and that those who know it rest as love that is Siva. 1128 says our father can enter only into love (அன்பிற் புகவல்லன் ஆம் எங்கள் அப்பன்), and adds what 270 does not: in the mire of sorrow within the bond, it is Parashakti the mother who is present (பாசத்துள் ... பாரசக்தி என்னம்மை). The love-is-Siva teaching is extended with a place for Shakti inside bondage.

1129 calls the saying 'my mother, my father' (என்னம்மை என்னப்பன் என்னும்) a conceit (செருக்கு) to be cut. 1770 says that speaking first of the union of my father the Supreme and my mother (எந்தை பரமனும் என்னம்மை கூட்டமும்) and telling it in order is jnana. The conflict holds on the reading that 1129 rejects the possessive naming itself; if it rejects only the pride in it, the two agree that the naming must be free of self.
audit_text_issue: 1129 has a stray Latin letter in உரைசெய்Yயும்.

note: Both verses give the goddess the same phrase, தீபத்து ஒளியுடன், 'with the light of the lamp': in 1132 a lamp welling with honey by which one is to know the hall of the dance, in 1139 a good lamp with which the nectar-breasted lady wells up for those with inner sight. The repeated phrase ties the inner light to Shakti across the chapter's yogic run.

1133 makes the lady knowledge itself, both within maya and within the five senses (அறிவான மாயையும் ... அறிவான மங்கை). 402 calls Manonmani the one mingled as cause and effect and the knowing at the root of all knowing (போதாதி போதம்). Both refuse to set bound knowledge apart from Shakti: even the knowing in maya is hers.

A near-repeat: both open இரவும் பகலும் இலாத இடத்தே குரவம் செய்கின்ற குழலியை and both say to join her without sound (அரவம் செய்யாமல்). 1134 ends with becoming a child that age does not touch (பருவம் செய்யாத பாலன்), 1528 with the Supreme ruling one without other care (பரிவொன்றிலாளும் பராபரை). The same instruction is given two fruits, ageless youth and the Supreme's rule.

331 reproaches those who do not stay in the place where there is neither night nor day (இராப்பகல் அற்ற இடத்தே) and drink the nectar of bliss. 1134 says what staying there brings: seeking the lady who dances in that place and sleeping in silence with grace, one becomes a child age does not touch. The same placeless place is the target of the reproach in 331 and of the promise in 1134.

1135 says release that is the root comes when bindu and nada are left behind (விந்து நாதங்கள் விட்டிட), with Parashakti. 1929 says bindu, joined with Shakti and Siva's feet, grants release (வீடு அளிக்கும்). On the reading that 1135 makes bindu a stage to be passed, the two disagree on whether bindu is what is shed for release or what gives it.

1136 says Parashakti, standing with the Supreme, becomes the powers of knowledge and will and, with the power of action, enters all else (ஞானமும் இச்சையுமாய் ... கிரியாசக்தி). 2334 says the action, will and knowledge of ancient Siva and of souls arise from undying Mahamaya and maya (தொழில் இச்சை ஞானங்கள் ... மாமாயை மாயையின் ஆகும்). On the reading that 2334 derives even Siva's three powers from maya, it conflicts with 1136, which makes them Shakti's own form.

1137 says no one perceives (ஒன்றும் உணரார்) that the lady and the Lord stand in one form (உருவொத்து நின்றமை). 1751 says no one knows (ஆரும் அறியார்) that he is A and she, spread through the world, is U, the two together becoming the earth and rising as sound. Both name the unity of Siva and Shakti as the thing people miss; 1751 gives it as the syllables of the pranava.

1142 says that because the lady stays where the Supreme is as his banner and light, the world moves on as the woman-creeper (பெண்கொடியாக நடந்தது உலகே). Thiruppugazh 322's praise names the goddess as the creeper-woman born of the mountain whose womb bore the whole world (பெண்கொடி உலகடையப் பெற்ற). Both use கொடி, the creeper, for the goddess on whom the whole world depends.

1143 sets maidens 'eight with one' (கன்னிகள் எட்டுடன் ஒன்றாய்) inside the lotus; 1084 sets a noble lady within the eight petals of the full-blown flower with eight maidens around her (எண்மர் கன்னியர்). The same figure of eight maidens round one Shakti in the inner lotus appears in both, and 1084 helps read 1143's obscure count.

1144 gives the stacked lotuses (அடுக்குத் தாமரை) as the Primal one's seat, rising from the body to the crown; 2529 has three lotuses in bud (மொட்டலர் தாமரை மூன்று) all opened by a spreading light. Both picture the yogic body as a column of lotuses; 2529 adds the light that opens them, which 1145 names as the sprouting flame.

Both use the rare word முச்சதுரம், the triple square: 627 places it just above the base (மூலத்து மேலது முச்சதுரத்தது), and 1145 has the sprouting flame (முளைச்சுடர்) rise from it and run to every square. 627 locates the figure; 1145 makes it the starting point of the flame's ascent.

335 says yogis who bind the breath (கால்கட்டி) taste the nectar of knowledge-bliss from the bright moon. 1146 describes the same event as the breaths, spread to every quarter, drawing together to look at the pearl-bright face, after which the nectar flows downward (தேறல் அதோமுகம்). 1146 gives the movement that 335 states as a result, and sets it within Shakti's presence.

1148 has the great goddess stand adorned with the three lights (முச்சோதி புனைய); 3005 has the First Lord stand as the light of the three lights (சுடர் மூன்று ஒளியாய்). The same cosmic figure is Shakti's ornament in one verse and Siva's own form in the other, which fits the book's teaching that the two are one.

417 makes the Lord a potter: he shapes the world and births, the wheel, the pot and the jar (வனைவான் ... வனையவல்லானே). 1149 gives the same verb to Shakti: she who can shape the countless cosmic eggs within (வனையவல்லாள் அண்டகோடிகள்). The potter's work of creation passes from the Lord to the goddess with the same word.

1151 says Tripura destroys the deeds of her devotees (அடியார் வினைகெடுத்து) and is the Primal one. 1077 says Tripura goes with those of merit so that they gain light (கதிர்பெறப் போகும் திரிபுரை புண்ணியத்தோரே), while those who do not reach her refuge do not. Both make Tripura's saving work fall on those who are hers.

443 says that as a potter shapes whatever is in his mind (மனத்துற்றது), so if Nandi wills, the world becomes this or that. 1153 also makes creation an act of the Lord's thought (பாவித்து உலகம் படைக்கின்ற காலத்து), and adds that Parashakti joins him and runs through it above and below. The will that shapes the world in 443 is in 1153 given its extension in Shakti.

1154 says those who do not know the Lord do not see the cause that stands for release to come (கதிவர நின்றதோர் காரணம் காணார்), and links this to not considering the lady. 2425 spells out that cause: the foot is Shakti, grace, the cause (கால் அந்தச் சத்தி அருள் என்பர் காரணம்), and when it shows the soul knowledge, release comes. 2425 answers what 1154 says is unseen.

Both make learning the start of a way that ends in seeing the true: the Kural's learners who see the true thing (மெய்ப்பொருள்) take the road of no return; Tirumular's learn what is to be learned, then pass through yoga and knowledge to see the Supreme.

Both say those who saw Nadanta are unwavering (நாதாந்தங் கண்டோர் நடுக்கற்ற). 1422 sets Vedanta and Siddhanta side by side; 1435 distinguishes what the seers of Vedanta, of Nadanta and of Siddhanta each hold.
audit_text_issue: TM 1422 புதாந்த likely for பூதாந்த; மாதுப் புனஞ்செய்ய obscure.

note: The Kural calls the wealth of the பேரறிவாளன், the man of great knowledge who acts for the world (உலகவாம்), a village tank (ஊருணி) full of water. 1419 gives the same title, பேரறிவாளன், to the Lord who makes town and world alike (ஊரும் உலகமும்). The word and the pairing of town and world move from the generous wise man to the Creator.

The two verses share their frame word for word: சத்தும் அசத்தும் சதசத்தும், சித்தும் அசித்தும், சுத்தம் அசுத்தம். In 2058 the grace-guru shows these and speaks the word beyond pure and impure; in 1420 the pure Saiva has discerned them and stands untouched by pure and impure. What the guru gives in 2058 is what defines the disciple in 1420.

1421 says those who learn what is to be learned and go in due order (முறைமுறை) through yoga and knowledge reach the Supreme and are Siddhantins. Naladiyar 317 says books are easy for those who learn them in order (நெறிப்பட்டுக் கற்பவர்க்கு), but their meaning is hard for anyone to grasp. The Naladiyar warns that ordered learning does not by itself reach the meaning, which 1421 places only at the end of yoga and knowledge.

1422 sets pure Vedanta and clear Siddhanta side by side as what the steady-sighted have seen (வேதாந்தம் சுத்தம் விளங்கிய சித்தாந்த). 2393 says becoming Siva is both Vedanta and Siddhanta, and that the new Vedanta is the Siddhanta of knowledge. Both refuse to oppose the two schools.

1423 commends earrings, seals and beads for those of service and rite; 1438 says the pure Saiva goes beyond outward garb (வேடம் கடந்து), without show. The signs are fitting at one stage and passed beyond at another.

1423 assigns the paired earrings, seals and rudraksha garland to those of chariyai and kiriyai (அணைவாஞ் சரியை கிரியையினார்க்கே). 1670 says the emblems are not futile (அவமான சாதனம் ஆகாது) for Siva-gnanis and Siva-yogis and, on its plain reading, futile for the others (அவமாம் அவர்க்கு). The conflict holds on that plain reading of 1670, which gives the signs to the higher paths where 1423 gives them to the lower; on the other reading of அவமாம் அவர்க்கு the two agree.

1424 describes a Saiva who wears two gold earrings (காதுப்பொன் ஆர்ந்த கடுக்கன்) and keeps reciting (ஓதி இருப்பார்), and calls him only 'one kind of Saiva'. 1662 lists ash, copper earrings (காதணி தாம்பிர குண்டலம்) and the rudraksha string as Rudra's emblems for those who recite (ஓதியவர்க்கும்). The same earrings-and-recitation figure is placed by 1424 at the lower, outward grade of Saivism and by 1662 among the marks of the Siva-yogi.

1425 says those who have seen the nine divisions (கண்டங்கள் ஒன்பதும் கண்டவர்) have seen the rare thing. 2221 is a first-person report: knowing the intent, the speaker saw the nine regions fit together (ஒன்பது கண்டமும் ஆங்கே பொருந்தறிந்தேன்) and then knew the Lord of the gods in his fullness. Both make the seeing of the nine கண்டம் the step to knowing the Lord, and 2221's sequence helps read the obscure punning of 1425.

1426 lists what the jnani sees: all the good books of the earth (நன்னூல் அனைத்து), the way of silence, the sixty-four attainments, and finally himself with the Lord (கோனொடு தன்னையும்). 1461 says letters, songs and the sixty-four arts (எண்ணெண் கலை) do not remove fettered birth (பாசப் பிறவியும் நீங்கா). Read together, the books and arts in 1426's list are not themselves release; what counts is the last item, seeing oneself with the Lord.

115 states that pasu and pasam cannot reach the Lord; 1436 repeats the line and gives it images, clouds that never reach the sky and sights that never reach the eye. It leaves out 115's other half, that when the Lord approaches they cease.
115 sets out Pati, Pasu and Pasam as beginningless; 1432 makes that triad, with impurity and release, the matter the pure Saiva contemplates.
63 names the nine Agamas Nandi received (Karanam, Kamikam and the rest); 1429 begins from the same nine before naming the twenty-eight.
1420's pure Saiva discerns the real, the unreal and what is both, and keeps clear of the sentient and the insentient; 1431's has passed beyond them, into a state where they are no longer told apart.
Both make the feet the way: in the Kural reaching the Lord's feet takes one across the sea of births; in Tirumular going by the feet of the Supreme power one becomes Siva.

1427 lists the means (சாதனம்) of pure Saivas, among them the means against the wrong path (துன்மார்க்க சாதனம்) and the means of the true path (சன்மார்க்க சாதனம்), without saying what the latter is. 1483 says it: the means of sanmarga is knowledge and its object (ஞான ஞேயம்), while the means of the lower paths suits the simple, and those who have left the evil path (துன்மார்க்கம் விட்ட) become Him. 1483 fills in the content of the term 1427 only names.

1428 places the dawning of knowledge within the joined portion of Vedanta and Siddhanta (வேதாந்த சித்தாந்த பாகத்தின் ஊடுறு ஞானோதயன்), written as one compound. 2393 states the claim outright: becoming Siva is Vedanta and Siddhanta (சிவமாதல் வேதாந்த சித்தாந்தமாகும்), and each apart is in vain. 2393 supplies the reason behind 1428's single compound: the two are one where they end in becoming Siva.

381 sets the Supreme without beginning or end (பராபரம்) in union with his consort power பராபரை, from whom Para and nada appear. 1430 says the same பராபரை stands apart from the pure and impure, the real and unreal, both impels and dwells within, and is the Father's power of grace (அத்தன் அருட்சத்தி), everywhere. 1430 takes 381's cosmological consort and names her as grace.

1431 says those beyond the real and unreal reach the state of 'I am Siva' (சிவோகமாய்), sink into the bliss of release, and attainment too is at its height there (சித்தியும் அங்கே சிறந்துளது). 1585 says that joining 'I am Siva' (சிவோகமே சேர்தல்) is the seed of the supreme siddhi (பரசித்திக்கு வித்து) and makes the knowledge of release sprout. Both tie the highest siddhi to சிவோகம், 1431 as its fullness and 1585 as its seed.

1432 sets Lord, soul and bond (பதி பசு பாசம்) as what pure Saivas must reflect on. The Thiruppugazh song turns the same triad into a plea: that Lord, soul and bond be made distinct each from each without stain (பதிபசு பாசமானவை கசடற வேறு வேறுசெய்தருள்வாயே). What Tirumular gives as a subject of thought, Arunagirinathar asks for as a grace of discrimination.

1474 says each path is contained in jnana for the jnani and names jnana in jnana, yoga in jnana and kiriyai in jnana, leaving out chariyai. 1434 names exactly that missing item: settling the unsettled mind, making it Siva and keeping to contemplation is the jnani's charya (ஞானி சரிதை). Read together they give the full nesting of the four paths within jnana.

1437 makes the attainment of Siddhanta leaving the sects and the formless (சமய நிராகார நீங்கி) and becoming Siva, neither one nor two. The Thiruppugazh song asks to know, without quarrelling with the many sectarians (வெகுவித சமயிகள்), the Lord whose form passes beyond the formless and the formed (அருவுரு ஒழிதரு உருவுடையது பதி). Both put the knowledge of the Lord past both the sects and the doctrine of the formless.

The Kural says the senses must be crushed as part of renouncing; Tirumular says the five, hard to curb, subside once the truth beyond speech is attained. The same subduing is a task in one and a result in the other.
Both cut the bonds of desire by turning to the Lord: the Kural by clinging to the one without clinging, Tirumular by going to Siva's side and crushing ஆசாபாசம்.
The Kural ends the pride of 'I' and 'mine' between a person and his goods; Tirumular ends the speech of 'I' and 'He' between the soul and the Lord. Both close with the 'I' given up.

1438 says pure Saivas go beyond garb (வேடம் கடந்து), without show, crushing desire and bondage. 1673 says that for the gnani even a handsome garb is fitting and the garb he has taken is itself Siva-yoga (தானுற்ற வேடமுந் தற்சிவ யோகமே). 1673 limits 1438: going beyond the garb need not mean shedding it, since for the knower the garb is no longer a bond.

The Kural says neither shaving nor long hair is needed if one gives up what the world condemns (மழித்தலும் நீட்டலும் வேண்டா). 1438 says the pure Saiva goes beyond outward garb (வேடம் கடந்து) and crushes the bonds of desire (ஆசாபாசம் செற்று). Both move the test from the ascetic's marks to what is given up, one in common ethics and one in Saiva doctrine.

1439 makes the path of Siddhanta the stripping of the tattvas, wiping off the bond of the kevala state (கேவல பாசம் துடைத்து), and firmly reaching oneself (தனையுறல்). 2348 sets out the states: the tattvas speak of two, self and He; those in kevala do not think 'I'; and becoming oneself without a self (தான்இன்றித் தானாக) is the purity of the tattva. 2348 says what the 'reaching oneself' at the end of 1439 is.

1440 says souls that reach Hara so that the separate self ceases (அரனை அடைந்து அற்றால்) become pure Siva (சுத்த சிவமாவரே). The Thiruppugazh song asks for its self to be known as Siva's form (சீவன் சிவச்சொருபம் என தேறி) and for the 'I' to cease (நானென்பது அற்று). Both describe the goal as becoming Siva through the end of the separate 'I'.

1441 reports the end of speaking of 'He' and 'I' once the not-two state was granted. 1607 gives a means: seeing self and He as two within oneself and offering the flower called 'self' at His feet (தானென்ற பூவை அவனடி சாத்தினால்), after which saying 'I' and 'He' is not right. 1607 turns 1441's report into an act of worship.
1445 ends the pilgrim's search with the Lord taking the heart as his temple; 1823 builds the whole temple inside: heart as shrine, body as temple, mouth as gate, the soul as linga.
Both make Nandi the giver of the paths: in 1449 he sets the four paths for deluded men, in 1478 he lays down the guru-path so that those on earth may be saved.

1443 names Kalangi, Kanjamalaiyan and Kandhuru as those who examined the root chariyai (காலாங்கி கஞ்சமலையமான் ... கந்துரு). 69 names the same three (கந்துருக் காலாங்கி கஞ்ச மலையனோடு) among the seven of Tirumular's line who received the mantra. The pair shows the disciples of the preface's lineage also cited as authorities for the paths.

1443 calls chariyai the life of pure Saivam on earth (சுத்த சைவத்து உயிரதே). The Thiruppugazh song asks when the poet, leaving the base trade of praise songs for patrons, will live doing chariyai and kiriyai (சரியை கிரியைசெய்து உயிர்வாழ்வேன்). Both make chariyai what one lives by, in Tirumular as doctrine and in Arunagirinathar as a hope.

1444 ranks the pujas: standing as the life of life is jnana-puja, invoking the deity into a form (ஆவாகனம்) is outer puja. 1607 gives an inner puja in the same terms: seeing self and He within and offering the flower called 'self' at His feet (தானென்ற பூவை அவனடி சாத்தினால்). 1607 shows what the inner worship 1444 ranks highest looks like as an act.

2614 says he is not in the temple, not in the garb (கோயிலுள் ளானலன் ... வேடத்துள் ளானலன்), but in the hidden heart of those who gave up longing. 1445 tells one to seek through lands, towns and temples (நற்றிருக் கோயிலும் தேடித் திரிந்து), sing and bow, and then he takes the heart as his temple (நெஞ்சத்துக் கோயிலாய்க் கொள்வனே). 1445 qualifies 2614's denial: the temple is not where he stays, but seeking it is the road to the heart where he does.

1445 tells one to wander searching (தேடித் திரிந்து) through towns and temples and sing (பாடுமின்) 'Siva Peruman'. The Thiruppugazh song asks to stop wandering, singing (பாடிப் பாடி) crores of Tamil garlands and searching (தேடித் தேடி) for the doors of fools. The same searching and singing is the chariyai of the Saiva in one and the poet's begging trade in the other; the object, the Lord or the patron, decides its worth.

1447 names those of jnana who have become Him, the yogis, the kiriyai people who never fail in archana and the chariyai people, and calls them all of the wide earth (நீள்நிலத்தோரே). The Thiruppugazh song says the One is hard to speak of for any who have joined chariyai and kiriyai (சரியை க்ரியையும் புணர்ந்தவர் எவராலும் ஓத அரிய) and is seen by those with ample Siva-jnana. The song supports the reading of 1447 that ranks the four, with only the jnanis reaching beyond.

1448 sets kiriyai, the yogas and jnana-puja beside Siva's form (சிவனுரு) and the formless (அரூபம்), chosen by the worshipper's stage. The Thiruppugazh song asks whether Murugan's form is the sum of Veda, chariyai, yoga, kiriyai and jnana, the form with parts (சகளம்), the support-less, or the formless (நிராகார வடிவேயோ). Both pair the four paths with form and formless, Tirumular as graded worship and Arunagirinathar as an open question about the god's form.
Both make the Lord's feet the only crossing of a sea: the Kural's great sea of births, Tirumular's leaping sea of deeds. Reaching the feet is the condition in both.
Both set one abstention above a mass of offerings: the Kural puts not killing and eating above a thousand fire sacrifices, Tirumular puts giving up flesh above crores of sandal and flowers.
199 threatens meat-eaters with hell; 1452 adds that their worship, however rich, does not reach the Lord's feet.
272 says even burning one's bones as firewood wins nothing without melting in love; in 1456 the devotee melts in love and the Lord shines within the bones.

Tirumanthiram 1451 says that for one who takes the shade of the Pure One's feet as refuge (திருவடி நீழல் சரண்), the surging sea of deeds (தத்தும் வினைக்கடல்) will not reach him. Kural 7 says that only those who reach the feet of the incomparable one (தனக்குவமை இல்லாதான் தாள் சேர்ந்தார்க்கு) can remove the mind's anxiety. Both make reaching the feet the single way out; the Kural names inner care, Tirumular the force of karma.

Tirumanthiram 1454, in dense wordplay on பணி, seems to say that the service humans do (மானுடர் செய்பணி) is service to the Lord (ஈசன் பதிபணி). Tirumanthiram 1857 says plainly that what is given to the 'walking temple' (நடமாடக் கோயில்) reaches the god of the temple of images (படமாடக் கோயில்). If 1454 is read so, 1857 is its clear statement; the link depends on that uncertain reading of 1454.
audit_text_issue: 1454's repeated இது/அது/பணி leaves the grammar unclear.

note: Tirumanthiram 1455 makes chariyai and kiriyai, then yoga, then jnana, a ladder by which the devotee's mind becomes Siva (சித்தம் ... சிவமாகுமே), each step carried by grace. Thiruppugazh 643 asks for the reality that is hard to reach (எட்டரிதாய) for those of chariyai, kiriyai and yoga. On the reading that the song sets those paths aside as unable to reach the goal, it conflicts with 1455's claim that they lead to it; if it only means they fall short on their own, the two agree.
375 tells how Hari and Brahma went to the crown and the foot and could not reach him; 1458 recalls their ages of striving and places him in the crown, perceived only by those who perceive.
audit_text_issue: 1458's ஒருச்சி is likely a corruption of உச்சி

note: The same four grades, samaya, visesha, nirvana and abhisheka, are initiations in 1450 and stages of yoga in 1466.

The Kural says those who learn and know the truth here do not come back; Tirumular says letters, songs and the sixty-four arts do not remove birth, and only the yogic way does. The difference may lie in what each means by learning.

Tirumanthiram 1457 describes the yogi set like a planted post (தறியிருந் தாற்போல்), who does not start whether scratched or struck (சொறியினும் தாக்கினும் துண்ணென்று உணரா). Tirumanthiram 121 says the Siva-yogis, senses and life made one, remain with the body as if dead (உடம்பொடு செத்திட்டிருப்பார்). Both mark the yogi by the body's indifference to what touches it, one in the chapter on yoga, the other in the opening upadesam.

Tirumanthiram 1457 describes the yogi who holds himself still as a post and does not react to scratch or blow. Kural 126 speaks of drawing in the five senses like a tortoise (ஆமைபோல் ஐந்தடக்கல்) as a protection for seven births. The same withdrawal of the senses appears in the Kural as a moral discipline with a reward, and in Tirumular as the posture that makes union (கூடல்) possible.

Tirumanthiram 1459 says that as scent dwells in a flower (பூவினிற் கந்தம்), the fragrance of Siva has blossomed within the soul. Tirumanthiram 2639 lists fragrance in the flower (பூவினுள் நாற்றம்) with jaggery in cane and ghee in milk as the way the Lord is mingled everywhere. The same simile is used for Siva in the soul and for Siva in all things.

Tirumanthiram 1460 calls Nandi the one who mingles in the fragrant flower (கந்த மலரிற் கலக்கின்ற நந்தி), to be seen once the mind clears. Tirumanthiram 304 says the Lord, become love to those who speak of him, abides like the scent in a fragrant flower (வாச மலர்க்கந்தம் மன்னிநின்றானே). Both use the flower's scent for a presence that is there unseen until one perceives it.

Tirumanthiram 1461 says letters, songs and the sixty-four arts (எழுத்தோடு பாடலும் எண்ணெண் கலையும்) do not remove fettered birth. In Thiruppugazh 76 the poet lists his mastery of Sangam songs, kavyas and the sixty-four arts (எணெண்கலை) and asks whether the pride of it will not be removed. Both set the full range of learning and art against what it cannot do; the song shows learning turning into the very bond.
audit_text_issue: 1461's second half is yogic and obscure.

note: Tirumanthiram 1462 repeats that if one acts standing firm in longing (விரும்பி நின்றே செயின்), one becomes a true ascetic, true speech, true tapas, a dweller of heaven. Kural 666 says people gain what they resolved as they resolved it, if they are firm (திண்ணியர் ஆகப் பெறின்). Both put the outcome in the steadiness of the will rather than the act; the Kural says it of worldly aims, Tirumular of the spiritual path.

Tirumanthiram 1464 says kings of just sceptre (ஒத்தசெங் கோலார்) and countless ascetics have fallen (வீழ்ந்தனர்). Naladiyar 21 says even kings under umbrellas on elephants were carried off as dead and no one has been left (எஞ்சினார் இவ்வுலகத்தில்). Both use the fall of kings as proof of impermanence; Tirumular adds ascetics to the fallen and sets against them those who come to the Lord in love.

Tirumanthiram 1465 seems to divide yoga by the four paths, with kiriyai and chariyai found within the yogi's practice. Tirumanthiram 1474 does the same for jnana: the four beginning with jnana are within jnana (ஞானத்தின் ஞானாதி நான்கு). The same scheme, each path containing all four, is applied to yoga and to jnana; 1474 is clear where 1465 is compressed and helps read it.

The Kural asks what gain is greater than aram, which yields distinction and wealth; Tirumular says no path of aram is higher than jnana. They conflict only if the Kural's aram is meant to rank above liberating knowledge; Tirumular keeps aram but places it below jnana.
Both set the cutting off of 'I' and 'mine' at the summit: the Kural says whoever cuts that pride enters a world above the gods', Tirumular makes it jnana within jnana itself.
Both free the one who knows or praises the Lord from both kinds of deed: the Kural's twofold deeds of darkness do not cling to him, Tirumular's knower has passed beyond merit and sin alike.
The same four grades are applied to yoga and to jnana; yoga's summit is siddhi (1466), jnana's is the good guru's feet (1476).

Tirumanthiram 1468 lists sound, reflection, mind, awareness, ego and chitta, and says those who go beyond them gain the true path. Tirumanthiram 2153 says that once the five senses, their objects and the four inner instruments (உண்டன நான்கும்) are understood together, the soul becomes as it was of old. Both make passing through the inner instruments the step to the soul's own state; 2153 sets it in the doctrine of the states (அவத்தை).

Tirumanthiram 1469 says those who can speak of the world in him and the grace that comes through love gain jnana and reach Sivoham (சிவோகம், 'I am Siva'). Tirumanthiram 2403 calls the abiding So'ham (சோகம்) the crowning Siva-yoga of the knowers of the Veda and the meaning of the Siddhanta. 1469 gives the identity formula as the fruit of jnana; 2403 places the same formula at the head of Veda and Agama alike.

Kural 123 says that restraint (அடங்க), recognised as knowledge (அறிவறிந்து), yields distinction. Tirumanthiram 1471 names knowledge, restraint and love (அறிவும் அடக்கமும் அன்பும்) as never parting from the city where the gracious Lord dwells. The Kural joins knowledge and restraint for worldly honour; Tirumular adds love and makes the three together the Lord's dwelling.

Tirumanthiram 1473 seems to rank the jnani and the silent one above those of chariyai and kiriyai (சரியை கிரியையே), the lower class. Thiruppugazh 1157 says the reality is far from those infatuated with chariyai, kiriyai, sacrifice and yoga (சரியை கிரியைமக யோக மோகிகள்). Both set the ritual and yogic paths below the knowing of the goal, though 1473's grammar is too compressed to fix in detail.
Both promise victory over death to those of disciplined practice: the Kural to those who have gained the power of tapas, Tirumular to Siva-yoga siddhas who have put away anger.

Both make clear knowledge of what is the condition of ending birth: the Kural's mind that has examined and known what is real need not think of another birth; Tirumular says those without clarity do not end their births.
audit_text_issue: Kural 357 reads உணரான் in the base text; the commentators' உணரின் is needed for the sense.

note: 2406 says that when the soul's bound nature is removed and its bonds cut, souls cling to their Lord; 1486 calls that removal and joining sanmarga, and adds the melting heart.

Tirumanthiram 1479 lists seeing, worshipping, contemplating, touching and praising the guru and wearing his sandals as the sanmarga that brings release. Tirumanthiram 139 says clarity (தெளிவு) is seeing the guru's form, uttering his name, hearing his words and thinking on his form. The two lists nearly coincide: what 139 calls clarity, 1479 calls the true path.

Tirumanthiram 1480 says those who do not know clarity (தெளிவறியாதார்) do not know Siva, do not become Siva and do not end their births. Tirumanthiram 139 defines clarity as seeing, naming, hearing and thinking on the guru (தெளிவு குருவின் திருமேனி காண்டல்). Read together, the clarity without which there is no release is the guru's presence.

Tirumanthiram 1481 counts being freed by a speech that is silence (மோனமதாம் மொழி) as part of sanmarga. Tirumanthiram 1896 says silence is when both speech and mind are still (வாக்கு மனமும் இரண்டும் மவுனமாம்), and speech alone falling silent is mere muteness. 1896 says what kind of silence 1481's freeing speech must be.

Tirumanthiram 1483 says the means of sanmarga is knowledge and the known, while the means of the lower paths stands for the simple (பின்மார்க்க சாதனம் பேதையர்க்காய் நிற்கும்). Thiruppugazh 643 asks for the reality hard to reach for those of chariyai, kiriyai and yoga. Both rank the lower paths below the knowing that reaches the goal.

Tirumanthiram 1484 says the three lower paths come naturally (பெறவியல்பாம்) to the rare disciples who reach sanmarga. Tirumanthiram 1474 says for the jnani the four paths beginning with jnana are all within jnana. Both say the higher path contains the lower rather than discarding them.

631 says samadhis are not needed for one who goes with the Lord and there is no samadhi once one becomes Him; 1490 praises yoga-samadhi as holding space, light and Shakti. Samadhi is honoured as a means and set below union.

Both arm the mind against the five senses: the Kural's goad of firmness guards them like elephants, Tirumular's sharp sword of the mind cuts them down. The Kural guides the five; Tirumular strikes them.

Tirumanthiram 1489 says that for those without the joining path the fearful Lakshmi will not be in their house (வெருவுந் திருமகள் வீட்டில்லை). Kural 167 says the fair goddess (செய்யவள்), grudging the envious man, shows him to her elder sister. Both use the figure of Lakshmi leaving a house as the mark of failure, the Kural for envy, Tirumular for lacking the yogic path; 1489's reading is uncertain.

Tirumanthiram 274 tells the reader to melt in love (அன்புருக்கி) and seek the First One, and Nandi's love then stands foremost. Tirumanthiram 1494 says that for those whose hearts have ripened (உளங்கனிந்து), he, the ripe fruit, splits open and stands within (பழங்கனிந்து உள்ளே பகுந்துநின்றானே). 1494 turns 274's melting into ripening, and has the Lord ripen in answer.

Both make reaching the Lord's feet the crossing of a sea. The Kural names the great sea of births; Tirumular names only the shore, four times over, and makes it both the shade of the feet and the Lord's command.

The Kural calls a head that does not bow to the Lord's feet as useless as a sense that cannot sense; Tirumular says bowing and serving at Hara's feet is the very fruit of birth. One states the loss, the other the gain.
Both make the Lord answer worship itself: 1500 says he comes forth each time one worships, 1505 that he stands held by the great love of those who make him their eye.

Tirumanthiram 252 says anyone can give a green leaf to God, grass to a cow, a handful of food and a kind word. Tirumanthiram 1497 says that though people see the bee and the swan gathering flowers, they do not join even a small path of virtue (சிறுகால் அறநெறி சேர்கிலாரே). 252 says what the small path is and that it is open to all; 1497 says that even so people do not take it.
1496 counts worship and recitation as the faultless good son's path; 1506 says the same acts, done by a mind like a stone in moss, do not know the Lord. The acts are necessary, not sufficient.

Both set the quarrel of 'this one or that one is supreme' against seeking the Lord himself: here by the ordained way of service, in 1545 by leaving the delusion of those who praise one sect over another.

Tirumanthiram 1502 counts lighting lamps, gathering flowers, smearing and sweeping the floor and bathing the image as the servant's path. In Tirumanthiram 1640 the speaker touched leaves and plucked flowers 'for my father' (எந்தைக்கென்று) but did not see the water that comes, until scripture turned him to tapas. 1640 limits the flower-gathering 1502 prescribes: as a stage it is the path, taken as the end it misses what it serves.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 1502: 'தீப miடல்' contains stray Latin letters.

note: Tirumanthiram 1504 says the speaker worships at the twilights (அந்திப்பன்) and thinks always on the Lord's anklet, so all worship is completed in order. Tirumanthiram 958 mocks those who perform the twilight rites (சந்திசெய்யா நிற்பர்) without knowing the mantra rising within and go off making noise. The rite 1504 practises is the one 958 says is empty without inner knowing; 1504's 'always thinking' (சிந்திப்பன் என்றும்) supplies that condition.

Tirumanthiram 1506 says that though people recite, worship and gather flowers, their mind is a stone fallen in a mossy pond (பாசிக் குளத்தில்வீழ் கல்), not knowing the love for the stainless light. Kural 278 says many bathe with impurity in their minds (மனத்தது மாசாக) and go about concealed. Both set outward observance against an untouched mind; Tirumular's stone sinks under the surface it disturbs.
725 finds that the Highest has made the body his temple; 1508 makes the worshipper's own mind the temple in kiriyai. Both move the shrine inside the person.

Tirumanthiram 1508 says that in kiriyai one's own mind is the temple (தன்மனங் கோயில்). Tirumanthiram 1823 says that for the Lord the heart is the great temple (உள்ளம் பெருங்கோயில்) and the body the shrine. The same claim stands in the stages of initiation and in the chapter on Siva-puja.
1507 matches the states of release to the paths; 1509 ranks the same states by what happens to the bond in each, ending in its dissolving.
audit_text_issue: 1509's சிரமானது and 1507's பாலோகம் இல்லா are doubtful readings

note: Both make lesser things gain worth by nearness: in the Naladiyar the hare is worshipped with the moon, and the slight gain worth through friends steady as a hill; in Tirumular all that nears the golden mountain turns its colour, and the disciple takes the Lord's form.

1518 repeats 1514's line, 'removing blindness and showing many good qualities', but with the Lord as the doer where 1514 had the old woman, and adds that he cut away deeds and gave knowledge. It unlocks part of the riddle: the woman's act is the Lord's.

Both use the lamp entering a dark room. The Naladiyar makes it austerity before which sin cannot stand, and warns the dark returns when the oil runs out; Tirumular makes it the Lord and the Mother entering delusion, with no warning that the light fails.

Both treat good and bad deeds alike as what must be overcome, not good deeds as a ladder. The Kural says the two dark deeds do not cling to those who praise the Lord truly; Tirumular says grace descends when the two stand in balance.

1516 says the First removes darkness, carries one past countless births and joins one to the வானவர் கோன்; 1552 says the வானவர் கோன் keeps the penitent from suffering and grants that there is no birth (பிறப்பில்லை). In 1552 the title plainly names the Lord who ends birth, which supports reading the awkward வானவர் கோன் of 1516 the same way rather than as Indra.

1517 compares the coming of the Lord and the Mother into delusion to a lamp brought into a dark room; 1793 says Nandi, far off to those who would touch him, ends the darkness like the light of a lamp (விளக்கொளி) when the heart lies gathered in longing. The pair shows the lamp-in-darkness figure used for grace both as a descent from outside (புக்கெரிந்தாற் போல்) and as what the longing heart receives.
