1805 says maya, the instruments (கரணம்), the five elements and the senses are all அருள் ஐந்துமாம் அருட்செய்கை, the fivefold work of grace. 2211 says the Lord fashioned the bonds, the thirty-six tattvas and set the instruments (கருவியும் வைத்தனன்) so that the malas may be cut. Both treat the whole bodily apparatus as given by the Lord for the soul's release.

1737 says Shakti and Siva fill all that is fixed and all that moves (தாபர சங்கமம்) and are the earth and the cosmos. 1806 says the same of grace: அருளே சகலமும் ஆய பவுதிகம், grace is all the elemental world, and அருளே சராசரம், grace is the moving and unmoving. Put together, they show the Shakti of 1737 renamed as grace in 1806.

Kural 393 says only the learned have eyes (கண்ணுடையர்); the unlearned have two sores on their face. 1808 says only those with அருட்கண் (the eye of grace) see Hara, as the dark-eyed (இருட்கண்ணினோர்) cannot see even the sun. Both say having eyes is not the same as seeing: in the Kural the missing eye is learning, in Tirumular it is grace.

1810 sorts the Lord's forms into formless, அருவுரு (Sadasiva) and form, and says the Lord is all of them and yet one. Thiruppugazh 1247 seeks a Lord whose form is அருவுரு ஒழிதரு, past both form and the formless, and beyond talk of அவன் இவள் அது. On the reading that 1810 makes the Lord these nine forms, 1247 adds the condition that he is not exhausted by them; 1810's last words (துலையா இறை ... ஒன்றே) leave room for this.

1811 says the Lord stands உயிர்க்குயிராய், as the life of life, both one with the soul and other than it. 2504 opens உயிர்க்குயிராகி ஒழிவற்று அழிவற்று and adds that without him anava does not leave. Both name the Lord the life of life; 2504 draws from it the soul's dependence for release.

1812 has the Spotless one with Shakti reach குடிலை and நாதம், join to become many கலை, and ripen as விந்து. 964 has நாதம் rise spiralling from விந்து and the mistress of bonds become sixteen கலை and the fifty-one letters. Both trace the same chain of bindu, nada and kala, in opposite directions.

The Kural asks what learning has achieved if it does not bow at the feet of the one of pure knowledge, so bowing is learning's fruit. Tirumular bows by leaving what he learned (கற்றன விட்டேன்): the feet are reached by setting learning down.
Both set a true lamp above ordinary lamps. For the Kural it is truthfulness; for Tirumular it is the lamp that lights the lamp, and its bearer becomes the lamp.

Tirumanthiram 1814 says those who do not stand in grace (அருளில் தலைநில்லார்) do not leave the five bonds, and ends 'born in grace, they know by knowing' (அருளில் பிறந்திட்டு அறிந்துஅறிவாரே). 1800 traces the whole life in grace, born, grown and vanishing in it (அருளில் பிறந்திட்டு அருளில் வளர்ந்திட்டு), until Nandi enters the heart. The shared phrase shows 1814 turning 1800's testimony into a rule: the birth in grace that 1800 narrates is what makes knowing possible.

Tirumanthiram 1815 says great Nandi gave the way of no return (வாரா வழிதந்த மாநந்தி) and bade the poet bathe in the sea of grace. Kural 356 says those who have learned here and seen the true thing reach the path of not coming back (மற்றீண்டு வாரா நெறி). Both name release by the same phrase; the Kural reaches it by learning and seeing, the Tirumanthiram receives it as a gift of the guru.

Tirumanthiram 1816 says the poet found Siva by weeping and crying out (அழுதும் அரற்றியும்) and seeking, and the Lord stood within him. 43 says that for those who name Hara's feet, crying and weeping (அரற்றி அழுது) and seeking the Supreme's feet daily, he fills them. Both make tearful seeking the way in; 1816 is the poet's own report of what 43 states as a rule.

Tirumanthiram 1817 says the poet, bowing to Nandi as father, left what he had learned (கற்றன விட்டேன்) and bowed at the anklet. 290, in the chapter on learning, says that once the Lord entered his heart he learned a learning that surpasses (மிகுங் கல்வி கற்றேனே). The pair limits each: what is put down in 1817 is learning that stops short of the feet, while 290 names the learning that comes after the Lord enters.

Kural 352 says that for those of stainless sight who have left confusion (மருள்நீங்கி), darkness leaves and joy comes (இருள்நீங்கி இன்பம் பயக்கும்). Tirumanthiram 1819 says light and darkness never end once and for all, and only when both light and darkness go (ஒளியிருள் நீங்க) does the soul become Siva. The Tirumanthiram limits the Kural's picture: release is not light winning over darkness but passing beyond the pair.

Tirumanthiram 1820 says the Lord crowned the poet, who wandered outside, with his golden anklets (பொற்கழல் சூட்டி) and made him spotless. Thiruppugazh 202 asks that one day Murugan set his lotus feet as a crown on this dog-like servant's head (வாரிஜபதங்கள் நாயடியேன் முடிபுனைந்து) and rule him with teaching. The feet worn on the head are the same mark of initiation; in Tirumular it is done and leaves him dazed, in Arunagiri it is still asked for.

Kural 351 says a joyless birth comes from the confusion (மருள்) that takes what is not the real thing (பொருளல்லவற்றை) for the real. Tirumanthiram 1821 names one refuge called the real thing (பொருளது என்ற புகலிடம்) and says that when the one who entered the mind to remove confusion (மருளது நீங்க) is grasped with clarity, the way to Siva follows. The Kural diagnoses the confusion; the Tirumanthiram names who removes it and where it leads.
725 tells how Tirumular once thought the body a flaw, then found the Highest had made it his temple and so guards it; 1823 maps the temple onto the body part by part.

The Naladiyar calls the body a pot seeping filth from nine openings, dressed in skin that fools the eye; Tirumular makes the same flesh body (ஊனுடம்பு) the Lord's shrine and the mouth its gate. The conflict holds if the Naladiyar is read as judging the body's worth itself, not only rebuking lust.

The Kural says water gives outer purity and truth inner purity. Tirumular makes truthful speech and thought the condition without which the Lord is not seen, and only then counts flowers and water as praise.
Both say worship needs almost nothing: 252 offers the Lord one green leaf, open to anyone; 1828 says flowers and water are always there, so those who fail to approach are evading.

Both redirect offering from the Lord's image to his living devotees: 1857 says what is given to the walking temple reaches the Lord, 1829 that the water washing a jnani's feet is the Lord's bath in the nine holy waters.
Both make the sea of births what drowns those who do not turn to the Lord: the Kural's who do not reach his feet cannot swim it, Tirumular's who do not worship sink (அழுந்துகின்றார்) in it.
The Kural says a spotless mind is the whole of virtue and the rest is noisy show; Tirumular says daily adorning and praise do not bring knowledge of the Lord until the inner stain is gone.

Kural 259 says not killing one creature to eat is better than pouring oblations in a thousand sacrifices (அவிசொரிந் தாயிரம் வேட்டலின்). Tirumanthiram 1824, playing on அவி, says we have nothing to show Nandi who eats the sacrificial oblation (வேட்டவி) and offer instead the song that cools the heart (பாட்டவி). Both take the word of the fire offering and put something else in its place, abstention in the Kural and sung praise in Tirumular.

Tirumanthiram 1825 describes the outer rite: invoking Sadasiva into the image (ஆவாகித்து), taking the upper face as Isana, until he becomes Siva. 1842 says people do not know the mantra by which to call (கூவி), contemplate and lead Nandi, who roams beyond the lotus of the breath, and establish him in Siva. 1842 carries the same steps of invocation and installation inside the body, where 1825 does them on the image.

Tirumanthiram 1827 says the Lord stays fixed in the hearts of the gods because they worshipped with the five nectars, the many services and joined palms (அஞ்சலியோடும் கலந்து அர்ச்சித்தார்). 1837 says that those who strew flowers and praise his red feet do not, for all their praise, come to know him (யாரும் துதித்து உணராரே). Set together, 1837 limits 1827: worship can bring the Lord into the heart and still not bring knowing of him.

Tirumanthiram 1829 says that washing clean and sprinkling the feet of those high in true knowledge is release, and 1866 that drinking the remnant of the true devotees' meal is release; both close with the same formula, முத்தியாம் என்று நம்மூலன் மொழிந்ததே. Across two chapters the same authority is set on the same claim: what touches the realised person's body, water at the feet or food left over, carries release.

Tirumanthiram 1830 prays that, though the poet stays forgetful on this path (மறப்புற்று), he may worship without forgetting (மறப்பின்றி). Kural 537 says nothing is too hard if done with the tool of unforgetting care (பொச்சாவாக் கருவியால்). The Kural makes not forgetting the instrument of any achievement; the Tirumanthiram asks for it in worship as a gift, admitting he cannot keep it by himself.

Tirumanthiram 1815 says the Lord of a thousand names (பேராயிரமுடைப் பெம்மான்) spoke in a single name and bade the poet bathe in the insatiable sea of grace (ஆரா அருட்கடல்). 1831 says the thousand names and the Lord's holy name are a way that never sates (பேராயிரமும் பிரான் திருநாமமும் ஆரா வழி). Both pair the thousand names with the one name and the word ஆரா, so the name in each is something one does not come to the end of.

Tirumanthiram 1505 says the gods call the Lord by a thousand names (ஆயிரம் பேர்சொல்லி) and worship his feet within, and he stands held by their love. 1831 places the gods' hosts, the worship and the thousand names (பேராயிரமும்) all within the Lord as his own. Both treat the thousand names as the gods' worship; 1831 adds that the names and the worship themselves belong to him.

Tirumanthiram 1814 says those who do not stand in grace do not leave the five bonds (ஐம்பாசம் நீங்கார்). 1833 says the gods praise with flowers and water while their thick bonds (தழைக்கொண்ட பாசம்) still waver on them, and the Lord's grace comes without fail. 1833 limits 1814's order: grace does not wait for the bonds to go, it answers worship while they are still there.

Kural 2 asks what fruit (பயன்) learning has if one does not bow at the good feet of the pure knower. Tirumanthiram 1836 says there is one knowledge of the fruit (பயனறிவு ஒன்றுண்டு): to those who strew flowers knowing the fruit, Hara keeps near so that they reach the three-eyed one's feet. The Kural makes reaching the feet the fruit of knowing; Tirumular makes knowing the fruit what turns flower-worship toward the feet.

Tirumanthiram 601 says that not once do people contemplate Siva within the life or the mind where Siva dwells (ஒருபொழு துன்னார் உயிருட் சிவனை). 1843 says no one knows the worth of the ruby sunk within the body (ஆகத்துள்ளே அழுந்திய மாணிக்கம்) until they see it, and to those who think of him again and again he enters the mind. Both make the Lord within the body unknown for lack of thinking on him; 1843 adds what follows when one does.

Tirumanthiram 1845 is a near-repeat of 1450: both list samaya as purification in which one's own action ceases (தன்செயல் அற்றிடும்), vishesha as mantra-purification, nirvana as kala-purification and abhisheka as the last grade. They differ slightly: 1450 calls the mantra Hara's and ends on the path of settled jnana (ஞானமார்க்கம்), while 1845 places abhisheka for those who have become knowledge in the hall (மன்று ஞானம் ஆனார்க்கு). The same scheme appears in the chapter on chariyai and again in the chapter on worship.
audit_text_issue: 1450 பலசுத்தி vs 1845 மலசுத்தி, அரன் vs ஆன, look like variants.

note: Tirumanthiram 88 tells how Brahma and Vishnu sought the Lord's foot and crown (அடிமுடி காண்பார் அயன்மால் இருவர்) and did not see him, and Brahma lied. 1846 says he lets no soul in its fate know him except those who have perceived him age after age, and stands beyond the ages and beyond Hari and Ayan at the one summit (ஓர்உச்சியுளானே). 1846 turns 88's story into a doctrine: the summit the two gods missed is reached only by long perceiving.
1852 says worship belongs where moon and sun do not shine; 1853 says what moon and sun become there, bindu and nada, and where the worship is done.
1855 says the Lord takes the worship not done by day and night; 1856 speaks from that place, where night and day are not and the worship is drinking bliss.

Tirumanthiram 1848 says that however much sandal and flowers one offers, she is reached only by those who put away the flesh and perceive (ஊனினை நீக்கி உணர்பவர்க்கு அல்லது). 724 says that if the body perishes the life perishes and true knowledge cannot be attained, so the poet nurtured the body (உடம்பை வளர்த்தேன்). The conflict holds only if ஊனினை நீக்கி is read as leaving the body; on the usual reading, giving up identification with it, the two can stand together.

Tirumanthiram 1845 says that at the first initiation one's own acting ceases (தன்செயல் அற்றிடும்). 1849 redefines worship as standing in knowledge and ends that reaching the red feet is the ceasing of acts (சேவடி சேரல் செயலறல் தானே). The ceasing that 1845 places at the first stage of initiation, 1849 makes the goal of inner worship itself.

Tirumanthiram 1850 bids one long for the Lord at noon, morning and evening and sow his name with 'nama' (நமவென்று நாமத்தை விச்சுமின்). 993 says the gods, showering flowers, draw near and saying 'nama' with the name (நமஎன்று நாமத்தை) stand merged with it. Both make the name joined to நம the act of worship; 1850 gives it as daily practice for people, 993 as what the gods do.

Tirumanthiram 1852 says worship in the place where moon and sun shine goes to the asuras, and worship where moon and sun do not shine (இந்துவும் பானுவும் இலங்காத் தலம்) is Nandi's great worship. 1989 says to worship when moon and sun come together (சந்திரன் சூரியன் தான்வரின் பூசனை), and those clear in the place of the two become Siva. On the yogic reading both place true worship where the two breaths cease to run apart; on a plain reading they would conflict.

Tirumanthiram 1854 describes the solitary worship of Sadasiva: turning mind and breath back at the root, making the body into its elements and setting it aside (உடல்பூதமாக்கி அகற்றி), and entering grace. 597 defines dharana as placing the dissolved body in the five elements (அரித்த உடலைஐம் பூதத்தில் வைத்து) and those in the subtle ones, held with the Supreme. The same dissolving of the body into the elements is yoga in 597 and worship in 1854.
1823 makes the body a temple and the soul a Siva-linga; 1857 draws the consequence for giving: the devotee is a walking temple, and what he receives reaches the god of the built one.
Both rank feeding a jnani above the great religious gifts; 1851 by multiples of merit, 1860 against a thousand villages and a thousand temple towers.
Both set one simple act above a thousand great rites: the Kural puts not killing and eating above a thousand sacrifices, Tirumular puts one meal for a jnani above a thousand gifts to Brahmins.
The Kural sees householders as those who provide for renunciants, perhaps at the cost of their own austerity; Tirumular makes that provision the highest merit, above feeding Brahmins.
1858 says what the ascetic eats the three worlds eat; 1866 says the three gods eat it, and adds that his leavings give release.

Tirumanthiram 1829 says the Lord bathes in the nine holy waters when one washes the feet of those high in true knowledge. 1859 says a gift made to the realised one (ஆத்தனுக்கு ஈந்த) becomes holy water (தீர்த்தமதாம்) for the three gods and the forebears. Both move the sacred waters from the river to the service of the realised person, by washing in 1829 and by giving in 1859.

Tirumanthiram 1857 says what is given to the walking temple (நடமாடக் கோயில்), the devotee, reaches the god of the built temple. 1862 calls the ash-wearing devotees gods walking on earth (நிகழ் தேவர்கள்) and says those who honour them as the Lord himself have no karma. Both see the Lord in the living devotee; 1857 states where offerings go, 1862 what honouring the devotee earns.

Tirumanthiram 2626 says no one can speak of the Lord unless they come to share in the devotion of his devotees (பத்தர்தம் பத்தியிற் பாற்படில் அல்லது). 1864 says that by worshipping Hara's devotees (அரன் அடியாரைத் தொழுகை) the world's thick darkness leaves, and rising after worship there is joy. 1864 extends 2626's claim from knowing the Lord to the whole world's darkness and the worshipper's joy.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 1864: stray Latin 'f' in தூfங்கிருள். Tirumanthiram 2626: ற்த்தன் is garbled (அத்தன்).

note: Kural 278 says many go about concealed, bathing as if great while their minds are defiled (மனத்தது மாசாக). Tirumanthiram 1865 says those who worship without the fitting disposition, matching only in outward face (முகமத்தோடு ஒத்து), stay deluded within (அகமத்தர்) age after age. Both set a correct outward rite against an inner state that does not match it; the Kural names the defiled mind, Tirumular the frenzy that passes for devotion.

Kural 263 asks whether others have forgotten tapas in order to provide for those who have renounced (துறந்தார்க்குத் துப்புரவு வேண்டி). Tirumanthiram 1867 says that charity done to those who never fall still and strive at rare austerity (அருந்தவம்) removes deep karma and becomes the golden world. The Kural observes that householders serve renunciants in place of their own tapas; Tirumular names what that service gains them.
Both say the land where a devotee lives is blessed: 1868 with peace and rain, 1882 with true knowers and good order, and release from births.
The Kural makes giving and austerity depend on rain; Tirumular runs it the other way, making rain depend on the presence of one who seeks the Lord.
audit_text_issue: 1868's ஒரு வாது இருக்கில் is probably a corruption of ஒருவன் இருக்கில்

note: Both speak of Tirumular as bound and sent by the Lord: 1863 as Nandi's message, 1876 by a deed of servitude written before birth.

1868 says that where one person seeks the Lord in the fitting way, 'பார்மழை பெய்யும்', rain falls and the land lacks nothing. Kural 55 says the wife who worships her husband commands the rain: 'பெய்யெனப் பெய்யும் மழை'. Both make one person's devotion, to the Lord in one case and to the husband in the other, the cause of rain for everyone.

1869 insists the devotee attains Hara's feet and grace 'அவ்வுடலோடும்', in the very body he was born with, in this same world. 724 gives the reason that body must be kept: 'உடம்பார் அழியில் உயிரார் அழிவர்', without the body true knowledge cannot be won, so 'உடம்பை வளர்த்தேன் உயிர்வளர்த்தேனே'. 724 supplies the method behind 1869's claim.

1871 says the seven worlds, all beings, the Veda, the five acts and Siva himself are not apart from 'என் கண்', the knower's eye. 1909 says of the Siva-jnani that Siva is 'எங்கும்' for him and that, dying here, he stands everywhere. 1871 puts everything within the knower's sight; 1909 carries the knower out into everything.

1872 says the light within is 'பெண்ணல்ல ஆணல்ல பேடல்ல', neither woman, man nor neuter, and cannot be known. 434 praises the First 'ஆண்பெண் அலியுரு வாய்நின்ற', standing in the form of male, female and neuter. On a literal reading one denies him all three forms and the other gives him all three; the conflict eases if 434 means immanence and 1872 transcendence.

3004 gives the Lord a cosmic body: the world-eggs are his crown and his red feet reach 'பாதாளம்', the underworld. 1873 gives this same body to the devotees: their arms are the eight directions, their feet the 'பாதாள', their crown the 'பகிரண்டம்'. The pairing shows the chapter on the devotee's greatness transferring the Lord's own cosmic image to his servants.

1874 tells us to contemplate the Lord who dwells in 'அகம்படி', the inner chamber, and says those who enter it escape grief. 2605 places Nandi 'மெய்த்தாள் அகம்படி', in the inner apartment behind a bolt no hand can open until falsehood is put away. Both use the palace's inner quarters for the Lord's place in the heart; 2605 adds what bars the way in.

1875 says the first Lord 'என் ஆவி உழவுகொண்டானே', has taken my soul to plough, so praise and blame fall away. 1886 says the field is fenced and 'உச்சிக்கு முன்னே உழவு சமைந்தது', the ploughing is done before noon, yet the fearful will not reap and eat and go begging instead. Read together, the Lord does the ploughing and the soul is left only to harvest.

1876 says a deed of bondage (ஆவணம்) to Siva was written for my mother, father and seven times seven births, with Brahma writing and Vishnu witnessing. Thiruppugazh 403 retells Siva coming as an old man to a youth's wedding, claiming him 'இவன் அடிமை' and producing 'பழைய ... ஆவணத்தை', the old deed the youth tore. Both rest on the image of hereditary servitude to Siva fixed by a written deed.

1879 calls it true servitude to recognise Hara's devotees 'குறியால்', by their signs, and delight in them. 1660 warns that 'பொய்வேடம் மெய்வேடம் போலவே பூணினும்', the false garb is worn just like the true, and the garb saves only those who know. 1660 limits 1879: the outward sign does not by itself mark a true devotee.

1880 says those who approach 'அவன்', the devotee, with love can approach Siva too. 2624 says the poet became servant of the servants of his servants, and 'அடியார் அருளால் அவனடி கூட', it was by the devotees' grace that he reached the Lord's feet. Both route the way to Siva through his devotees.

1880 says approaching the devotee with love is the way to approach Siva. Thiruppugazh 484, sunk in the sea of desire, asks for one remedy: 'உனது அடியாராகிய மோன ஞானிகளுடனே சேரவும் அருள்வாயே', grace to join the Lord's silent devotees. The song turns 1880's teaching into a prayer.
Both place the Lord in the devotee: 1857 tells the giver that food for the walking temple reaches the god, 1885 tells the devotee that he begs and eats for the Lord in the temple within.

1884 says people in all eight directions welcome the Lord's devotees with prepared food, calling it nectar. Kural 263 asks whether the others have forgotten tapas 'துறந்தார்க்குத் துப்புரவு வேண்டி', in wanting to provide for renouncers. Both describe the householder's role as feeding those who have renounced; the Kural adds a note of irony that the Tirumanthiram lacks.

Both put the world's creator beside begging. The Kural says that if the maker of the world decreed that people live by begging he should wander and perish; Tirumular says the maker of the seven worlds begged himself so that his devotees could reach him by begging. The conflict holds if the Kural is read as condemning all living by alms, not only the beggary of the poor.

Both fault begging that comes from desire when the remedy lies within: the Naladiyar asks why one should beg of strangers when poverty can be ended by asking of oneself, Tirumular faults those who beg for their desires instead of reaping the field already ploughed.
The Kural says pain ends when desire, anger and confusion are gone; Tirumular says hunger, craving and anger do not stay in Siva's devotees, and adds that they pass beyond the heavens too.
audit_text_issue: kural:360: இநவ்முன்றன் is corrupt; read இவ்மூன்றன்.

note: Both use வர இருந்தான் (waiting so as to come or be come to): in 1889 the Lord waits on the way, in 1891 the ascetic waits and the world comes to him.

1886 says those who cannot reap what is ready 'இச்சைக்குப் பிச்சை இரக்கின்ற', beg alms for their desires. 1626 says those who beg many things 'பிறப்பறியார்' get the wealth they want, while those who do tapas end birth. Both separate begging for desire from the begging of the path, and both rank it lower.

1886 pictures a fenced field (வேலிச்செய்) already ploughed that the fearful will not reap. 2871 pictures fields high and low and says 'உள்ளச்செய் அங்கே உழவுசெய்வார்கட்கு', for those who plough the heart's field, it grows into a flooded field of itself. Both turn the farm into inner practice; 2871 shows the harvest that 1886's beggars refuse.

1887 says Siva took alms 'பிரமன் தலைதன்னில்', in Brahma's skull, and did so for the sake of dharma. 371 says he rose 'எலும்புங் கபாலமும் ஏந்தி', bearing bones and skull, and that without his bearing them they would turn to dust. Both read the skull Siva carries as an act that serves others, not as a mark of shame.
1893 names shambhavi and khechari among the mudras; 1894 says what each one is: the Lord's glance, and the truth that rises with Om.
Both put the mudra of silence highest: 1895 calls it release beyond release, 1900 the seal of the liberated.
The Kural says whatever else one fails to guard, one should guard the tongue; Tirumular says guarding the tongue alone only makes one mute, and silence is true only when the mind is still too.
audit_text_issue: Line 4 has the typo சுத்த்ததை for சுத்தத்தை.

note: 1892 says the mudra is fixed 'மோன மொழியில்', in the speech of silence, and leads to release at Nandi's feet. Thiruppugazh 1112 asks to pass beyond the tattvas and the six centres and reach 'முத்திரையா மோனம்', silence that is the seal. Both name the final seal as silence, and the song draws on the Tirumanthiram's own terms.
audit_text_issue: Thiruppugazh 1112 line 5 has a corrupt word (likely வாரிச).

note: 1893 says that when 'சாம்பவி கேசரி' join, the mudras give growing knowledge. 642, in the chapter on the eight siddhis, says with shambhavi and khechari joined 'பெரிய சிவகதி', the great Siva-state, is the gain. The same pair of seals leads to knowledge in one verse and to the siddhis and Siva's state in the other.

1897 says 'யோகத்தின் முத்திரை ஓர் அட்ட சித்தியாம்', the mudra of yoga is the eight siddhis. 1904 says siddhis come to one who is 'ஊனத்தோர்', still lacking, before he becomes a full Siva-yogi. 1904 places the powers that 1897 calls yoga's seal below the goal.

1899 says that considering 'வேதாந்த சித்தாந்தத் தன்மை' together with the Agamas is 'நற்சுத்த சைவம்'. 1422, in the chapter on pure Saivam, says those who have seen 'வேதாந்தம் சுத்தம் விளங்கிய சித்தாந்தம்' have unwavering sight. Both define pure Saivam by holding Vedanta and Siddhanta together, not against each other.

1900 ranks 'மோனத்து முத்திரை', the seal of silence, as the seal of the liberated and puts the displayed seal with 'கண்ட சமயம்', outward religion. Thiruppugazh 394 seeks 'மோன முத்திரை', the seal of silence, which 'கோலாகலச் சமய' sinners, the noisy sects, cannot know. Both set the inner seal of silence against sectarian display.
audit_text_issue: 394: garbled word in first line (தொழுத்மு டூடு).

note: The Siva-yogi of 1905 goes to a higher world and comes back; the faultless jnani of 1906 does not return. Together they rank the yogi below the jnani in what death brings.

Both make release a matter of not coming back: the Kural's மற்றீண்டு வாரா நெறி and Tirumular's மீளார். Tirumular adds the setting of a silent samadhi at death; the Kural says only that seeing the true thing here leads there.

1902 traces the yogi who dies in the waxing fortnight through the sun, the fathers' station and the moon. 1906 says the faultless jnani-yogi 'பரகாயம் சாராதே ... மீளார்', takes no other body and does not return. 1906 limits the celestial journeys of 1902 to those short of the jnani's state, which ends without any further station.

1903 says a yogi who dies before completing samadhi goes to a world of refuge and returns to take up unbroken yoga again. Kural 398 says learning gained in one birth 'எழுமையும் ஏமாப்புடைத்து', protects for seven. Both teach that inner gains outlast one life, the Kural for learning and the Tirumanthiram for yoga.
audit_text_issue: 1903 line 1 is corrupt (சமாதிaக கூடாது); 'without reaching samadhi' is a reconstruction.

note: 1904 says that before a yogi becomes a full Siva-yogi, siddhis come to him while he is still 'ஊனத்தோர்', lacking. 2619 separates 'ஒண்சித்தி முத்தியாம்', the bright attainment that is release, from the eight siddhis won by ending desire. Both rank the powers below release.

1909 says that for the Siva-jnani 'எங்கும் சிவமாய்', Siva is everywhere and the Supreme is present everywhere. 2722 says 'எங்கும் சிவமாய் இருத்தலால்', because Siva is everywhere, Chidambaram and the dance are everywhere too. They share the phrase; 2722 frees the sacred place, and 1909 frees the knower.

Both speak of what is done with a corpse once its life has left. The Naladiyar asks what it matters whether it is dragged off, buried or thrown anywhere; Tirumular says that burning or exposing a jnani's body ruins the land. The conflict holds if the Naladiyar's indifference covers every body; if it speaks only of ordinary people, Tirumular's exception for the jnani escapes it.

Both tie the failure of rain to a wrong: in the Kural a king's crooked rule, in Tirumular the burning of a jnani's body. The same belief that the sky answers moral or sacred offence is applied to kingship and to the rites of the dead.
1823 makes the body of flesh a temple of the Lord; 1911 draws the consequence for the jnani's corpse: to burn it is to set fire to the Lord's temple.

1868 says that where one seeker of the Lord lives 'பார்மழை பெய்யும்', rain falls and the land has no want. 1911 gives the reverse: if fire touches the jnani's body 'மண்ணில் மழைவிழா', rain fails, famine comes and kings lose their kingdoms. Together they make the holy one's presence, living and dead, the condition of rain and of the land's welfare.

1912 says burying the jnani 'புண்ணியமாம்', is merit, while heaping fire on him ruins the land and letting him decay in the open disgraces him. Naladiyar 26 says that once the dancer has left the skin bag it does not matter whether the body is dragged off, 'நன்றாய்ந்து அடக்கிலென்', carefully buried, or thrown away. One makes the disposal of the body decisive and the other declares it meaningless.

1882 says the land where a 'சிவயோகி ஞானி' dwells gains knowers and good order and becomes the higher world. 1913 says that if the jnani's body is kept in a cave-tomb, kings and all who live on the earth 'அந்தமில் இன்ப அருள்பெறுவாரே'. 1913 extends 1882's blessing of place from the living sage to his tomb.

1911 says fire touching the jnani's body is 'அண்ணல்தம் கோயில் அழல்இட்டது', like setting the Lord's own temple ablaze. 1922 ends the burial rite by installing a Siva linga over the tomb and performing 'சோடசம் ... உபசாரம்', the sixteen services of temple worship. The rite makes literal what 1911 put as a simile: the jnani's body is a temple.

The chapter's two bindus: the cosmic one from which kundalini, gods and speech unfold (1923), and the drop distilled from food in the body (1934). Tirumular gives both the same name and the same generative role.
audit_text_issue: 1923's last line (கலைவை கரியே) is compressed or corrupt

note: 1931 says the Lord is in the seed unperceived; 1932 states the logic: no sprout apart from its seed, and seed and sprout only together.

Both use dew on a grass blade. The Naladiyar makes it the body's brief life and urges good deeds now; Tirumular makes it the rare drop of bindu from which the body's strength grows, something to be kept rather than a reminder of loss.
724 says that if the body perishes the life perishes, and that Tirumular learned how to nourish the body; 1936 names one way it perishes, the unguarded loss of bindu.

Both start from the perishing body. The Naladiyar's wise see it as a bubble and resolve to end their births; Tirumular faults people for not guarding what keeps the body. The facts agree, the response differs.

1928 says bindu, the seed, spreads out both அகண்டமும் அண்டமும் and, once the bodily elements arise, is அகம் புறம் (inside and outside). 466 makes the same body-cosmos match for birth and death: the senses arise and die in the பிண்டம், the soul likewise in the அண்டம். Both read the body and the cosmos as one pattern, 1928 for bindu, 466 for life and death.

1929 gives bindu the colour வெண்மை and nada செம்மை, joined with Shakti and Siva and granting release. 2802 describes the guru Nandi's body in the hall as தீயுறு செம்மை வெளுப்பொடும் (fire-red with white) and calls it a refuge. The red-and-white pair recurs; 1929 supplies the key (nada and bindu) that 2802 leaves unstated.

1935 says the bindu that becomes mind is not lost (நீங்கா) to those who stand steady, while those who follow maya perish with their mind. 877 says that for the yogi bindu does not go out by its way anywhere (போம்வழி எங்கணும் போகாது), bound at the root through freedom from desire. Both make keeping bindu a matter of the mind's steadiness and desirelessness, not of the body alone.
1936 laments that people do not know how bindu is lost or how to guard it; 1948 lists what stays when it is kept: breath, strength, intellect, tapas, japa, silence and siddhi.

Both give the same sequence: kindle the fire at the root, raise it through the sealed central way, and drink the nectar. 1949 calls those who do it Siva-yogis; 1962 calls it bindu's victory by Shakti.
1946 says there is no harvest except for the sower; 1964 turns this into a riddle of three men who pound, roast or sow the seed, and only the sower is apart.
1933 traces food into body and mind, and 1934 into bindu; 1966 names the bindu of food and the bindu of breath and makes knowing both the way to the golden body.
1923 makes cosmic bindu the source of powers, gods and speech; 1969 makes bindu and nada the source of all lives and mantras, and then turns to the bodily bindu whose containment brings Sivoham.
Both see woman as கூற்று, Death. In the Kural the lover discovers it, struck by her eyes; Tirumular makes it a deliberate meditation that ends desire and with it death.

The Naladiyar quells desire by taking the woman's body apart into entrails and blood. Tirumular does not reject union: kept with bindu unspent, it is Siva's own pleasure, and only the fool's infatuation is condemned.

Kural 148 calls not looking at another man's wife (பிறன்மனை நோக்காத) the great manliness of the worthy. 1937 asks the yogi to leave without looking at the women he sees (பார்க்கின்ற மாதரைப் பாராது அகன்று) and to lay waste the eye's desire. The Kural's rule of conduct about one class of women becomes in 1937 a discipline of the eye toward all, turned to the root centre.

Kural 360 says pain perishes when even the names of காமம் வெகுளி மயக்கம் perish. 1938 says one who harbours காமாதி (lust and its kin) lives in fear (உட்கும்), and that Siva-yoga does not stay without grace. Both name the same triad as the root of suffering; 1938 adds that removing it is grace's work before technique's.

830 fixes the measure of paryanka yoga in nazhigai within one act of union (அஞ்சு கடிகைமேல் ஆறாங் கடிகையில்). 1939 extends the timing to the lunar calendar, naming days in the waxing and waning fortnights (வளர் பக்கம், அபரம்) for those who go into a woman's power. Together they show the yogic treatment of union as governed by time at both scales.

790 assigns the breath to the left or right side by weekday and by waxing or waning fortnight. 1941 says the act is to be done when the moon and sun breaths weaken (இந்து பருதிகால் நையுமிடத்து), leaving right and left (வலம் இடம் தீர்ந்து). 790's regime of alternating sides is the ordinary order; 1941 names the moment that order is suspended, as the breath leaves both channels.

837 says those who keep the intent mingled feel no strain (வருத்தமும் இல்லை) even when sharing themselves with a woman, and the silver rises unflagging. 1942 asks for one who stays unshaken (நடுங்காது இருப்பான்) as the senses press, letting go clinging to the woman while holding the breath. Both locate the discipline inside union rather than in abstaining from it.

826 says that when enjoyment is willed the breath does not leave (போகாது வாயுவும்) and the silver turns back from passion. 1943 has the lover speak endearments and then, at the moment of release, watch the faculty go within (கண்ட கரணம் உட்செல்ல). Both describe the same practice of the breath turned inward at the height of union.

1944 says the times that came into play at union determine the child's life span, death day and qualities (கட்டிய வாழ்நாள் சாம்நாள் குணம்). 453 says that at the hour of love the Lord, present in the house of bondage, fixes the span and the earthly life (பண்புறு காலமும் பார்மிசை வாழ்க்கையும்). 453 places in the Lord's act what 1944 reads off the calendar of union.

1947 says thought becomes seed, cause and effect, and that when thought is cut off these are கற்பனை (imagination). 2505 places the Supreme in the void beyond காரிய காரணம் கற்பனை (imagined effect and cause). Both call the chain of cause and effect a construct; 1947 ties its end to the cutting of thought.

477 says the embryo's form seen as male, female or neither (ஆண்பெண் அலியெனுங் கற்பனை) is fashioned by the Light's power. 1947 puns கருத்து on கரு and says that, when thought is cut, womb, seed and life span are கற்பனை. The same word for the embryo's fashioning is in 477 the Lord's making and in 1947 the mind's.

1948 says that when bindu stays unspent the undying breath, strength, intellect, tapas, japa and silence stay, and siddhi comes. Thiruppugazh 709 asks for the bindu that books and creeds cannot give (பேசிக்கொடாத விந்து) made steady as the light of truth, with the breath in the nose turned into the skull. Both join kept bindu and turned breath as the yogic way past what learning gives.

1950 counts among those whose bindu does not perish one who drinks the nectar in order even though passion comes (மோகம் உறினும்). 1904 says one keeping to the path open to people on earth (புவியோர் நெறி) advances in Siva-yoga by way of bindu. Both open the bindu discipline to the householder, not only the renouncer.

1951 speaks obscurely of a fire-bindu and a breath-bindu (பிராணனாம் விந்து) burnt together into nectar and knowledge. 1966 names the two bindus plainly as அன்னம் and பிராணன் and says those who know them gain a golden form and the eight siddhis. 1966 gives the terms that make 1951 readable.

1952 says people perish through the senses unknowing, and that the beyond is to be reached in waking (நனவில் அதீதம்). 2159 says turiya lies within waking itself (துரியம் இருப்பதும் சாக்கிரத்து உள்ளே). Both refuse to place the highest state apart from the waking life where the senses ruin people.

841 says those who in union can join self with self may live on earth for many ages (மண்ணிடைப் பல்லூழி வாழலும் ஆமே). 1954 says the one who has mastered bindu has passed beyond time (காலம் கடந்தவன்), while the waster passed through time and perished. 1954 turns 841's long life into escape from time itself, and adds the waster's contrast.

481 says that if the mother's belly is heavy with waste (மாதா உதரம் மலமிகில்) the child is dull, with water mute. 1955 tells the man to clear the woman's belly (நாரி உதரக் கலத்தின் மலத்தை) of waste, cold and bile before union. 1955 prescribes the remedy whose reason 481 gives.

Kural 941 says the three humours the learned count, beginning with wind (வளிமுதலா எண்ணிய மூன்று), cause disease in excess or lack. 1955 names சீதம் and பித்தம் with waste as what must be removed before union. The same humoral medicine that the Kural applies to daily health Tirumular applies to conception.

Kural 350 says: cling to the clinging of the one without clinging, in order to let clinging go (பற்றுக பற்று விடற்கு). 1956 says that if one holds without clinging (பற்றறப் பற்றினால்) the pride of delusion dies. Both turn the word பற்று against itself: a holding that frees from holding.
audit_text_issue: 1956 line 1 has a stray Latin character (சமாதிaக).

note: Kural 122 says to guard restraint as wealth, for life has no greater gain (ஆக்கம்) than அடக்கம். 1957 names among the things one must know about bindu அடக்கத்தில் ஆக்கமும், the increase that comes by restraint. The same pairing of restraint and gain, ethical in the Kural, is bodily in Tirumular.

1491 says both yoga and enjoyment (யோகமும் போகமும்) belong to the yogi who does not perish. 1960 says that when two bodies mingle with bindu kept, the pleasure is சிவபோகம், the true pleasure of the enjoyer, while fools embrace without ending infatuation. 1960 shows how 1491's union of yoga and bhoga is meant: within the act of union itself.

828 says that in bodily union one who guards bindu so it is not spoiled (பங்கப் படாமற் பரிகரித்து) becomes lord. 1961 says those joined in yoga, though they turn to women, do not release bindu out of love, while those who take hold of craving waste away. Both make the keeping of bindu within union the line between the yogi and the one who is drained.

1963 says the fire from the root settles in every hair-root (மயிர்க்கால் தோறும்) as Sivam becomes the self. 2856 says nectar wells up at every hair-root (மயிர்க்கால் தோறும் அமுதூறிய) in a bliss beyond difference. The same figure of the whole body pervaded marks in one the yogic fire and in the other the realised bliss.

1934 traces how food becomes chyle and, through the seven bodily elements, a drop of bindu like dew on grass. 1965 starts from there, seeing how bindu is contained in food (அன்னத்தில் விந்து அடங்கும்), and turns it back and releases it to the end of nada. 1934 is the physiology; 1965 is the practice built on it.

1095 tells one to take the letter Sa first and, for the teaching of the breath (வாசிப் பிராணன் உபதேசம்), join it with the bindu. 1967 sets the letter Si as the breath (சிகாரம் ... பிராணனாய்) and calls joining bindu's victory the உபதேசம். Both bind a mantra letter, the breath and bindu into one guru-given teaching.

1968 says the fourteen that came from bindu subside like deer (பதினான்கு மானேர் அடங்க) before the Siva-state comes. 2159 says the fourteen jackals ate poison and died (நரிகள் பதினாலு நஞ்சுண்டு செத்தன) and turiya is reached within waking. Both figure the fourteen faculties as animals whose stilling opens the highest state.

1971 repeats 961 almost word for word: bindu and nada join, meet the moon, nectar wells up, and the mantra uttered there becomes the oblation (ஆகுதி). Only அந்தர வானத்து becomes சுந்தர வானத்து. The near-repeat sets the bindu chapter's nectar teaching inside the earlier chakra chapter's rite.
Both open on the sun's hidden road under the earth (பகலோன் வரும்வழி) and say no one knows it; 1984 adds what the learned say, that it circles the mountain, and that those who know the town know.

1981 says the world's divided talk babbles and passes while the truth in the light goes unseen; 1986, in the body's sun, says those who find where the sun settles still all that babble with it. Same words, பேதித்து and பிதற்று.

1975 says the sun and gods circle Meru (மேரு வலம்வரு) as tapas, bowing to the Lord's feet. 2465 has the yogi think on Meru with the disc of spreading rays (மேருவினோடே விரிகதிர் மண்டலம்) and gain Siva's grace by tapas. Meru and the sun's disc serve in one as cosmic worship and in the other as the yogi's object of contemplation.

1976 calls the sun (பகலவன்) the holy Lord who is refuge and origin of all lives. 2533 names பகலோன் இறையவன், the sun as the Lord of many ages. Both identify the sun with the Lord rather than treating it as a lesser god.

270 says love and Siva are not two (அன்பே சிவம்). 1977 says that whatever the Vedic priests ask and the gods say, this is how love ripens toward the First (ஆதியில் அன்பு பழுக்கின்ற வாறே). 1977 gives love the same final place as 270, set against ritual request.

Both verses open every line with தானே: in 10 the Lord is earth, sky, fire, sun and moon and the lady who pours rain (தையலுமாய்); in 1978 he is the world's principle, the woman (தையலுமாய்), Shambhu and the cool light. The near-repeat of form and figure places the sun chapter's Lord in the opening invocation's.

1980 says the sun shines as four in the triangle and as sixteen (சோடசம்) in its spreading. 853 says the unchanging sun takes in all sixteen kalas (கலைமுற்றும் ... ஈரெட்டு) when fire joins. Both give the sun the sixteen kalas usually the moon's.
audit_text_issue: 853 line 2 (நாறா நலங்கினார் ஞாலங் கவர்க்கொள) and 1980's கேத முறுங்கேணி look corrupt.

note: 1983 has the Lord cleaving earth, sky and eye (மண்ணை இடந்து, விண்ணை இடந்து) and giving bliss. 1984 says no one knows the way the sun comes cleaving the earth (பாரை இடந்து). The shared verb shows 1983's cleaving one to be the sun of 1984.

Both put the decisive event in the குழல்வழி, the tube or central channel: in 754 the Dancer stands there for those who see the feet, in 1985 a victorious light shines there once the malams are killed.
audit_text_issue: 1985 மலங்கன் likely for மலங்கள்; கன்றாய unclear

note: 1985 says the practiser stays within Nandi's thought 'நின்றும் இருந்தும் கிடந்தும் நடந்தும்'; 325 says those who drink Siva's bliss in samadhi do not leave it 'நித்தல் இருத்தல் கிடத்தல்'. Both use the list of bodily postures to say the inner state is not tied to a seat or a session but holds through every posture.
audit_text_issue: 325 last line obscure; நித்தல் possibly for நிற்றல்

note: 1988 says the breath moving among the spreading rays will stop roaming (உலாஅது) once it becomes 'ஒருகதிர்', a single ray; 714 says the even breath stands still like an unflickering lamp and knowing the union along the kalas is the way 'அலைவற', free of wavering. Both make the joining of the breaths the end of the mind's wandering, one by the image of rays, the other of a lamp.

1989 bids worship when moon and sun meet (சந்திரன் சூரியன் தான்வரின்) and says those clear in the ground of both become Siva; 704 says the yogi of samadhi sees at the juncture (சந்தியிலே) how the moon meets the sun and becomes one. Both place the goal at the meeting of the two lights, and 704 names the juncture that 1989 calls உபய நிலம்.

1990 says that when the sun (அருக்கன்) joins fire and moon, that is பூரணை, fullness; 853 says sun and moon have unceasing kalas and when fire joins (அங்கி கூடவே) the sun takes in all the kalas of fulfilment (பேறாம் கலைமுற்றும்). The same three lights and the same claim that their union completes the kalas; 853 adds that it is done through the great breath (பெருங்கால்).
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 853 line 2 (நாறா நலங்கினார் ஞாலங் கவர்க்கொள) unconstruable.

note: 1923 lists what comes from bindu; 1993 divides bindu into lower and higher and pictures the unfolding as a dawn in the heart, setting up the chapter's sun of knowledge.
audit_text_issue: 1923's last line (கலைவை கரியே) looks compressed or corrupt

note: 1996 says moon, fire and sun (மதி அங்கி ஞாயிறு) remove the outer black darkness, but Nandi, rising within, removes the darkness of deeds; 2684 makes those same three lights Isan's eyes, sun and moon two and fire the third. Read together, the lights 1996 sets beneath the inner light are in 2684 parts of the Lord's own body, so the outer lights are his too.

1997 lights the single flame so darkness leaves and the juice of the rare fruit above (மேலை அருங்கனி ஊறல்) comes, the Lord of Kailash standing as flame above; Arunagiri asks to see, where the light of moon and sun strikes the central pillar (நடுத்தூண்), the taste of nectar-milk (பாலமுதச் சுவை) and the dance in the jewelled hall. Both picture the yogic summit as light above with nectar flowing, the Thiruppugazh borrowing the Tirumanthiram's inner geography for its plea.

1999 says the sun blossoming 'மண்டலத்துள்ளே' becomes rays of light within the region; 818 binds the mind's girdle 'மண்டலத்துள்ளே' so that daylight shines in the inner vessel (பகலே ஒளியாக). Both place an inner daylight in the same மண்டலம, one as a sun that goes out and stays, the other as the fruit of a yogic lock.

2000 says the Lord of the gods, Tirumal and Brahma perceived the flame 'சுடர்விடு சோதி' in the five places, navel, nose, eyes, middle and crown; 657 says Isa, Tirumal and Brahma stood and knew 'சுடர்விடு சோதி' reached through the sound in the channel, the eye and the heart. A near-repeat: the same three know the same radiant light at body-centres, the lists of centres differing.

2002 says Siva is in each body like the sun in many pots, not shut in by them; 2010 says he is in the soul and the soul in him, while being everywhere. Presence within without confinement, in two images.

2001 says the darkness of bond and ignorance (அஞ்ஞானம்) vanished by the light of Siva that is knowledge, as dense darkness leaves at dawn; Kural 352 says true perception removes darkness (இருள்நீங்கி) and brings joy to those free of confusion (மருள்நீங்கி). Both make knowledge the light that ends inner darkness; the Tirumanthiram names that light as Siva's, the Kural leaves it as clear sight.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 2001: இருசட looks like a slip for இருசுடர்.

note: 2003 repeats தானே: he is the three lights in one, stands as Brahma and Vishnu, is not other than body and soul (உடலுயிர் வேறன்றி), and is space, light and darkness; 412 repeats தானே: he stands as directions and gods, as body, life and tattvas (உடலுயிர் தத்துவமாய்), as ocean and mountain. The same anaphoric claim of one agent as everything; 2003 goes further by including darkness itself.

2004 lists fire, sun and moon with earth, water, fire, wind and sky (வையம் புனல் அனல் மாருதம் வானகம்) and the many souls as what the Lord bears; 859 lists earth, water, fire, air and space with sun, moon, fire and star as the nine that become the pranava. Both use the elements-plus-lights list as the Lord's cosmic body, 859 folding it into the sacred syllable.
2006 has the two swans that never part and faults the swan that holds itself apart; 2017 says there is no difference of soul and Siva once Siva is known. Both deny the soul a separate standing.
Both measure subtlety by repeated division: 2008 divides the atom into a thousand to reach the Lord in it, 2011 divides a cow's hair into a hundred and then a thousand to give the soul's size.

2009 makes the soul pure by the light 'as with the seed of the spreading banyan' (படர்கொண்ட ஆலதின் வித்து); Naladiyar 38 says a tiny banyan seed (ஆலம்வித்து) grows to shade so vast the sky seems small, and so does a small gift given to the worthy. Both use the banyan seed for something minute that holds a vast growth: in the Naladiyar the fruit of virtue, in the Tirumanthiram the soul (அணு) once its bonds are driven off.

2010 says people do not perceive the mingling, without a seam (கணுஅற), in which he is in the soul and the soul in him; 2440 says when soul and Supreme mingle with Siva 'கணு ஒன்று இலாத', who has not a single node, joy appears once words cease. Both use the cane's joint for the join that is absent, 2440 adding what the mingling is like when known.

2012 and 490 are near-identical: though our Lord is greater than all (ஏனோர் பெருமையன்), he is mingled within the smallness of flesh (ஊனே சிறுமையுள் உட்கலந்து), beyond the gods' measure, known by tapas. The verse appears again in the chapter on the soul, where it answers 2011's soul measured as a hair split a hundred thousand ways.

2012 and 3024 are the same verse with small differences (தவத்தின் அளவே in both); the Lord great beyond all yet mingled in the flesh in smallness. Its third appearance, in the closing hymns, shows the verse working as a refrain across the book.
Both picture the senses as fields where animals graze: 2016 has cows that must be led past the boundary, 2025 birds feeding in five fields and a herdsman with a staff.

2016 and 2903 are near-repeats: cows grazing in the field (கொல்லையின் மேயும் பசுக்கள்) must be led past the boundary and joined to the Lord's feet before the heart knows the sign (குறிப்பு / குறி). 2903 reads கொல்ல செய் நெஞ்சம், the heart that kills, where 2016 has கொல்லை செய் நெஞ்சம், the heart that makes its field, showing how the variant changes the sense.
1924 counts the thirty-six tattvas; 2020 says the count is learned from Nandi by grace and is the step to standing beyond them.
audit_text_issue: 1924's numbers (25 + 6 + two twos) do not sum to 36 as read; a number may be lost.

note: Both judge outward ascetic marks worthless without inner change: the Kural says neither shaving nor matted hair is needed if one gives up what is condemned (Parimelazhagar counts hair-plucking under shaving); Tirumular says hair-tearers do not know the impurities or grace.

2018 calls the dancing Lord the கண்காணி, the overseeing witness and lamp in the eye, for souls whose lamp is the mind; 2072 repeats கண்காணி four times: he rises in the hand, stays in the mind, mingles and makes the way, the beloved who is overseer. Both make the Lord the witness inside the mind, 2072 adding that the witness is also the beloved.

2019 and 2363 are near-repeats: knowledge removing ignorance, the sense-doors closed (பொறிவாய் ஒழிந்து), himself everywhere, knowing as knowledge within them, made dense (செறிவாகி). 2019 ends that he is also that soul (சீவனும் ஆகுமே), 2363 that he is Siva too (சிவனும் ஆமே): the variant states the soul-Siva identity from each end.

2020 says Nandi made known the nature of the thirty-six (ஆறாறு) and, once it was known by grace, stood beyond them; 2271 says those who know, who receive grace, are beyond the thirty-six (ஆறாறுக்கு அப்பால்), and beyond it Hara is sweet. 2271 carries 2020's teaching to its fruit: the knower too goes beyond where the teacher stands.

Both picture the senses as five elephants to be controlled. The Kural says the one who guards them with the goad of firmness is a seed for release; Tirumular shows the mahout exhausted and confesses he does not know how to manage it. The goal agrees; the confidence that it can be done does not.
Two animal images for the same discipline: the Kural's tortoise draws its five limbs in; Tirumular's five lions go out to feed and must have claws and teeth cut. Withdrawal against disarming.

Both count five senses and the gates through which craving comes and goes, and make guarding them the way to release; the Naladiyar names the five gates, Tirumular adds the nine openings and a herdsman.
2024 shows a mahout who cannot steer the leaping beast; in 2028 the poet says he himself has become that unruly horse.

The Kural asks what is stronger than fate; Tirumular gives fate's great strength the earth but assigns heaven to praise and human life to the mind, so fate is one power among several. The tension depends on reading 2030's domains as limits.

2026 says five lions live in the forest (அஞ்சுள சிங்கம் அடவியுள் வாழ்வன) and reaching the Lord is possible once their claws and teeth are cut; 977 opens the same way with five elephants (அஞ்சுள ஆனை அடவியுள் வாழ்வன) and makes the five letters their goad. The same frame gives two methods: disarming the senses in 2026, steering them with the mantra in 977.

2027 names five ministers with ninety-six (தொண்ணூற்று அறுவர்) under them who mean to rule; 2146 counts the ninety-six instruments of the first state: elements, senses, malas, gunas and adharas. 2146 supplies the list behind 2027's court, so the five senses' ninety-six servants are the tattvas.

2029 bids one shut the pot of countless holes (எண்ணிலி இல்லி) in the dark room and not go along with it; Naladiyar 47 calls the body a pot (கும்பம்) seeping through nine openings that the fool praises. If இல்லி is the perforated pot, both picture the body as a leaking vessel: the Naladiyar to cure desire for it, the Tirumanthiram to bid its openings closed. The reading of 2029 is uncertain.

The Kural says the field of the five must be crushed (அடல்வேண்டும்); Tirumular calls those who say 'curb the five' ignorant and says full curbing makes one inert. The conflict holds if 2033 is read as rejecting suppression of the senses, as its wording says, rather than only a wrong method of it.
The same chapter that mocks curbing the five (அடக்கு) praises subsiding in the five (ஒடுங்கு) as tapas and Hara's state: the objection is to forcing the senses, not to their stilling.

Both treat the five senses as elephants to be held, the Kural's guarded by the goad of firmness (on Parimelazhagar's reading), Tirumular's by a fort of knowledge. In the Kural the guard works; in Tirumular the elephants break out.
In 977 the five elephants of the forest are held by the goad of the five letters; in 2034 a fort of knowledge fails to hold them. Mantra succeeds where bare knowledge did not.
Both make mastery of the five a supreme power: the Kural calls Indra witness to it, Tirumular calls it the wide world, tapas and Hara's state.
Both count life away by its units of time, the Kural's day a saw cutting life, Tirumular's nazhigais and days already gone; Tirumular draws the lesson of conquering the senses now.

2032 says he who sets about curbing the restless senses (இந்திரியம் அடக்கல்) is himself immortal (அமரன்); Kural 6 says those who keep the path of the one who quenched the five sense-doors (பொறிவாயில் ஐந்தவித்தான்) live long (நீடுவாழ்வார்). Both promise lasting life for sense-restraint; the Kural gives it to those who follow the restrained one, the Tirumanthiram to the one who restrains.

2036 asks what use babbling (பிதற்றில்) is and says the mind is the seed of all that spreads, growing or shrinking with it; 2956 says the mind's maya is maya, when it dies nothing else remains, there is no need to babble (பிதற்றவும் வேண்டா), and to remain having examined oneself is the truth. Both make the mind the root of the world one lives in and examination (ஆராய்ந்து / ஆய்ந்து) the answer.

2038 bids one tie the leaping five to the post of knowledge (ஞானத் தறி); 2023 says the five rutting elephants of the body will not come to the post of the Agamas (ஆகமத் தறி) and the mahout is spent. The same tethering post, failing in 2023 when it is scripture, holding in 2038 when it is knowledge and grace grants bliss.

2040 says the wealth that seemed lasting (நீள்பொருள்) is like writing on water (நீர்மேல் எழுத்து), so conquer the senses now; 64 says crores of Agamas are writing on water (நீர்மேல் எழுத்தே) if one does not know the knowledge the Lord declared. The same figure strikes wealth in one and unread scripture in the other: both are void without the inner work.

2041 begins 'போற்றிசைத்துப் புனிதன்', worships the Lord of the four directions (நாற்றிசைக்கும் நாதனை), then turns the senses back and pours him into the heart; 2, the book's opening praise, has 'போற்றிசைத்து ... புனிதனை' and 'நாற்றிசைக்கும் ... நாதனை'. 2041 reuses the invocation's words and makes the praise the first step of sense-withdrawal.

2043 says 'கைவிடலாவது ஒன்று இல்லை', there is nothing one must give up, if one reaches him in thought and sings; Kural 341 says from whatever one has left, from that one has no pain, making release from pain follow each thing renounced. On the reading that 2043 answers the call to renounce objects, the two disagree on whether giving things up is the way; if 2043 means only that renunciation is secondary to praise, they differ in emphasis.
Both end with blind and blind falling into the pit; 1680 blames the pupils who choose a guru who cannot cure blindness, 2048 the blind guru who shows the stick.

2044 lists the false guru: no inner feeling, not seeing the Veda-Agama path, doing no service, reviling, of the bound soul's nature (அணுவின் குணத்தோன்); 2053 describes the lasting guru (நீடும் குரவன்), stainless, able to give a love free of mala, to those who have grasped the tattvas. Together they set the condition on taking a guru: the bound cannot free, only the mala-free can give.

2045 says false gurus have looked over mantra, tantra, yoga and jnana but do not reflect and do not make others clear (தெளிவியாது), teaching for food; Naladiyar 318 says some fill houses with books without grasping their meaning, and those who understand and make others understand (தேற்றும் புலவர்) are another kind. Both separate possessing the texts from understanding them well enough to make another clear.

2046 calls a false guru one not free of lust and the rest (காமாதி நீங்கா) who teaches the unreal to others; Kural 834 says no fool is greater than one who studies, understands and teaches others (பிறர்க்குரைத்தும்) but does not restrain himself (தானடங்கா). Both condemn the teacher whose own passions are unrestrained; the Tirumanthiram adds that what such a teacher passes on is அசத்து, the unreal.

2047 says teaching without removing the false learning lowers one's own state and brings ruin to the good king and the land (அரசுக்கும் நாட்டுக்கும் கேடு); 241 says if those whose ignorance remains take up tuft and thread, the land withers and the king loses standing. Both tie the fitness of religious teachers to the health of the realm, and 2047 cites Nandi for it.
Both define the Siva-guru by the same act, showing the real, the unreal and the real-unreal (சத்தும் அசத்தும் சதசத்தும்).

Both use transmutation by contact: whatever comes to the golden mountain takes its colour (1511), whatever the philosopher's stone touches becomes gold (2054); both make the guru's presence change the one who comes near.
2051 says the iron once turned to gold never turns back; 2054 names the agent, the guru as a touchstone, and widens it to all the world he touches.
Both make the guru's path the one road that Nandi set out for salvation.

2049 makes தாள்தந்து, the giving of the feet, the true guru's single act, repeated in every line with four effects. 2384 uses the same phrase of Nandi (சீர்நந்தி தாள்தந்து), who gave his feet and then taught Vedanta and Siddhanta. Together they show the gift of the feet as Tirumular's term for initiation, preceding the teaching.

2050 says the guru set his feet on the devotee's head (சிரத்தோடு தன் பாதம்) and ended the sorrow of birth. Arunagiri asks Murugan to set his lotus feet as a crown on his head (வாரிஜபதங்கள் ... முடிபுனைந்து) and rule him with a word of teaching (போதக வாசகம்). Both treat the feet on the head as the act by which the guru takes a disciple.

2050 states as done what the song pleads for: the guru kept away the band of Yama's messengers (நமன் தூதுவர் கூட்டம்). Arunagiri pictures those messengers (நமனுடைய தூதர்) seizing and cutting him and asks Murugan, 'the guru who came to rule those who trust him', to come quickly at that hour. The pairing sets Tirumular's assurance beside the devotee's petition for it.

2052 says those moved by clamour, without knowledge, are not போதக் குரு, gurus who give understanding. 2045, in the chapter on false gurus, calls false those who have seen mantra, yoga and jnana but do not reflect or make others clear (சிந்தனை செய்யாத் தெளிவியாது). Both make the power to bring understanding the test that separates the true guru from the false.

2055 says that when the guru's presence is revealed 'the self must win itself' (தானே தனைப்பெற வேண்டும்). The Kural praises one who has wholly gained his own self (தன்னுயிர் தான் அறப்பெற்றானை), whom all beings worship. Tirumular places the same self-gaining inside the guru's presence, as the fruit of initiation rather than of tapas alone.

2060 says all is the Lord's bliss with the Lady, and that the soul's rise to the Siva-state is play (விளையாட்டே). 396 says one He and one She set to play (ஒருவன் ஒருத்தி விளையாடல்) and their play brings forth everything. 396 makes creation the couple's play; 2060 extends the same word to the soul's release.

2061 lists the Lord's acts toward the soul, ending in setting it in silence once it reaches release (வீடுற்று மோனத்துள் வைத்தலும்). 1611 says that for those to whom silence has come, release comes and the five acts come forward. 2061 makes silence the Lord's final gift; 1611 makes it the condition from which release and the five acts follow.

2064 says nectar ripened in the mandala of rubies, and those who guarded and drank it were freed from birth while the brutes (மாக்கள்) lived for the flesh. 335 sets yogis who taste the nectar of the moon (ஒண்மதி ... அமுதை) against fools who drink liquor and lose understanding. Both divide people by which drink they take, the inner nectar or the body's.

2058 says the guru, when he speaks, shows the real, the unreal and the real-unreal (சத்தும் அசத்தும் சதசத்தும்). 2065 says the Lord sets apart the same three (அசத்தொடு சத்தும் அசத்சத்து) and makes the one thing known. The same triad is assigned once to the guru and once to the Lord, which the chapter resolves in 2066 by calling the Supreme the guru.

The chapter opens with 'the lord who gives his feet is the true guru' (தலைவனே சற்குரு) and closes with 'the Supreme, if you would name him, is the guru' (பரனே குருவாம்). Both list the guru's acts on the bonds (பாசம் தணிக்கும், பசுபாசம் வாட்டலால்). Read together, the identity runs both ways: the guru is the Lord and the Lord is the guru.

Both deny that hidden wrong is hidden: in the Kural the five elements within laugh at the deceiver's concealed conduct, in Tirumular the Lord stands everywhere as overseer. The Kural's witness is in the body, Tirumular's is the Lord.
2039 makes north and south the temple of the mind; 2070 says the world gathered in the north is within, against those who walk north to find it.
1729 says Nandi took the body as his temple; 2071 faults those who search the land for the one fragrant within the body.
Both end in களவொழிந்தாரே; 2067 says stealth ends when the overseer is seen, 2074 says how he is seen: not with the eye, whose film hides the light.

2068 opens 'he knows what was done' (செய்தான் அறியும்), which the nuance notes may also be 'the doer himself knows', and promises that those who speak truth will be worshipped by the gods. The Kural says not to lie about what one's own heart knows (தன்நெஞ்சு அறிவது), for the heart will burn the liar. On the second reading of செய்தான் அறியும், both ground truthfulness in the doer's own knowledge of the deed; on the first, Siva stands where the Kural puts the heart.

2069's riddle says those who pound and eat the seed-grain (வித்துக்குற்றுண்டு) and lay waste the field have no birth, read as destroying the seed of karma. The Kural names craving as the seed (வித்து) that produces unceasing birth. The Kural says what the seed is; Tirumular's madmen are those who destroy it.

2067 uses கண்காணி, the overseer, to end stealth: no place is without him, and those who see him give up theft. 2072 repeats கண்காணி in every line but ends by calling the overseer the beloved (காதலன்) who mingles and makes the way. The pair turns the watchman of 2067 from a check on wrongdoing into the lover.

2073 sees virgins, the learned, ascetics and contemplatives each in their own enclosure (ஒருசிறை) and says none knows the Lord's nature. 1530 says the six sects standing in the assembly (ஆயத்துள்) do not see the God standing in the body. Both fault division into separate camps as the cause of missing the Lord.

2075 says that when Nandi gave grace, 'I, clear in mind, ceased from doing' (செயல் ஒழிந்தேன்). 288 says that if devotees abide radiant and cease from action (செயலற்றிருந்திடில்), the Lord comes and stands among them. 288 makes actionlessness the condition for the Lord's coming; 2075 reports it as the result of his grace.

2076 says the schemers intent on சுராமயம், read as intoxication, gave up thinking of the One free of ill, and do not see the eight as filled with the Supreme. 329 says the great fools who drink deluding liquor do not discern maya or release from it. On the liquor reading of சுராமயம, both make intoxication the thing that blinds people to the Lord; on the reading 'of the gods' the link lapses.

2077 says that for those who have become one by uniting, 'one' and 'two' never come together, while for those who keep saying 'one or two' the One stands as both. 1441 reports that after reaching the state where He and I are not two, 'I can no longer speak of He and I' (சாற்றகில்லேனே). 1441 is the first-person case of 2077's claim that the united drop the one-or-two terms.

2079 says 'if one knows the soul, awareness becomes knowledge' (உயிரை அறியில் உணர்வு அறிவாகும்). 2318 says 'knowing oneself is knowledge' (தன்னை அறிவது அறிவாம்) and anything else is a ghoul's knowing. Both define real knowledge as knowledge of the self.

2080 ends that the chief work toward the Lord of the gods is knowing oneself (தலைவாணி செய்வது தன்னை அறிவதே). 2355 says knowing oneself brings no harm and, once known, one stays worshipping oneself. Both put self-knowledge at the head of worship.

2081 tells the reader to give up சிற்றின்பம், petty pleasure, for the sweetness of the Lord. The Kural says those who want the other joy do not do wrong out of desire for சிற்றின்பம். Both set the same word against a greater joy, though in the Kural the small joy is gain from coveting and in Tirumular it is sensual pleasure.

2083 says the senses and inner organs came to the soul as the subtle body (சூக்க உடல்), not the gross. 2201 counts the states by how much of the eightfold subtle body (புரியட்டகம்) is active: all in waking, three in dream, two in sleep, one in turiya. 2083 names what the subtle body is made of; 2201 uses it to define the states.
Both ask what is gained by learning or argument that does not end in bowing at the Lord's feet; Tirumular names disputation (வாது) where the Kural names learning.
The Kural says only those who reach the Lord's feet cross the sea of births; Tirumular laments those who, given a rare human birth, never cherish those feet and so lose what that birth was for.
Both press for action before death arrives: the Kural before the hiccup stops the tongue, Tirumular while the porridge still boils and death runs near.

2084 mocks those who store seed, sow and plant out seedlings without knowing their lifespan is ending (அற்றதம் வாணாள் அறிகிலா). The Kural mocks those who cannot know they will live one moment yet think thoughts in crores. Both set long-range plans against a span no one can count on; Tirumular's example is the farming year.

2086 describes those who tend the body as if it were life (உடம்பினை ஓம்பி உயிரா) and end on a pyre of rough logs. Naladiyar 37 says one should not live doing service only to the body (உடம்பிற்கே ஒப்புரவு செய்தொழுகாது) but act for the world above. Both fault spending a life on the body's upkeep; the Naladiyar adds what to do instead.

2087 refers to the Supreme taught to the four (நால்வர்க்கு) by the holy one under the banyan's shade, and blames those who do not grasp it. 71 speaks of what the Lord told the three and the four (மொழிந்தது மூவர்க்கும் நால்வர்க்கும் ஈசன்), a greatness beyond death and birth. Both point to the same primal teaching to the four; 2087 adds the lament for those who ignore it.

2091 says that in boundless youth people stand in the work of lust, which soon runs out (தீர வருவதோர் காமத் தொழில்), and forget the great one's joy. Naladiyar 17 says youth falls like fruit and the spear-eyed woman too will walk bent with a staff, so she should not be desired. Both tie lust to youth and argue against it from youth's passing.

2094 warns that one who does not worship daily becomes an elephant that has thrown off its fear (அஞ்சு அற்று விட்டதோர் ஆனை), with அஞ்சு also 'the five'. The Kural praises one who guards the five with the goad of firmness (உரனென்னும் தோட்டியான் ஓரைந்தும்). Both picture the uncontrolled self as an elephant; Tirumular's goad is worship, the Kural's is firmness.

2094's elephant that has broken loose (அஞ்சு அற்று) may pun on the five senses. 977 makes the pun explicit: five elephants live in the forest and the five letters (அஞ்செழுத்து) are their goad. Read with 977, 2094's worship of the Lord is the goad that keeps the five in check.

171 shows bees gathering honey and storing it on a branch, only for the strong to drive them off and take it. 2097 says people do not grasp how the bee builds its great store, and do not know the honey that enters the mouth without toil (வருந்தேன் நுகராது வாய்புகு தேனை). Against the toiling bee's lost hoard, 2097 sets an unearned honey, read as the Lord's bliss.

Naladiyar 10 says misers who hoard without giving lose it, as the honey bee's store shows (தேனீக் கரி). 2097 uses the bee's labour over honey too, but sets beside it a honey that comes to the mouth without toil. The Naladiyar's bee teaches loss; Tirumular's contrast points to a sweetness not gathered by effort.

2099 says death comes leaping and the allotted days have fallen away, so stir the porridge while it boils (கொதிக்கின்ற கூழில் துடுப்பிடலாமே). Naladiyar 20 says death roams looking for its people, so take provisions in good time. Both argue from death's nearness that the work must be done now.

2100 warns that the days before grey hair (நரை) are few, with திரை (wave, wrinkle) for the coming of age. Naladiyar 11 says the wise, knowing grey hair (நரை) will come, renounced in childhood. Both use grey hair as the deadline for turning to austerity.

Both deny that birth ranks people: the Kural says birth is alike for all and distinction comes from deeds; Tirumular says kin is one and God is one. The Kural keeps a distinction by deeds that Tirumular does not mention.
1581 says Nandi taught that the guru is Siva; 2120 adds the condition, a guru who is a flawless knower, and says such a one is to be called nothing but the Supreme.
Both make reaching the Lord the end of births: the Kural's crossing of the sea of births, Tirumular's freedom from all birth for the soul that holds the Lord in mind at death.

2102 bids one to think of the Lord even when dying (இறந்தொழி காலத்தும் ஈசனை உள்கும்) so that the Siva way ends the soul's fluttering distress; 2108 repeats the line almost word for word (இறக்கின்ற காலத்தும் ஈசனை உள்கும்) and names the result as Siva's state and no further birth. The near-repeat shows the thought held at death is the chapter's fixed counsel, with 2108 supplying what 2102 only implies.

2106 asks when this body came to be ours (எக்காலத்து இவ்வுடல் வந்து எமக்கு ஆனது) and bids one seek the way not to enter another body; Kural 340 asks whether the life, a lodger (துச்சில்) in the body, has no home of its own. The Kural's question about the soul's tenancy becomes in the Tirumanthiram a practice: reflecting on the body as not one's own is the way to grace and to ending further lodgings.

2107 says Hara knows 'that thing' (அப்பொருள்) that leaves one body and enters another, and that seeking the Lord even when dying (சாகின்ற போதும்) brings it to the other shore (அக்கரை); 2108 calls the same soul 'the one that flies' (பறக்கின்ற ஒன்று) and makes the result Siva's state and no further birth. Read together, the unnamed அப்பொருள் of 2107 is the flying soul of 2108, and the other shore is the end of birth.

2108 pictures the soul as 'the one that flies' (பறக்கின்ற ஒன்று), which reaches its goal if the Lord is thought of at death; Kural 338 likens the bond of body and life to a bird flying off and leaving its nest (குடம்பை தனித்து ஒழியப் புள் பறந்தற்றே). The Kural uses the flight to show how slight the bond is; the Tirumanthiram asks where the flight ends, and makes its end depend on the last thought.

2109 says that for those who stand within and know, the Lord becomes a cow long in milk after calving (நீடிய ஈற்றுப் பசு); 2627 has the devotee call the Lord as a calf calls a cow (ஆன்கன்று தேடி அழைக்கும் அதுபோல்), and the Lord comes and enters the body. Both make the Lord's giving the cow's unforced giving to its calf; 2627 adds the devotee's side, the calf's calling.

2110 says the one of unfailing fame (கேடில் புகழோன்), by whom strong deeds perish (கெடுகின்ற வல்வினை), places those who seek his feet among the celestials; Kural 5 says the two deeds born of darkness do not cling to those devoted to the Lord's true praise (பொருள்சேர் புகழ்). Both join the Lord's fame to the ending of deeds; the Tirumanthiram sets this at the moment of rising upward, which the Kural does not.

2111 repeats 1862 line for line in its first two lines (ஏறுடையாய் இறைவா எம்பிரான் என்று நீறிடுவார் அடியார் நிகழ் தேவர்கள்) and ends alike, வேறு அணிவார்க்கு வினையில்லை. The difference is the third line: in 1862 one honours the ash-wearing devotees as the Lord himself (அண்ணல் இவர் என்று), in 2111 one wears the Lord's feet (அண்ணல் திருவடி); the near-repeat moves freedom from deeds from honouring devotees to holding the feet.

2113 says there is one true austerity (மெய்த்தவம்), one true foot and one true path to take up, for those who stand wishing to take them up (வேண்டி நின்றோர்க்கே); Kural 265 says austerity is striven for here because one obtains what one wants as one wants it (வேண்டிய வேண்டியாங்கு எய்தலால்). Both tie tapas to the seeker's wanting; the Kural to what it yields, the Tirumanthiram to who may take it up.

2114 says the fire-coloured one gives joy to those who come to him (சார்ந்தவர்க்கு இன்பம்) and painful birth to those who turn away (பேர்ந்தவர்க்கு இன்னாப் பிறவி); Kural 4 says those who reach the feet of the one without liking or aversion have no suffering anywhere (அடி சேர்ந்தார்க்கு யாண்டும் இடும்பை இல). The Tirumanthiram adds the other half the Kural leaves unstated, and its verb கொடுத்திடும் puts the painful birth in the Lord's giving, where the Kural's வேண்டாமை இலான் names no aversion at all.

2115 says the Stainless one is present as ghee within milk (நெய்த்தலைப் பால்போல்) yet those who praise do not desire that light; 134 says those who grasp the guru's word beyond speech, when the body falls, mix into the shoreless light like ghee in pure milk (பாலினுள் நெய் கலந்தாற்போல்). The same image runs both ways: in 2115 the Lord is hidden in the world as ghee in milk, in 134 the freed soul is lost in the light as ghee in milk.

2118 says that if deceivers (வஞ்சகர்) stay before the true guru, famine (பஞ்சம்) comes to the land; 535 says that if falsehood enters the presence of the true guru (சற்குருச் சந்நிதி பொய்வரின்), the good path fails, knowledge does not stay and famine comes too (பஞ்சமும் ஆமே). The pair fixes the reading of 2118's doubtful text: famine as the public consequence of deceit near the guru is the book's settled claim.

1581 says Nandi taught that the guru is Siva (குருவே சிவம்); 2119 says countless gods worshipped Siva without finding the way to become him (ஆமாறு ஒன்று இல்லை), and union comes by worshipping the guru who shows that way. 2119 limits the identity of 1581 to a function: the guru counts as Siva because he shows the way of becoming, which worship of Siva alone did not give.

2120 says that since men and gods, held by soul and bond, pass away through deeds, only a flawless knower (ஞானி கோதிலன்) called guru is to be named the Supreme (பரம்); 2057 describes that guru as one of supreme bliss (பரஇன்பன்) who practises Siva-yoga and removes the soul's bonds (உயிர்பாசம் நீக்கி). 2120 gives the condition for calling a guru பரம்; 2057 spells out what such a guru does.

Both make the body a bag left behind when its occupant goes: in 167 the dancer leaves the leather bag, so what crows do to it no longer matters; in 2122 the thief leaves and the maya-bag turns to earth.
2124 repeats 473 almost word for word; in the chapter on conception it describes the forming embryo, here the subtle body of eight.

Both list the body's stuffs, fat, blood, bone, flesh, skin. The Naladiyar asks which of these is the beloved, to cure desire; Tirumular names them as the gross adjunct beneath the subtle bodies, without disgust.
494 names the classes of soul (விஞ்ஞானர், எஞ்ஞானர், மெய்ஞ்ஞானர்) by the malas they have left; 2136 gives each its body: anava, maya, karma, or Siva.
725 says Tirumular once thought the body a flaw, then found the Lord's temple within it and now tends it; 2137 calls those who dismiss the body as filth dull.

The Naladiyar says the great saw the body's foulness and abandoned it; Tirumular calls those who disregard the body as filth dull and finds the cosmos in it. The conflict holds if மலம் in 2137 is read as bodily filth, as here.

2122 calls the body a bag (காயப்பை) which turns to earth once the thief inside goes out; 441 calls the same five-element body a bag (காயப்பை) which the brow-eyed Lord ties and unties (கட்டி அவிழ்ப்பான்). The shared காயப்பை shows two views of the body's end: in 2122 the soul's leaving, in 441 the Lord's untying.
