2123 names the subtle body as the eightfold புரியட்ட காயம்: sound, touch, form, taste, smell, intellect, mind and ego; 2201 makes the same புரியட்டகம் the measure of the states, union with it being waking and its narrowing to three, two and one being dream, deep sleep and turiya. 2201 puts to use the eightfold body that 2123 lists.

2124 ends with the clinging bond and the eight, which the brow-eyed one binds and unbinds (கட்டி அவிழ்ந்திடும் கண்ணுதல் காணுமே); 441 ends with the body-bag of five elements that the brow-eyed one ties and unties (கட்டி அவிழ்ப்பான் கண்ணுதல் காணுமே). The near-identical last line is applied in 441 to the gross body and in 2124 to the subtle body of senses and instruments: Siva binds and frees both.

2126 asks who knows the sixty-eight bodies (அறுபத்தெட்டு ஆக்கை); 2127 places those sixty-eight bodies within the body of eight spans, where their joining makes the body a body. The obscure number occurs only in these two verses, so each is the other's only gloss: the question of 2126 is partly answered in 2127.

2128 says Brahman shows the measure that stands in each pot (கடந்தொறும் நின்ற கணக்கு) as the soul subsides into the Supreme; 137 speaks of the life that stands in each pot (கடந்தொறும் நின்ற உயிர்) and says its shore is the Lord's holy feet. Both use the pot for the single body holding the life; 137 names the end as the feet, 2128 in Vedanta terms as Brahman.

2131 says the subtle body leaves one coat of flesh and puts on another (காயத் துகிர் போர்வை ஒன்றுவிட்டு ஆங்கு ஒன்றிட்டு), going far and near like a galloping horse's steps; 491 says the body dissolved into the Supreme takes form again and is born by grace, as salt crystallizes from the sea (திரைக்கடல் உப்புத் திரண்டது போல). 491 explains how the new coat is formed; 2131 how the subtle body passes into it.

2132 says the soul, leaving the body like a snake its slough, goes by Hara's grace to the place it must go and eats the two fruits (இருபயன் உண்ணுமே); 166 says when the man goes, the precious life at once reaches its place, left or right (அடையும் இடம் வலம்). Both make the place the soul reaches after death a matter of its two kinds of deed.

2134 says one who has borne the Supreme and become Him (தான் அவன் ஆகிய) reaches the highest, while other souls go where their deeds bring them; 2954 asks, once one has become He (தான் அவன் ஆனபின்), whom is there to think of. Both name union by the same phrase; 2134 contrasts it with the round of deeds, 2954 draws out that no object of thought remains.

2135 says that for the jnani the body, once established, becomes Siva (ஞானிக்குக் காயம் சிவமாகும்); 1911 says that if fire touches the body of a jnani it is as if the Lord's own temple were set alight (அண்ணல்தம் கோயில் அழல் இட்டது), and famine follows. 1911 applies what 2135 states: because the knower's body is Siva's, it is not to be burnt.

The Kural calls virtue the companion that does not perish when one perishes; Tirumular says vows and gifts are no sure support for the perishing flesh. The two can agree if the Kural speaks of the person and Tirumular of the body; the verse does not settle which it means.

2139 says that when one looks upward (அண்ணாந்து பார்க்க), desire, speech, breath-sound and mind fall away with the body; 800, in the Khechari yoga chapter, says that when the tank is filled with the sky-river, on looking upward (அண்ணாந்து பார்க்க) one is free of dirt. The same phrase in a yoga verse supports the yogic reading of 2139: the upturned attention is a practice, not only the dying gaze.
Both picture the body as a king's realm with horses and a company of five: in 2147 as the arrayed camp of the waking instruments, in 2165 as a city whose five servants sleep when the king rides in.
2142 places dream at the throat with fourteen instruments; 2154 says which ten fall away and that dream is built from the impressions of household life.
2162 describes anava as a stupor from which the soul falls into the states; 2163 gives the Lord's side: the states are his waking of the sleeper through maya.
2160 says the five malas keep every soul in endless birth and death; 2166 says the same five, seen plainly in waking, are the way to stand with the Supreme.
Tirumular takes the Kural's own phrase, உடம்பொடு உயிரிடை நட்பு. The Kural says that bond ends as a bird leaves its shell; Tirumular faults people who never come to know it.
Both separate the life from the body it lives in: the Naladiyar's dancer leaves the skin bag, and Tirumular's fools cling to bodies without knowing the life inside.
Both use the tortoise drawing in for the five senses held in. In the Kural it is self-restraint that guards through seven births; in Tirumular it follows when the silent and spoken letters meet.
audit_text_issue: tm:2158 begins with a stray 'Y' before ஊமை.

note: Both treat birth as a waking from sleep. The Kural uses it to show how quickly birth and death alternate; Tirumular makes embodiment the Lord's waking of the soul from anava's deeper sleep.

2143 maps the states onto the tattvas 'from niyati to Siva' (நியதி முதலாகச் செப்பும் சிவம் ஈறாய்) without listing them. 2191 lists the thirty-six from Siva down through niyati to the soul (ஆன்மா ஈறாறே), supplying the scale 2143 only names by its two ends.

2144 sums the instruments of waking as ten senses, ten objects, ten airs, four inner instruments and the soul: thirty-five. 2200 states the same count in one phrase, 'waking is twenty-five with ten' (ஐஐந்து பத்துடன் ஆனது சாக்கிரம்), so the two confirm the thirty-five reckoning against the twenty-five of 2142.

2145 gives each element its colour: earth golden, water white, fire red, air black, sky smoky. 947 says the elements and the colours (வண்ணம்) each match the letters and that the Lord stands within the matched letters, using the correspondence 2145 sets out as a support for worship.
audit_text_issue: 2145 line 1 has பசுமை with no element of its own; possibly a slip.

note: 2146 counts the instruments of the first state as ninety-six (தொண்ணூற்றாறே) and, on the reading of ஏதம் படஞ்செய்து as 'working harm', calls them harmful. Arunagiri lists the ninety-six tattva-agents (தத்துவ காரர் தொணூற்றறுவாரும்) among the cheats living around a man; both treat the ninety-six as the soul's hindrance, not its self.

Both verses end on the same line, 'the long gate, five with four' (நெடுங்கடை ஐந்தொடு நான்கே), and both picture the body as a lord's camp or town with its owner (உடையவன்). 2147 sets the figure among the tattvas of the waking state; 2925 uses it in a riddle of the temple buffalo, so the image recurs as a fixed formula across distant chapters.

2149 says that by turning back the ajapa breath (அசபையை மாற்றி) the body that has taken form will not perish (உடல் ஒழியாதே). 724 gives the reason this is wanted: if the body perishes, life perishes before true knowledge is firmly reached, so 'I nurtured the body and with it life'.

2149 promises that breath turned back keeps the body from perishing. Arunagiri asks not to be a foolish yogi who, thinking the impermanent flesh will last (அனித்தமான ஊன் நாளும் இருப்பதாக), stops the breath from leaving the nostrils, and seeks instead removal of mala by knowledge. The conflict holds if 2149's promise is read literally of the body, as its last line says.

2151 says that contemplating earth, water, fire, air, sky and the inner faculties one by one wins mastery of the elements (பூத சயம்). 687 says that firmly turning back the five elements spread out in many forms (பரந்த ஐம்பூதத்தை மறித்திடில்) brings sight of the subtle true thing in a year; both make the elements a ladder to be climbed back.

Kural 27 says the world is within the grasp of one who discerns the five, taste, light, touch, sound and smell (ஐந்தின் வகைதெரிவான் கட்டே உலகு). 2153 says that once the five senses, their five objects and the four inner instruments are understood together (ஒருங்கே உணர்ந்தபின்), he abides as the whole cosmos (அண்டமும் தானாய்), turning the Kural's mastery of the world into identity with it.

Kural 339 explains death by sleep: dying is like falling asleep (உறங்குவது போலும் சாக்காடு). 2155 describes deep sleep in the terms of death: self-regard gone, understanding gone, the body undone (மேனி அழிந்து), knowing nothing in the unmanifest. The same likeness is read from opposite ends.

2156 says three remain in deep sleep (கழுமுனையைச் சேர்ந்துள மூன்றுடன்): chitta, breath and the soul's seeing. 2200 places in deep sleep 'the three, with purusha' (மூவர் புருடன் சுழுனையின்), the same count of three joined to the soul.

2157 says the soul, beyond the world at the summit of thought, casts off ignorance and stands as a mute (ஊமன் நின்றானே). 1896 warns that if only speech falls silent one is merely mute (மூங்கையாம்); silence is speech and mind both stilled. 1896 sets the condition under which 2157's muteness is silence and not mere speechlessness.

2158 joins the silent letter (ஊமை எழுத்து) with the tortoise drawing in the five (ஆமை அகத்தினில் அஞ்சம் அடங்கிடும்). 2304 puts a tortoise with five hollows inside a silent well (ஊமைக் கிணறு) and promises long life if it withdraws into truth. Both pair ஊமை and ஆமை with the five drawn in, a figure Tirumular returns to in distant chapters.
audit_text_issue: 2158 begins with a stray 'Y' before ஊமை.

note: 2159 says turiya lies within waking itself (துரியம் இருப்பதும் சாக்கிரத்து உள்ளே). 2265 says that if the beyond state is reached within waking (சாக்கிரத் தன்னில் அதீதம் தலைப்படில்), birth is cut off and release attained; both place the highest state inside waking rather than in sleep.

2159 has the fourteen jackals (நரிகள் பதினாலு) die and the great horse bolt as turiya is reached. 2276 has the Lord set the soul riding the horse of turiya (துரியப் பரி) inside the tiger and drive the jackals (நரிகளை) off; the same horse and jackals figure the faculties overcome in the high state.

2161 says the soul reaches release directly through the knowledge it contemplates (எண்ணுறு ஞானத்தின் நேர்முத்தி எய்துமே). Kural 356 says those who have learned here and seen the true thing reach the path of not returning here; both make knowledge the direct way out of birth, though 2161 adds the Lord's grace (அண்ணல் அருள்).

2166 says one who sees the five malas plainly while fully awake (நீடு நனவினில்) stands always with the Supreme. 2265 says the beyond state reached within waking (சாக்கிரத் தன்னில் அதீதம்) cuts off birth and gives firm release; both locate release in waking.
Both reach the Vedanta count of twenty-eight from the twenty-four, but add different items to it: 2172 purusha, the Supreme and the void, 2176 turiya, inner time, the void and the higher turiya.
2178 reduces the countless tattvas to ninety-six and twenty-five; 2179 says which school counts which, making ninety-six common and thirty-six the Saiva count.
2170 pictures one who sits in the web of the senses and consumes their objects; 2181 separates the knower from all thirty-six inert tattvas, a knowledge the soul gets only from Nandi.
Both make the letter A stand for what is first: the Kural compares God's place in the world to A among letters, and Tirumular names the real tattva the letter A.
2160 says the five malas bind every soul; 2183 grades them by the rank of beings, from five in the lowest to anava alone in Sadasiva.

2167 assigns the sub-states within waking to bonds: waking-of-waking to the concealing power, waking-dream to Mahamaya, and so on. 2253 lists the same sub-states (சாக்கிர சாக்கிரம் தன்னில் கனவொடு ...) and says the five mala-bonds, concealment first (மறையாதி ஐம்மல பாசமே), produce them, giving the general rule of 2167's table.

2163 says the Lord wakes those sunk in anava through blameless Maya (மாயாள் தன்னாலே எழுப்புமே) without saying how. 2168 names what Maya rouses (மாயை எழுப்பும் கலாதியை): kala, raga and the other tattvas, through which the soul comes into the sakala state.

2169 compares the embodied soul to a blind man who sees only the step ahead and goes with a stick (தடிகொண்டு). 2048 has the blind show the stick to the blind (குருடர்க்குக் கோல்காட்டி) and all fall into the pit. In 2169 the stick is the soul's own limited help; in 2048 it is false guidance by another, so the image marks both partial sight and its danger.

2171 calls the One beyond the tattvas the mad one, the great one, the unborn (பிச்சன் பெரியன் பிறப்பிலி) and is saved by longing for him. 1616 names Siva the unborn (பிறப்பிலி) who eats alms and the mad one (பித்தன்) who cuts off births; the same epithets carry the same claim, that the beggar-god is the one who ends birth.

665 says the airs in ida and pingala (இடையொடு பிங்கலை) stand reversed and their hindrances subside. 2173 takes the same two channels, twists the breath at the root triangle (மூலம் கொண்டு முறுக்கி முக்கோணிலும்) and makes the goal the feet of the Lord of time, carrying the practice of 665 to its object.

A near-repeat: 504 has the same four lines (ஆவன ஆவ அழிவ அழிவன / போவன போவ புகுவ புகுவன ...), differing mainly in the last word (இளங்கிளையோன் for இலங்கிழையோன்). The repetition in chapter 49 and here shows the saying, that what is to come comes and what is to go goes, as one Nandi taught in more than one setting.

2175 says what is to come comes and what is to go goes (போவன போவ புகுவ புகுவன). Kural 376 says what is not yours will not stay though guarded, and what is yours will not leave though thrown away (சொரியினும் போகா தம). Both teach that things run their appointed course; 2175 adds that Nandi showed it.

2179 calls the ninety-six tattvas common to all (பொது என்பர்) and lists each school's own count. Arunagiri asks for the common ground (பொதுவை) that holds all the ninety-six tattvas yet stands free of them, which the six sects (அறுவரும்) quarrel over in anger. Both use பொது for what lies under the schools' counts; Arunagiri makes it the truth itself.

A near-repeat: 2323 has the same four lines with small variants (அறிகின்றிலாதன for அறிவொன்றிலாதன, அருள்செய்தான் for அருள்செய்தார்). Both say the thirty-six tattvas do not know, and the soul learns from Nandi's word 'you are the one who knows' that it is the knower; the verse recurs in the chapter on the stainless state.
2182 removes the five states, the five mala-states and the false thirty-six so that the soul stands as one; 2186 names where that ends, in the dance and in becoming Siva, with the five made Sivaya.

2184 counts the six paths: thirty-six tattvas, mantras, fifty-one letters, worlds, eighty-one words and five kalas. 2782 has 'the six paths of love' (அன்புறு மார்க்கங்கள் ஆறும்) dance with the Lord in the dance of bliss; the paths 2184 counts as the soul's bondage become, in 2782, part of Siva's dance.

2185 says those who study the three regions and follow the path by its marks (குறிவழியே சென்று) are left bewildered after searching (திகைத்திருந்தார்). 2955 asks whether the shore of the shoreless can be seen and says the Lord stands unveiled to those whose thought is clear as waveless water. On the reading of 2185 as failure, 2955 names the condition the searchers lacked.

2186 begins from waking-within-waking and ends in becoming Siva (சிவமாதல்) with the five as சிவாய. 2713 begins 'from ந and from waking' (நமாதி நனாதி) and ends with the syllables and samadhi as becoming Siva (சிவமாதல்); both join the states to the five syllables and end in the same word.

A near-repetition: both place waking, dream, deep sleep and turiya at the brow, throat, heart and navel with fewer instruments in each. They differ in the counts (ஐஐந்தில் against பன்னான்கில்) and in the third line (பொய்கண்ட மூவர் against பொய்கண்டிலாத புருடன்), which may show a corrupt copy in one or both.
audit_text_issue: counts (ஐஐந்தில் vs பன்னான்கில்) and line 3 differ; one or both may be corrupt

note: Both use பசு in its double sense of cattle and bound soul. 2015 sorts the cows by what they yield, only the mature ones giving milk; 2193 makes them all one in their milk and one in their herdsman.
2192 names the three malas and calls for separating the soul from them; 2211 says the Lord gave the tattvas and instruments for exactly that, so that the malas might be cut.

Both make release the end of an obscuring mixture: the Kural's stainless sight, freed from confusion, removes darkness and brings joy; Tirumular says Shakti, knowledge and Siva are hidden by mala and light appears when the mixture ends. Tirumular names what hides; the Kural names only confusion.
Both trace a bad end to delusion: the Kural's confusion that takes the unreal as real yields a joyless birth, and in 2194 the soul whose delusion grows reaches the seven hells.

The Kural guards the five senses with the elephant goad of firmness; Tirumular ends his verse on standing in the true way before the mind scatters with a charging elephant. The pairing holds if 2215's elephant is the mastered senses or mind; if it is the strength one gains, the images only touch.
2209 says that after knowing the knowledge that knows, one becomes that knower; 2224 turns this into a riddle: who can know the knower who knows without knowing?
audit_text_issue: TM 2224 அறியாதவத்தை may divide two ways.

note: 2187 says the twenty-five are the power of bindu (ஐஐந்தும் விந்துவின் சத்தி). 1924 counts the thirty-six the same way, the distinctions of bindu making twenty-five (விந்துபேதத்திறன் ஐ ஐந்தும்) and nada six. 1924 supplies the scheme behind 2187's compressed opening line.
audit_text_issue: 1924's numbers (25, 6, 2x2) do not sum to ஆறுஆறு as written

note: 2188 lays the states within waking on a child's growth: born and lying (பிறந்தார் கிடந்தார்), crawling (தவழ்ந்தார்), walking and growing (நடந்தார் வளர்ந்தார்). Thiruppugazh 110 runs the same stages (பிறந்து, தவழ்ந்து, நடந்து) as a life spent without praising the devotees' feet. The same sequence is a lament of wasted years in the song and, in 2188, a map in which the highest state is the newborn lying still.

2190 and 2191 are near-repeats: both list the tattvas from Siva, Shakti, Sadasiva and Isa down through vidya, kala, time, niyati and mahamaya. 2191 adds raga and purusha and closes the count as six sixes (ஆறாறே), while 2190 ends 'down to the last' (நீதிஈறாக); the differences in order show the list was not fixed in one form.
audit_text_issue: 2190's போதம் and நீதி are non-standard tattva names, possibly corrupt

note: 2192 makes the husk and bran on the grain (முளைக்குத் தவிடுஉமி) the malas round the soul, to be separated (பாசம் பிரித்தே). Naladiyar 221 uses the same husk (நெல்லுக்கு உமியுண்டு) for the faults a chosen friend is born with, which one should bear rather than cast off. The same image argues for removal in the one and for forbearance in the other.

2197 counts the tattvas that withdraw as waking passes into dream and sleep: twenty-five of the thirty-six, then six, then five more (ஆறாறில் ஐஐந்து ... ஆறாம் ... வேறான ஐந்தும்). 2208 gives the same twenty-five, six and five (ஐஐந்தும் ஆறும்ஓர் ஐந்தும்) as waking, dream and deep sleep within waking. 2208 is a near-repeat that names what lies beyond them, turiya.

2204 calls turiya within deep sleep the void where words end (சொல்லறும் பாழே). 2483 places the experience at the end in the three voids where words end (சொல்லறும் முப்பாழில்). The shared phrase shows that Tirumular's பாழ் is a positive state beyond speech, not mere blankness.

2206 defines the four states as states of knowing: knowledge knowing knowledge is waking, knowledge reaching unknowing (அறிவுஅறியாமை) is dream and sleep, knowledge become knowledge is turiya. 2224 asks who can know the knower who knows by joining the unknowing state (அறியாது அறிவானை யார்அறிவாரே). 2224 turns 2206's scheme into the question of the knower himself.

2207 has the soul leave the five malas (ஐம்மலம் தான்விட்டு), take knowledge as its form and rise beyond the subtle. 2401 has the beginningless soul free of the five malas (ஐம்மலமற்று) see itself and become Hara, beyond the tattvas. Both name five malas, not three, and both make their loss the soul's passing beyond.
audit_text_issue: 2401's வினாவு may be a misprint for விரவு.

note: 2195 sets the beyond-state that does not know itself down as anava (தன்தெரியாத அதீதம்தற்கு ஆணவம்). 2212 agrees that in waking-atita anava is in its own truth, but adds that when that atita reaches turiya the truth of the Supreme abides there (பரன்உண்மை தங்குமே). So atita is anava's only for the bound; the same state can hold the Supreme.

2212 says that in waking-atita, once it reaches turiya, the truth of the Supreme abides (சாக்கிராதீதம் பரன்உண்மை தங்குமே). 2265 says that if the beyond-state is reached within waking (சாக்கிரத் தன்னில் அதீதம் தலைப்படில்) there is bliss, birth is cut off and release attained. 2265 states the fruit of the state 2212 defines.

2214 puts five elephant calves (ஆனைக்கன்று ஐந்து) in the divided heart among other beasts. 977 has five elephants in the forest tamed with the five letters as goad (அஞ்சுக்கும் அஞ்செழுத்து அங்குசம்). Tirumular's other use of five elephants for the senses supports reading 2214's animals as the faculties, and shows what 2214 leaves untamed.

2217 has the teacher take on the rules beginning with niyama (நியமாதிகள் உற்று), pass to turiya-atita and become the Supreme, stainless (பரனாய் நின்மலனாமே). 2376 defines yoganta the same way: going past yama, niyama and the rest (இயம நியமாதி சென்றகன்று) into samadhi, the soul becoming the Supreme (சீவன் பரமாக). 2376 names as an end of yoga the passage 2217 narrates through the states.

2218 ends with the soul leaving the pure tattvas, becoming Siva and reaching silence (சிவமாகி மோனம் அடைந்து). 2382 ends the six ends the same way: when the knower and knowledge subside, the clear silence becomes Siva's bliss (தேறிய மோனம் சிவானந்தமாமே). The ascent through the states and the ascent through the ends close in the same silence.

2222 sets a lamp burning at the root (மூலத்தானத்தில் அவ்விளக்கு) that takes in the moon region above. 345 turns the one who blazes at the root opening upward to the upper opening (மூலத் துவாரத்து மூளும் ஒருவனை மேலைத் துவாரத்து) and burns Death. Both describe a fire lit at the base and joined to what is above; 345 names the fruit.

2223 answers where the inner space is: look up (அண்ணாந்து பார்த்து) to the junction where the five gather. 588 likewise has the yogi look up through the spine into the space above (வெளியுறத் தானோக்கி) with eyes that do not see. Both make the upward gaze into inner space the practice, with the senses drawn in.

Both say a person is the maker of his own rise and fall: the Naladiyar names who sets a man up and casts him down and answers 'himself', Tirumular says he is his own enemy, friend, next world and master.
The Kural traces joyless birth to taking the unreal for the real; Tirumular's first error is the same kind, taking the body for the self, and it too ends in birth again.
2014 has the soul enter turiya and become knowledge; 2264 adds that turiya not joined to the Lord still leads back to birth.
Near-repetition: both open with the two deeds balancing and grace-power coming as or through the guru, and end with the impurities removed, as becoming Siva in 1527 and as non-birth here.
audit_text_issue: 2262 இருவிடை is evidently a slip for இருவினை.

note: 1924's numbers for the thirty-six tattvas do not add up as read; 2267 gives the standard grouping clearly, twenty-four impure, seven pure-impure and five pure.
audit_text_issue: 1924's counts (ஐ ஐந்து, ஆறு, ஈரிரண்டு) do not sum to ஆறுஆறு; a number may be corrupt

note: 2228 makes the soul answerable for itself: it eats the fruit of the deeds it did and is its own master (தானே தான்செய்த வினைப்பயன் துய்ப்பானும், தானே தனக்குத் தலைவனும்). 2628 says that in bondage and in release alike the soul has no task of its own (பெத்தத்தும் தன்பணி இல்லை ... முத்தத்தும் தன்பணி இல்லை), since the Father gives both by grace. The conflict holds if 2228's தலைவன் makes the soul master of its own bondage and release, not only answerable inside it.

The Kural says that one who loves himself should go near no evil deed, however small (தன்னைத்தான் காதலனாயின்). 2228 states the ground of that advice: the self is its own friend and enemy and itself eats the fruit of the deeds it did (தானே தனக்குப் பகைவனும் நட்டானும்).

Both verses list the sakalas, those joined to the three impurities, from Brahma and the gods through men down to the insect (மலரோன்மால் ... நரர் சீடம் / வேதா ... கீடாந்தத்து). 2244 adds that the sakalas enter the womb (யோனிபுக்கு), so the near-repeat ties the three impurities to birth.

Both verses place the hundred and eight Rudras (நூற்றெட்டு உருத்திரர்) among souls still in maya, 2231 with Srikantha in the pralaya class, 2243 in the sakala of anava, karma and mahamaya. The shared figure shows the chapter counting even high Rudras among bound souls, though the two verses do not settle which class they belong to.

2232 says those in kevala with anava alone are the vijnanakalas, Ananta and the other lords (கேவலத்து ஆணவத்து ஆனவர்). 498 opens its scheme the same way (விஞ்ஞானர் ஆணவ கேவல மேவுவோர்), from a chapter on the kinds of soul far earlier in the book.
audit_text_issue: 498: second விஞ்ஞானர் may be a slip for pralayakalas

note: 1929 makes bindu, joined with Shakti and Siva, the power that grants release (வீடுஅளிக்கும் செயல்). 2233 says those graced by Siva leave bindu and nada behind as the impurity goes (விந்து நாதம் விட்டு) and so become stainless. The conflict holds on the reading that 2233 treats bindu as something release must leave, not as its giver.

115 says the soul and its bond cannot go to the Lord, but when the Lord draws near they do not remain (பதியணுகிற் பசு பாசம் நில்லாவே). 2234 ends on the same act: the Lord gathers the impurities and cuts them away (ஈசன் மலம் அறுத்தானே). In both the removal of the bond is the Lord's doing, not the soul's.

2235 calls the suddha state the soul's leaving the false thirty-six behind (பொய்யான போதாந்தம் ஆறாறும் விட்டகன்று) and reaching without reaching. 2308 says the good soul in turiya does not go into the evil thirty-six (பொல்லாத ஆறாறுள் போகாது) but reaches Siva's state. Both define purity as standing clear of the thirty-six tattvas.

2405 sets three things without beginning: the knowing soul, the Lord and the bond (அனாதி), and says birth ends when the soul rests in the Lord. 2236 repeats அனாதி for the soul, its five impurities, kevala and its births, yet ends in the suddha state. Together they show beginningless bondage is not endless.

2237 calls knowing oneself by oneself within turiya the reality itself (தன்பால் தனையறி தத்துவந் தானே). 2279 warns that birth does not end merely by knowing oneself (தன்னை அறிந்தும் பிறவி தணவாதால்), and points to the pervading Stainless one. The later verse puts a condition on the earlier: self-knowledge in turiya must go on to the Lord.

2238 says the twenty-five subside in the soul and the soul, seeing truth, finds release in the suddha state (ஐஐந்து ஒடுங்கும் ஆன்மாவில்). 2306 takes the step further: if the soul is Hara's son, the soul as a separate thing is gone and so are the twenty-five (ஆன்மாவும் இல்லையால் ஐஐந்தும் இல்லையே).

2197 counts the tattvas withdrawing in stages, the twenty-five and then the six, to make waking, dream and deep sleep (ஆறாறில் ஐஐந்து அகல ... ஆறாம் அவைவிட). 2239 uses the same count, the twenty-five with the six subsiding into the soul (ஐஐந்தும் ஆன்மாவில் ஆறோடு அடங்கி), but carries it past the states to Shakti in Siva's portion.

2192 names the three impurities, anava, maya and karma, and likens them to the bran and husk on the grain of the soul. 2240 sorts beings by how many of these they bear: anava alone for the kevalas, maya for the pralayakalas, all three for the sakalas (முப்பாசமும் புக்கோரே).

2245 has the bonds, the maddening darkness, let go by the ray that is Siva (மத்த இருள் சிவனான கதிராலே). 2293 has the five impurities leave like evening dark before a flame (சுடர்முனம் அந்தி இருள்போலும் ஐம்மலம்). Both picture purification as darkness giving way to light, the light in each being grace.

The Kural says stainless sight removes darkness and confusion and brings joy (இருள்நீங்கி ... மாசறு காட்சி). 2245 also has darkness end and purity come (மத்த இருள் ... சுத்தஆவார்கள்), but the light that ends it is Siva's ray, not the seer's own clear sight.

2247 describes kevala as the soul without knowledge, without action and pervaded by impurity (அறிவின்றி ... செயலிலான் ... மலவியாபி). 2162 calls the same state anava's sleep of utter stupor (அதிமூட நித்திரை ஆணவம்). Both make kevala a blank, not a freedom.

2249 says kevala, sakala and suddha each divide into three, making an unceasing nine (ஓவலில்லா ஒன்பான்). 498 likewise ends by counting the kinds of soul as nine (விஞ்ஞானராதிகள் ஒன்பான் வேறுயிர்களே). Both reach a ninefold scheme from the three states, 2249 by states within states, 498 by classes of soul.
audit_text_issue: 498 line 2 repeats விஞ்ஞானர் where Pralayakalas are expected

note: 2250 says that in the suddha within kevala, the Lord is there as the form of grace (ஆவயின் நாதன் அருண்மூர்த்தி). 2312 has the Father, with a grace that makes no division, stay joined to the soul left in kevala (வேறுசெய்யா அருள் கேவலத்தே விட்டு). Both find the Lord present by grace even in kevala.

2251 names kevala within sakala as the state beyond waking (சகலத்தில் கேவலம் சாக்கிராதீதம்). 2265 says what that state brings when reached: bliss, the end of birth and firm release beyond speech and mind (சாக்கிரத் தன்னில் அதீதம் தலைப்படில்).

2252 calls kevala within suddha the ancient stillness (சுத்தத்தில் கேவலம் தொல்லுபசாந்தமாம்). 2509, in the chapter named for that stillness, sets out what உபசாந்தம் contains: removing anava, knowing oneself, purity and the state beyond waking.

2254 says that in the state beyond waking anava itself is cut off (சாக்கிராதீதத்தில் தானறும் ஆணவம்). 2212 says that in that same state anava does not leave (சாக்கிராதீதத்தில் ஆணவம் தான்விடா). The conflict depends on reading both as the same state at the same stage; 2212 may mean the state before grace completes it.

2254 links the state beyond waking, where anava is cut off, with the stillness that looks on the impurities (உபசாந்தத்தை நோக்கும்). 2509 defines that stillness as removing anava and reaching the unspoken state beyond waking (கூறாத சாக்கிராதீதம் ... உபசாந்தமே).

2255 says that once one knows bondage and release are the Father's grace, there is no mind and no action of one's own (சித்தமும் இல்லை செயல்இல்லை). 2628 says the same from devotion: since the Father gives both bondage and release by grace, the devotee has no task (பணியொன்றும் இல்லையே).

2256 says bondage and release both come by Hara's grace (பெத்தமும் முத்தமும் ... அரன் அருளே). 2628 makes the same claim (அத்தற்கு இரண்டும் அருளால் அளித்தலால்) in the chapter on devotion, where it becomes the reason the devotee need do nothing.

2257 says those with five impurities go even on the path to heaven (ஐம்மலத்தார் சுவர்க்கந்நெறி யான்பவர்). 2337 says those still in the darkness of the five impurities go from earth to heaven and hell (பாரின்கண் விண்நரகம் புகும்), while those freed become Siva. Both count heaven as a place of the bound, not of release.

2258 says maya mixes the states into the soul in the womb, beginning with the beyond state and turiya (கருவில் அதீதம் கலப்பிக்கும் மாயை). 460 likewise has maya, in the womb, join her brood to the kevala soul and break turiya so thought arises (கர்ப்பத்துக் ... துரியமும் பேதித்து). Both place the soul's states in its embryonic beginning.

2259 matches the five impurities to five states: concealment in waking, mahamaya in dream, karma in deep sleep, maya in turiya, anava beyond. 2167 gives the same matches inside waking (திரோதாயி, மாமாயை, காமியம், மாயை), so the two verses apply one scheme at two scales.

2259 places maya in turiya and karma in deep sleep (பூணும் துரியம் ... சுழுத்திபொய்க் காமியம்). 2195 places karma in turiya (துரியம் சொல் காமியம்) and desire in deep sleep. Both agree that anava belongs beyond, but on the reading that each assigns one impurity per state, their turiya differs.

2144 lists what makes the bound waking state: the senses, their objects, the airs, the four inner instruments and the soul (பந்தஅச் சாக்கரம்). 2261 lists the sakala soul's equipment in nearly the same terms, body, elements, mind and the objects beginning with sound (சத்தாதி), and ends with entry into the womb.

The Kural defines purity as the absence of craving, which comes by wanting truth (தூஉய்மை என்பது அவாவின்மை). 2262 defines purity as non-birth (பிறவாமை சுத்தமே), reached when the two deeds balance, grace descends and the guru removes the great impurity. The verse puts purity's cause in grace, where the Kural puts it in the person's own ending of desire.

2263 has the soul pass the tattvas and states to the beyond-turiya, where supreme Siva comes to dwell in it (பரம்சிவம் ஆதேயமாகுமே). 2539 describes the end of the nine states the same way, with Siva-knowledge taking the place of the scattered impurities and the self becoming itself and not itself (நவமான அந்தத்தின் நற்சிவ போதம்).

A near-repeat: both open with the soul once taking the body as itself (உடலைமுன் தான்என்றான் / உடலைமுன் நான்ஒன்றாய்) and then seeing turiya. 2264 says turiya not made one with the Lord leads to rebirth; 2279 says birth does not end by self-knowledge alone. Both warn against stopping at the self.

2265 says that if the beyond is reached within waking, birth is cut off and release is firm (சாக்கிரத் தன்னில் அதீதம் தலைப்படில் ... நோன்முத்தி). 2302 places purity in the same faultless state beyond waking (தீதறு சாக்கிராதீதத்தில் சுத்தமே). Both set release inside the waking life, not after it.

Both verses play on water and fire (அப்பும் அனலும்) and their mixing (கலந்தது / கலப்பும்) as a riddle. 2581 adds that only the Knower present within makes one know it. The pairing suggests the riddle of 2266 is meant to be solved by inner teaching, not by reckoning.

2179 says the thirty-six are the Saivas' tattvas, against the counts of other schools (ஆறாறு அருஞ்சைவர் தத்துவம்). 2267 sets out how those thirty-six divide: twenty-four impure, seven pure-impure and five pure (அறுநான்கு அசுத்தம் ... ஐந்தே சுத்தம்).

Both use the figure of a child raised by a foster-mother (செவிலி / கைத்தாய்). In the Kural grace, born of love, is nursed by wealth; in 2268 the soul, born of mahamaya with Siva as father, is raised by maya. In both the nurse is a lower thing that serves a higher end.
Paired images of mutual concealment: gold and ornament for the soul and its faculties, wood and carved elephant for the Lord and the elements.
2288 makes knowing oneself the way to know the Lord; 2279 adds that knowing oneself alone doesn't end birth unless one knows the pervading Lord.
Both play on பற்று: the Kural bids one cling to the one without clinging in order to let go, Tirumular says the Supreme is grasped as attachment ends.

2269 says the beginningless Lord stayed in concealment (வஞ்சத்து இருந்த) so as to set body and soul apart; 111 says he stands hidden (கரத்தினுள் நின்று) and works dissolution (கழிவுசெய்தானே). Both make the parting of body and soul, or the world's dissolution, the work of a Lord who acts while unseen.

2275 says that when maya's confusion ends past breath and mind, pure knowledge itself becomes Siva's bliss (தூய அறிவு சிவானந்தமாகி); 1587 says Siva-knowledge gives Siva's bliss (சிவமான ஞானம் சிவானந்தம் நல்குமே). The two make knowledge, not practice alone, the thing that turns into bliss.

In 121 வியாக்கிரத்தே, read as 'in waking', is where pure turiya arises; in 2276 the soul on turiya's horse is put inside the great வியாக்கிரம், read as 'tiger'. The pairing suggests 2276's tiger may also be a play on waking, which fits the chapter's teaching that turiya is reached within waking.

2277 says that when the Lord of the hall marries the soul, maya vanishes and the soul becomes his form (அவன்வடிவாமே); 2013 says souls who practised of old will later see and take Siva's form within (சிவனுருக் கொள்வர்). Both name the end as the soul taking Siva's form, 2277 through union and 2013 through long practice.

2279 says birth does not end even when one knows oneself (தன்னை அறிந்தும் பிறவி தணவாதால்), so one must know the pervading Stainless One; 2331 says birth ends (பிறப்பறும்) when one knows oneself and becomes oneself with Siva (சிவனுடன் தானாக). 2331 supplies the condition 2279 says self-knowledge lacks: union with Siva.

2280 says that once those who have the guru's boon (குருவரம்) unite, the two are gone and they stand as one; 1608 says Nandi changed the thirty-six in him and made him Siva (சிவமாக்கி). Both make the guru the one who ends the division between soul and Lord.

Both verses use the same scheme and words: the soul's turiya (அணுவின் துரியம்) holding the lower states, and a para-turiya tied to பணி (பணியில் பரதுரியம் in 2281, பணியும் பரதுரியம் in 2468). 2468, in a distant chapter, is a near-restatement of 2281 that adds how the two sets of four combine into five.

2282 sets waking, a dream that swallows the world, peace and deep sleep inside para-turiya, ending in Siva's turiya; 2444 says that in para-turiya waking is absorbed (பரதுரியத்து நனவு படியுண்ட), dream spreads, and calm (உபசாந்தம்) leads to the rare turiya at Siva. 2444, in a distant chapter, is a near-repeat of the scheme in 2282 and 2283.

2282 maps the states within para-turiya (பரதுரியத்து) on the way to Siva's turiya. Thiruppugazh 203 asks for the light beyond the thirty-six and beyond para-turiya (பரதுரி யாதீதம்), which it says no master of yoga reaches. Arunagiri uses the Tirumanthiram's technical grade பரதுரியம் and places the goal past it.

2283 is a near-variant of 2282: both run waking, a dream that has eaten the world (சகமுண்ட / சகம் உண்ட கனவு), deep sleep and calm up to Siva's turiya (சிவதுரியத்தனும் ஆமே). 2283 adds that reaching these is renunciation (துறவே).

2284 says Nandi stood having freed the soul from the நாலேழ் (twenty-eight) after the ten states cease; 2176 counts the twenty-eight tattvas (தத்துவ நாலேழ்), including turiya and the higher turiya. Read with 2176, 2284's obscure count may be these tattvas, from which the soul is released.

2285 says the sushumna (கழுமுனை) ends the distress of the spreading dream within the supreme waking of Para; 2444 places the sushumna (துரிய கழுமுனை) in the calm of para-turiya, before cessation at Siva. Both put the yogic channel inside the higher states, not only in breath practice.

2286 lists Siva's descending forms: Paramasiva, Shakti, supreme nada, bindu and Sadasiva, then Brahma, Hari, Rudra and Isa; 384 gives the same order of emergence, light becoming Shakti, nada becoming bindu, and Sadasiva as support of the five elements. 384 shows the sequence in 2286 is a creation sequence.

2288 says that if one knows oneself (தன்னை அறியில்) the compassionate Supreme is our Lord, and the speaker came to joy by setting out to know himself; 2349 says the one who knows himself within himself goes on to know his Lord within himself (தன் ஐ அறியத் தலைப்படும்). Both make self-knowledge the way to knowing the Lord.

Both use gold and its ornaments. 1087 says the many gods are like the many ornaments (பூணும் பலபல பொன்போல) that are all gold, to show one Mistress as cause; 2289 says the ornament hides the gold (பொன்னை மறைத்தது பொன்னணி பூடணம்), to show how the faculties hide the soul. The same image teaches unity in 1087 and concealment in 2289.

2291 reads the mantra as a path: dropping நம, the soul rises as ய and release comes in சிவாய; 979 says சிவாய, joined, becomes the soul, enjoyment and knowledge, and becoming Siva by it is release (அச்சிவம் ஆவது வீடே). 2291 spells out the letter-by-letter path to the release that 979 names.

2293 says the five malas leave like evening darkness before a flame (சுடர்முனம் அந்தி இருள்போலும் ஐம்மலம் மாறுமே); Naladiyar 51 says sin cannot stand before austerity, as darkness dies when a lamp enters (விளக்குப் புக இருள் மாய்ந்தாங்கு). The same image does the work of grace in one verse and of tapas in the other, and the Naladiyar adds that darkness returns when the oil runs out.

1517 says Nandi, wrapped in grace, comes into the confusion of delusion like a lamp brought into a dark room (இருள்சூழ் அறையில்... விளக்கு); 2293 says that by grace (அருளால்) the malas leave like darkness before a flame. Both verses use the image of light and darkness for grace.

2295 says the Lord of nada left me and went there yet did not go (சென்றான்... செல்லாமையும்); 1628 says he is hidden yet not hidden (கரந்துங் கரந்திலன்). Both describe the Lord's presence as a paradox of being both gone and present.

2296 maps sattva, rajas and tamas onto waking, dream and deep sleep and makes the gunaless state stainless turiya; 2538 says that when the states from waking are let go, unattached to the birth-bound malas and gunas (மலங்குணம் பற்றற்று), the twofold turiya becomes the true form. 2538 turns 2296's map into a practice of release.

2297 says the cosmic eggs are as many as the sand of the seven seas (எறிகடல் ஏழின் மணல்அளவாக) and the Lord sits on them as his seat; 1149 praises Shakti who shapes the countless eggs (அண்டகோடிகள்) within. The countless eggs are the Lord's seat in one verse and Shakti's work in the other.

2299 assigns nectar, bliss, Om and the body to the fifth, seventh, ninth and eleventh stations; 648 assigns Rudra to the tenth, the eight siddhis to the eleventh and all-pervasion to the twelfth. Both count numbered stations of yogic practice but give the eleventh different fruits, and neither verse names the stations.
audit_text_issue: 648 first words vary across copies; 2299 முஞ்சில் obscure

note: Both place the giving up of anger where one has the power to act on it: the Kural says restraint counts only where anger can take effect, Tirumular says let it go while you can still win.
audit_text_issue: 2303 line 2 செலுத்துமிஹ் has a stray ஹ் (likely செலுத்துமிச்).

note: 2302 says that when one sees oneself (தனைக்கண்டால்) spread through the kevala, sakala and leaving conditions, the three cease and purity (சுத்தமே) follows; 2237 says that within the suddha state, beyond kevala, one knows oneself by oneself (தன்பால் தனையறி). Both make seeing oneself the mark of the pure state.

Both use the tortoise drawing in its five. The Kural makes restraint of the senses in one birth a shelter through seven; Tirumular puts the tortoise in a silent well and promises it a thousand years if it withdraws into truth.

Both treat the five senses as elephants to be mastered (in the Kural through the goad of firmness, as Parimelazhagar reads it). The Kural's reward is the field of release; Tirumular adds a lamp of knowledge lit inside the body.
The Kural defines understanding as seeing the true thing in whatever thing appears; Tirumular narrows it to knowing oneself, and calls every other knowing a ghoul's.
251 says those who know themselves bow to the Lord and find him kin; 2318 says such self-knowing is the only knowledge that counts.
2323 has Nandi tell the soul it is the knower; 2329 adds that the soul does not know by itself and knows only when grace illumines it.
Both use fire and its heat. In 2309 the heat left in iron after the fire is gone is karma's residue; in 2341 heat inseparable from fire is grace inseparable from the Lord.

417 makes the Lord the potter who shapes pots and births; 2351 likens him instead to the one clay in all vessels, and to the eye that sees all but itself. The two images give maker and inner presence.

2305 says that for those who can run past the five elements and their gods, காலனும் இல்லை, there is no Death. Kural 269 says those who have gained the power of austerity can even leap past Death (கூற்றம் குதித்தலும் கைகூடும்). Both make Death something a disciplined person passes beyond; the Kural names the means as tapas, the Tirumanthiram as passing through the elements.

2307 places the soul's fulfilment in turiya: held by the Lord there (பற்றாம் துரியத்து) it becomes supremely auspicious. Thiruppugazh 1049 says the abode of supreme wisdom is not reached even above turiya (துரிய மீது சாராது). The conflict holds on the reading that 2307's turiya is the goal itself; if 2307 describes only a stage, as later verses of the chapter suggest, the two agree.

2308 says that dwelling in turiya the soul does not go into the evil thirty-six (பொல்லாத ஆறாறு) and reaches Siva's state. Thiruppugazh 203 also seeks a light beyond the thirty-six (ஆறாறின் அதிகம்) but places it beyond turiya (பர துரியாதீதம்), past what yogis reach. The song keeps the Tirumanthiram's terms and moves the goal one step further.

2309 says that in turiya, even with the instruments gone, the stain of karma stays, like heat in iron taken from the fire. 2279 says birth does not end merely by knowing oneself in turiya (தன்னை அறிந்தும் பிறவி தணவாதால்). Both verses, in the chapters on the states, refuse to make turiya by itself the end of bondage.

Both use iron changed by a process. In 2309 iron taken from the fire keeps its heat (வாய்ந்த கனலென வாதனை), so the old state lingers; in 2051 iron turned to gold never becomes iron again (மறித்து இரும்பாகா), so the new state is final. Together they set karma's residue against the guru's grace as two kinds of lasting change.

2309 warns that in turiya, where the instruments have died (கரணம் இறந்த), karma's stain stays. Thiruppugazh 1055 asks for a state beyond turiya (துரிய மேற்படு) that has left the instruments (கருவி கரண நீத்த), and implies that Kama's arrows cannot strike there. Read together, the song places beyond turiya the immunity that 2309 denies to turiya itself.

Thiruppugazh 1218 asks the Lord to separate Pati, pasu and pasam each from each without stain (வேறு வேறு செய்தருள்வாயே) so the poet may find the way. 2312 uses the same verb four times: the Lord separates (வேறுசெய்தான்) and then, with a grace that does not separate (வேறுசெய்யா அருள்), stays joined with the soul. The verse carries the song's plea one step on: discrimination is followed by union.

2313 pictures the soul in its malam turning endlessly like waves on the sea (கடலில் திரை) through heaven, hell and earth, freed only by grace. Kural 10 says only those who reach the Lord's feet swim the great sea of births. Both make release from the round of births depend on the Lord, and both use the sea for it.

2314 says that when the soul becomes Siva, malam, bonds and gunas fade like the moon before the sun. Naladiyar 51 says sin cannot stand before austerity as darkness dies when a lamp comes in, but darkness rushes back when the oil runs out. The Naladiyar's lamp limits the victory to the life of the merit that feeds it; the Tirumanthiram's sun is the Siva-state itself and has no oil to run out.

2315 says fire, water, air, sun, moon, Mal, Brahma and Rudra's light are all within the heart (உள்ளத்துளாரே). 1823 makes the heart the great temple (உள்ளம் பெருங்கோயில்) and the body the shrine. 2315 places the cosmos and its gods in the heart; 1823 turns the same inner space into a place of worship.

2316 tells the one who tames the five senses to light the wick of knowledge (ஞானத் திரி) and look into the flesh until its darkness goes. 2367 sets the lamps of maya and of the body, which go out or smoulder, against the pure lamp and a distant lamp the speaker seeks. Both put the body's light against knowledge's light; 2367 adds that even the pure lamp is not the end of the search.

2318 says the ancient austerity of former understanding (முன்னை அறிவு) is known when later understanding (பின்னை அறிவு) comes, and that knowing oneself is knowledge. 2288 uses the same pair: knowing oneself through the truth of austerity known afterwards, and coming to joy when former knowledge ends. The two are close variants in different chapters, and 2288 names the Lord found by that self-knowing.

2319 says that being without action (செயலற்றிருக்க) is Siva's bliss, and that those who rest so do not even seek Siva-yoga. 2635 calls simply staying still (சும்மா இருந்திடம்), maya left and the self hidden, the test. Both make the end a stillness beyond effort, even spiritual effort.

1678 defines the Siva garb as those who, free of delusion and desire, rest without action (செயலற்றிருப்பார் சிவவேடத்தாரே). 2319 uses the same phrase four times and calls that rest Siva's bliss. The Siva-garb chapter makes it the mark of the true ascetic; 2319 makes it the state itself.

724 says the body must be kept because without it true knowledge cannot be firmly gained (உடம்பை வளர்த்தேன் உயிர் வளர்த்தேனே). 2320 says that after the samadhi in which one becomes Him, malam is cut and the flawless body (ஈனமில் காயம்) stays on earth. 724 keeps the body for the sake of knowledge; 2320 shows the body that remains once that knowledge is reached.

2322 says that under the one Shakti who surrounds bondage and release the soul is now bewildered and now clear (மான்றும் தெருண்டும்). 2336 says Shakti first feeds the soul's desire and then withers it (ஊட்டி ... வாட்டி) to bring it to the high state. Both give one power both the binding and the freeing.

In 2323 Nandi tells the speaker 'you are the one who knows' (அறிகின்றாய் நீ), and he comes to know himself as the knower. In 2357 Nandi teaches him that knowledge is his form (அறிவு வடிவு), and he remains as that form. The two are close variants: the guru does not add knowledge but shows the soul its own nature as knowing.
audit_text_issue: 2357 அருந்திருந்தானே is odd, as the marker notes.

note: 2324 ends a list of Siva and Shakti with one verb: they were seen within the flesh (ஊனிடைக் கண்டதே). 1823 calls the body of flesh the Lord's shrine (ஊனுடம்பு ஆலயம்). Both place the Lord in the flesh, which is honoured, not despised.

2326 says that when the soul ends in Hara's grace and feels itself as awareness, the Lord's end is reached, and calls this the great saying (மகாவாக்கியம்) without naming it. 2402 names it: knowing soul and Siva is 'thou art that' (தொந்தத்தசி), and action ceasing, the soul becomes knowledge and subsides. 2402 supplies the saying 2326 points to and reads it as both Vedanta and Siddhanta.

2327 says there is no need to teach those already full of knowledge (அறிவிற் செறிவோர்); the wise teach only those who have learned and stand in unknowing. Kural 718 says speaking before those who understand (உணர்வது உடையார்) is like watering a crop that is already growing. On Parimelazhagar's reading, that such speech makes the growth greater, the two disagree on whether the knowing are worth addressing; on the plain reading that the watering is redundant, they agree.

2328 joins sat, asat and sadasat, sets the conscious and inert in Siva's consciousness (சித்தும் அசித்தும் சிவசித்ததாய்), and names a state where pure and impure do not begin. 2058 uses the same three and the same pairs: the guru shows sat, asat and sadasat, sets சித்தும் அசித்தும் in Siva, and speaks a word beyond சுத்தம் அசுத்தம். The two are a near-repeat; 2058 makes the doctrine the guru's teaching, 2328 the state of the pure.

2330 says that in tattva-knowledge (தத்துவ ஞானம்), as the self becomes Him, its bliss begins. 2611 says the knowers of tattva who know themselves (தத்துவ ஞானிகள்) untie former karma and crush later karma by Siva's grace. 2611 shows what that knowledge does to karma; 2330 what it becomes.

2331: knowing oneself and becoming one with Siva, malam and the gunas die and birth ends (பிறப்பறும்). 2369: removing the great malam, knowing oneself and abiding in the ancient Lord, birth does not come again (வாரா பிறப்பே). The same sequence of self-knowledge, loss of malam and end of birth closes two neighbouring chapters.

2332 says the silent sages (மோனிகள்) obtained the seal of knowledge (ஞானத்து முத்திரை). Thiruppugazh 1112 asks to attain the silence that is the seal (முத்திரையா மோனம்), beyond the thirty-six tattvas and the instruments. The song uses the Tirumanthiram's pairing of silence and seal as the goal of its plea.
audit_text_issue: Thiruppugazh 1112 line 5 has a corrupt glyph (மொட்டலர்வா஡ணச).

note: 1540 calls Nandi far and near (சேயன் அணியன்), pure to those who can look without wavering. 2335 explains the pair: whatever one says of the Lord he is far beyond far (தூராகி தூரம்), but understood quickly he is the life of life. 2335 makes speech the cause of the distance and understanding the cause of the nearness.

Kural 370 says that giving up craving, never satisfied, at once gives a nature that never shifts (ஆரா இயற்கை அவாநீப்பின் ... பேரா இயற்கை தரும்). 2336 says the soul's desire is withered by knowledge and so reaches the high state, but adds that the same Shakti first fed that desire (உயிரிச்சை யூட்டி). The Kural states the result; the Tirumanthiram makes both the craving and its ending the work of one power.

2337 ends: no one sees that heaven, hell and earth, through which the bound go, are grace (அவையருள்). 2544 says the Lord set hell, heaven and endless births for souls by grace (உயிர்க்கு அருளால் வைத்தான்) to make the unclear mind clear. Both make even hell part of grace; 2544 says what it is for.

2319 says that those who rest without action are the ones who have the work done (செய்தியுண்டாமே). 2338 says that whatever those who have reached do, through the Shaktis of maya, knowledge and the world, is the Lord's grace (இறையருள் தானே). 2338 explains the paradox of 2319: the freed act, but the acts are not theirs.

2339 says the reformed leave hell, leave splendid heaven too (திருவார் சுவர்க்கம்), and become Siva. Kural 346 says one who cuts off 'I' and 'mine' enters a world higher than the gods' (வானோர்க்கு உயர்ந்த உலகம்). Both place the goal above heaven; the Tirumanthiram says outright that heaven must be left.

2337 says no one sees that heaven, hell and the darkness of malam are grace. 2340 says that when the vain and Siva (அவமும் சிவமும்) are known through grace, both become his grace. 2340 states as a rule of knowing what 2337 states of the soul's journeys: what is seen through grace is grace.

2342 says one sun opens some flowers and not others according to their deeds, so grace divides without dividing (பேதித்தப் பேதியா). 248 says one rain feeds sweet trees and the bitter kanjirai alike. The same pattern of one undivided giver and many different receivers appears for grace and for rain; 2342 puts the difference in the receivers' karma.

Thiruppugazh 207 has the poet dance like a string-puppet (பாவை ... கயிறுவிதம்) driven by his two deeds, a picture of misery. 2344 uses the false puppet made to dance by the deed (பொய்க்கரி யாட்டும் வினை) for the Lord moving the elements, and calls it Hara's grace that settles the soul. The same image is a complaint in the song and a theology of grace in the verse.

564 speaks of a horse the lord of the five rides to salvation, traditionally the breath, which throws the false. 2346 makes the horse Siva-knowledge (சிவஞான மா), mounted and spurred to leap across to Siva. The same mount carries the soul in both, breath in the yoga chapter and knowledge here.

2347 lists siddhas and those in samadhi (சித்தர் சமாதியர்) among those who have reached the Lord. Thiruppugazh 1016 lists the nine siddhas in their caves (குகையில் நவநாதர்) first among those who do not know him. The conflict holds if the siddhas are the same class in both; the song may mean siddhas who rely on their powers, which 2347 does not praise.

2279 says birth does not end merely by knowing oneself (தன்னை அறிந்தும் பிறவி தணவாது); the pervading Stainless must be known. 2349 says the one who knows himself within himself sets out to know his Lord within, and without resting in himself the Lord is hard to reach. Together they make self-knowledge necessary but not sufficient.

704 speaks of the yogi who sees at the juncture how the moon meets the sun. 2350 says that the one who works as two lights (இருசுடர்) comes as one light within the heart. Both join the two lights; 704 as a yogic seeing, 2350 as the Lord's coming to one who said 'I cannot know'.

1540 says people bewildered by the deceiver (மாயன் மயக்கிய மானுடர்) do not know what the body is for. 2354 says that while the Lady of the gods holds them bewildered (மயக்கத்து உறநிற்க), people who think they know do not know their own birth and death. Both trace this ignorance of the body and its life to a divine bewildering.
1512 defines Saivam as knowing oneself and reaching Siva; 2355 opens the chapter on knowledge with the same claim from the other side: not to know oneself is ruin.
2355 states the rule that knowing oneself brings no harm; 2366 tells it as the speaker's own history, from long not knowing to a knowing after which nothing else is known.

The Kural sets understanding against the folly (பேதைமை) that is birth. Tirumular says the knowledge that frees lies beyond both the world's knowledge and its ignorance, so the line falls not between them but past them.
Both make understanding a kind of total possession: the Kural says those with it have everything, Tirumular that their heart is the wide world itself and the place where the first Lord stays.

2357 says Nandi taught that knowledge is one's form (அறிவு வடிவு) and the speaker remained as that form. Thiruppugazh 1016 asks to know that the Lord's holy body is knowledge beyond knowing and not-knowing (அறிவு திருமேனி). Both treat knowledge as a form, not a possession; the song gives the form to the Lord, the verse to the realised self.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 2357 ends in the odd அருந்திருந்தானே.

note: Kural 400 calls learning the wealth that does not perish (கேடில் விழுச்செல்வம்). 2358 says knowledge has neither destruction nor making (அழிவில்லை ஆக்கமும் இல்லை) and rests on nothing but itself. Both praise what cannot be lost, but the Kural's learning is acquired while the Tirumanthiram's knowledge was never made.
audit_text_issue: 2358 line 1 reads அழிவில்aல with a stray Latin 'a' (for அழிவில்லை).

note: 270 says the ignorant think love and Siva are two, and those who know rest as love that is Siva. 2361 tells the reader to know knowledge as knowledge and to love (அறிந்து அன்பு செய்மின்), setting love beside knowing. 270 makes love the goal known; 2361 makes loving part of the knowing.

2362 says true knowledge is reached by passing beyond knowledge and ignorance (அறிவு அறியாமை கடந்து அறிவானால்). Thiruppugazh 1016 calls the Lord's form the knowledge that has passed beyond knowing and not-knowing (அறிவும் அறியாமையும் கடந்த அறிவு). The two use the same formula; the song identifies that knowledge with the Lord's body.

2363 says that when the senses cease (பொறிவாய் ஒழிந்து), knowing and not-knowing removed, one stands as knowledge made dense and is Siva too. Thiruppugazh 1055 asks to become a form of knowledge (அறிவின் வடிவமாய்) beyond turiya and beyond the instruments (கருவி கரண நீத்த). Both describe the same state: knowledge left when the senses and instruments are gone.

2639 says the Lord is in all things like jaggery in sugarcane (கரும்பினில் கட்டியும்), present but not seen. 2365 says the Lord, far and near, is sweet sugarcane and nectar that tastes sweet (தித்திக்கும் தீங்கரும்பு). The cane stands for hidden presence in 2639 and for the sweetness of the Lord when tasted in 2365.

Kural 299 says not all lamps are lamps; for the worthy only the unfailing lamp (பொய்யா விளக்கு) is a lamp. 2367 sets the lamp of maya that goes out and the lamp of the body that smoulders against the pure lamp that keeps its flame. Both rank lamps and keep one; the Kural's is truth, the Tirumanthiram's is pure knowledge, with a farther lamp still sought.

2368 searches the eight directions and the two besides (திசை எட்டோடு இரண்டையும்) for the feet of the Lord. 406 says the Nandi people search for in all eight directions (தேடுந் திசைஎட்டும்) stands within those who seek him. 406 limits the outward search of 2368: what is sought in every direction is within the seeker.

2369 says those who remove the great malam, know themselves and abide in their ancient Lord do not come to birth again (வாரா பிறப்பே). Kural 357 says one whose mind ponders and knows what is (உள்ளது உணரின்) need not think again of birth. Both make true knowing the end of rebirth; the Tirumanthiram adds the removal of malam and union with the Lord.
audit_text_issue: Kural 357 text reads உணரான்; the reading depends on the commentators' உணரின்.

note: 1449 mentions the six of wide Vedanta and Siddhanta without listing them, if மாறும் is read as ஆறும்; 2370 names the six ends, Vedanta and Siddhanta first.
2381 turns the ends into the triad of knowing, known and knower; 2382 then dissolves the triad itself, ends into known, knower into known, knowledge gone, leaving silence and bliss.
Both make silence a mudra, a seal: 1900 calls the seal of silence the mark of the liberated, and 2386 ends the unity of Vedanta and Siddhanta in sinking into the silence of the seal.

1509 ends the grades of release when the bond dissolves and the Lord is sayujya; 2392 reads tat tvam asi onto the same scheme: 'thou' is the soul, 'that' the Lord left when the bond goes, and their union sayujya.
1435 calls Siddhanta not other than Vedanta; 2393 says both are the one aim of becoming Siva, each in vain apart from it.
2399 counts the ends as five, not six; 2400 holds the five together with Vedanta and Siddhanta made one, which explains the count.
audit_text_issue: TM 2400 அன்னை after ஐவகைஅந்தம் may be corrupt.

note: Both make the Veda and the Agama the Lord's own speech and, read rightly, the source of one Vedanta-Siddhanta; 2397 adds that the Veda is general and the Agama special.
2017 says soul and Siva are not different and that souls who know Siva remain as Siva; 2402 calls that knowing of soul and Siva the meaning of tat tvam asi.
Both call what true knowledge reaches செம்பொருள், the perfect thing, and tie it to release. The Kural leaves it unnamed; Tirumular says Siddhanta and Vedanta are that perfect meaning and show Siva.
audit_text_issue: TM 2394 line 4 சிந்தாந்த is a typo for சித்தாந்த.

note: 2372 joins Vedanta, which has become the self, and Siddhanta, which declares it, in Siva-yoga that removes malam and gives the rare attainment (அரும்சித்தி). 1428 places the knower's dawning knowledge and true release in the joined portion of Vedanta and Siddhanta (வேதாந்த சித்தாந்த பாகத்தின் ஊடுறு ஞானோதயன்). Both make release lie where the two ends meet.

2373 makes Siddhanta the soul's reaching the Father, holding that neither pure nor impure follows it (சுத்தம் அசுத்தம் தொடரா வகை). 1420 says the pure Saivas stand untouched by pure and impure (சுத்தம் அசுத்தமும் தோய்வுறாமே நின்று) and hold the Supreme dear. The same phrase defines Siddhanta in one and the pure Saiva in the other.

2374 says that when the thirty-six cease, the soul alone remains (ஓவும் பொழுதுஅணு ஒன்றுஉளதாம்). 2197 traces the same falling away of tattvas through waking into deep sleep and finds there 'maya alone' (இதில்மாயை தானே). Shedding the tattvas leaves the soul alone only at nadanta; in sleep the same shedding leaves maya.

2380 ends kalanta in Nandi, beyond speech, word and feeling (பேசா உரையுணர்வற்ற), beyond speech and mind (வாசாமகோசரம்). 2854 bids the reader look at the hidden thing where speech and mind disappear (வாக்கும் மனமும் மறைந்த மறைபொருள்). The same limit marks the goal in both, and 2854 adds that it can still be looked at.

2387 and 2392 are near-repeats reading tat tvam asi: 'thou' (தொம்பதம்) is the soul freed at nadanta, 'that' (தற்பதம்) is the Supreme at bodhanta. 2392 names them pasu and pati and calls the 'art' Siva-sayujya, where 2387 counts seven adjuncts on each side; the repeat fixes the Saiva reading of the saying.

2388 places within the great light beyond the seven worlds an inner light called Parashakti, and the Lord stands there holding her, yet not as her. 1768 puts Parashakti above Shakti and within her the pure state of Siva, an untouched light (தோயாத தூவொளி). Both set Siva within Parashakti and yet distinct from her.

2390 says that though souls do not think of the One, of themselves, their two deeds or the two mayas, the One stands within and feeds them (உள் உணர்ந்து நின்று ஊட்டி). The Kural says that even those who amass millions can enjoy only as the apportioner apportioned (வகுத்தான் வகுத்த வகையல்லால்). 2390 names who the apportioner is and makes the feeding inward.

2390 has the One stand within and feed the souls (ஒருவனுமேயுள் உணர்ந்துநின் றூட்டி). 2421 says the Lord kindly feeds the soul its experience through the maya he set working (மாயையில் ஊட்டல் பரிந்தனன்). 2421 shows the feeding as grace that leads toward his feet, not only as fate.

2391 calls Hara the steady one of Siva's bliss whom nothing touches (தோயாச் சிவாநந்தி), though he acts through his powers. 1538 says pure Siva stands everywhere untouched (தோய்வற்று நிற்கின்றான்). Both use தோய் for the Lord who pervades and acts yet is not stained.

2206 reads the states as stages of knowing that end in knowledge become knowledge as turiya (அறிவுஅறிவாகும் ஆன துரியமே). 2395 says that when Vedanta and Siddhanta show Siva within, knowledge made new in the states becomes Siva (அவத்தையில் ஞானம் சிவமாம்). 2395 names the goal the states of 2206 lead to.

2398 lists the kinds of Siva's bliss, among them the bliss of the true dance (மெய்நடன ஆனந்தம்), which fill the heart that does not contend. 2635 has Nandi dance in the great bliss beyond speech (பேச்சற்ற பேரின்பத்து அம்மா நடிதந்து) and asks the soul to stay still. Both make the dance the form the bliss takes.

2401 ends with the soul become Hara as water becomes milk (நீர் பாலாதல்). Naladiyar 177 says water mixed with milk becomes milk and no longer shows its own colour (பாலோடு அளாயநீர் பாலாகும்), of small men joined to the great. The same image of losing one's colour in a greater body is used of company in the Naladiyar and of the soul's union with Siva in 2401.
audit_text_issue: 2401 வினாவு is likely a misprint for விரவு.

note: 2411 calls the bond the good bond, the altar before the lingam; 2422 explains why it is good: like dirt put on cloth to clean it, the bond is grace's instrument.
Both name the Lord as the one who performs the five acts (ஐங்கருமம்) through bindu; 1927 calls him the seed and root, 2416 places the acts in the subtle order of bindu and nada.
The Kural asks for cutting the pride that says 'I' and 'mine'; Tirumular names that 'I'-saying as anava, the root bond itself, and adds that grace is the means of its removal.

2405 says line by line that the soul, the Lord and the bond are each அனாதி, and that birth ends when the soul rests in the Lord. 115 says the same thing: பசு and பாசம் are அனாதி just as பதி is, and they do not remain once பதி draws near (பதியணுகிற் பசு பாசம் நில்லாவே). Read together, 2405's 'birth is cut' (பிறப்பறும்) and 115's 'they do not remain' name one outcome, and the two verses are Tirumular's two plainest statements of the three beginningless realities.

Both verses end on the same line, பசுக்கள் தலைவனைப் பற்றி விடாவே: the souls (or cows) hold to their master and do not let go. 2406 reaches it by doctrine, once பசுத்தன்மை is removed and the threefold bond is cut; 2193 reaches it by image, once the herdsman lays down his staff (ஆயன்கோல் போடில்). The pairing shows the herdsman's staff in 2193 standing for the bond that 2406 says must be cut.

2408 calls the Lord பாசம்செய்தான், 'he who made the bond', and says he keeps souls in it. 115 says the bond is beginningless just as the Lord is (பதியினைப் போற் பசு பாசம் அனாதி), so it was never made. The conflict holds only if செய்தான் is read as 'created'; on the Siddhanta reading, where the Lord sets an already-existing bond to work, it dissolves.

2409 says the one who has seen the truth does not return to the bond, and speaks of the kevala state seeing the sakala and burning it away. 2236 sets out the course 2409 presupposes: the soul is driven by the beginningless malas, placed from kevala into sakala (கேவலம் அச்சகலத்திட்டு), and through births comes into the pure state. 2409 describes the end of the road that 2236 lays out from the start.

2410 says Nandi gave the Saivas who sought it the removal of soul-state and bond (பசுபாச நீக்கமும்). Thiruppugazh 925 asks Murugan for the same thing: that the poet, leaving pasu and pasam (பசுபாசமும் விட்டு), be brought into the contemplation of the Pati known by knowledge. What the Tirumanthiram records as given by the guru, the song asks for as a gift still to come, in the same Siddhanta terms.

Both verses read the temple as doctrine, in the same frame: ஆய ... ஆய பலிபீடம் ... ஆய அரன்நிலை ஆய்ந்துகொள்வார்கட்கே. 1718 maps tower, Sadasiva and altar onto the gross, subtle and bhadra lingas; 2411 maps lingam, bull and altar onto pati, pasu and pasam. The same altar of offerings is the bhadra linga in one and the good bond (நற்பாசம்) in the other, which shows how freely the frame is reused.

2413 says Nandi showed pati, pasu and pasam, the higher goal and the removal of the bond, and set them in Saivism. Thiruppugazh 900 asks Murugan, as one who knows nothing, for exactly that teaching: உன் பதிபசு பாசோபதேசம் பெறவேணும். The pairing shows the three categories passed from Siva's guru-line in Tirumular into the Murugan songs as the content of the guru's instruction.

2413 says Nandi showed the Lord with soul and bond, the higher goal and the removal of soul-state and bond, and set them in சத்தசைவம். 1432 lists what the pure Saivas (சுத்த சைவர்) are to reflect on: பதிபசு பாசம், the ancient malam, the prior bondage and release. The two lists match, which supports reading சத்தசைவம் in 2413 as suddha Saivism.

2414 speaks of அணு மூன்று, three kinds of soul, all pervaded by the Lord who creates for them. 2240 names the three: the kevalas with anava alone, the pralayakalas who hold maya, and the sakalas who take on all three bonds (சகலர் முப்பாசமும் புக்கோரே). 2240 supplies the classes 2414 only counts.

2418 names the Lord's five acts and calls dissolution இளைப்பாற்றும் துடைப்பு, removal that gives rest. 428, in the chapter on dissolution, opens with the same idea: daily dissolution lies in relieving long weariness (நீடிளைப் பாற்றலின்), and it goes on to name four kinds of dissolution, the last by grace. 428 works out what 2418 compresses into one phrase: that destruction is relief for tired souls.

2419 ends: வேறாம் பதிபசு பாசம் வீடாகுமே, pati, pasu and pasam stand distinct, and that is release. Thiruppugazh 1218 asks Murugan for exactly this: that pati, pasu and pasam be separated each from each without stain (பதிபசு பாசமானவை கசடற வேறு வேறுசெய்து அருள்வாயே). The song confirms the reading of 2419's last line as release by telling the three apart.

2424 says the ascetics were held close by the hand (அத்தத்தினாலே அணையப் பிடித்தலும்) and so reached themselves. 1590 tells of the guru red as Siva placing his hand on the speaker's head (சென்னிகை வைக்க), after which the guru's feet came into his heart. If அத்தம் in 2424 is read as 'hand', 1590 supplies the scene of initiation by touch that 2424 only hints at.
Both join the Lord's feet to the head. The Kural calls a head that does not bow to them useless; in Tirumular the feet come down onto the head, as grace given rather than worship offered.
2427 says Nandi's feet came onto the poet's head; 2433 says what they did there: cut his bonds and his delusion and took him.
2421 makes grace the means to reach the Lord's feet; 2425 makes the feet themselves grace, which shows the soul knowledge.
audit_text_issue: 2425 line 3 (பாலொன்று ஞானமே பண்பார் தலைஉயிர்) is hard to divide

note: 2428 makes knowing mutual: if my father does not know me, I cannot know my father (எந்தையும் என்னை அறியகிலான் ஆகில் எந்தையை யானும் அறியகிலேனே). 2965 asks who knows Mother and Father, and who knows me, apart from the love they bore (அன்புற்றது அல்லது). 2965 grounds the reciprocal knowing of 2428 in the divine parents' love.

2429 says the Lord told him the light that cannot be thought and the mantra that cannot be spoken, and he stands wearing the feet (கழலிணை சூடி). 1596 says Nandi set his feet in his heart, eyes and head, and how he gave the goal and showed the truth cannot be spoken (விளம்பவொண்ணாதே). Both put the guru's feet on the head together with a teaching that words cannot carry.

2431 says the Lord stands bearing souls according to their ripeness (பரித்துநின்றான் அப்பரிபாகத்தானே). Thiruppugazh 316 asks Murugan for that ripeness, பக்வம், to reach the state where the mind's action ceases. The Siddhanta idea that grace waits on the soul's ripeness appears in 2431 as a statement about the Lord and in 316 as the devotee's request for it.

2433 says the Lord set his foot on the speaker's head (கால்கொண்டு என் சென்னியில்) so that his bonds were cut and cut. Thiruppugazh 1219 asks Murugan to drive off the twofold disease of malam and set his paired feet on the poet's head (எனது முடிமேலே இணைதாள் அளித்து). The foot on the head as the act that ends impurity is the same in both; Tirumular reports it done, the song asks for it.

2434 says the Lord, like a parent who has seen his sons' faults, deals with each soul by its nature (உயிரது பான்மைக்கு) and without anger (செற்றமிலா). Kural 561 says a king is one who examines fittingly and punishes in proportion (தக்காங்கு நாடி ... ஒத்தாங்கு ஒறுப்பது). The same logic of weighing the case and answering it in measure appears for the Lord's dealing with souls and for a king's justice.

2434 pictures the Lord as a parent who sees both the good and the faults of the sons he begot. Thiruppugazh 251 argues from the same figure: Murugan is father and mother, and when a child runs crying before its father, who else would pick it up (அப்பன்முன் மைந்தன் ஓடி ... யாரெடுப்பது). Tirumular uses the parent to explain the Lord's measured dealing; the song uses it to claim the Lord's help as a child's right.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 2434's lines are loosely built (நாற்றம் unclear).

note: Tirumular takes the Kural's three, காமம் வெகுளி மயக்கம், word for word. The Kural says that when their very names perish, suffering perishes; Tirumular says that with them driven out he reached the abode within Om.

2435 says those who leave the three faults are freed and those who do not are caught in the three and perish (மூன்றினுள் பட்டு முடிகின்றவாறே). Kural 360 says that when even the names of the three, desire, anger and confusion, perish, pain perishes. The link holds if 2435's unnamed three are the ones 2436 names next (காமம் வெகுளி மயக்கம்), as the chapter suggests.
audit_text_issue: Kural 360 இநவ்முன்றன் is garbled for இம்மூன்றன்.

note: 2425 makes the Lord's foot Shakti as grace, which brings the soul to knowledge; 2439 makes 'art', the word that joins soul and Lord, the station of Shakti.
2443 has the Lord setting going waking and the other states; 2444 places them inside the supreme turiya and names its rare turiya as the joining word.

2146 counts the instruments of the first state as ninety-six (ஆதி அவத்தைக் கருவி தொண்ணூற்றாறே): elements, senses, malas, gunas and adharas. 2438 says that letting go of those same instruments (கருவி தொண்ணூறுடன் ஓராறு) at nada's end is how one becomes the 'thou' the Veda speaks of. 2438 takes 2146's inventory and makes discarding it the way to know the soul.

2438 says the soul becomes 'thou' by letting go of the ninety-six instruments. Thiruppugazh 314 calls Murugan the common ground that holds all the ninety-six tattvas yet stands free of them (சகலமும் பற்றிப் பற்றற நிற்கும்). The same count of ninety-six appears for what the soul must drop and for what the Lord holds without clinging.

965 says the fifty letters are all the Vedas and Agamas, and once one knows what they become, they become the five letters. 2442 says even some who do not know the fifty (ஐம்பது அறியாதவரும்) become He by the three-word teaching and the breath. 2442 opens a way to the goal that does not depend on the mastery of letters 965 describes.

Both turn on பற்று: the Kural bids one cling to the one without clinging in order to let go of clinging; Tirumular repeats 'clinging so that clinging ends' in every line and makes it the way to the supreme beyond the supreme.

Both use the cow and her calf. In the Naladiyar the calf finds its mother among many cows as an old deed finds its doer; in Tirumular the mother rises at the thought of her calf, as the Lord comes to the soul. One image carries karma, the other grace.
Both end on a lamp on a hill: in 2407 worship makes the knowledge like a lamp on the western hill, in 2446 Nandi becomes a lamp of virtue filling the hill.
Both have the freed soul passing through kevala to the state beyond while still in waking (நனவில் அதீதம்).
2456 says Nandi cut away the tattvas, the two mayas and fear; 2457 adds what followed: he led the speaker beyond knowing and gave himself.
Both make Shakti the Supreme's body or form: in 2459 as his body moving in will and knowledge, in 2464 as the open space within the five elements.
Both use the crystal that shows what is near it. The Kural makes it the face showing the mind; Tirumular makes it the soul taking the colour of the Supreme it comes within.

2452 says the soul in the state beyond is அறிவிலோன், without knowing, until it gains understanding and leaves its darkness. 2240 names the soul with anava alone, which knows nothing, the kevala (ஆணவத்தார் ஒன்று அறியாத கேவலர்). On the traditional reading that the soul's atita is this kevala condition, 2240 explains why the same word அதீதம் means transcendence for Nandi and blankness for the soul in 2452.

2453 calls the Lord without beginning or end (ஆதியும் அந்தமும் இல்லா) a supreme flame that appears and yet does not appear (தோன்றத் தோன்றாமை). 381 opens with the same words, ஆதியோடு அந்தம் இலாத பராபரம், and says that as light spreads in it Para appears (சோதி யதனிற் பரந்தோன்றத் தோன்றும்). The shared phrase about light and appearing is used in 381 for creation's first emergence and in 2453 for the Lord's elusive presence.

2458 says the Lord, expanding and contracting, becomes earth, water, air, sun and moon and bears the one sky. 2004 lists the same forms, fire, sun and moon, earth, water, fire, wind and sky, with the many souls the great Lord bears. Both draw on the Lord's eight forms; 2004's full list shows what 2458's (missing fire, doubling air) likely intends.
audit_text_issue: 2458 has both வாயு and வளி (air twice) and no fire; possibly corrupt.

note: 2466 matches the three turiyas with the three padas; 2488 restates it as soul, Supreme and Siva appearing in turiya as tvam tat asi.
Both name the goal செம்பொருள். For the Kural, seeing it is the work of knowledge that ends birth; for Tirumular, Nandi as the true reality takes him and gives it by grace.

2467 says the soul's turiya in waking is its தொம்பதம் and that in the higher three (மேல்மூன்றில்) Siva's turiya draws near. 2573 tells the seeker to search for the three padas above the three trusted turiyas (முத்துரியத்து மேல் நாடவே), where soul and Supreme may be called Siva. Both place the goal above the three turiyas rather than in any one of them; 2573 helps with 2467's obscure line.

2469 tells the seeker to go straight through the ten states (ஈர்ஐந்து அவத்தை) within the three turiyas and join the two halves at the end. 2490 takes the same tenfold order (ஈர் ஐந்தாக மதித்திட்டு) and makes it the order in which தொந்தத்தசி is brought forth in the breath and recited before Siva. The second verse turns the first one's path through the states into a practice of recitation.

2470 says that when the Lord is known as he truly is (பட்டாங்கு அறிந்திடில்), the lips no longer strike together to recite (பன்னா உதடுகள் தட்டாது). 2955 mocks the mutes who speak of what is beyond speech (உரையற்றது ஒன்றை உரைசெய்யும் ஊமர்காள்) and says he stays unveiled for those whose thought is clear like water without waves. Both make true knowing the end of speech; 2470 states it as the knower's own silence, 2955 as a rebuke to talkers.

2471 says the devotees knew the thirty-six (ஆறாறு) as inert and left them, and broke dense maya (செறிவாய மாயை) by grace, reaching grace never parted.
