Thiruppugazh 203 asks when, with the darkness of great maya gone (மாமாய இருள் அற்று), he will reach the light beyond the thirty-six (ஆறாறின் அதிகம்) and beyond turiya. The same Siddhanta sequence, leaving the thirty-six and breaking maya, appears in Tirumular as a thing done and in Arunagirinathar as a prayer.

2472 says the turiya that is the waking within waking is the soul's தொம்பதம். 2502 reaches the same term from the other side: once the thirty-six adjuncts of effect are gone, the soul passing through waking, dream within waking (கனாநனா) and deep sleep is what is called தொம்பதம் (உயிர் தொம்பதம் பேசிலே). Both define the tvam word as the soul graded through the waking states; 2502 adds that the adjuncts must go first.

2473 and 2826 are the same verse with small variants: as tvam-pada and tat-pada are named as turiyas, the third trusted turiya (நம்பிய மூன்றாம் துரியத்து) is the good one, and beyond the very subtle (அதிசூக்கம் அப்பால்) glorious Nandi, the true reality (செம்பொருள்), took him and gave grace. They differ in line 3, where 2473 has அம்புலி (moon) and 2826 அம்புவி (earth). This is a near-repeat across chapters 180 and 212, and the variant changes what the Supreme is said to be beyond.
audit_text_issue: அம்புலி vs அம்புவி and நல்நாமம் vs நன்றாகும் look like textual variants of one verse.

note: Both trace birth to not knowing what truly is: the Kural to the delusion that takes the unreal as real, Tirumular to souls that do not know what is. Tirumular adds that those who know come to grace.

2476 says Siva stands forth for those who destroy the three malas and gunas and say சோகம், 'I am he', on the path of union. 2403 calls the abiding சோகம் the crowning Siva-yoga of the Veda-knowers and the meaning of Siddhanta too. The two verses name so'ham as the end of the path, one as practice that brings Siva forth, the other as the point where Veda and Agama meet.

2477 says the Lord who cut bondage becomes சித்தியும் முத்தியும், the purity (சுத்தி) that is firm Siva, and the Shakti of blissful joy (சுகானந்த சத்தி). 2862 uses the same terms: one of complete knowledge holds முத்தியும் சித்தியும், and those within Shakti pass beyond purification (சுத்தி அகன்றோர்) to become knowers of சுகானந்தம். In 2477 purity is a form the Lord takes; in 2862 it is a stage the knower leaves behind.
Both use a gem whose light, lustre and rays belong to it: 2482 for the three forms resting in the Lord, 2483 for the experience in the three voids.
audit_text_issue: 2483's நாடிஒண் முப்பதும் and முத்திராந்தத்து are obscure, possibly corrupt

note: 2478 says the seeker rises past the five malas to the knowledge of சிவோகம், and at the end (ஈறதில்) the ancient Supreme makes the truth plain. 1593 says the guru did away even with becoming Siva (சிவமாதல் தீர்த்து) and set him in the true form beyond words. Both put a further truth past the stage of 'I am Siva'; 1593 says what that truth removes.

2481 says the Lord becomes form, formless and both, comes as Shakti, guru and the many souls, and dwelling with them is one and not one (ஒன்றாய் அன்றாமே). 1811 says he stands as the life of life yet, pressing close, is not those things (அவைஅல்ல வாகும்) but a companion. Both state the Siddhanta relation of Lord and souls, union without identity, in nearly the same words.

2482 compares the three forms and Shaktis resting in Nandi to a gem's light and lustre (மணிஒளி சோபை), which are the gem's own marks. 1028 says Shakti stays mingled within as the light of a gem (கல்லொளி) and stands in the eye as that light. Both use the gem and its light for a power that cannot be parted from its source; 2482 rests it in Nandi, 1028 in the world and the eye.

2484 tells the yogi to open from above the doorway that பயோதரி has sealed. 1139 speaks of the nectar-breasted lady (அமுத பயோதரி) whose reversed way (மாறியிருந்த வழி) no one knows and who wells up for those with inner sight. The rare name பயோதரி in both points to the same inner power that both blocks and opens the way up, which supports reading 2484's figure as Shakti or kundalini.

2486 doubles each noun, making light light, breath breath and space space (ஒளியை ஒளிசெய்து, வெளியை வெளிசெய்து), until Siva's state grows clear (தெளியத் தெளியும்). 124 uses the same doubling for absorption: space into space, light into light (வெளியில் வெளிபோய், ஒளியில் ஒளிபோய்), and those who see it clearly (தெளியும் அவரே) are Siva-siddhas. 2486 makes the figure a practice and 124 a state, and both end on the verb தெளி.

2487 says that when the stupor of the three instruments is cleared, great Manonmani goes on alone, and that unmani is the inner samadhi. 1114 lists among the names of the Goddess 'samadhi, Manonmani' (மாது சமாதி மனோன்மணி) side by side. The litany in 1114 sets Manonmani next to samadhi as one of her names; 2487 makes Manonmani the state in which samadhi is reached.
Both argue identity through one man seen differently: 2485 one man in three roles, 2493 Devadatta recognised as the same man once changed circumstances are set aside.
Both name a set of three whose ending ends the trouble: the Kural desire, anger and delusion, whose very names must perish; Tirumular the impurities and qualities, whose dying lets Siva appear.
audit_text_issue: Kural 360 reads இநவ்முன்றன் for இம்மூன்றன்; 2489 காமதம் is doubtful.

note: 2489 says that when the malas and gunas die and Siva appears, it is like darkness going before the moon (இந்துவின் முன் இருள் ஏகுதல்). 1996 grants that moon, fire and sun remove black darkness but says Nandi removes the darkness that deeds make (செய்யிருள்). 2489 uses the moon as a likeness for Siva's coming, while 1996 sets Nandi above the moon, for a darkness it cannot reach.

2490 tells the seeker to bring forth தொந்தத்தசி in the breath (வாசியில் தோற்றி) and recite it before Siva. 2442 says that even some who do not know the fifty letters, seeking within the three-pada saying and driving the breath (வாசி செலுத்திட), become He by that supreme yoga. Both join the great saying to the breath; 2442 adds that this needs no learning of the letters.

2491 ends the one who took Om as teaching in servitude: he knew the truth and stood as the Father's servant (அத்தற்கு அடிமை அடைந்து நின்றானே). 2493, two verses on, ends the same practice of the saying in identity: the soul is Parasiva (சீவன் பரசிவன் ஆமே). The conflict holds if 2493 is read as strict identity; Siddhanta's union-without-identity can hold both.

2492 places tvam in maya, tat in the beyond, and asi-pada in trusted peace (அசிபதம் நம்புறு சாந்தியில் நண்ணும்). 2569 says it is tat-pada that is reached in the stilled state (தற்பதம் எய்து உபசாந்தத்து). The two assign the state of peace to different words of the saying; the conflict depends on taking சாந்தி and உபசாந்தம் as the same state.

2494 lists the great malas as தாமதம், காமியம் and a dark quality and places them with A, U and M in the turiya that is தொந்தத்தசி. 2489 says the impurities beginning with காமியம் and the qualities (தொல்கா மதமாதி, likely தாமதம்) lie in the three of தொந்தத்தசி, and Siva appears when they die. The same pair, kamya and tamas, is set inside the saying in both; 2494 adds the letters of Om, 2489 what happens when they die.
2497 ends at rest in a void beyond imagining; 2500 says that for those who know, there is no void either, nor heart nor form.
2503 maps the letters சி, வா, ய to Siva, the Supreme and the soul; 2499 drops நம to leave those letters as the clear form of the mantra.

2495 says that seeing and leaving the seven effects and seven causes and ending the traces (வாதனை) of effect and cause, the bond ends in the void of calm (உபசாந்த முப்பாழ்). 2507 repeats the scheme almost line for line: the seven effects hide in maya, the seven causes in the void, and cutting attachment to the traces of effect and cause (காரிய காரண வாதனைப் பற்றற) is upasantam. This is a near-repeat across two chapters; 2507 calls 'void of calm' simply upasantam.

2496 makes the third void the soul pervaded in Siva-Shakti, where speech comes to its end (சொல்முடிவு). 2455 says the soul, entering the Supreme in the empty void of knowledge that swallowed the false world (போத வெறும்பாழில்), becomes the flag that joins the red Siva-Meru, as white turns red before red. 2455 gives an image for what 2496 states as doctrine: in the last void the soul takes on Siva's colour.

2497 says that to join Nandi's feet he takes the void as his way, crosses it, and comes to rest in the void that has shaken off that imagining (கற்பனை உதறிய பாழில் ஒடுங்குகின்றேனே). 2948 ends with the same words in the third person: he subsides in the void that shook off the imagining (கற்பனை உதறிய பாழில் ஒடுங்குகின்றானே), after unhurried study of the Veda. This is a near-repeat of the closing line; 2497 reaches it through the Lord's feet, 2948 through examination.
2495 lets go the seven effects and seven causes to reach the voids; 2505 says the bound soul mixes in the seven effects and Parasiva in the seven causes, and the Supreme is in the void beyond both.
Both say the Supreme too has adjuncts: 2463 that even the Supreme clinging to a causal adjunct is not pure, 2501 that the seven adjuncts of the Supreme must be cut away with the soul's.

2503 and 975 share their first line and most of the rest, but differ on two letters: 2503 says M is Siva (மகாரம் சிவமாய்) and VA is the Supreme, while 975 says M is impurity (மகார மலமாய்) and VA is form. On the plain reading they assign incompatible meanings to the same letters of the same three-part word, a near-repeat whose changes point to two different traditions of analysing Om and சிவாய.
audit_text_issue: The single-word differences may be textual variants of one verse.

note: 2504 calls the Lord the life of life (உயிர்க்குயிராகி) and says that without him the wearying anava will not leave. 2210 says the Lord and Shakti, as the life of life (உயிர்க்குஉயிராகி), are all things, and without them all is the delusion of darkness (இருண்மூடம்). Both name the Lord the life of life and make him the only remover of the dark; 2504 names that dark as anava.
Both speak of a sea to be crossed. The Kural's sea is births, swum only by those at the Lord's feet; Tirumular's knower has already seen the shore, the waves of the soul settled to clear water.

2506 is built on வித்து: the seed of release is the Lord's knowledge, of devotion bowing and clinging, of attainment becoming Siva, of power one's own stillness. Kural 361 says craving is the seed (வித்து) that produces unceasing birth for all beings. Set together, the Kural names the seed of birth and Tirumular names the seeds of release, with stillness as the opposite of craving.

Kural 24 says that one who guards the five senses with the goad of firmness is a seed (வித்து) for the highest ground. 2506 says the seed of power is one's own stilling (தனது உபசாந்தம்). Both make self-restraint the seed of something higher; the Kural places the fruit in the world above, 2506 in the soul's own power and release.

2507 says upasantam is the state when attachment (பற்று) to the traces of effect and cause is cut away. 2376 says the yoganta doctrine is the union in upasantam, when the soul becomes the Supreme with attachment gone (பற்றற). Both define upasantam by the ending of பற்று; 2376 places it after samadhi, 2507 after the seven effects and causes are hidden.

2508 says that turiya is the purifying of the soul and that upasantam lies in the Lord's pervading of oneself (தன்னின் வியாத்தி). 2283 sets the strong upasantam (உரமாம் உபசாந்தம்) in the graded higher states after the supreme waking, and calls reaching them renunciation that makes one the bearer of Siva's turiya. 2283 places in the series of states the upasantam that 2508 defines.

2474 names three releases: the soul's is the state beyond, the Supreme's is upasantam, and Siva's is bliss (சிவமுத்தி ஆனந்தம்). 2510 shows the passage from the second to the third: when even the traces of upasantam leave, one has become Siva, steeped in சிவானந்தம். 2510 turns 2474's list into a sequence.

2511 says the knower, one with the Supreme, settles like clear water that had been in waves (திரையின் நின்று ஆகிய தெண்புனல்). 1593 says the guru set him, like water without waves (திரையற்ற நீர்போல்), past even becoming Siva and beyond words. The stilled water serves both for the soul at rest, and both end beyond speech (உரையற்ற, சொல்லிறந்தோமே).

2955 asks whether the shore of what has no shore can be seen (கரையற்றது ஒன்றைக் கரைகாணலாகுமோ) and mocks those who speak of the speechless. 2511 says the knower has seen the shore (கரைகண்டான்), but only in a reckoning beyond words (உரையற்ற கணக்கிலே). 2511 answers 2955's question with a condition: the shore is seen, but not as something that can be said.
The Kural defines folly as the conceit 'we are wise'; Tirumular's heartless men say 'we know fully' while blind to the Lord, as futile as cutting the hare from the moon.

Both name the pride of 'I' and 'mine' as what must be cut. The Kural promises a world beyond the gods' to the one who cuts it; Tirumular makes cutting it, with the lesser releases set aside, the mark of the Siva-siddha.
Both make mastering the five senses the condition of reaching the Lord: the Kural's one who quenched the five senses, Tirumular's one who conquers them and knows him as one.

2512 likens those who claim full knowledge without seeing Siva to men taking up a sword to strike the hare in the crescent moon (பிறையுள் கிடந்த முயலை). Naladiyar 176 says the hare in the bright moon is worshipped along with it (முயலும் தொழப்படுஉம்), as the lowly gain worth from friends like hills. Both use the hare in the moon, the Naladiyar for borrowed worth and Tirumular for an idle reach at what cannot be touched.

2513 sets the black-legged eagle passing through the sky (கருடன் விசும்பூடு இறப்ப) beside the black snake leaving the pool, and tells the heart to stop talking of its greatness. 2659 says that as poison clears and fear ends when one thinks of Garuda's form, the three malas clear when one fixes on the guru's form. 2659 makes plain the figure 2513 leaves open: Garuda is the greater power before which the snake, and the bond, give way.

Kural 331 calls it petty knowledge (புல்லறி வாண்மை) to take what does not last for what lasts. 2514 uses the same word for standing at the womb's gate (கருவாயில்) and fighting so that foes may die. 2514 applies the Kural's term to hostile striving bound to birth, where the Kural applies it to mistaking the transient.

2515 says there is no need to quarrel (பிணங்கவும் வேண்டாம்): if the world agrees that our Lord is the Lord, even the hosts of heaven come to his feet. 1558 says the six sects are like six roads to one great city, and those who say 'this is good, that is bad' are like a dog barking at a hill. Both reject sectarian dispute; 1558 gives the reason, that all the paths lead to one end.

1557 says the First Lord moves among the six sects so that they seek his pair of feet (சமயங்கள் ஆறும் தன் தாளிணை நாட). 2515 says that when the world agrees he is the Lord, the eighteen hosts seek his anklet-bound feet (கழலடி காண). In 1557 the sects seek the feet; 2515 says that agreement rather than quarrel brings all beings to them.

2516 calls the Lord my life more than I am (என்னிலும் என்னுயிராய) and says he comes in the very way he is thought of (உன்னும் உறும் வகையாலே). 2335 says that whatever is said of him he is far beyond far, yet understood quickly he becomes the life of life (உயிர்க்குயிராகுமே). Both join a Lord past speech with one who is nearer than the self to the one who thinks on him.

2519 says that if one holds within with eyes closed the one even the celestials cannot know, at the three times, one's nature becomes the Parapara (தன்மை பராபரனாமே). 2659 says that the moment one fixes on the guru's form the three malas clear and he becomes Siva (சிவன் அவன் ஆமே). Both teach that one becomes what one holds in thought; 2659 makes the object the guru's form.

Kural 2 asks what learning has achieved if the learned do not bow at the feet of the one of pure knowledge (வாலறிவன்). 2520 says the Lord is good within the learning of those whose minds are not soured (கன்றா மனத்தார்தம் கல்வியுள் நல்லவன்). Both tie learning's worth to the Lord; 2520 adds the condition that the learner's mind be unsoured.

2521 says the struck bell (எறிமணி) is the lamp of the inner breath, and the speaker heard it and saw the hall. 1009 says that those who look steadily within will find the Lord inside the struck bell (எறிமணி உள்ளே இருக்கலும் ஆமே), where sense-bound seekers fail. The struck bell in both is an inner sound in which the Lord is met.
audit_text_issue: 2521's அற்றலும் may be a corruption of அரற்றலும்.

note: 2522 says Nandi comes before him when sought within him (என்னுள்ளே நேர்தரு நந்தியை), and with closed eyes, having entered the nest (கூடு), he saw the seven worlds. 2550 says people wander everywhere searching for Nandi who is fragrant within the body (காயத்தினுள்ளே கமழ்கின்ற நந்தி) and do not know the meaning that stands there. Both find Nandi inside the body; 2550 names the outward search that misses him, and 2522 the inward one that finds him.

2524 says the great ascetics, their mind become supreme bliss, entered a peace that swallows the world (சகமுணச் சாந்திபுக்கு) and, their malas gone, reached rest. 334, in the chapter against liquor, says one who removes the tattvas and delusion, takes the world and leaves it (சகமுண்டு விட்டு), gains supreme bliss as the true toddy of Siva's bliss. Both use 'swallowing the world' for the passage into supreme bliss.

124 says those who see clearly space into space, sweetness into sweetness and light into light are the Siva-siddhas (சிவ சித்தர் தாமே). 2525 ends with the same words but defines them otherwise: those who cast off the three graded releases as flawed, drive out the pleasant darkness of bonds and change 'I' and 'mine'. One definition is by the seeing of absorption, the other by what the siddha gives up.

2526 says the siddhas have seen Siva and, steeped in pure and impure, remain unsteeped (தோய்ந்தும் தோயாதவர்), of the nature of Sadasiva. 127 says they remained having become Sivam and everything (இருந்தார் சிவமாகி எங்குந் தாமாகி), watching all of Siva's acts. Both describe the siddha who has become Siva and still remains among things.
2530 names a river and an inner tank; 2535 places the tank on a hilltop, filled without a river, and adds the lotus without mud worn by Siva.
Both set standing and sitting and many words against the one who conquers and seeks the Lord: talk and posture do not reach him, mastery does.

2529 speaks obscurely of three lotuses in bud opened by the light, under a chapter title naming the three gunas and the states. 2296 states the mapping outright: சாத்திகம் is waking, இராசதம் dream, தாமதம் deep sleep, and the gunaless turiya ends them. Read together, 2296 supplies the scheme that 2529's three buds and its dream line seem to presuppose, though 2529's own terms remain uncertain.
2537 only names the nine presiding selves; 2545 sets them in the nine states and makes passing beyond their three turiyas into Siva the goal.

Both verses end on the same words, துவமார் துரியம் சொரூபம், reached in a தவமான சத்திய ஞான state once the birth-bound (பவமான) malas are let go. 2538 starts from releasing the nine states from waking; 2834 from becoming Siva so the three malas end. A near-repeat in a distant chapter, it fixes 2538's obscure phrase as part of a stable formula.

2539: in a mind become Siva (சிவமான சிந்தை) the three malas (மும்மலம்) scatter and Siva-knowledge takes their place. 2969: those whose mind has become Siva (சித்தம் சிவமாய்) and who have destroyed the three malas (மலமூன்றும் செற்றவர்) become pure Siva. The same claim in two chapters: the mind becoming Siva and the malas' end are one event.

2541: saying 'my Lord' within night and day, the poet found the Lord cut away strong karma (வல்வினை). Kural 5: the two deeds born of darkness (இருள்சேர் இருவினை) do not cling to those who hold to the Lord's true praise. Both make constant turning to the Lord the thing that frees one from deeds; Tirumular puts it as the Lord's act, the Kural as a fact about the devotee.
The same verse appears word for word as 2071; the repetition places the search for Nandi within the body under the heading of purity as well.
725 tells how Tirumular once thought the body a flaw, then found the Lord's temple within it and began to tend it; 2550 faults those who search the land for the Lord fragrant within the body.

Both say people do not know what the body is. For the Naladiyar its truth is the stinking cart the vultures tear when life leaves it; for Tirumular it holds Nandi, fragrant within. The tension holds if the Naladiyar's verse is read as a judgement of the body itself, not only of vanity about adorning it.

The Kural sets outer purity by water against inner purity by truthfulness; Tirumular also moves purity inward but keeps ritual among its sources: discipline, worship, the fire rite and knowledge free one from ritual impurity.
Both fix a place by finger-breadths from the nose: 581 twelve below it, as a point of meditation that keeps the body; 2546 three or four from its tip, as the Lord's unknown dwelling.
Both set the Real (பொருள்) against delusion (மருள்): the Kural makes taking the unreal for the real the cause of base births; Tirumular leaves all but the Lord's devotees whirling in delusion.

2547: once one sees the deed, the claim on it and inherited karma, and departs from them, what one does after enters the wearing-out of karma (கன்மக் கயம்). 2309: as heated iron keeps its heat when the fire is gone, even in turiya the stain of karma steeped in (தோய்ந்த கருமத் துரிசு) does not leave. 2309 limits 2547: seeing frees later action from binding, but the residue of past karma lingers.

2548 plays on மறை: the hidden Thing is hidden because maya hides it, and appears when maya is hidden. 2290 uses the wooden elephant: the elephant hides the wood and disappears into the wood; the elements hide the Supreme and disappear into it. The same reversal of concealment, in a riddle of words and in an image; 2290 shows what 'hiding maya' looks like.

2551: the ignorant cry 'impurity, impurity' (ஆசூசம்) but do not know where impurity lies. Kural 278: many with impurity in their minds (மனத்தது மாசாக) bathe as if distinguished and go about concealed. Both move impurity from the rites people observe to the mind, and the Kural names the place 2551 says no one knows.

2554 repeats தூய்மணி (pure gem) beside the pure fire, without naming what it is. In 1544 தூய்மணி வண்ணன், 'the one of pure gem colour', is a name of the Lord himself. The shared phrase supports reading 2554's pure gem as the Lord rather than a yogic light.

2557 closes: the servants of karma do not know its great outcome (மிக்க விளைவறியாரே). 1635 opens each line with விளைவறிவார், those who know the outcome, who do the true tapas, word and dharma of old. The two verses name the same knowledge from both sides: lacking it binds one to karma, having it puts one above heaven and earth.

2558: those who say there is no higher state (பரகதி இல்லை) go the way of hell, as the world knows. Kural 850: one who says 'it is not' to what the world says is (உண்டென்பது இல்லென்பான்) is set down on earth as a demon. Both condemn the denier and both appeal to the world's agreement (ஞாலம் அறியும், உலகத்தார்); the Kural places the penalty in this life, Tirumular in the next.

2559 is a near-verbatim repeat of 2093: those who cannot reach the guru's mark (குரு வைத்த குறி) wander making fine talk, and cannot sing what he did; what gain have they? In 2093 it stands among laments over ruin, in 2559 among the scorners of release; the repetition marks the talker without the guru's mark as a fixed type in the book.

On the reading that 2560 mocks a seeker who takes his opened mind (திறப்பட்ட சிந்தை) for God and calls it the Lord beyond all, it conflicts with 1555, where the abiding one is மனோமயன், the one who dwells in the mind, and those who scorn this are fools. 1555 calls the mind the place to worship and reach him; 2560 treats equating mind and God as delusion. The tension depends on 2560's voice being satirical, which the chapter suggests but the verse does not state.

2562: the wretched (கலதிகள்), shown the way to see (காண்வழி காட்ட), cannot see (கண் காணா). Kural 849: one who shows the unseeing (காணாதான் காட்டுவான்) himself does not see, and the unseeing sees only as he already saw. Both use showing and not seeing for the fool beyond teaching; the Kural adds that the shower is the one shamed.

2563: the others cannot conceive the form that runs through (ஊடும்) forest, hill, field and every place. 2639: like jaggery in cane and fragrance in the flower, our Lord stands mingled everywhere (எங்குங் கலந்துநின்றானே). Both say the Lord pervades all; 2639 gives the images, 2563 says failing to see this is what keeps one from him.

2564: while the gods go south, north, west and east, the short way (குறுவழி) is the mantra on the tongue and the fire within. 509: there are holy waters inside the heart, and those who do not bathe there wander over hollow and height (பள்ளமும் மேடும் பரந்து திரிவரே). Both set an inward practice against roaming in space, whether gods to the quarters or pilgrims over the land.

2565: the evildoers who speak to provoke anger stand bearing heavy karma (வல்வினை) for themselves. 538: one who reviles the jnani (ஞானியை நிந்திப்பவன்) takes on his deeds, as the worshipper takes his good. Both say scorn of the holy returns as karma on the scorner; 538 adds that it is a transfer from the one scorned, on the usual reading of its compressed lines.

2566 names the third mode, implication that leaves and keeps (விட்டுவிடாத இலக்கணை); 2570 applies it to the great saying, as in the Vedantic example 'this is that Devadatta', to make the soul the Supreme.

2567: when the aimed arrow struck, the five killing elephants (கொல்லுங் களிறு ஐந்தும்) fell. Kural 24: one who guards the five (ஓரைந்தும்) with the goad (தோட்டி) of firmness is a seed for heaven. Both treat the five senses as elephants; the Kural controls them with a goad, Tirumular's aimed arrow fells them.
2568 sets out the saying analytically, word by word and turiya by turiya; 2577 says what completes it: 'you are that' must become 'I have become that', and this happens by Nandi's grace.

2580 tells the seeker to put away both knowing and not-knowing before Siva who is knowledge itself; 2581 gives the reason: the soul knows the elements, but knows the Lord only as the Lord makes it know.

2568 sets 'you' in the soul's turiya (சீவ துரியம்), 'that' in the supreme turiya (பரதுரியம்) and 'are' in Siva's turiya (சிவதுரியம்). 2466 names the same three turiyas and says they match the padas of tvam tat asi. A restatement four chapters on; 2568 adds that the truth of the saying is that the three distinctions fall away (ஓவி விடும்).

2545 says the attainment of Siddhanta is to pass beyond the three turiyas (முத்துரியம்) in the nine states and become Siva. 2568 says what those three turiyas are, the soul's, the Supreme's and Siva's, and ties each to a word of tat tvam asi. 2568 fills in the scheme that 2545 names.

2502: when the thirty-six effect-adjuncts (ஆறாறு காரியோபாதி) have gone, the soul in that ground is called tvam-pada. 2569 begins from the same point, the soul beyond the six sixes as the pure 'you', and carries it on to 'that' in the stilled state and the union of all three in grace. 2569 extends 2502's account of 'you' into the whole saying.

2570 and 2493 open almost identically (ஆகிய அச்சோயம் தேவகத்தன் / தேவதத்தன் இடத்து), using 'this is that Devadatta' to show how tat tvam asi keeps the person and drops the circumstances, and both end with the soul becoming the Supreme Siva. A near-repeat; 2570 names the mode as the implication that both leaves and keeps (விட்டுவிடாத இலக்கணை), which 2493 leaves implicit.
audit_text_issue: 2570 தேவகத்தன் is likely a corruption of தேவதத்தன்.

note: 2571: 'that you are' becoming one is Siva, and that is சித்தாந்த வேதாந்தம். 2393: becoming Siva (சிவமாதல்) is Vedanta and Siddhanta, and apart from that each is in vain. Both make becoming Siva the point where the two schools meet; 2571 reaches it through the great saying.

2572 and 2498 share their first and last lines: the wordless void where turiya subsides (துரியம் அடங்கிய சொல்லறும் பாழ்) and the question who knows the rare ground (அருநிலம்). 2498 calls those who name the void Paramparam fools (ஆதர்); 2572 has them call it the rare Supreme and not deny it form. A near-repeat with a changed middle, which bears on how 2572's obscure line 2 should be read.

2573: seeking the three words above the three trusted turiyas (முத்துரியத்து மேல்), soul and Supreme can be called Siva. 2657: the light that shines beyond the three turiyas (துரியங்கள் மூன்றும் கடந்து) is Parasiva, become all things, and the guru's state there cannot be spoken. 2657 says what lies above the three turiyas that 2573 points to.

2574 is a near-repeat of 2491: in the bliss of one's own form (சொருபானந்தம்), the teaching of Om (பிரணவ உபதேசம்) is let go in the true heart (மெய்த்த இதயத்து விட்டிடு) and true awareness reached. 2491 ends with him become the Father's servant (அத்தற்கு அடிமை), 2574 with him standing as he was given; the pair fixes the subject as the disciple.

2575: place the five states from waking (நனவாதி ஐந்து) in nada, put the corpse-like mala behind, and seek the king beyond mind and speech. 2182: putting away the five states from waking-of-waking, the five mala-states and the false thirty-six, the soul stands as one. Both prescribe the same clearing of the five states and of mala before union.

2576: it takes no name, since no speech reaches it (பேச்சொன்றிலாமையின்), and it shows itself without cause. Thiruppugazh 1043 worships the Siva-form beyond all Vedas and all words (சகல வேதனாதீத, சகல வாசகாதீத) in a temple of silence (மோனமே கோயில்). Both put the highest beyond speech; Arunagiri turns that into a form of worship.

2578: the soul becomes the Supreme (உயிர் பரமாக) and the supreme soul becomes rare Siva. 984: NAVA and SIVA become the soul and the Supreme (உயிர் பரம்), and those at one with Siva reach the clarity that they are what is called Siva. Both state the soul's passage through the Supreme to Siva; 984 ties it to the letters of the mantra, 2578 to Om.

2581: unless the Knower makes it known (அறிவிக்கின் அல்லால்), we do not know what he knows. 2329: the soul does not know by itself (தானே அறியான்) yet is not without knowing; when both stand as Hara's grace it knows and abides with Siva. Both make the soul's knowledge of the Lord depend on the Lord's act; 2329 adds that the soul is not simply ignorant.

2582 repeats 2452 almost word for word: Nandi is in the beyond-state (அதீதம்) and apart, the soul there is without knowing, and the soul that gains understanding settles in the Lord (பதியிற் பதியும்). Only one word differs: 2452 has the soul leave its darkness (இருள்விட்ட), 2582 its rolling (உருள்விட்ட), the round of births.
audit_text_issue: one-word variant உருள்/இருள் may be a copying difference

note: 2584: the spotless Lord came into my heart, said 'this one is my servant' (என்னடியான்) and took away my impurity, saying 'be spotless'. Thiruppugazh 747: Murugan showed the anklet feet that dried up my anava mala (ஆணவ மலம் அற்றிட) and brought me among the devotees. Both describe the Lord's own coming as what removes the root impurity and claims the poet as his; Arunagiri vows not to forget it.

Thiruppugazh 978 asks whether, like devotees who left household life, the poet may end the dance of coming into the world in a karma-strung body. 2585: renouncing (துறந்து) and seeing the light, the poet was set here by the king of the heavens so that he would not die and be born again (இறந்து பிறவாமல்). What 978 asks, 2585 reports as given, in this life (ஈங்கு).

2586: every soul dances as the Lord makes it dance (இறை ஆட்ட ஆடலால்), body, senses and inner instruments alike. 2344: like the deed that makes a false puppet dance (பொய்க்கரி யாட்டும்), he makes the elements dance and settles the soul. Both make the Lord the mover of all the soul's action through the figure of a dance he directs.
Both see the body as a bubble. The Naladiyar's wise draw from it the resolve to end their births; Tirumular sets the bubble beside camphor in fire and has the body go into the Supreme.
2590 says the Supreme eats the world and spits it out again; 2593 says what is swallowed, soul, Supreme, turiya and the cosmos, and that it stays outwardly whole like the emptied wood-apple.

2588 says that when body and soul become one, the soul leaving the body (உடலைவிட்டு இந்த உயிர் எங்குமாகி) becomes everywhere and end and beginning vanish in Siva. 134 says those who feel the teacher's word, once the body falls here (உடம்பிங்கு ஒழிந்தால்), become reality mixed in the shoreless light (கரையற்ற சோதி). Both make the body's ending a widening into the boundless, not a loss.

2591 says that one who draws in the knowledge of turiya and reaches Supreme Siva becomes the bright open space (விளங்கிய வெட்ட வெளியனும் ஆமே). Thiruppugazh 1316 asks to reach Murugan's feet of knowledge that dance in the formless void, the open space (உருவிலாத பாழில் வெட்டவெளியில் ஆடு). The same yogic term வெட்டவெளி is in one the state the knower becomes and in the other the stage of the god's dance.

2592 says Nandi drew the poet in as heated iron draws in water (இரும்பிடை நீரென), the water vanishing wholly. 2309 says heated iron keeps a fire-like heat after the fire is gone (காய்ந்த இரும்பு கனலை அகன்றாலும்), as karma's residue stays even in turiya. The one image of hot iron shows total absorption in one verse and stubborn residue in the other.

2593 says Siva swallows soul, Supreme, turiya and world like the wood-apple eaten by the elephant (கரியுண் விளவின் கனிபோல்): shell intact, substance gone into him. Thiruppugazh 653 uses the same proverb (வேழம் உண்ட விளாங்கனி அதுபோல) for the poet's body hollowed by infatuation. The image is grace's absorption in Tirumular and desire's ruin in Arunagiri.
audit_text_issue: 653 has a broken glyph in மயலு஡றி.

note: The Kural says one who is not false in his heart dwells in the hearts of all people; Tirumular says the Lord dwells with those mingled in truth and does not enter before the false. Truthfulness opens the heart in both: to others in the Kural, to the Lord in Tirumular.
The Kural says knowledge from the five senses is no gain without true perception; Tirumular says knowing everything is no gain apart from the knowledge that knows everything.

Both deny that knowledge profits by itself: the Kural asks what learning gains without worship of the one of pure knowledge, Tirumular says knowing all things gains nothing apart from the all-knowing.

Both make the way out of bondage a following: the Kural says cling to the one without clinging in order to let clinging go, Tirumular says cut the senses' bond and follow the one who cut away confusion.
The Kural praises those who keep to the path of the one who quenched the five senses; Tirumular tells the seeker to cut the five senses' bond and follow the one who has done so.

2595 says the teachings of grace, held through the fire, are like gold refined of its flaw in fire (குற்றம் அறுத்த பொன் போலும் கனலிடை), and one becomes a bright flame (செழுஞ்சுடர்). Kural 267 says those who endure pain shine like gold that brightens the more it is burned (சுடச்சுடரும் பொன்போல்). Both use firing of gold for purification; the Kural's fire is ascetic suffering, Tirumular's is holding to the guru's teaching.

2597 calls Siva the thief who stands in the kalas (கலைநின்ற கள்வனை), found after passing beyond birth. 2122 calls the soul the thief inside the body-bag (காயப்பைக்கு உள்நின்ற கள்வன்) whose leaving turns the body to earth. Tirumular uses கள்வன் both for the hidden Lord and for the soul slipping unseen out of the body.

2598 says the heart whose flesh has melted (ஊனே உருகிய உள்ளம்) becomes one with the Lord. 1796 says that when the flesh melts and one perceives awareness (ஊனே உருகி உணர்வை உணர்ந்தபின்) the Lord is like honey. The same phrase marks in both the bodily melting of love as the moment of union.

2599 says grace comes to those who, with minds free of darkness (இருளற்ற சிந்தை), change their deluded mind (மருளுற்ற சிந்தையை மாற்றி) and praise the feet. Kural 352 says that for those of stainless sight, free of confusion (மருள்நீங்கி), darkness goes and joy comes (இருள்நீங்கி இன்பம்). Both pair the clearing of இருள் and மருள் as the condition of the good that follows; Tirumular names it grace, the Kural joy.

Thiruppugazh 28 asks that when mind fails and speech goes (அறிவழிய ... உரையுமற) at death, Murugan grant the boon of drawing near his feet. 2601 says only those who have already joined hands with the Lord (கைகலந்தார்க்கே) can fix him in thought when the breath rises to leave (ஆவி எழும்பொழுது). Tirumular sets a condition on the deathbed plea: the hold on the Lord at death must be made before it.

2603 says that if one masters the nine paths of the lying senses one can mount the horse called truth (மெய்யென் புரவியை மேற்கொள்ளலாமே). 566 says riding the horse swifter than a bird (புள்ளினும் மிக்க புரவியை மேற்கொண்டால்), the controlled breath, gives joy without toddy. The same mounting of a horse is breath-control in the yoga chapter and truth in the chapter on truth.

2604 says the pure one who does not enter before the false is a refuge only to those who have cast off falsehood (பொய்யொழிந்தார்க்கே புகலிடமாமே). 503 has the poet say he has not left truth and, putting away falsehood, seeks the Lord's feet and becomes like a lamp needing no ghee. Both make leaving falsehood the way to the Lord, 2604 as doctrine and 503 as the poet's own account.

2606 says the Lord sits in the midst of those who shine without any falsehood (பொய்யொன்றுமின்றிப் புறம்பொலிவார்). Kural 299 says that for the worthy the only lamp is the lamp of not lying (பொய்யா விளக்கே விளக்கு). Both picture truthfulness as a light; Tirumular adds that the Lord is found among such people.

2607 has a bird kept from a fruit of the fragrant flower and driven off with an arrow so that one reaches the Siva-state. 2634 has a strong-legged bird that sought rich fruit wander seeking the fruit of the heart (உளங்கனி) while four seekers light a lamp. Both are unexplained figures of a bird and an inner fruit on the way to release; read together they suggest a fixed symbol, though neither verse says what it means.
2610 says how the jnani deals with former and later karma; 2611 says by what power: Siva's grace placed on the head.
audit_text_issue: tm:2610 line 3 has the typo தததுவ for தத்துவ.

note: Both have the wise meet arriving karma calmly: the Naladiyar's wise take it as old debt and are freed of confusion, Tirumular's jnanis live it out and are rid of it.

The Kural says nothing is stronger than what is apportioned, which arrives before any scheme to avoid it. Tirumular grants that former karma must be lived out, but adds that the jnani can stop karma not yet made, which the Kural's verse does not address.
audit_text_issue: 2610 has the typo தததுவ for தத்துவ

note: Both free the Lord's own from the hold of deeds: in the Kural the two kinds of deed do not cling to those who praise him, in Tirumular the jnani unties former karma by Siva's grace.

2612 says strong karma kindles through mind, speech and body, and does not last if mind and speech stand straight (மனவாக்கு நேர்நிற்கில்). 1896 says silence is mind and speech both stilled; speech alone stilled is mere muteness (மூங்கையாம்). Both refuse to treat speech apart from mind: 2612 for checking karma, 1896 for true silence.
Both make cutting desire the one test that counts: the Kural says only those free of desire are truly free, Tirumular says yogic talk of breath is useless until desire and attachment are cut.

In verse 298 Tirumular says if you cling, cling to the Supreme; here he says cut desire even if it is for the Lord. The conflict holds if ஆசை here is the same as பற்று there; if 2615 means desire for gains from the Lord, the two fit.

The Kural tells the renouncer to cling to the one free of clinging as the means of letting go; Tirumular tells him to cut desire even for the Lord. It depends on reading ஈசனோடாயினும் as desire directed at the Lord himself.
Both say desire is the source of sorrow and its ending brings unbroken joy: the Kural calls desire the sorrow of sorrows, Tirumular says bliss grows as desire is let go.
Both tie release to mastering the longing (வேட்கை) that works through the five: the Naladiyar has it guarded at the five gates of the senses, Tirumular has it flung away with the five elements.
audit_text_issue: 2616's last line தொடுவது தம்மைத் தொடர்தலுமாமே is compressed and unclear

note: Both set அவா (desire) beside தவா (unfailing): the Kural calls desire the seed of unfailing births, Tirumular has humans sunk in the sea of desire while the Lord holds the unfailing sea.
Both deny the Lord a dwelling outside the person: 2614 says he is in no mansion, hall or temple but in the desireless heart, 2650 says this one's house is his only house.

2614 says the Lord is not in the temple or in the ascetic's garb (வேடத்துளான் அலன) but in the heart of those who have given up longing. Kural 280 says neither shaving nor long hair is needed if one gives up what the world condemns (மழித்தலும் நீட்டலும் வேண்டா). Both set the ascetic's outward marks aside for the inner giving up.

2616 says to fling away attachment (பற்றற வீசி) that makes the path of suffering, and that letting go of longing is true knowledge. Kural 349 says the moment attachment ends (பற்றற்ற கண்ணே) births are cut off. Both make the ending of பற்று the decisive act; the Kural names birth as what ends, Tirumular suffering.

2617 says the gods slept caught in one sea and earth's people sank in the sea of desire (அவாக்கடல் உட்பட்டு அழுந்தினர்), while the Lord holds the sea that never fails. Kural 10 says only those who reach the Lord's feet swim the great sea of births (பிறவிப் பெருங்கடல்). Both picture bondage as a sea, the Kural's of births, Tirumular's of desire, with the Lord as what stands above it.

2619 says that when infatuation with women is destroyed (பெண்மயல் கெட்டற) the gain is the eight siddhis. 1948 says that when bindu stays unspent, breath, strength, tapas and silence stay, and undying siddhi comes (அழியாத சித்தியுண்டாம்). 1948 gives the yogic mechanism behind 2619's claim.

2619 places the eight siddhis below release, which comes only from realising truth (உண்மை உணர்ந்துற ஒண்சித்தி முத்தியாம்). 1006 ranks the fruits of worship: Indra's wealth, then the eight siddhis (எண்சித்தி), at last release. Both treat the powers as a lesser gain on the road, not the goal.

2620 says people seek the Lord as 'that one' (அவன்) and do not grasp that Siva here (சிவன் இவன்) is the Lord. 766 says no one knows where the Lord dwells, but whoever sees him within becomes him (அவனிவ ஆகுமே). 766 carries 2620's point from where the Lord is to what the seer becomes.

2624 says the poet, servant of the servants of the Lord's servants, reached the feet by the grace of the devotees (அடியார் அருளால்). 1861 says thinking of the ash-wearing servant (நீறிடும் தொண்டர்) brings more than feeding ten million Brahmins. Both make the Lord's servants the channel of his favour.

2624 reaches the Lord's feet through the grace of the devotees. Thiruppugazh 110 confesses that the poet never praised the feet of the devotees (அன்பர் திருவடிகளே நினைந்து துதியாமல்) and asks Murugan to join him to his feet. The same link between the devotees' feet and the Lord's is gratitude in one and confession of a lack in the other.

2625 says the Lord is cool in water and burns in fire (நீரிற் குளிரும் நெருப்பினிற் சுட்டிடும்) and asks who can know Nandi. 8 says he is hotter than fire and cooler than water, yet no one knows his grace (தீயினும் வெய்யன் புனலினும் தண்ணியன் ... அருளறிவாரில்லை). A near-repeat of the opening invocation, with the same pairing of opposites and unknowability.

2626 asks who can say where the Father dwells (அத்தன் இருந்திடம் ஆரறிவார்) and answers that only those who share his devotees' devotion can. 766 says no one knows where the Lord dwells (அண்ணல் இருப்பிடம் ஆரும் அறிகிலர்) but he is within for those who search it out. The same question gets two routes: searching in 766, devotion in 2626.

2627 has the poet call like a calf for his Lord, and the Lord come seeking him like the cow. Naladiyar 101 says a calf among many cows finds its own mother, and an old deed likewise seeks out its doer (தாய்நாடிக் கோடலை). The calf-and-mother search is in one the Lord seeking the soul, in the other karma seeking the man.

2627 says the Lord came seeking the poet as a cow seeks its calf (ஆன்கன்று தேடி அழைக்கும் அதுபோல்). 2446 says Nandi came like a mother rising at the thought of her calf (கன்று நினைந்தெழு தாயென). Both turn the devotee's search around: grace comes like the mother cow to her calf.

2628 says that in bondage and in release the soul has no task of its own (தன்பணி இல்லை), since the Father gives both through grace. 1527 says that when one's own doing ends (தன்செயல் அற்றால்) through the knowledge grace gives, the three impurities end and one becomes Siva. 1527 makes the ending of one's own agency, which 2628 states as a fact of devotion, the step to becoming Siva.

2633 says those in release, having received the Father's full grace, are in true devotion in which their own service (தன்பணி) has left deeds behind. 2628 says that in release there is no task of one's own (முத்தத்துந் தன்பணி இல்லை) and that the devoted have nothing to do. Both use தன்பணி to say that the released soul's own action falls away in grace.

2615 says cut desire even for the Lord; here the creeper reaches the Lord joined with longing (விருப்பொடு கூடி). Read together, longing that seeks the Lord is not the desire 2615 cuts, unless 2640's longing belongs to Uma alone.
audit_text_issue: 2640 has a typo: விகிர்த்னை for விகிர்தனை

note: 2614 says the Lord is in no temple but in the desireless heart; 2641 tells it as experience: Nandi comes and takes the inner self as his temple.

2635 says Nandi danced in the great bliss beyond speech (பேச்சற்ற பேரின்பத்து) and the test is to hide oneself away and stay still. 1595 says that in the great bliss beyond speech (பேச்சற்ற இன்பத்துப் பேரானந்தத்திலே) the Lord made the poet Siva and made him die. Both phrase the bliss the same way and pair it with the self's disappearance.

2637 says no one knows what knowledge and ignorance are, and both are rightly seen when knowledge goes beyond both (அறிவறியாமை கடந்து). 2580 calls for putting away both knowing and not-knowing (அறிவறியாமை இரண்டும் அகற்றி) to grasp the Siva who is dense knowledge. Both set the goal past the pair of knowing and ignorance, not on the side of knowing.

2638 names the goal by negations: the sign that is no sign, the union that does not join, the knowledge that does not know (குறியாக் குறி ... அறியா அறிவு). 2353 says to unite in a way the mark is not known and stay without knowing knowledge (குறிஅறியாவகை கூடுமின் ... அறிவறியா இருந்து). The two use the same terms, குறி, கூடல, அறிவு, each negated, for the same state.

2639 says the Lord is like ghee in milk, juice in fruit and fragrance in the flower (பாலினுள் நெய்யும்), mingled everywhere. 2115 says the Stainless one is there as ghee within milk (நெய்த்தலைப் பால்போல்) yet people do not desire that light. Both use ghee in milk for a presence everywhere but unseen; 2115 adds that people still fail to seek it.

2639 likens the Lord's pervasion to juice in fruit (பழத்துள் இரதமும்). 2831 uses the same phrase (பழத்துள் இரதமும்) for the sweetness of turiya flooding the body. The image is the Lord's hidden presence in one and the felt bliss of the state in the other.

2645 speaks of drawing and striking with the sword of knowledge (ஞானத் துறைவாள் உருவி) to know and join the Lord. 2968 says that if Yama comes the poet will strike him with the sword of knowledge (ஞானவாள் கொண்டே எறிவன்). The same weapon is aimed at the Lord's attainment in one and at death in the other.

2646 says that once the poet took the sword the First Lord gave (ஆதிப்பிரான் தந்த வாள்), no one could turn him aside. 1591 says the Lord, when he gave his feet, gave the strength of knowledge that is a sword (வாள்தந்த ஞான வலி). Both make the sword of knowledge the Lord's gift, not the seeker's own.

2648 says the teacher told the poet the one thing beyond telling (உரையற்றதொன்றை உரைத்தான்), cut the boundless craving (கரையற்றெழுந்த) and entered him. 134 says those who feel beyond words what the teacher of waveless mind speaks (உரையற்று உணர்வோர்) become reality in the shoreless light (கரையற்ற சோதி). Both share உரையற்று and கரையற்ற, and both make the guru's word beyond words the means of union.

2649 says those who have seen the guru's matha (குருமடம் கண்டவர்), where the offerings, smoke and sounds are known to be the Lord's, go on to stand at his feet. 2148 says those who do not know the life within the body wander bewildered like a dog that has strayed into a matha (மடம்புகு நாய்போல் மயங்குகின்றாரே). The same building yields the feet to the one who knows what is done there and only confusion to the one who does not.

2650 says the Lord has no house but this one's house (இவன்இல்லம் அல்லது அவனுக்கு அங்கு இல்லை), yet people who know it still wail that he is outside. 725 tells how the poet came to see that the Highest had made the body his temple (உடம்புளே உத்தமன் கோயில்கொண்டான்) and so cherishes it. 725 is the turn of mind that the people of 2650 know about but never make.

2653 sets each thing of a matha within the person and ends: Chidambaram, the cave of the self, is the centre (சிதம்பரம் தற்குகை ஆதாரம் தானே). 1726 says outright that the form of the human body is Chidambaram (மானுடர் ஆக்கை வடிவு சிதம்பரம்), as it is the linga and the dance. The two place the shrine in the body; 2653 adds the matha's seat and rites to the list.

2655 says that when the two mayas are veiled and the five bodies pass, those who search within their own form are silent ones who begin from knowledge (ஞானாதி மோனத்தர்). 1674 says the Siva-gnani who reaches the state through knowledge is released and a siddha because he is one of silence (மோனத்தன் ஆதலின் முத்தனாம்). 1674 states as a rule what 2655 describes as an outcome: knowledge leads into silence, and silence is release.

2940, in the chapter on the samadhi of silence, opens with the same line, the light shining beyond the three turiyas, and also speaks of expanding and contracting; here the state is the guru's and cannot be spoken, there it is a state of experience beyond speech.

The Kural calls a head that does not bow to the Lord's feet as useless as a sense that cannot perceive; Tirumular says the same from the other side, that his head, mouth, eyes and mind were given to him for Nandi.

Both make the small great by what they cling to: in the Naladiyar the hare is worshipped with the moon it lives in, so the slight gain worth by friendship with steady men; in Tirumular those as small as a split millet seed become high by reaching the Lord with a firm mind.

The Kural makes one's own deeds the touchstone of greatness and smallness; Tirumular names another measure, the mind that reaches the Lord, by which even the smallest become high. The two need not conflict, but the test differs.

2656 says that when the six and thirty subside (ஆறொடு முப்பதும் அங்கே அடங்கிடில்) the supreme guru gives Siva's state and bliss swells. Thiruppugazh 203 asks to reach the light of consciousness that lies beyond the six-times-six (ஆறாறின் அதிகம்) and beyond turiya, and to join with joy the unchanging Sthanu of bliss. Both place the goal past the thirty-six tattvas and name it as bliss; the Tirumanthiram says the guru gives it, the Thiruppugazh asks Murugan for it.

2659 says that as heavy poison clears as soon as one thinks of Garuda's form, so the three malams clear the moment one fixes on the guru's form (குருவின் உருவம் குறித்த அப்போதே திரிமலம் தீர்ந்து). 2409 uses the poison cure the other way: as poison once drawn out does not rise again (விட்ட விடம் ஏறாவாறு போல்), the one who has seen the truth does not return to the bond. Read together, the image covers both the speed of the cure and its permanence.

2660 says no one knows where the Lord dwells (அண்ணல் இருப்பிடம் ஆரும் அறிகிலர்), yet for those who search it out he settles within (உள்ளே அமர்ந்திடும்). 1722 says the Lord stood where nothing could know him, and yet he made the poet's body his temple (என்னுடல் கோயில்கொண்டானே). Both make the unknowable Lord a dweller in the seeker; 1722 names the dwelling as the body.

2661 says that when the three turiyas end (துரியங்கள் மூன்றற) Nandi stands fixed in the high silence (உயர்மோனத்தானே). 2159 places turiya within waking and ends that where turiya ceases cannot be told (துரியம் இறந்திடம் சொல்லஒண்ணாதே). Both put what lies past turiya beyond speech; 2661 names it as the guru's silence.

2663 lists the Lord entering the mind, the earth, wrath and the forest and ends: this is what is meant by 'his town is to the north' (ஊர் வடக்கென்பது ஆமே). 2070 says people say 'north, north' though nothing is placed there, and that for those who know, all the world in the north lies within (அகத்தில் அடங்கும்). 2070 gives the rule that 2663 applies: the northern dwelling is to be read inwardly.

2666 says that by cutting the many bonds and contemplating beyond thought one reaches the Lord of the tattvas, and he himself is dharma (தருமமும் தானே). Kural 8 calls the Lord whose feet one must reach a sea of dharma (அறவாழி அந்தணன்), without whom the other seas are hard to swim. Both make the Lord himself the dharma one reaches, not a giver of rules; the Tirumanthiram names bond-cutting as the way, the Kural reaching the feet.

2671 says the yogic god dwells as the mouth that eats, the body, the life and the eye, and as earth, water, fire, air and sky (மண்ணு நீரனல் காலொடு வானுமாய்). 2967 says he himself stands as the directions and the gods, and as body, life and tattvas (தானே உடலுயிர் தத்துவமாய் நிற்கும்). Both make the Lord the very constituents of the body and the world; 2671 adds that those who have become the open expanse go beyond even the sky.

2673 says the gods in heaven and the asuras did not see him (உம்பருள் வானவர் தானவர் கண்டிலர்), but those who received his grace remained in it. 1533 says those who saw all six sects did not see him (ஆறு சமயமும் கண்டவர் கண்டிலர்) and bids one become clear and settle. Both say the Lord is not seen by rank or by survey of doctrines; 2673 names grace as what does see, 1533 clarity.

2674 ends with Tirumular saying that, his mind made clear by Nandi's grace, he will bow to gods no more and has become what others go to worship (போய்வணங்கும் பொருளாயிருந்தோமே). Kural 268 says all other lives bow to the one who has wholly won his own self (தன்னுயிர் தான்அறப் பெற்றானை ஏனைய மன்னுயிர் எல்லாந் தொழும்). Both make the one who is inwardly won the object of others' worship; the Kural gives the cause as tapas, the Tirumanthiram as the guru's grace.

2664 says that one who stands in the sixteen-fold path (சோடச மார்க்கம்) sees as other what seemed oneself; 2680 places the same path among the sanmargis and names the stages they pass beyond to rest at the end of knowing.
audit_text_issue: both verses are highly compressed; 2664's argument cannot be fixed

note: 2677 makes Om the source of elements, world and souls; 2699, on the five letters, takes Om apart as A, U and M and turns from it to Na, the first letter of Nandi's name.

2676 says that within the Om are the one word, form and the formless (உருஅரு) and many distinctions, and that Om is release and attainment. Thiruppugazh 160 addresses Murugan as the formless nature (நிட்கள சொரூபம்) and as the guru who came as the form of the pranava mantra (உருபிரணவா மந்த்ர ... குருநாதா), root and crown of the religions and the Veda. The Thiruppugazh gives the all-containing Om of 2676 a person, the guru who embodies it.

2677 says omkara is the form of both the soul and Parasiva (ஓங்கார சீவ பரசிவ ரூபமே). Thiruppugazh 176 tells how Siva's mind was made clear only when the child guru spoke the secret of the pranava into his ear (செவியுட் பிரணவ ரகசியம்). If Parasiva is himself the form of Om, he cannot lack its meaning; the conflict holds on a literal reading of the Palani story and falls away if the Thiruppugazh is read as play.
audit_text_issue: 176 has a corrupt line; 2677 'ஓங்கார தீதத்து' odd.

note: Both give Siva three eyes that are three lights: here sun, moon and the forehead fire, in 2774 the three eyes in the dancer's body whose limbs are space and the eight directions.

Both use light driving out darkness: in the Naladiyar austerity drives out sin as a lamp does darkness, and evil returns when good deeds run out like a lamp's oil; in Tirumular the Lord's light casts off maya's darkness through renunciation, with no word of its return.

2683 says fire, sun and moon received their wavering light by the grace of that light, and that the great light is other (பேரொளி வேறு). Thiruppugazh 1111 asks for an inner vision of a ground of light that sun and moon do not reach (சூரியனுடன் சோமன் ... அண்டாத சோதி), a lotus of light joined like flower and fragrance. Both set the Lord's light apart from the lights of the sky; the Thiruppugazh makes it a place the devotee asks to enter.

2686 lists the lights and says that, by pure words recited daily, the light matches the way one has contemplated it (உன்னியவாறு ஒளி ஒத்தது). Kural 666 says people obtain what they have thought of as they thought of it, if they are firm (எண்ணிய எண்ணியாங்கு எய்துப). The same logic, that the result takes the shape of the steady thought behind it, governs the yogi's inner light in one and worldly undertakings in the other.

2688 says it is the intent of Isan to take as nectar the poison that came from the salt sea (அளங்கொளி ஆரமுதாக நஞ்சாரும்). Kural 580 says those who want a refinement worth loving drink poison though they see it poured (பெயக்கண்டும் நஞ்சுண்டு அமைவர்). Both make knowingly swallowing poison the mark of a larger nature, in the god's cosmic act and in the courtesy of a cultivated man.

2693 says that saying 'it is' and 'it is not' (உண்டில்லை என்னும்) is the way of this world, and asks after a supreme goal of which 'it was not before' cannot be said. Kural 336 says this world's greatness is that one who was here yesterday is not today (நெருநல் உளனொருவன் இன்றில்லை). On the reading that 2693's 'is and is not' is the world's transience, the Kural gives the plain fact and the Tirumanthiram sets against it the light within that has no gap.

2694 says Isan is the sun of a spreading vision (படருறு காட்சிப் பகலவன்), and that the dense darkness of maya (மாயையின் ஆரிருள்) is cast off by renouncing the world that clings to the body. Kural 352 says that for those of stainless sight who have left confusion, it removes darkness and brings joy (இருள்நீங்கி இன்பம் பயக்கும் மருள்நீங்கி மாசறு காட்சியவர்க்கு). Both tie the ending of darkness to a clear seeing; the Tirumanthiram names that seeing as the Lord himself and adds renunciation as its condition.

2695 has Isan with a holy body of shining coral and white ash, and ends that with the black darkness gone he stood with the poet in coral light (காரிருள் நீங்கி ஒளிபவளத்து என்னோடு ஈசன் நின்றானே). 114 says Nandi cut away the verdigris, showed a light no tarnish touches and set coral in crystal (பளிங்கிற் பவளம் பதித்தான்). In both the coral is the Lord's presence shown once the darkness or stain is removed; in 114 the crystal is the cleansed soul that holds it.

2696 says that when the bonds become one and old karma's hold ends, it is like a flower and its single fragrance (வாசம் ஒன்றா மலர் போன்றது). 2829 says that as the water lily's form, colour, bright fragrance and beauty stand together (உருஉற்பல நிறம் ஒண்மணம் சோபை), so the soul stands merged in the Supreme. Both use a flower and its scent for the soul's union, inseparable but not erased.

2697 says he alone is and is the chief among them (தானே யிருக்கும் அவற்றில் தலைவனும்), to be approached as the one who alone is. 2967 runs the same anaphora, he himself stands as directions, gods, body, life and tattvas, and ends that he himself is the Lord in the world (தானே உலகில் தலைவனும் ஆமே). The two say the same thing in nearly the same words; 2967 spells out what the 'all' is over which he alone is chief.

965, in the chapter on the chakra of the holy hall, is nearly the same verse; there the fifty letters 'go' and become the five (எழுத்தும்போய்), here they simply are the five. The repetition ties the five letters of this chapter to the earlier letter diagrams.

Both begin from the letter A as the first of all letters. The Kural uses it as a simile for the Lord as first of the world; Tirumular traces the letters from A through Om to Na, the first letter of Nandi's name, so the alphabet itself leads to the Lord.
2094 tells people to worship the Lord daily until they sleep (துஞ்சும் அளவும்); 2707 gives the words for that hour, calling him Lord and his feet refuge.

2704 says that saying Sivaya nama makes nectar well up; 2709, opening the next chapter, makes the same formula an alchemical pill that turns the body to gold. Both give the recited name a bodily effect.

2701 sets the five letters in places of the devotee's body, mouth, throat, heart, navel and on to the crown (இருமத்தகம்), five with five. Thiruppugazh 1165 makes the Lord's own form of the five letters: na the two feet, ma the belly, si the chest, va the mouth, and ya the crown (நகரமிரு பாதமாகி மகரவயிறாகி). The same mapping of na-ma-si-va-ya onto a body is made once on the reciter and once on the god, which is the meeting point the recitation aims at.

2702 says that when the soul rises leaving its instruments and Death lays hand on it (மரணம்கை வைத்து), it is the five letters that bring protection (அரணம்கை கூட்டுவது அஞ்செழுத்தாமே). Thiruppugazh 75 draws Yama in full and asks Murugan to come on his peacock at the hour of his coming, to a servant who has the refuge (தஞ்சமாகிய) received from generation to generation. Both name a single guard at the moment of death; for the Tirumanthiram it is the mantra itself, for the Thiruppugazh the god's coming in person.

2703 says that no one knows the fitting mantra (ஆயுறு மந்திரம் ஆரும் அறிகிலார்), but one can recite the holy five letters with the mouth (வாயுற ஓதி). 962 says those who recite the six letters do not know them (ஓதும் அறிவார் அறிகிலர்), and that life is won only by those who can utter it as one letter with no other. 962 adds a condition that 2703 leaves out: recitation counts when it is gathered into one, not merely spoken.

2705 says that for those who cut the reckoning of the womb's way (கருவழியாய கணக்கை அறுக்க), it is the five letters that show the way of grace. Thiruppugazh 525 asks that, chanting 'Saravanabhava ... guru' and melting in Tamil, his birth and death end (சனனம் மரணமதை ஒழிவுற) and he reach Sivam. Both make a mantra the means of ending rebirth; the Tirumanthiram's is the five letters with the guru's way, the Thiruppugazh's the six letters of Murugan's name.

2708 asks whether poor people, not grasping the greatness of the five the Lord set down (பிரான்வைத்த ஐந்தின் பெருமை உணராது), will go on with empty talk. 980 says what follows once the truth of the five letters is known (அஞ்செழுத்து உண்மை அறிந்தபின்): the Supreme stays firm in the heart and there is no ruin to the house. 980 supplies the gain that 2708's people miss by not knowing.
Both make the five letters an alchemy: chanting turns copper to gold in 905, and in 2709 the mantra is a குளிகை that turns the body to gold, which makes the body the metal transformed.
Both drop நம from the mantra as the soul's bound part: 1013 calls it the soul and says when it falls away the search ends, 2712 calls it impurity and leaves சிவாய as the truth free of it.

979 says சிவாய becomes the soul, its enjoyment and knowledge and ends in becoming Siva; 2711 spells out what the full name holds (Siva, grace, soul, concealment, impurity) and how the last are stilled before the soul becomes the supreme Siva.

Both free a person from deeds through the Lord's name: the Kural says the two kinds of deed do not cling to those who love his true praise, Tirumular that saying Siva Siva makes evil deeds die. Tirumular adds the converse, that evil-doers do not say it.

2060 says that when the five malas subside (சொல்லா மலம்ஐந்து அடங்கிட்டு) the soul reaches the Siva-state, all being the Lord's bliss with the Lady (இறைவன் இறைவி). 2710 uses the same count, பாச மலம்ஐந்து அகல, and the same end, the soul joining Siva with Shakti. The pairing shows the 'five malas' formula carried from the guru chapter into the mantra chapter.

983 says the hard deeds held in the five (அம்முதல் ஐந்தில் அடங்கிய வல்வினை) fall for those who see clearly within the first சி. 2714 says that, when maya and the three malas go and one chants சிவாய, it is those letters that end hard karma (அருவினை தீர்ப்பதும் அவ்வெழுத்து). Both credit the Siva-first form of the letters, not the full mantra, with ending karma.

Thiruppugazh 851 asks for a heart made clear by saying Siva Siva (சிவசிவ என்று தெளிவுறு நெஞ்சு), alongside the fading of mala and maya. 2715 says those who do not come clear by saying Siva Siva (சிவசிவ என்றே தெளிகிலர்) are mute, and that those standing in that clarity (தெளிவின் உள்ளார்கள்) receive grace. The same pairing of the repeated name with தெளிவு appears in the Thiruppugazh's plea to Murugan.

976 has the syllables recited with the breath (வகாரம் இரண்டும் வளியுடன் கூடி) so that the Lord stands in the mind. 2715 takes the subtle form Siva Siva into the breath and has it stilled within (சிவசிவ வாயுவும் தேர்ந்துள் அடங்க). The later verse carries the yoga of breath-and-mantra from the full mantra to the reduced name.

2499 says that when 'nama' and the rest withdraw (நமவாதி அகன்றிட்டு) the Supreme joins one, which the unclear cannot grasp. 2717 gives the practice: still the name நவம் on the tongue (நாவில் ஒடுக்கி) and raise சிவம் in the mind, and birth ends; then even that touch goes. 2717 turns 2499's withdrawal of நம into a method of tongue and mind.

Both answer endless learning with a choice: the Naladiyar says learning has no shore and life is short, so take only what is fitting, as the swan takes milk from water; Tirumular names the one thing to take, the Lord's letter, and makes it the vessel that does reach the shore.

Both picture release as crossing to a shore: the Kural's great sea of births is crossed only by those who reach the Lord's feet, and in 2720 the one who masters the Lord's letter is a vessel that has reached the farther shore.

The Kural calls letters and numbers the two eyes of the living; 2721 calls those who boast of knowing letters fools, because they don't know the letter that masters letters. The difference rests on எழுத்து meaning script in the Kural and the mantra in Tirumular, so it qualifies rather than contradicts.

940 says the Vedic man esteemed by birth is not the true one; the மறையவன் in whom the five letters stand becomes those letters. 2721 says the five lie ripened within the ancient Veda (பழமறை யுள்ளே), and those who boast 'we know the letters' (எழுத்துஅறிவோம்) do not know the letter that masters letters. Both set the five letters above learning of the Veda as such.

Both use liquor to measure an intoxication that comes without drinking. The Kural says brewed liquor delights only those who drink it, while love delights those who merely see; Tirumular says the frenzy of Siva's bliss comes to those who saw the dance and even to those who only heard of it.

Both put a dancer inside the body. The Naladiyar's dancer is the soul in its skin bag, and once it leaves, the body does not matter; Tirumular's dancers in every embodied life are Siva and Shakti themselves.

The Kural says only those who reach the Lord's feet cross the sea of births; Tirumular uses the same 'reaching the feet' to define the devotee, and makes the feet those of the dancer seen in the golden hall.
1726 says the human body's form is Chidambaram and the holy dance; 2770 locates the small hall at one point in it, the space between the brows reached by fixed gaze.
919 says the five letters are seated as the temple; 2775 says the hall of the dance is the five letters. Both make the mantra the shrine.

Two verses of nearly the same shape: the dancing foot, the sound that rises with it and the songs, and then 'this is how I saw'. 2317 sees them within the nadi; 2760 sees them within at the guru's word and ends the search there.
2727 says the five dances are the five acts; 2799 assigns each act to a part of the dancer: drum, hand, fire and the two feet.
Both map the body's three channels onto the land, with Meru and Tillai as the central channel and the Himalaya and Lanka at the sides; 2754 states the matching more plainly.
2797 reads the dancer's hands as syllables; 2798 adds the foot and tells the reader to recite சிவாயநம in that form.
The same four-line pattern: what the ignorant say, that no one knows the dance, and what the dance is once known. In 2787 it is the Shakti of grace; in 2796 it is the end of the self.
2778 says seeing the dance works as the sight of tamarind does on the mouth; 2779 extends the effect from seeing to hearing.

2723 strings epithets of the dancer, the dancer of Siva's bliss (சிவானந்தக் கூத்தனை), of the golden city and of golden Tillai, and asks who can know him (யார் அறிவாரே); 2743 strings the ruby dancer, the dancer of Tillai and again the dancer of Siva's bliss (சிவானந்தக் கூத்தனை), and asks who can describe him (யாருரைப்பாரே). The near-repeat sets knowing and telling side by side as the two things the list of names cannot reach.

2724 says that for the Lord who dances beyond knowledge, the endless Shakti of eternal bliss became the stage (ஆடரங்கு ஆனதே); 889 says that for the tattva-dance of the supreme light he himself is the ground, ground to himself (தானே தனக்குத் தராதலம்). If Shakti is taken as other than him, the two verses give the dance floor to different bearers; the conflict dissolves on the reading of 2803, where Shakti is தானான சத்தி, himself.

2729 makes the Vedas and the great Agamas dance (வேதங்கள் ஆட மிகுஆகமம் ஆட) as he dances with nada through the whole world; 2317 sees the breath swaying the dancing foot, the drum's sound and the Vedas and Agamas rising in song (பாடி எழுகின்ற வேதாகமங்களும) within the nadi (நாடியின் உள்ளாக). What 2729 spreads over the cosmos, 2317 locates inside the body's channel.

2731 lists the creeds (சமயம்) among all the beings that dance as our Lord dances (எம்மிறை ஆடவே); 1557 calls the First Lord the one who moves among the six creeds (அமையங் குழல்கின்ற) so that they seek his pair of feet. Both make the creeds' movement his: 2731 as a dance led by his, 1557 as a search directed to his feet.

2732 says the dark-throated one took a form of compassion above Sadasiva and delighted in the dance for Uma to see (உமைகாணக் கூத்துஉகந்தானே); 2800 has the tender-eyed one who saw the dancer (கூத்தனைக் கண்ட அக் கோமளக் கண்ணினள்) look on and sing the Vedas. 2800 supplies the spectator's side that 2732 only names: the dance done for Uma is answered by her song.

2733 names Siva's dances Kodukotti, Pandarangam and Samharam (பாண்டுரங்) and the places he is king of; 2776 describes drums and flutes sounding Om, men dancing and hosts and goblins singing, so that it became a Pandarangam (ஒரு பாண்டரங்காமே). The name that 2733 only lists, 2776 fills out as a scene of music and the dancing of his hosts.

2739 has the Supreme dance in the south, north, east, west and zenith, in five wondrous faces (அஞ்சு முகத்திலும்); 1735 lists the five faces given to the devotee facing zenith, east, south, north and west (நடுவு கிழக்குத் தெற்குஉத்தரமேற்கு), each with its colour. 1735 confirms that 2739's directions are Sadasiva's faces, and 2739 sets those faces dancing.

2741 says Nandi subdued the speaker who would not be subdued and set his foot on him (அடங்காத என்னை அடக்கி அடிவைத்து), placing him in supreme bliss; 2433 says he set his foot on my head (கால்கொண்டு என் சென்னியில்) so that the bonds and the heart's confusion were cut, and the state after cannot be told. Both make the guru's foot the act that ends the self's resistance; 2741 names the result as bliss and the dancer settling within.

2742 lists the dancer in the heavens and in the hall of red gold and ends: seeking with joy, I placed him in my love (என் அன்பில் வைத்தேனே); 285 says, after seeing the Lord's feet and anklets, I saw the anklet within my love (கண்டேன் கழலதென் அன்பினுள்). Both make the speaker's love the place where the Lord is kept and seen.

2744 says those who set love on the golden flower-feet in the hall's dance sob, tremble, fall, rise and lose themselves (விம்மும் வெருவும் விழும்எழும்); 1655 tells guise-wearers that though they dance, sing, weep and wail (ஆடியும் பாடியும் அழுதும் அரற்றியும்) they will not see Siva's feet. 1655 limits 2744: the signs of rapture count only where the love for the feet (அன்புவைப்பார்கட்கே) comes first.

2745 says that to see the drama of the dance, seeking ends, the senses stop running and desire ends (ஆசை அறும்), and the gaze of bliss is held; Kural 370 says that if one gives up craving, never filled by nature (அவாநீப்பின்), that very state gives a nature that does not shift. The Kural makes the end of desire the gate of a lasting state; 2745 sets that end of desire inside the vision of the dance, beside the stilled breath and gaze.

2746 says he danced with Kali (காளியோடு ஆடி), on the golden mountain and with the goblins; Thiruppugazh 1053 sets Kali dancing (காளி தானாட), Meru, and Siva on his bull who danced against her in contest, with ghosts and vetalas, as the company in which Murugan should come dancing. The same mythic dance with Kali on Meru is Siva's own in the Tirumanthiram and the backdrop for Murugan's in the Thiruppugazh.

Kural 332 likens great wealth to the crowd gathering at a dance hall (கூத்தாட்டு அவைக் குழாத்து), and its loss to that crowd breaking up; 2746, after the mythic dances, ends with the Lord who dances in the hall for all days (நாளுற அம்பலத்தே ஆடும்). The Kural's dance hall is the figure of what disperses; Tirumular's is the one whose dance does not end.

2747 makes Meru the central nadi (மேரு நடுநாடி) and the body's channels holy ground; 619 says that if bindu and nada rise high in Meru (மேருவில் ஓங்கிடில்), they join in samadhi and a beautiful light appears. Both use Meru for the body's central axis; 619 gives the practice on it, 2747 maps it onto the land of Tillai.

2749 and 2771 end with the same line (கொண்டு பரஞ்சோதி கூத்துகந்தானே) and both place Shakti or the seats in the staff (தெண்டினில், தண்டினில்). 2749 takes the worlds and spaces as his city and Shakti in the staff as the hall; 2771 takes the worlds as tattvas and the seven in the staff as Siva's seat. The near-repeat confirms the reading of தெண்டு as the spinal staff in which the dance is set.

2751 ends with the dance at the end of nada (நாதமோடு ஆடினான் நாதாந்த நட்டமே) after a refrain of things that dance; 2729 ends with the dance at the end of knowledge (நாதம்கொண்டு ஆடினான் ஞானாந்தக் கூத்தே) after the same refrain. The near-repeat shows nada's end and knowledge's end used for one place of the dance, with 2751 turning the refrain to his own body (palm-fire, hair, moon) and 2729 to the scriptures and worlds.

2752 moves from the king's dance in the hall where we bow to the truth in the supreme silence at knowledge's end (மோன ... ஞானந்தத்தில் உண்மையே); 1611 says that for those to whom silence has come (மோனம் கைவந்தோர்க்கு), release, the powers and the five acts come forward. 1611 says what that silence yields; 2752 places it past the visible dance.

2754 says Meru standing in the middle is sushumna in the middle (நடுநின்ற மேரு நடுவாம் சுழுமுனை) and Tillai is the root; Thiruppugazh 863 asks to see, where moon and sun strike the central pillar (நடுத்தூண்), the Lord of eight qualities dancing in the jewelled hall (மணிச்சபை). Both put the dance on the body's central axis; the Thiruppugazh asks for the vision that 2754 maps.

2758 says the Lord shines in the southern hall as lord over the six faces and supreme guru of the declared creeds (கூறு சமயக் குருபரன்); 1533 says those who saw the six creeds did not see him and he is not what they hold (ஆறு சமயப் பொருளும் அவனலன்). On the reading of ஆறுமுகம் as the six creeds, 1533 limits 2758: to be their lord and teacher is not to be reached by them; only those who have come to clarity (தேறினர்) know him.

2761 says that as breath rising in the heart spreads through hands and feet, the ruby dancer as guru delights in dancing everywhere (எங்கணும் கூத்துகந்தானே); 2018 calls the dancing Lord (கூத்தப் பிரான்) the overseeing witness in all souls, as the jewel is the serpent's lamp. Both give an image for the dancer's presence in every life: 2761 as pervading motion, 2018 as an inner light that watches.

2763 says the holy way is in the small hall, in the form that dances within the guru's form (குருவடிவுள் ஆக் குனிக்கும் உருவே); 1574 says the faultless true guru who cuts the bonds and joins one to release is the hall itself (சற்குரு அம்பலமாமே). Both make the guru and the dance hall one place, so that the way to the dance lies through the guru.

2764 tells the reader to seek where the life-breath runs twelve finger-breadths (பன்னிரண்டு அங்குலம்), the place where the Lord of nada's end dances; 581 says that if one fixes the mind twelve finger-breadths down from the nose (பன்னிரண் டங்குலம்), great yoga comes and the body does not decay. The same yogic measure is used in 581 for the gain of the body and in 2764 for finding the hall.

2765 says that as wind, cloud, lightning, rainbow and thunder (வானக ஓசை) shine in the sky, the six of joy and light mingle and stay distinct, and he stands as a form of light, hidden; 20 says thunder and its roar are the Lord's form (இடியும் முழக்கமும் ஈசர் உருவம்). The sky's phenomena are in 20 his form, in 2765 the figure for how he holds the many while hiding as light.

2767 joins the dancer with her of rounded bangles and calls them dancer and dancing woman (கூத்தனும் கூத்தியும்); 1134 has the seeker find the long-haired lady dancing (குரவம் செய்கின்ற குழலி) in the place without night or day. Both picture Shakti herself as a dancer; 1134 makes finding her dance the yogi's practice.

2772 opens with the lamp-light filling the hall (மன்று நிறைந்த விளக்கொளி) as a great flower of many petals; 2446 says what filled the hall became the great Supreme (மன்று நிறைந்தது மாபரம்) and Nandi became a lamp of virtue (குணவிளக்கு). Both fill the hall with light; 2446 says whose light it is, which 2772's petal counts leave unsaid.
audit_text_issue: 2772's petal counts (நாலொடு நூறு, பத்திரு நூறு) look non-standard and may be corrupt.

note: 2773 says seven crores of worlds and seven crores of bodies (பிண்டம் எழுகோடி) and lingas are the temple where he dances the cosmic dance; 1726 says the form of the human body is the Sivalinga, Chidambaram, Sadasiva and the holy dance (மானுடர் ஆக்கை வடிவு திருக்கூத்தே). 1726 states for one body what 2773 multiplies across all bodies and worlds.

2778 says that for all who see the holy dance tears of grace drip and the faint heart melts (சோர்நெஞ்சு உருக்கும்); Thiruppugazh 1294 has the poor one seek the dance of knowledge (ஞான நிருத்தம்) with a melting that grows daily (நாளும் மிகுத்த கசிவு). The melting that 2778 makes the effect of seeing the dance is in the Thiruppugazh the state in which one seeks it.
