Kural 9 says a head that does not bow at the feet of the one of eight qualities (எண்குணத்தான் தாளை வணங்காத் தலை) is useless; 2785 calls the Lord's flower feet the great jewel on the crowns of the crowned gods (வானவர் தம்முடி மேலுறை மாமணி) and the jewel rising in loving hearts. The Kural's head bowed to the feet becomes in 2785 a head the feet adorn.

2786 says that when he dances the worlds and elements dance and our thought dances to his measure (ஆடும் அளவு எங்கள் சிந்தை); Thiruppugazh 1053 has every figure of the cosmos dance (ஆட repeated) and ends with the heart of the king dancing too (உளமும் ஆட). Both carry the cosmic dance into the mind; 2786 makes the mind's movement follow his.

2787 says that once someone knows the First's dancing, it is the Shakti of grace (ஆதி நடமாடல் ஆம் அருட் சத்தியே); 888 says the dance is the work of grace (தாண்டவமானது அனுக்கிரகத் தொழில்). Both define the dance as grace at work; 2787 adds that saying merely that he danced is the ignorant view.

2787 says no one knows the First's dancing (ஆதி நடஞ்செய்கை யாரும் அறிகிலர்); Thiruppugazh 1309 asks Murugan to come performing the dance of knowledge that Narayana and Brahma never knew (நாரணனும் வேதன் முன்பு தெரியாத ஞானநடம்). The unknown dance, Siva's in the Tirumanthiram, is given to Murugan in the Thiruppugazh and asked for as a coming.

2790 says the Lord danced in the beautiful hall for the two to see (இருவருங் காண) without naming them; 67 names among Nandi's masters Patanjali and Vyaghra who worshipped at the hall (மன்று தொழுத பதஞ்சலி வியாக்ரமர்). 67 supplies from within the book the pair whom tradition reads into 2790's இருவர்.

2791 says Siva dances within Vedanta-Siddhanta (வேதாந்தச் சித்தாந்தத்துள்ளே) as nada's end and the tattvas dance; 2400 says that holding the ends together with Vedanta and Siddhanta made one (ஒன்றான வேதாந்த சித்தாந்தம்), one reaches the feet of the dancer in the hall (மன்றாடி பாதம்). Both join the two systems and put the dancer at their meeting.

2792 names the end of nada, the end of the four knowledges (நாற்போத அந்தமும்) and the end of the Veda, and makes the Nada-Brahman in Sadasiva's bliss Siva's dance; 1422 says those who have seen Vedanta, Siddhanta and nada's end (நாதாந்தம்), past the ends of the elements and of knowing (போதாந்த), have unwavering sight. The same list of ends is in 1422 the seer's vision and in 2792 the dance itself.

2796 says that once the great dance of bliss is known, the place where the self comes to an end is bliss (தான் அந்தம் அற்றிடம் ஆனந்தம்); Kural 346 says one who cuts the pride of 'I' and 'mine' (யான் எனது என்னும் செருக்கு அறுப்பான்) enters a world above the gods'. Both put the highest state where the self ends; 2796 names that end bliss and reaches it through the dance.

892 says few know that bliss is Sivaya (ஆனந்தம் சிவாய அறிவார் பலரில்லை) and that for those who can know it, it is caught as the dance of bliss; 2796 says the ignorant say 'bliss, bliss' but no one knows the dance of bliss (ஆரும் அறிகிலர்), and once known it is the self's end. 2796 takes 892's rare knowledge further: the dance of bliss once known is where the self ceases.

2798 reads the drum, the sweeping arm, the fire and the foot on the embryo as the dancer's form and bids one recite Sivayanama in it (உருவில் சிவாய நமவென ஓதே); 905 says that chanting Sivayanama (சிவாய நமச்சிவாய நம) ends birth and by grace one may see the growing dance. 905 goes from the mantra to the dance; 2798 from the dance back to the mantra, and its foot on the embryo answers 905's no further birth.

2801 reaches the beautiful dancer by dwelling in the one mantra and passing beyond it (மந்திரம் ஒன்றுள் மருவி அதுகடந்து); 1013 splits the mantra into நம, the soul, and சிவம, the Lord, and says that when நம falls away one joins the great silence (மாமோனம்) that is release. 1013 shows what passing beyond the mantra means: the soul's part of it falling away.

2803 repeats 2459 nearly word for word: Shakti who is himself stands as Tatpara (தானான சத்தியும் தற்பரையாய் நிற்கும்) and conducts the distinctions beginning with knowledge (ஞானாதி பேதம் நடத்தும்), and dances. The difference is the end: 2459 has her dance in great love (மா நேயத்தே), 2803 makes her dance turn souls to love Hara's feet (அரனடி நேயத்ததாமே); the near-repeat moves the love from Shakti to the souls.

2685 ranks the lights of the five elements, with space among them, and gathers all five into one; 2812 takes space alone and grades it from the outer worlds to the knowing within and the light in Siva.
audit_text_issue: Both verses are obscure; 2685's order is unclear.

note: 2805 says the Lord stands as the great earth and bears it with his feet (பெருநிலமாய் நின்று தாங்கிய தாளோன்); 3008 says he bore this wide world (இவ் அகலிடம் தாங்கி) as தராபரன் yet stands needing no support (நிராபரன்). Both make the Lord the bearer of the earth; 3008 adds that people do not grasp this bearing (உணரார்) and that the bearer himself rests on nothing.

2808 says the three great lights (பேரொளி மூன்றும்) sink into the Father's feet; 110 says the great light that stood as three and five (பேரொளி மூன்று ஐந்து எனநின்ற) is one at the beginning, and fools babble dividing it into three gods. The shared count of the three great lights resolving into one source shows 2808's yogic lights and 110's three gods as the same figure of plurality returning to the First.

Both verses are built on repeated விளக்கு (lamp): in 1818 lighting the lamp lets one know the open space and those who light it shine in it; in 2816 the lamp lit within the lamp leads to the feet of the lamp's owner.
2815 names the churning, Siva taking the poison so the gods could drink nectar; 2823 turns that nectar into what Siva himself is to those who can see.

46 has devotees naming the Lord by colours, அந்திவண்ணா, முந்திவண்ணா, while the one who enters the mind is புந்திவண்ணன், the one coloured as the intellect. 2814 carries this further: the poet became his servant calling him rare and great, but cannot say whether he is dark or red (கரியன்கொல் சேயன்கொல் காண்கின்றிலேனே). Together they show colour-names as the devotee's speech, not a seen attribute.

2817 says that once the nature of tattva-knowledge is known, the Lord of the tattvas appears there (தத்துவன் அங்கே தலைப்படும்); 2666 uses the same words (தத்துவன் தன்னைத் தலைப்படலாம்) but makes the way cutting the many bonds and contemplating beyond thought (நினைப்பற உள்கில்). 2666 adds conditions to 2817's knowledge: reaching the தத்துவன் also needs the bonds cut and thinking stilled.

2819 asks how one can call the light dwelling in all, like pearl, diamond, coral, gold and ruby, different and divide it (எத்தன்மை வேறென்று கூறுசெய்வீரே); 104 says the three gods, examined, are one in continuity, and the world quarrels dividing them (பேதித்து உலகம் பிணங்குகின்றார்கள்). Both rebuke division of the one: 2819 through the many gems, 104 through the three gods.

Near-repeat. 2820 (நான்என்றும் தான்என்றும் நாடினேன் ... இரண்டில்லை ... நல்கினான்) and 1441 (நானென்றும் தானென்றும் நாடி ... இரண்டிலாத் தற்பதம் ... நல்கலால்) both search 'I' and 'He', are granted that they are not two, and end with the 'I' falling silent. 1441 ends 'I cannot speak of He and I', 2820 'I ceased to think': the same experience told as loss of speech and as loss of thought.

Kural 346 says one who cuts off the pride of saying 'I' and 'mine' (யான் எனது என்னும் செருக்கு) enters a world above the gods. 2820 goes past cutting pride: after the gift that 'I' and 'He' are not two, even the 'I' that said 'I' ceases to think (நான்என்ற நானும் நினைப்பு ஒழிந்தேனே). The Kural's renunciation of the ego is carried to its disappearance in knowledge.

2821 names the good path of knowledge as the path of nadanta and its release as the Veda of nadanta (நாதாந்த வேதமே); 2386 joins Vedanta and Siddhanta as one seal and lists bodhanta, yoganta and nadanta with bliss rising when one sinks into silence. 2386 sets 2821's nadanta within the full scheme of the six ends, showing it as one of them rather than the whole path.

2822 says Om is the place of dissolution (ஒடுக்கம் பிரணவம்) for those who can be saved; 2676 says within Om are the one word, form and formless and many distinctions, and Om is bright release and attainment (ஒண்முத்தி சித்தியே). 2676 explains why Om can be the saved ones' ஒடுக்கம்: everything is held within it.

In 2592 the Lord takes the poet into himself like water into hot iron and swallows the light of the three voids; 2825 describes the bliss of one who has gone past the three voids into supreme knowledge-bliss.
2437 names the three padas, 'thou', 'that' and 'art', which bring one to Siva; 2826 gives each its turiya and puts the good in the third.

The water lily (உற்பலம்) whose form, colour, scent and beauty cannot be separated: in 2829 for truth and the rest in the soul's union, in 2843 for the guru in whom form and quality are swallowed into the true form.

2483 uses a gem's stone-light, colour, lustre and rays (கல்லொளி மாநிறம் சோபை கதிர்) as the image of experience in the three voids; 2827 says comparing truth and the rest to a stainless gem's light does not fit (மணியொளி ... ஒப்பம் இடல் ஒன்றா) and offers the water lily's form, colour, fragrance and beauty instead. On this reading 2827 limits the gem simile: a gem's glow is one, while the qualities are distinct yet inseparable like the lily's.

2828 likens Shakti, Siva-bliss, the coming guru and the given body to the water lily (உற்பலம் போலுமே); 2843 again uses the lily (உற்பலம் ஆமாறு போல) for the guru of true form (சொரூபக்குரவன்) who holds truth and the rest. In both the lily's inseparable aspects carry the claim that the guru is not apart from the Lord's own nature.

Kural 396 says understanding wells up as far as one has learned (கற்றனைத் தூறும் அறிவு), as water does in a sand well as far as it is dug. 2830 uses the same measure, நினையும் அளவில் (as far as one thinks), but ends that Nandi, joining his grace, made him think as far as he thinks (நினைப்பித்தனனே). The Kural puts the measure in one's effort; the Tirumanthiram says even that measure is given.

2834 speaks of holding the three voids that are birth (பவமான முப்பாழ்) so as to cling no more, ending in true form; 2496 names the three voids: the void of maya is the soul, the void of space the Supreme, the third the soul pervaded in Siva-Shakti, ending where speech ends in pure form (தூய சொரூபத்தில்). 2496 supplies the scheme that 2834 assumes.
audit_text_issue: 2834 last line seems short a syllable or two

note: 2820 says the Lord granted that 'I' and 'He' are not two and the poet's thinking ceased; 2846 speaks from the far side of that gift: the First can now be called 'I'.

2836 says the Lord stretches through water, wind, fire, space, earth and sky so that the poet cannot mark him off to walk around him (வரைந்து வலம்செயுமாறு அறியேனே); 2632 seeks him in the mountain, the sky, outside, the forge and the heart, and stands immersed (மூழ்கிநின்றேனே). Both start from the Lord everywhere: 2836 finds bounded worship impossible, 2632 finds the seeker immersed instead of circling.

1533 says those who saw the six sects did not see him, and tells the reader to be clear (தேறுமின் தெளிமின்) and enter without wavering. 2838 describes those who have done so: standing in clarity (தெளிவுடன் நின்றோர்) without even a trace of the sects (சமயச் சுவடும்) and beyond the eight causes from desire, they become lords of the gods.

2840 says the Lord, beyond form and formlessness, cannot be reached by anyone without the guru (குருவன்றி யாவர்க்கும் கூடஒண்ணாதே); 2559 describes those who cannot join the mark the guru set (கூடகில்லார் குரு வைத்த குறி) and wander making fine talk. The shared verb கூட shows 2559 as the consequence of 2840's rule.

Kural 3 says those who reach the feet of the one who walked on the flower will live long on earth (நிலமிசை நீடுவாழ்வார்); 2841 says those who think on his form see the aeons (ஊழியும் காண்பர்) and become celestials (உம்பரும் ஆவர்). Both promise lasting life to those who hold the Lord in mind; 2841 makes the means meditation on his form (உருவம் நினைப்பவர்).

141 says what one thinks on is Nandi's red holy form (சிந்திப்பது நந்தி செய்ய திருமேனி); 2841 repeats உருவம் நினைப்பவர் four times and gives the fruits: inner light, the aeons, celestial state. 141 states the practice as the guru's teaching; 2841 states what it yields.

2844 says that in the true form of speechless bliss and silence, A, U and M merge into the speechless letter (உரையற்ற காரத்தில்) and become inner light; 2496 says the three voids end in pure form where speech comes to its end (தூய சொரூபத்தில் சொல்முடிவாகுமே). Both place the true form where speech ends; 2844 reaches it through the letters of Om, 2496 through the three voids.

Near-repeat: 2845 and 2597 are the same verse (தலைநின்ற தாழ்வரை மீது தவஞ்செய்து முலைநின்ற மாதறி மூர்த்தியை ... கலைநின்ற கள்வன்), differing only in கள்வனில் and கள்வனை. The poet crossing vile birth and seeing the form the goddess knew through penance stands once under truthfulness (வாய்மை) and once under the rising of the true form.

Both ground equanimity in fate: the Kural asks why those who accept good fortune grieve at bad; Tirumular's knowers are unchanged whether anointed with sandal or struck with a chisel, since all comes by Nandi's decree.

The Kural says one enjoys only as the apportioner (வகுத்தான்) apportioned; Tirumular says nothing is laid by from heaven except by the decree one has made oneself, placing the apportioning in one's own former deeds.
Both make fate one's own past deeds: the Naladiyar's old deed finds its doer as a calf finds its mother among many cows; Tirumular's decree is the one 'one made oneself before'.
Both picture the body as a bird's nest or shell the life leaves; the Kural uses it to show how slight the bond of body and life is, Tirumular to say the Lord will build another nest.

The Kural asks whether the life lodging in the body has found no home of its own; Tirumular accepts the body as a passing house and draws comfort from it: losing one is like entering another, for those who know Nandi.

Kural 621 tells one to laugh when trouble comes, since nothing presses back on it as well. 2850 lists thunder, the surging sea, forest fire burning the body and fierce wind (என் ... என்) and answers that, at one with him, he will seek the Lord (நான்ஒன்றி நாதனை நாடுவன்). The same steadiness before calamity appears as worldly resilience in the Kural and as union with the Lord in the Tirumanthiram.

1886 speaks of a seed pot and a fenced field where the ploughing was finished before noon, and of those who cannot lose their fear (அச்சம்கெட்டு) to reap and eat it. 2851 ploughs the ploughing of knowledge (ஞானத்து உழவு) in the field the Lord gave, unmoved by elephant, arrow and tiger. Both make inner practice a ploughing and tie its fruit to fearlessness.

Kural 1031 says that though it is toilsome, ploughing is foremost (உழந்தும் உழவே தலை), since the world follows the plough. 2851 keeps to the ploughing of knowledge (ஞானத்து உழவினை நான் உழுவேனே) though elephant, arrow and tiger threaten. The Kural's ploughing that holds through hardship becomes the jnani's practice that holds through danger.
If 2854's 'no going, no coming' is read of the knower, both say that examining and grasping what truly is ends birth: the Kural's mind that ponders and knows what is need not think of birth again.
audit_text_issue: Kural 357 base text reads உணரான் where the commentators read உணரின்; 2854's யாக்கமும் obscure

note: 2804 places the Lord as Om, fire and right order within the heart; 2853 goes further and says the mind and Siva are not different, Siva showing within the mind as it clears.

2853 says there is no difference between what is called the mind and Siva (சிந்தையது என்னச் சிவனென்ன வேறில்லை); 2017 uses the same formula for the soul (சீவன் எனச் சிவன் என்ன வேறில்லை) and adds that souls do not know it until they do. Both deny a gap and make knowing the condition: 2853 by clearing the mind (சிந்தை தெளிய), 2017 by the soul knowing Siva.

1896 says that when speech and mind are both still it is silence, and the pure are those in whom they are; 2854 points to the hidden thing in which speech and mind disappear (வாக்கும் மனமும் மறைந்த மறைபொருள்) and says the one who grasps it has no going, coming or ruin. 1896 describes the practice of stilling வாக்கு and மனம்; 2854 names what is found where they vanish.

2855 says he is the Supreme, the Paraparan, strength, the bright flame, the bearer, and as Hara gave grace (பரனாய் ... உரனாய் ... ஒண்சுடர் தானாய் தரனாய் ... அரனாய்); 2861 takes the same list and denies each item (பரன்அல்ல ... உரன்அல்ல ... ஒண்சுடர் அல்ல தரன்அல்ல ... அரன்அல்ல), placing it beyond bliss. 2861 itself joins the two (தான் அவையாய் அல்லவாகும்): being all these it is none of them, so it limits 2855's names rather than cancelling them.
Both make the bliss bodily: in 2831 turiya, sweet as milk and honey, soaks every hair-root; in 2856 nectar wells up at each hair-root.
Both end on the Lord who stays as scent in a flower (மலர்க்கந்தம் ... நின்றானே); 304 sets the image after the devotee's babbling praise, 2857 after naming him as all things yet beyond thought.
The Kural names sulking and union as what lovers gain from love; Tirumular, using the same pair (புலவி, புணர்வு), says the Lord is both, carrying love's moments over to the soul and God.
2857 affirms that he is awareness, life, union; 2861 denies him every name, then reconciles the two: being all these, it is none of them.
Both call the state where turiya subsides the void where words cease (சொல்லறும் பாழ்) and say it is hard to know or tell.

2163 says as a teacher wakes sleeping pupils with a rod, the Lord wakes those long sunk in anava through Maya (எழுப்புமே); 2859 tells the waking from inside: with mind lit as by lightning he woke, and Nandi opened his eyes (என்விழித்தானே). 2163 gives the general rule of the Lord waking souls; 2859 is one soul's report of it, with the guru as the one who wakes.

2862 says the one of complete knowledge holds both release and attainment (முத்தியும் சித்தியும்) and stands within devotion and the Supreme; 2394 says those who stand in Siddhanta attain release and siddhi (முத்தி சித்தி) while living. Both join முத்தி and சித்தி as fruits of one state; 2394 names that state as Siddhanta, 2862 as complete knowledge within Shakti.

Both make the one without attachment the only thing to cling to: the Kural bids one hold to his hold to let go of holding, Tirumular says the unattached hold to the Supreme and the kinless find him their kin.

In 38 the poet vows never to stop babbling Nandi's name; 2865 says those who gain his light stop babbling. If பிதற்று is the same praise in both, the vow belongs to the seeker and the silence to the one who has arrived.

2864 says when release is reached the soul attains the Supreme, that Siva, without distinction (பேதமில் அச்சிவம் எய்தும்), and faultless nirvana is born; 1431 says those beyond real and unreal become that one in சிவோகம் and sink into the power of bliss in release, attainment too at its height there. Both describe release as union with Siva without division; 1431 adds that siddhi is also fulfilled there.
Both put a single herdsman over the five (senses): 2025 has one man graze them with a staff, 2883 says that once herded and checked the five cows give milk.
The Kural guards the five with the goad of firmness and calls that man a seed for release; Tirumular herds them and they yield milk. Both make the senses useful once controlled.

The Kural says the field of the five must be destroyed (அடல், which Parimelazhagar glosses as கெடுத்தல்); Tirumular wants the five herded so they give milk. If அடல் means only 'conquer', the two agree; on the stronger reading they differ on whether the senses are ended or tamed.

Both use the man who passes over sweet fruit at hand to toil for a poor one: in 201 the jackfruit and the wild date stand for wife and another's wife; in 2901 the banana, jaggery and honey against the poisonous etti are left unnamed.
The Kural uses the ripe fruit left for the raw one for harsh speech when sweet words are at hand; Tirumular sets the sweet beside the poisonous etti, and his riddle leaves the referent open.
2872 ends with those who plough barren land with the breath-yoke; 2880 says their intent is unknowable and what sprouts in such soil may wither.
2883 has the wild cows herded so they give milk; 2903 drives the grazing cows beyond the field to the Lord's feet.
audit_text_issue: 2903's last line (கொல்லசெய் நெஞ்சம் குறியறியாதே) is obscure

note: The Kural says birth is cut only when attachment is cut; Tirumular says the bud's flowering is seen only by those who have let the bond go.

935 says those who clung in pride to the dice (கவறும் கழகமும் கையும்) came to nothing. 2866 takes the same dice (கவறு ஐந்து) and makes the body the board and the Lord the player (பெருமான் இருந்து பொருகின்ற மாயக் கவறு), whose secret the poet cannot read. The pairing shows the gambler's vice of the Kural turned into an image of the Lord's hidden play in the body.

1139 says no one knows the reversed way of the nectar-breasted lady (மாறி யிருந்த வழியறி வாரில்லை), who wells up for those with inner sight. 2867 uses nearly the same line of the pure path (மாறிக் கிடக்கும் வகையறி வாரில்லை) and says love wells up (ஊறிக் கிடந்தது) for those who know it. The repeated formula, with ஊறி in both, lets 1139 name what the chapter's reversed path leads to.

126 makes the thirty-six tattvas the rungs of a ladder to release (முப்பதும் ஆறும் படிமுத்தி ஏணியாய்), climbed into inner light. 2868 sets up a ladder hard to climb (ஏறற்கு அரியதோர் ஏணி) on a palm at the junction of six streets and sees the seven seas from the top. The plain ladder of 126 offers one way to read the riddle's climb as an inner ascent.

Naladiyar 38 says a banyan seed, tiny as it is, casts vast shade, and so small virtue in worthy hands covers the sky. 2870 has an elephant grown from the seed called ஐ (ஐஎன்னும் வித்தினில் ஆனை விளைப்பது) in a field entered by the Lord's favour. The same logic of a minute seed and a huge yield works in ethics in one and in the mantra-field in the other.

41 speaks of those who praise the Lord in a heart tilled like a field (புனஞ்செய்த நெஞ்சு). 2871 says that for those who plough the field of the heart (உள்ளச்செய் உழவு செய்வார்), it grows of itself into a flooded field. Both make the heart a cultivated field; 41 says the Lord dwells there, 2871 that its yield overflows.

805 says that if the two breaths (இருகால்) are set in the upper palate there is no Death (காலனும் இல்லை). 2875 says that when the wind-cows are milked (காற்றுப் பசுக்கள் கறந்துண்ணும் காலத்து) the other cows' coming is not known (மாற்றுப் பசுக்கள் வரவு அறியோம்). If the other cows are births or changes, as is often guessed, 2875 puts 805's claim about mastered breath into the riddle's cattle images; the key is uncertain.

1946 says there is no harvest for the high (மேலோர் விளைவு) except for those who sow, and speaks of the seed within the seed. 2879 repeats விளைந்து and says the crop is seed for what is above (மேலைக்கு வித்தது), its yield spreading for those who reap again and again. Both use sowing and harvest for an inner yield reckoned 'above', and 1946's plainer wording suggests what the repeated reaping of 2879 is.

2276 says the Lord drove the jackals running (நரிகளை ஓடத் துரத்திய) and the soul's bound deeds stood and wailed. 2881 has the little jackal that won't come when called (கூப்பிடு கொள்ளாக் குறுநரி) and the noose (பாசம்) put into the fire, after which he lives sweetly in the house. In both the jackals are the unruly forces that must go before the soul settles; 2276 names deeds where 2881 names the bond.

595 says that for those who mark a boundary and make a way, it is possible to bag the monkey (குரங்கினைக் கொட்டை பொதியலும் ஆமே). 2884 lists wild cows, lions and other numbered beasts and says that if they are held as one's monkey (தாமாக் குரங்கொளில்) they are within one's mind. The caught monkey in both stands for the restless faculties brought under hand.
audit_text_issue: 2884's last line (மூவாக் கடாவிடின் மூட்டுகின்றாரே) may be corrupt.

note: 844 describes a lotus with no earth, no water, no stalk and no root that yet blooms, a light seen where there is no town. 2885 has an unschooled maiden reading an unwritten book and an unborn bee drinking from an unopened flower (எழுதாத, தெருளாத, மலராத, பிறவாத). Both state a direct experience by piling up negations of every means, and 844's explicit setting in yoga supports reading 2885 the same way.

151 describes death: the five who ate rice with ghee poured on it are gone (நெய்யட்டிச் சோறுண்ணும் ஐவரும் போயினார்). 2886 has the five who eat the green crop (ஐங்கூழ் அவையுண்ணும் ஐவரும்) prospering under a burning roof (வேகின்ற கூரை). The five eaters are the senses in both; 151 shows them leaving, 2886 feeding while the body-roof burns.

154 counts thirty, thirty and thirty-six who live in a walled temple and run off when it falls. 2888 lists ten tigers, fifteen elephants, five, sixteen, three, six and five who sit and stand there. Both give the body as a dwelling counted by its numbered occupants; 154 adds that they all leave when it falls.

805 says the two breaths (இருகால்) set swiftly in the upper palate open the door and keep Death away. 2889 says there are two buffaloes in this town (இரண்டு கடா) and if both are held fast they become one (ஒருகடா வாமே). Read as the two breaths, 2889 states the joining in its own image while 805 gives the place and the result.

118 praises the balance that first sets itself level and then weighs (சமன்செய்து சீர்தூக்குங் கோல்) as the ornament of the worthy. 2890 sets a balance in the field of the even mind (ஒத்த மனக்கொல்லை உள்ளே சமன்கட்டி) and weighs in the net of devotion. The same levelled scale is the image of fairness in the Kural and of the steadied mind in 2890.

2916 names its three: three banana trees that bore the three malas as fruit (திரிமலம் காய்த்தன). 2892 has three white rats (வெள்ளெலி மூன்று) brought to the forge, said to be born of baseness (புலைக்குப் பிறந்தவை). 2916's open naming of திரிமலம் is the chapter's own support for reading 2892's three as the three impurities.

126 says that if one draws in the five like a tortoise in one birth it guards for seven births. 2893 says that once the five horses have entered the nest (கூடுபுக்கு ஆனது ஐந்து குதிரையும்) those who have gone in will no longer see the womb-space (கருவெளி). Both tie drawing in the five senses to freedom from birth; 2893 makes it an end of birth, not a protection.

919 says the soft shoulders of women of fine jewels (மாணிழையார்) are the mire (அளறு) in which base men sink (ஆழும்). 2894 says those who set their eyes on clothing, food, oil, ornaments, marriage thread and bangles sink into a pit (ஆறைக் குழியில் அழுந்துகின்றார்). Both picture desire for adorned things as sinking in mud; the Kural's object is the courtesan, 2894's the goods of household life.

218 says that for those who know how the tall flame fed by ghee (நெய்நின்று எரியும் நெடுஞ்சுடர்) burns, the darkness (மை) loosens. 2897 says the fruit is easy for those who know the way of the lamp that drinks ghee and spits out soot (நெய்யுண்டு மைகான்று). Both use the ghee lamp and its மை as a figure for burning away darkness, and 218 explains the riddle's lamp.

844 says there is no earth and no water yet a lotus, no stalk and no root yet it bloomed. 2898 says there is no leaf yet a flower, no top yet a root, no stalk yet a flower to pluck, and the branch never withers. Both describe a flower defined by what it lacks; 844 adds that it is known only through hearing (கேள்வியிற் பூவே).

2087 speaks of what the holy one under the banyan's shade (கல்லால் நிழல் புண்ணியன்) taught the four. 2899 has people see a banyan on the far shore (அக்கரை நின்றதோர் ஆல மரம்), praise the Naked One and take its fruit. The banyan of Siva as teacher in 2087 helps read the riddle's tree as the place of his teaching.

1823 makes the body a temple and turns the thieving five senses (கள்ளப் புலன்ஐந்தும்) into its lamps. 2900 has guarding thieves (காப்பிடு கள்ளர்) in a forest, chased by the honest ones who take back the roof. Both call the senses thieves; 1823 converts them while 2900 drives them off.

536 likens the ritualist beside the knower to one who eats bitter things while ghee, milk and curd stand at hand (நெய்பால் தயிர்நிற்க). 2901 says those who will not eat jaggery and honey mixed waste away for the bitter etti fruit. Both make the same complaint, choosing the bitter with the sweet at hand; 536 says plainly who does it.

2193 says the cows are many-coloured but the herdsman is one, and when he lays down his staff they will not let go of their master (தலைவனைப் பற்றி விடாவே). 2903 says the cows grazing in the field must be driven past the boundary and gathered to the Lord's feet (இறையடிக் கூட்டி). Both picture the cows brought to cling to their Lord.

1823 makes the heart the great temple and the body of flesh the shrine. 2907 lists the seven seas, eight mountains, sky, fire, rain, wind and earth and says that, seeing their nature, if one thinks to live, it becomes a temple (ஆலயம் ஆமே). 2907 extends 1823's temple from the body to everything the body and world are made of.

3038 says the Lord stood as the tall mountains and the seven seas (நெடு மால்வரை ஏழ்கடல்) and as the earth below and above. 2907 lists the same seven seas and great mountain ranges and the elements, and calls them a temple (ஆலயம்). Both treat the whole cosmos as where the Lord is; 3038 says he is it, 2907 that it is his shrine.

380 asks what is stronger than fate (ஊழிற் பெருவலி யாவுள), which comes first whatever one devises. 2909 sets drum, marriage thread and crowbar against each other and says the Lord's grace and love is strongest of all (இட்டம் வலிதென்பர் ஈசன் அருளே). If ஊழ் and grace are taken as rival answers to what is strongest, the two claims conflict; 2909 does not name fate, so the tension depends on that reading.
audit_text_issue: 2909 riddle; meaning of drum, tali, crowbar unfixed

note: 591 tells the yogi to wait like a heron at the sluice-mouth (மடைவாயிற் கொக்குப்போல்) and so last an aeon. 2911 says the Lord settles in the pond not as a heron lies in wait (நாரை படுக்கின்றாற் போலல்ல). 591 makes the heron's watch a model for practice; 2911 limits it, saying the Lord's stillness is not that watchful, aiming kind.

490 says to fold up like a heron when the time calls and strike like it when the moment comes (கொக்கொக்க கூம்பும் பருவத்து). 2911 says the Lord rests in the pond not as a heron lies in wait. The Kural takes the heron's waiting-to-strike as a model of timing; 2911 uses the same image to mark what the Lord's stillness is not.

595 says that for those who mark out a boundary and make a way (வரம்பினைக் கோலி வழிசெய்குவார்க்கு) the monkey can be bagged. 2912 says two paths lie with their boundary confused and those who move without confusing it (எல்லை மயங்காது) reach the town. Both make keeping a boundary the condition of the way through.

619 says that even if fate denies the end, effort pays the wage of the body's labour (மெய்வருத்தக் கூலி தரும்). 2913 says that when ploughing and sowing are done the rain does not fall and the earth, though she works, yields nothing (தான்பய வாது). On the reading that 2913 shows labour without grace bearing no fruit at all, it denies the wage the Kural promises.

880 says the mind joined with the breath binds the five senses (ஐம்புலன் கட்டுண்ணும்) and they drink unfading nectar (அமுதமே). 2914 says the honeyed nectar wells up (ஆரமுது ஊற) and he went and hemmed in the five (ஐவரைப் போய்வளைத்தான்). The same pair, nectar and the five brought to bay, appears in both; 880 states it plainly.

2159 says that within waking the fourteen jackals ate poison and died (நரிகள் பதினாலு நஞ்சுண்டு செத்தன). 2918 has a herd of little jackals (சிறுநரிக் கூட்டம்) with other beasts, weighed until their weight is brought down to a kunri seed. Both use a pack of jackals for the faculties that must be ended or reduced.

879 says to cut a thorn tree while young, since grown hard it destroys the cutter's hand. 2922 says the thorny soorai is thought stronger than the banana, yet when both are cut to pieces the banana takes the place and lives. Both turn on the strength of the thorn plant; the Kural fears it, while 2922 shows the fruitful plant outlasting it once both are cut.

152 describes death: all nine gates are shut together (ஒன்பது வாசலும் ஒக்க அடைத்தன). 2925 speaks of the long gates that cannot be shut, five and four (அடையா நெடுங்கடை ஐந்தொடு நான்கே). Both count the body's nine openings; 2925 shows them open in life, 152 shut at its end.

194 likens the life to a bee that goes to flowers and drinks their scented honey. 2928 says Isan lies within a fresh flower as a bee and takes its fragrance (வண்டாய்க் கிடந்து மணங்கொள்வன் ஈசனே). The same bee-and-flower image is the soul's restless seeking in 194 and the Lord's dwelling in 2928.

607 lists the inner sounds, sea, cloud, elephant, the vina (வீணை), flute and conch, known only to the yogi. 2929 says the vina and its staff mingle and hum music (வீணையும் தண்டும் விரவி இசைமுரல்). 607's list supports reading 2929's vina as the inner sound of yoga.

2883 says the Brahmin's five cows roam wild with no herdsman, and when one comes and checks them they give milk. 2932 has a guide who keeps the deathless boundary and shows the way (வழிகாட்டி), at whose rebuke the five may be eaten (ஐந்துண்ணலாம்). 2932 gives 2883's herdsman the role of a guide and repeats that the checked five become usable.

1687 says the unripe do not know the dawning and will not open their eyes even when it dawns (விடிவது அறியார்). 2934 says birds and creeper announce dawn, but for the one who enjoys pleasure in his longing it has never dawned (புலர்ந்திலை போதே). Both say dawn comes and some never wake to it; 2934 names pleasure as what keeps them asleep.

In 1329 the lover wishes the night would last so he may go on pleading (நீடுக மன்னோ இரா). 2934 borrows the same love-poetry frame, the man with the woman for whom dawn never breaks (புலர்ந்திலை போதே), but turns the endless night into a fault. The pairing shows Tirumular reversing the Kural's wish.

Thiruppugazh 785 says the soul shut in the body-house is whipped by three lashes and driven like a boat on the sea (கடல் ஓடம் அது என). 2935 has a boat at the ferry with five planting their poles (ஐவர்கோல் ஊன்றல்) and warns that if the pin is shaken this becomes that. Both picture the body as a boat pushed by outside powers.
Both make the highest state a kind of sleep: in 129 the wise saw Siva-bhoga within while sleeping; here the Lord and the lady sleep in an enjoyment that has no sleep.
Both use the same phrase for the hidden way in, the ford no one knows (துறை அறியோம், துறையறிவார் இல்லை): in 1987 the breath that circles and lies plugged, here the place where devotees drew bliss.

Two arguments for the same claim, that the state is known only by having it: the mother can't tell her daughter her joy, and the taste of the fruit and the nature of a wife are known only to the eater and the husband.

Both use spreading and drawing in (விரிவு குவிவு, விரிந்து குவிந்தது): here the light beyond turiya swallows and spits out the movement; in 2981 it is the mind's movement, whose end with speech is release.

The Kural promises a world above the gods to one who cuts off the pride of 'I' and 'mine'; Tirumular describes the cutting from inside, the self, wealth, body and mind undone until even the 'I' that would notice is gone.

2936 says that of those who have gone into silent samadhi one cannot say they stood, sat or lay (நின்றார் இருந்தார் கிடந்தார் எனஇல்லை). 2517 grants that many speak of joining the Pure One standing, sitting or lying (நின்றும் இருந்தும் கிடந்தும்) but gives the knowing to the one who has conquered the five senses. Both set posture aside as the measure of union, from chapters far apart.

2937 asks what use it is to write on the outside of the palm leaf (ஏட்டின் புறத்தில் எழுதிவைத்து என்பயன்) the cause beyond all signs, unless guru Nandi joins one to it. The Thiruppugazh song says the attainment of knowledge cannot be completed by writing on book leaves (புத்தகத் தேட்டிற் றீட்டி முடியாது) and asks Murugan to reveal it by grace. The two books make the same claim, with the guru in one and the god's grace in the other doing what the leaf cannot.

The Naladiyar verse says that joining those with understanding (உணர்வுடையாரை) brings joy, while company with the undiscerning brings pain that ends only on parting. 2938 repeats உணர்வுடையார் in every line and says such people themselves have no sorrow (உறுதுயர் இல்லை). The pairing moves the same word from the benefit of good company to the state of the one who has the awareness.

Kural 4 names the Lord by an absence, the one without liking or aversion (வேண்டுதல் வேண்டாமை இலான்), and promises no suffering to those who reach his feet. 2941 builds a whole verse of such absences in -இலி, ending in மருவிலி, the one who clings to nothing, who then enters the speaker's mind. Both describe the Lord by what he lacks and make that the ground of the devotee's good.

Kural 1108 calls sweet the lovers' embrace that not even a breeze can part (வளியிடை போழப் படாஅ முயக்கு). 2943 says the Lord, beyond every grade of his being, stands mingled without imagining, like the desire of lovers in their enjoyment (அனுபோகக் காமம்போல் கற்பனை இன்றிக் கலந்து). The Tirumanthiram borrows the union with no gap between that the Kural praises in love and uses it for the soul's union with Siva.

2946 says the nux vomica fruit is lovely to look at but its taste is known only to those who eat it (தின்றார்க்கு அறியலாம்), and only the husband knows a young wife's qualities. Kural 1090 says brewed liquor delights only those who drink it (உண்டார்கண் அல்லது அடுநறா), unlike love, which delights even onlookers. Both rest on the point that some things are known only by taking them in; the Kural marks love as the exception, the Tirumanthiram applies the rule to the bliss of samadhi.

2947 says Nandi sat in the middle street (நடுவுத் தெருவிலே) and the junctions and samadhis ceased (சந்தி சமாதிகள் தாமே ஒழிந்தன). 2868, in the chapter before, places a junction where six streets meet (ஆறு தெருவில் அகப்பட்ட சந்தியில்) and climbs a palm from it to see the seven seas. Both map the yogic body as streets and junctions; read together, the street is the body's channel and the junction a point on it, which 2947 says falls away once the Lord sits at the centre.

Kural 1090 says love, unlike liquor, gives delight even to those who only see it (கண்டார் மகிழ்செய்தல்). 2950 says desire shows itself suddenly (பொதுக்கென) even on hearing the words of two lovers, and that the Lord gives his wealth just as fast to those who have made themselves ready. Both note that desire is kindled without contact, and the Tirumanthiram uses that quickness for the speed of grace.

1010 says the heart is twofold like darkness and light (இருளும் வெளியும்போல் இரண்டாம் இதயம்), delusion and abiding knowledge. 2952 begins by turning away both darkness and light (இருளும் வெளியும் இரண்டையும் மாற்றி) before joining the Father's feet with a mind that no longer rolls. Read with 1010, 2952 sets aside not only ignorance but knowledge as a state of the heart, which is what makes its closing stillness more than ordinary wisdom.

80, in Tirumular's own story, repeats இருந்தேன் four times: in this body for countless crores, in the place without night and day, beneath Nandi's feet. 2953 repeats ஒன்றிநின்று four times and ends 'I have seen many ages' (பல ஊழி கண்டேன்). The two refrains match in form and claim, and 80 supports the reading of பல ஊழி as the poet's long life in union.

Both use muteness against false silence: in 1896 one whose speech alone stops is merely mute (மூங்கை) while true silence stills the mind too; here those who talk of the unspeakable are the mutes, and the Lord is seen by the mind gone still.

2954 asks, once one has become He, whom is there to think of (தான்அவ னானபின் ஆரை நினைவது). 2970 says the Pure One dwells in the heart of those without thinking and forgetting, and that if one seeks and thinks of him he becomes far (நினைக்கப் பெறில்அவன் நீளியன்). 2970 turns 2954's rhetorical question into a warning: thinking of him is not only needless after union but keeps him away.

Both verses use water without waves (திரையற்ற நீர்போல்) for the state in which Siva is reached, and both set it beyond speech: 2955 mocks the mutes who speak of what is beyond speech (உரையற்றது), 1593 begins with speech ended (உரையற்று) and ends 'we passed beyond words'. The figure and the claim recur across the book.

Kural 357 says that if the mind ponders and knows with certainty what is, one need not think again of birth (பேர்த்துள்ள வேண்டா பிறப்பு). 2956 says that when the mind's maya dies nothing dies after (பினைமாய்வது இல்லை) and that to remain having examined oneself (தனைஆய்ந்து இருப்பது) is the truth. Both make inner examination the end of further births.
audit_text_issue: Kural 357 text reads உணரான் where the sense needs உணரின்.

note: 2718 says repeating சிவாய நம and சிவசிவ fixes the mind and is bliss; here the mantra has become a fruit already eaten, and the speaker reports its sweetness.
Both say death can be beaten by those who have the power of tapas: the Kural speaks of leaping past Yama, Tirumular of striking him with the sword of knowledge in a mind where tapas has come.
272 says only those who melt with love can reach 'my gem' (என்பொன் மணி), whatever austerity others do; here the speaker melts to the bone, weeping, and holds 'my golden gem' as his own.
audit_text_issue: 272 என்போல் மணி is likely a variant of என்பொன் மணி

note: Kural 345 says that for those set on cutting off births even the body is too much, so why any further ties (மற்றும் தொடர்ப்பாடு எவன்கொல்). 2958 names kinship itself a bond (உறவென்னும் பாசம்), says the speaker has left birth and it, and has become one with God. The Kural states the renouncer's aim; 2958 speaks as one who has reached it, naming the ties the Kural leaves general.

2961 cuts down karma with the sharp sword of the mind (அயில்மன வாளால்); 2968 strikes Yama with the sword of knowledge (ஞானவாள்) and says the karma that brings birth was cut long ago. The two verses of the same chapter arm the one who has reached with the same weapon, once against karma and once against death.

A near-repeat: 1870 has the same list of the mountain summit, the gods, the First and those of the eight directions coming into the palm of the hand (என்கைத் தலத்தினுள்), as a condition ('if they are there, we are saved'). 2966 states it as done in the first person singular (உண்டனர் நானினி உய்ந்தொழிந்தேனே), fitting a chapter on those who have reached.

A near-repeat: 412 has the same lines, தானே திசையொடு தேவருமாய் நிற்கும் and தானே உடலுயிர் தத்துவமாய் நிற்கும், in a chapter about the Lord. That supports reading தானே in 2967 as the Lord, though its place after 2966 leaves open that the one who has reached shares in that standing as all.

1455 says the devotee, through kiriyai, chariyai, yoga and jnana, by the guru's grace, finds the mind becoming Siva (சித்தங் குருவரு ளாற்சிவ மாகுமே). 2969 begins where that ends, with those whose mind has become Siva (சித்தம் சிவமாய்) and have destroyed the three malas, and says they become pure Siva and are untouched by bondage. 2969 describes the state whose way 1455 lays out.

2667 says he thinks of those who think of him (நினைக்கின் நினைக்கும் நினைப்பவர் தம்மை) and raises even the smallest who reach him with a weighty mind. 2970 says he dwells where there is neither thinking nor forgetting, and that if one seeks him and gets to think of him he becomes far off (நீளியன்). On the reading of நீளியன் as 'far', the two disagree on whether thinking of the Lord draws him near; if நீளியன் means 'vast', the tension falls away.

Kural 380 asks what is stronger than fate (ஊழிற் பெருவலி யாவுள) and says it gets there before any scheme to avoid it. 2973 says the Lord broke up the fate written on the speaker's head (தலைவிதி பின்னம்செய்து) once his heart joined the Lord's feet. The Kural makes ஊழ் unbeatable by human contriving; the Tirumanthiram makes it breakable by the Lord, so the conflict holds only if the Kural's 'nothing' is taken to include grace.

180 says that to young women the speaker was once like sugarcane and is now also like the bitter kaanjiram fruit (கரும்பொத்துக் காஞ்சிரங் காயுமொத்தேனே): age turns sweet to bitter. 2976 says that once the heart saw the bliss within, the cane turned bitter and the honey sour (கரும்பும் கைத்தது தேனும் புளித்ததே). The same reversal of sweetness marks loss in one verse and gain in the other.

1507 gives the fruits of the paths: salokam and samipam through chariyai, sarupam beyond. 2977 speaks as one who followed chariyai and the rest (சரியாதி) and then turned back, seeing all that is done as Siva, and crossed the womb with nothing in hand. Against 1507's graded rewards, 2977 says release came not as the fruit of the paths but when they were left.

A near-repeat: 2530 has the same four lines, the river, waterfall and inner tank, Siva's fine way, and the excellent thing that is a share with the Goddess yet stays apart (கூறே ... வேறே யிருக்கும் விழுப்பொருள்), with only spelling variants. The verse recurs in two chapters of the book.
audit_text_issue: 2530 reads கொண்பனை for கொம்பனை and விழுபொருள்.

note: 1823 makes the body of flesh the temple and the heart the shrine; 2982 tells the same as a story of search: those who chased the Lord across lands lost him, and the speaker found him in the body.
Both end on the same phrase, புகுந்துநின்றான்: in 27 the Lord enters the minds of those who bow to Nandi daily, in 2985 he enters and stays in his devotees' hearts.
Both make the Lord's thousand names (ஆயிர நாமம்) a practice: 34 praises them going and sitting, 2987 promises protection and the end of desire to those who recite them.
The Kural says the two kinds of deed do not cling to those devoted to the Lord's praise; Tirumular says the lord whom the worshipper keeps in mind cuts away deeds and the planets' sway.

If அள்ளற் கடல் is the sea of births, the two verses agree: the Kural's sea of births is crossed by those who reach the Lord's feet, and Tirumular's sea of mire is cut for those who proclaim his bounty.
Both set the Lord beyond those who would know him: in 13 Vishnu, Brahma and the gods cannot measure him, in 3019 the siddhas and gods think on him through all time without knowing him.
Both end with the Lord as rain: in 11 Nandi is the rain-pouring cloud, in 3021 the Lord is everywhere like rain, answering the question of where he is.

10 lists the Lord as bearer of the earth, fire, sun, moon, mountain and sea, ending தடவரை தண்கடலாமே; 3023 repeats the frame, ending தடம்கடலாமே, but grounds each line in his own strength and adds that he is lighter than an atom.

2982 says those who drove the mind's chariot after the மாயன் lament without knowing the land, while the poet found the Lord in the land of the body (காயம்மின் நாட்டிடை). 1540 says people bewildered by the மாயன் do not know the purpose the body serves (காயம் விளைக்குங் கருத்து). Both pair the elusive or deluding மாயன் with காயம், and 2982 supplies what 1540's bewildered miss: the body is where he is found.

2982 finds the Lord in the land of the body (காயம்மின் நாட்டிடை); 2365 calls the body a good land (காயநன் னாட்டு) of which the Lord is the first cause, and also has him as மாயன். The figure of the body as a country, with the Lord inside it, is shared and rare.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 2982: காயம்மின் looks misdivided or corrupt.

note: In 2984 people call the devotee who cries for the unseen Lord a madman (பித்தன் இவனென்று பேசுகின்றார்); in 1616 the Lord himself is the பித்தன், the beggar of the burning ground who cuts the births of renouncers. Read together, the name thrown at the devotee as mockery is the Lord's own name.

2986 sets the Lord in a series of mirrors (கண்ணாடி): not in that of the elements, but in the Veda, in right conduct and in song. 603 says that eight thousand years of yoga do not show him, but looking within until light comes, he stands merged as in a mirror (கண்ணாடி போலக் கலந்துநின்றான்). Both use the mirror for how he is seen, and both deny that the outward means alone reflects him.

2988 proclaims Siva-yoga as a crier calls (சாற்றுகின்றேன் அறையோ சிவயோகத்தை) but does not say what it is. 122 defines it: knowing the conscient and non-conscient, entering the yoga of tapas, becoming one's own light and going to his abode (சிவயோக மாவது ...). 122 gives the content of what 2988 announces.

2989 tells the seeker to pass through the lotus of the flesh and beyond (ஊனார் கமலத்தின் ஊடுசென்று அப்புறம்) and then taste honey; 2719 passes through the orb of red flame and beyond (செஞ்சுடர் மண்டலத்து ஊடுசென்று அப்புறம்) to a state where the Lord never leaves. The same phrase marks the yogic crossing of a bodily centre in both, ending in sweetness in one and in the Lord's abiding in the other.

2990 says the rare treasure comes and stands for his devotees, while Indra and the gods who ask get nothing but the clamour of heavenly women. 2673 says the gods and asuras did not see him (வானவர் தானவர் கண்டிலர்), but those who received his grace remained in it. Both set the gods' failure against what devotees or the graced receive.

2991 has the Lord settle the mind muddied like earthy water and make it clear (தெண்ணீர்ப் படுத்த சிவன்). 2075 says that as a madman is cleared by medicine, the poet's mind became clear when Nandi gave grace (நந்தி அருள்தரச் சித்தம் தெளிந்தோன்). In both the clearing of the mind is the Lord's work, not the person's.

2991 pictures the Lord scooping from the pond within and making clear water (தெண்ணீர்); 249 has his river spring up within the heart, foamless and stainless, fine clear water (நுண்ணிய தெண்ணீர்). Both make clear water inside the heart the image of the Lord's presence, in one as what he produces, in the other as what he is.

Naladiyar 150 says the well-born help even when they have nothing, as a dried river yields clear water at once when its bed is dug (அகழ்ந்தக்கால் தெற்றெனத் தெண்ணீர் படும்). 2991 has the Lord scoop the inner pond and make clear water (தெண்ணீர்ப் படுத்த). The same act, digging or scooping until clear water comes, figures hidden worth in a family and the Lord's clearing of a muddied mind.

2992 says that to one who longs for him the Lord is like a gooseberry in the palm (கைத்தலம் சேர்தரு நெல்லிக் கனி), the proverb for what is plainly had. 448 says he is not so easy that one can stand and say 'this is he' (இவன்றான் எனநின்று எளியனும் அல்லன்). 2992 sets the condition under which 448's difficulty falls away: the longing of the one who seeks.

2994 says the Lord hides within the heart (உள்ளத்தின் உள்ளே ஒளிந்திருந்து), wondering whether the deceitful (கள்ளப் பெருமக்கள்) will see him. 509 says there are holy waters within the heart (உள்ளத்தின் உள்ளே), but those of deceitful mind (கள்ள மனமுடை) wander over hill and hollow instead. Both place what is sought inside the heart and make deceit what keeps one from it.

2995 names the Lord who cuts the planets and deeds (கோளும் வினையும் அறுக்கும் குரிசில்) for those who worship daily. 2050 says he ended the deeds and the afflictions that seize his devotees (தவிரவைத்தான் வினை தன்னடியார் கோள்). The same pair, கோள் and வினை, is what the Lord removes for his own in both.

2996 says that for those who praise his feet, the feet are the heroes' heaven (வீர சுவர்க்கம்) and the world of merit, and for the reformed (திருந்தில்) the holy water. 2339 says the reformed (திருந்தினர்) left both hell and splendid heaven (திருவார் சுவர்க்கம்), becoming Siva. 2339 limits 2996's promise: heaven is one form of the feet's reward, but the reformed in 2339 go beyond heaven altogether.

2996 says the Lord's feet become the holy water (தீர்த்தமும் ஆகும்) for those who are set right. 509 says the many holy waters are within the heart (உள்ளத்தின் உள்ளே உளபல தீர்த்தங்கள்), and those who wander to outer ones miss them. Both move the தீர்த்தம் from the pilgrim's road to the Lord and the heart.

2997 calls the Lord a solitary teacher with no house of his own in this world (தானகம் இல்லாத் தனியாகும் போதகன்). 1616 calls him the one with no one of his own (யாரும் இலாதான்), who dwells in the burning ground and eats alms, the renouncer. Both picture the Lord as homeless and alone, the figure the renouncer copies.

3001 says the First Lord is like (ஒத்து) earth, wind, fire and the water of the clouds. 3045 says he is (ஆய் உளன்) water, earth, sky, fire and wind, and adds the light that dwells in the body (உடம்புறு சோதி). 3045 moves from 3001's comparison to presence and carries the list of elements into the body.

3002 opens each line with பரிசறிந்து (knowing the manner) and has the Lord there as fire and sun (அங்கி அருக்கன்). 1544 calls him the one who knows the manner (பரிசறி வானவன்), good, the sun (பகலோன்). The rare epithet பரிசறி and the Lord as the sun come together in both.

3004 gives the Lord's cosmic form a crown of world-eggs and red feet reaching to the underworld (பாதாளம் அளவுள்ள சேவடி), which the deluded do not know. 88 tells how Brahma and Vishnu sought his foot and crown (அடிமுடி) and did not find them. Both turn on the head and foot of the Lord; 3004 names their reach, while 88 makes them beyond finding even for the gods.

3005 says the First Lord stands as the light of the three lights (சுடர் மூன்றுஒளி யாய்நிற்கும்), beyond the cosmos, below it and in the middle. 2003 says he himself is the spreading light standing as the three lights in one (விரிசுடர் மூன்றும்ஒன்றாய் நிற்கும்), and space, light and darkness. Each builds on a refrain (ஆதிப்பிரான், தானே) to make one Lord the source of sun, moon and fire.

3006 says he is great, rising beyond the cosmos (பெருமையன்), and small in a birth beyond the body (சிறுமையன்). 3024 says that though great beyond all (பெருமையன்) he is mingled within the flesh in smallness (சிறுமையும் உட்கலந்து). The same pairing of greatness and smallness is made twice in the chapter, the second time placing the smallness in the body.

3008 plays on -பரன்: பராபரன், தராபரன் (bearer of the earth), நிராபரன். 1760 plays on the same ending: பராபரன், தராபரன், சிராபரன், அராபரன். 3008 uses the chain to say he bears all and needs no support; 1760 ends it with the Lord settled in the devotee's mind.

3009 says the one great god is the force, the sound and the subsiding of sound (ஓசை ஒடுக்கமும்). 609 places the Lord, Shakti and good yoga at the end of nada (நாத முடிவிலே). On the reading of ஓசை ஒடுக்கம் as nadanta, both put the Lord where sound subsides.

3012 says there are no words for the Lord even with the gods (உரையில்லை) and he is the one who dwells within (உள்ளுறும் உள்ளவன்). 249 says his clear river is beyond words (உரையில்லை) and springs up within the heart (உள்ளத் தகத்துநின் றூறும்). Both join speechlessness about him to his welling up within.

3013 says the Lord cut the bond made by Brahma (பிரமன்செய் பாசம்) and the attachment made by Vishnu, and saved his servant. 2406 counts the souls as many crores from Brahma downward (பசுப்பல கோடி பிரமன் முதலாய்), all bound by three bonds. 2406 sets Brahma among the bound, so the bond he makes in 3013 is the work of one himself bound, and only the Lord can cut it.

3014 says the Lord dwells in the land and its nine regions as fragrance in a flower (வாச மலர்போல் மருவி நின்றான்). 1459 says Siva's fragrance blossoms within the soul as scent dwells in a flower (பூவினிற் கந்தம் பொருந்திய வாறுபோல்). The flower's scent is the image of an unseen indwelling in both, spread over the world in 3014 and held within the soul in 1459.

Kural 346 says the one who cuts off the pride of 'I' and 'mine' (யான் எனது என்னும் செருக்கு) enters a world higher than the gods'. 3016 names the 'I' a thief-chief (நானெனும் கள்ளத் தலைவன்) within the heart and outside, and has the Lord cut through the sea of mire for those who proclaim his bounty. On the reading of நானெனும் கள்ளத் தலைவன் as the ego, 3016 makes the 'I' that the Kural tells one to cut a hidden thief, and gives the cutting to grace.

3017 says the gods and asuras (வானவர் தானவர்) seek his ringing anklet every day and he wells up in their hearts and becomes a lamp's light. 2673 says the gods and asuras did not see him (கண்டிலர்), and only those who received his grace remained in it. 2673 adds the condition 3017 leaves out: seeking day by day does not by itself give sight of him.

3020 says as many as are the virtues, so much is the joy (அறம்பல எவ்வண்ணம் அவ்வண்ணம் இன்பம்), and though people see many outward things (புறம்பல) they do not praise him. Kural 39 says only what comes through virtue is joy (அறத்தான் வருவதே இன்பம்), and all else is outside (புறத்த) and without praise. Both bind joy to அறம், and both set it against what is புறம்.

3021 asks where the Lord is and answers that he stands everywhere like rain (எங்குநின் றான்மழை போல்இறை). 30 has some hesitate whether the Lord, like rain calling from the sky (வான்நின்று அழைக்கும் மழைபோல்), will call them, while the poet calls out himself. The rain image serves pervasion in 3021 and the waiting for grace from above in 30.

3022 says that what perceives the Lord is subtle knowledge (உணர்வது நுண்ணறிவு எம்பெருமானை), along with the breath. 2518 says the Lord stands as subtle knowledge (நுண்ணறிவாய்) and as the world. 2518 makes the Lord himself the நுண்ணறிவு that in 3022 is the means of reaching him.

3023 says that by his own strength the Lord bore the seven worlds and is lighter than the atom (அணுவினும் தான்நொய்யன்). 668 lists the yogi's eight siddhis, beginning with being an atom within the atom (அணுவில் அணு), greatness and lightness. The powers the yogi gains by practice in 668 are in 3023 the Lord's own nature, held by his own strength (தன்வலியால்).

3025 is a riddle in which a sprout from the banyan's seed grows and a horse ripens (குதிரை பழுத்தது) in the body; 2869 is a riddle in which brinjal is sown, bitter gourd sprouts, and the banana ripens fully (முழுதும் பழுத்தது). Both build Tirumular's hidden-meaning verses on sowing that yields an unexpected ripening, and neither fixes what the plants stand for.

Nearly the same verse. 2857 makes the Lord union and lovers' sulking (புணரும், புலவி); 3035 makes him union and the senses (புணர்வும், புலனும்), so the love pair becomes a list of faculties he pervades. Both end on the scent in the flower cluster.

Nearly the same verse: the Lord stood where nothing could know him, and the eight worlds. 1722 ends with his taking the poet's body as his temple; 3044 ends with Nandi as the one who knows this, our lord.
Both turn on the same line, the bright flame that knows the flesh and breathes within. 1797 asks who could know the Lord if that flame did not; 3027 answers that when it knows, one can reach him.

Both place the Lord by the same four stations, within (உண்ணின்ற), in the sky (விண்ணின்று), on earth (மண்ணின்ற) and in the eye (கண்ணின்ற). 449 names him the light within and the gem in the eye; 3040 the breath within, the sun, the wind and thought.
The Kural calls number and letter (எண், எழுத்து) the eyes of living beings; Tirumular makes the Supreme their maker and goes on to the eye that takes things in. Learning's two eyes become his gift.
Both name the Lord as ஆதி, the first: the Kural makes the world have Adi Bhagavan as its first, as letters have அ; Tirumular calls Sankara 'the first, our first', present with all the world yet one.

Both open with the same line on the three thousand Tamil verses Mulan spoke. 99 makes the work Nandi's grace and promises the Lord to those who recite it; 3046 adds three hundred mantras and thirty teachings and declares the three one.

3028 says that living in the body and seeking the light within (உடலிடை வாழ்வுகொண்டு உள்ளொளி நாடி) one can see the god who dwells inside the body. 2982 says the poet, after wandering through lands, found the Lord within the land of the body (காயம்மின் நாட்டிடைக் கண்டுகொண்டேனே). Both say the body is where the Lord is seen, against search elsewhere.

3029 says the Lord is the inner light in the three great lights and stands knowingly as the body (பெருஞ்சுடர் மூன்றினும் உள்ளொளி ... உடலாய் நிற்கும்). 2003 says he is the three lights in one and stands not other than body and soul (உடலுயிர் வேறன்றி நின்றுளன்). Both join the three lights to his standing as or in the body.

3031 says the supreme flame gives a steady place as thought within the forehead (நெற்றியின் உள்ளே நினைவாய் நிலைதரு). 2770 gives the practice: gazing at the space between the brows straight from the forehead (நெற்றிக்கு நேரே புருவத்து இடைவெளி), where the mantra shines and the Supreme sits. 2770 spells out the forehead meditation that 3031 names in a line.

3032 says the Lord, becoming the one with the tongue, speaks (நாவனும் ஆகி நவிற்றுகின்றான்). 81 says the Lord made the poet well so that he would render him well in Tamil (தன்னை நன்றாகத் தமிழ்செய்யுமாறே). Read together, the speaking of the book is the Lord's: he made the poet for it in 81 and is himself the speaker in 3032.

3033 says the watching Garuda (நோக்கும் கருடன்) and the guardian of the worlds are in the Lord, who removes karma. 2659 says that as poison clears when one thinks of Garuda's form, the three malams clear when one fixes on the guru's form. Garuda, the curer of snake poison, stands beside the removal of karma or malam in both.

3034 says the Lord, though withdrawn, joins with everything together (ஒழிந்தனனாயும் ஒருங்குடன் கூடும்), gone from nowhere and born nowhere. 3043 says he went through the whole world with many things (பலவுடன் சென்ற) yet is skilled in standing as the one that is not many (பலவிலதாய் நிற்கும்). Both state the same paradox of one who is with all and apart.

3035 ends with the Lord close as scent in a cluster of flowers (துணரின் மலர்க்கந்தம் துன்னிநின்றான்), after naming him awareness, life and the senses. 3014 has him dwell in the land and its nine regions as fragrance in a flower (வாச மலர்போல் மருவி). The scent is the image for the inner faculties in 3035 and for the whole earth in 3014.

3038 says the Lord stood as Mal and the four-faced one (மாலொடு நான்முகன் தானாகி), as earth, mountains and seas, and as rich fruit. 2365 says he became Mayan and the lord of the flower (மாயனும் ஆகி மலரோன் இறையுமாய்) and stands as sweet cane and nectar. Both make him the other gods of the triad, not only their superior, and both end in sweetness.

3039 says he becomes the many rare souls (அவனே அரும்பல சீவனும் ஆகும்). 3011 says Siva himself becomes many, many souls (சிவன்தான் பலபல சீவனுமாகி). The two chapters near the book's end repeat the strongest statement of the Lord's oneness with souls, open in both to identity or to pervasion.
The book's frame: in 73 Tirumular puts Nandi's holy feet on his head before telling the Agama; in 3047 the work ends by blessing the same feet (நந்தி திருவடி).

Both honour the feet of the Lord named by his knowledge: the Kural's வாலறிவன் (one of pure knowledge), whose feet give learning its point, and Tirumular's மெய்ஞ்ஞானத்தவன் (one of true knowledge) and மலமிலான் (the one without impurity).
